Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvBoundaryMeshQuality.explanation: Extracts the boundary faces of a volume mesh as polydata and, for each face, measures its relation to the volume cell it belongs to: DistanceFromCellCenterToFaceCenter, DistanceFromCellCenterToFacePlane (both in dataset length units) and AngleFaceNormalAndCellCenterToFaceCenterVector in degrees. Use it to inspect near-wall cell size and skewness, e.g. first-cell height on CFD walls. Input must be a volumetric grid (unstructured, structured, rectilinear or image data); use pvMeshQuality for whole-cell shape metrics.
pitfalls: The output contains only boundary faces, so it cannot be combined cell by cell with the volume mesh without the original cell ids.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvBoundingRuler.explanation: Creates a line along the input's bounding box, along X, Y or Z, or along an oriented bounding-box axis, so its length is the extent of the data along that axis. ParaView displays it as a measured ruler; in Schemaxis the output is a polydata line that can be rendered or measured. Use pvRuler for a ruler between two chosen points.
pitfalls: Oriented-bounding-box axes need all points on one process; in MPI runs make sure the data fits on one rank.
The ruler graduations are a ParaView view representation and may not appear in Schemaxis renders; the geometry is a plain line.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvBox.explanation: Creates an axis-aligned box as polydata with normals and texture coordinates: six quadrilateral faces centred at Center with edge lengths XLength, YLength and ZLength. Use it as reference geometry, a bounding region or a simple test surface. For a box defined by minimum and maximum corners as a wireframe use pvOutlineSource.
pitfalls: Faces are single quadrilaterals; slicing or probing them gives few samples. Use pvPlane or a triangulated mesh when resolution matters.
Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

pvCGNSSeriesReader.explanation: Reads CFD General Notation System files (.cgns, ADF or HDF5 based) into a multiblock dataset organized by base and zone: each zone becomes a structured or unstructured grid and, with LoadPatches, its boundary-condition patches are added beside the volume mesh. Field arrays come from FlowSolution_t nodes as point, cell or face data, and several files in FileNames form a time series. Choose it for general CGNS solver output; use pvIOSSReader for CGNS files that the IOSS library supports, and pvCONVERGECFDCGNSReader for CONVERGE CGNS post files with parcels.
pitfalls: In the VTK reader every point, cell and face array starts disabled, so an unconfigured node usually has geometry but no fields; name the arrays in CellArrayStatus or PointArrayStatus.
Only the first base is read by default; list further bases in Bases.

Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so inspect the output blocks, arrays and time steps on your own files before relying on it.

pvCMLMoleculeReader.explanation: Reads a Chemical Markup Language file (.cml, an XML description of atoms and bonds) into a vtkMolecule: atoms with element numbers and 3-D positions plus the bonds between them. vtkMolecule is not a mesh, so most dataset filters do not accept it; use pvMoleculeToLines to obtain polydata, or pvComputeMoleculeBonds to derive bonds. Use pvXYZReader or pvPDBReader for those formats.
pitfalls: Coordinates are taken as written in the file (normally ångströms); nothing is converted.

Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so inspect the output blocks, arrays and time steps on your own files before relying on it.

pvCONVERGECFDCGNSReader.explanation: Reads CONVERGE CFD post-processing files written in CGNS (.cgns): the volume mesh, surfaces and parcels (Lagrangian spray or particle data stored in PARCEL_DATA UserDefinedData_t nodes) into a partitioned dataset collection with mesh and parcel datasets. Parcels become point clouds whose arrays are chosen in ParcelArrayStatus. Several files in FileNames form a time series. Use pvCONVERGECFDReader for CONVERGE HDF5 (.h5) post files and pvCGNSSeriesReader for general CGNS output.
pitfalls: Mesh and parcel blocks have different arrays; extract the block you need (extractBlock) before filters that expect one dataset.

Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so inspect the output blocks, arrays and time steps on your own files before relying on it.

pvCONVERGECFDReader.explanation: Reads CONVERGE CFD HDF5 post files (.h5) into a partitioned dataset collection: each stream in the file is a top-level group holding its mesh (cell data), surfaces and parcels (point clouds of spray or particle data). The reader detects a time series from files named <prefix><zero-padded index>[_<time>].h5 next to the chosen file and takes each file's time from its metadata. Use pvCONVERGECFDCGNSReader for CONVERGE output written as CGNS.
pitfalls: Name one file of the series; the other time steps are found by naming convention, so keep the files together and unrenamed.
The VTK reader does not support parallel loading.

Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so inspect the output blocks, arrays and time steps on your own files before relying on it.

pvCSVReader.explanation: Reads delimited text (.csv, .tsv, .txt) into a table (vtkTable): one column per field, typed as numbers when DetectNumericColumns is on (ParaView default), with the first line as column names by default. The ParaView XML calls the output a 1-D rectilinear grid, but the underlying vtkDelimitedTextReader produces a table. Use pvTableToPoints or pvTableToStructuredGrid to turn coordinate columns into geometry; several files form a time series.
pitfalls: The default delimiter is a comma only; set FieldDelimiterCharacters (or AddTabFieldDelimiter for tab-separated files) to match the file.
A table is not a dataset; filters that need points or cells reject it until it is converted.

Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so inspect the output blocks, arrays and time steps on your own files before relying on it.

pvCalculator.explanation: Full native Calculator: evaluates an expression over point, cell, row or other attribute arrays and stores the result as a new array of a chosen numeric type, or, with CoordinateResults, as new point coordinates (moving the mesh), or as normals or texture coordinates. Output has the input's data type. Use calculator for the common point/cell array case.
pitfalls: AttributeType is the ParaView entry text ("Point Data", "Cell Data", "Row Data" for tables, …), the same texts the calculator operation uses; the expression may only use arrays of that association.
CoordinateResults needs a 3-component result; a scalar expression cannot move points.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCellCenters.explanation: Replaces each cell by a point at its parametric centre and outputs polygonal data; the input cell arrays become point arrays on those points. Use it to place glyphs or labels per cell, to probe or export cell-centred solver values as a point cloud, or as seeds. With VertexCells on, a vertex cell is added per point so the points render and count as cells. pvCoordinates instead keeps the mesh and adds centres as an array.
pitfalls: The parametric centre is not the volume centroid for distorted or non-linear cells.
Without VertexCells (ParaView default false) the output has points but no cells, which some later operations and exports ignore.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCellDatatoPointData.explanation: Converts cell-centred arrays to point-centred arrays by averaging, at each point, the values of the cells that use it; the output has the same dataset type. Needed before operations that require point data, such as contouring, streamline tracing or smooth colouring of solver results stored per cell. It is the native filter behind cellToPoint, which keeps the cell data by Schemaxis default; pvCellDatatoPointData keeps ParaView's defaults, which convert all arrays and drop the original cell arrays.
pitfalls: Averaging smooths discontinuities such as shocks or material interfaces; keep the cell data (PassCellData) when exact cell values matter.
With PieceInvariant false (default), values at partition boundaries can differ between MPI processes.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCellGridElevation.explanation: Adds a scalar attribute (default name Elevation) to a cell grid (vtkCellGrid) measuring distance from Origin: along Axis for Planar distance (ParaView default), from the line through Origin along Axis for Cylindrical distance, or from Origin itself for Spherical distance. Shock adds an offset that makes the field jump between cells, intended to demonstrate discontinuous Galerkin (DG) cells. Use it on cell-grid data from pvConvertToCellGrid or pvIOSSCellGridReader; for ordinary datasets use elevation or pvElevation.
pitfalls: Input must be a vtkCellGrid; convert unstructured grids with pvConvertToCellGrid first.
Keep Shock at 0 for a continuous distance field; non-zero values deliberately create discontinuities at cell boundaries.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCellGridProbe.explanation: Probes a cell grid (Source port, vtkCellGrid) at the points of a polydata (Input port): the output polydata keeps the probe points that lie inside cells of the cell grid, with the chosen cell-grid attribute interpolated to them. A point inside several overlapping cells, typically on a shared boundary, appears once per cell. Use it to sample DG or other cell-grid fields along lines or at locations; for ordinary datasets use resample, pvResampleWithDataset or probeLine.
pitfalls: Probe points outside the cell grid are dropped, so the output can have fewer points than the probe input.
Repeated points on cell boundaries bias averages; remove or account for them before summarizing.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCellSize.explanation: Full native Cell Size filter: adds cell-data arrays with the point count of 0-D cells (VertexCount), the length of 1-D cells (Length), the area of 2-D cells (Area) and the volume of 3-D cells (Volume), in dataset coordinate units. Cells of other dimensions get 0 in each array. With ComputeSum the totals per array are also stored as one-value field-data arrays of the same names; for composite input the top-level output holds the sum over all blocks. Use it instead of cellSize when you need custom array names or to switch off the vertex count.
pitfalls: Ghost cells receive per-cell values but are excluded from the sums.
Nothing is converted: a mesh in millimetres gives areas in square millimetres.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCesium3DTilesReader.explanation: Reads a Cesium 3D Tiles tileset (the tileset .json file and the glTF, GLB or B3DM tiles it references) into a partitioned dataset collection with one partitioned dataset per tile. Coordinates stay in the tileset's Cartesian frame, typically Earth-centred metres for georeferenced city or terrain models. Use it to bring photogrammetry or city meshes into a pipeline; Level chooses how deep in the tile tree to read.
pitfalls: ParaView 5.13.3 starts from Level 0, the root (coarsest) tiles; increase Level for more detail, at the cost of reading many more tiles.
Earth-centred coordinates are millions of metres from the origin; translate the data before combining it with local-coordinate models.
Schemaxis generates this reader binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check with a sample file of this format.

pvCityGMLReader.explanation: Reads a CityGML (.gml) city model into a multiblock dataset: top-level blocks per CityGML element type (buildings, roads, water bodies, vegetation …) labelled by an element field array, with polygonal leaves carrying a gml_id field array and, when textured, tcoords and a texture_uri. Only the chosen level of detail (LOD) is read. Use it for urban geometry, e.g. as obstacles for wind or dispersion studies.
pitfalls: Objects that do not exist at the chosen LOD are missing from the output; lower LOD if buildings disappear.
Coordinates are in the file's coordinate reference system; nothing is reprojected.
Schemaxis generates this reader binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check with a sample file of this format.

pvClean.explanation: Cleans polygonal data: merges duplicate or nearby points, removes unused points and converts degenerate cells to lower-dimensional forms (a triangle with two merged points becomes a line, a zero-length line a point). Use it before operations that need connected topology, such as featureEdges, normals, pvDecimate or connectivity, on surfaces with duplicated vertices (STL, per-face exports). clean is the curated version; cleanGrid handles unstructured grids.
pitfalls: With the default Tolerance 0 only exactly coincident points merge; a relative tolerance is a fraction of the bounding-box diagonal, so even 0.001 can merge real detail on a large model.
Input must be polydata; use cleanGrid or pvCleantoGrid for unstructured grids.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCleanCellstoGrid.explanation: Removes duplicate cells (cells using the same set of points) from an unstructured grid and repairs cells that reference the same point more than once; the output is an unstructured grid. Use it after merging meshes or importing data with repeated elements. It assumes duplicate points were merged already, so run pvCleantoGrid first.
pitfalls: Cells that are geometrically identical but use different (unmerged) point IDs are not detected as duplicates.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCleantoGrid.explanation: Merges coincident or nearly coincident points and converts any dataset to an unstructured grid, e.g. to join blocks that share faces or to feed an operation that needs unstructured input. Merging uses Tolerance (fraction of the bounding-box diagonal) or AbsoluteTolerance, and PointDataWeightingStrategy decides how data on merged points is combined. Use cleanGrid for the common case with Schemaxis defaults.
pitfalls: Converting large structured grids to unstructured grids can use much more memory.
A tolerance that is too large fuses distinct points and collapses small cells.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvClientServerMoveData.explanation: ParaView-internal helper that copies data from the server's root process to the client in a client-server session; without a remote connection it is a pass-through filter. Because the receiving side must create its output before data arrive, the output type is fixed by OutputDataType (and image extent by WholeExtent) rather than taken from the input. It has no analysis value in a Schemaxis pipeline; use passArrays or no filter at all.
pitfalls: Keep OutputDataType equal to the input's VTK type id; the input is shallow-copied into an output of that type, so a mismatch gives incomplete or empty output.
Schemaxis serial examples do not establish MPI or client-server behaviour. Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvClip.explanation: Full native Clip: cuts the input with an implicit function chosen in ClipType (Plane, Box, Sphere, Cylinder) or with a scalar iso-value (ClipType Scalar plus Scalars and Value) and keeps one side, returning an unstructured grid. Crinkleclip keeps whole cells instead of cutting them. HyperTreeGridClipper replaces ClipType for hyper-tree-grid input. Use clip for a simple plane clip with Schemaxis defaults.
pitfalls: ParaView starts with Invert true, which keeps the region inside the function (behind a plane's normal, inside a sphere or box); set Invert false to keep the other side.
With ClipType Scalar, point arrays are clipped exactly at Value, while cell arrays remove whole cells (threshold-like).
Schemaxis ships a Plane clip example (examples/schemaxis/paraview-catalogue.json), but the operation's coverage records no native qualification run; other clip types are unexercised.

pvClipClosedSurface.explanation: Clips a closed, manifold polygonal surface with a plane and caps the cut with new faces, so the result is again a closed (watertight) surface, e.g. to cut a CAD solid or an STL body and still compute its volume. Output is polydata; GenerateCellOrigins can add cell scalars that distinguish original faces from cap faces. Use clip or pvClip for volume meshes.
pitfalls: The input must be closed and manifold (no open edges, no edges shared by more than two faces); otherwise caps are wrong or missing. Check with featureEdges first.
Face orientation defines the solid side: back faces must face the interior.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvColorByArray.explanation: Converts one single-component point array of an image (vtkImageData) into colour values by passing it through a lookup table, producing image data whose scalars are unsigned char luminance, luminance-alpha, RGB (ParaView default) or RGBA tuples. Connect the LookupTable input to a lookup-table resource node such as pvResourcePVLookupTable; its value range and colours decide the mapping. Use it to bake a colour map into image data, e.g. before writing a PNG with pvWritePNGWriter; for on-screen colouring use scene appearance settings instead.
pitfalls: Without a LookupTable the filter only passes the input through, which works only for unsigned char data already in the output format; always connect a lookup table.
The result holds colours, not the original values; keep the source image for quantitative work.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCompositeCellGridReader.explanation: Reads cell-grid data (.dg JSON files, e.g. discontinuous Galerkin or other high-order results) into a partitioned dataset collection of vtkCellGrid objects, keeping only the selected cell types and cell attributes. Cell grids store fields with their own interpolation rules rather than as ordinary point or cell arrays, so only filters that support vtkCellGrid accept the output directly. It is a distributed reader.
pitfalls: Most classic filters (slice, contour, threshold) do not accept cell grids; check that each following operation supports them.
Schemaxis generates this reader binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check with a sample file of this format.

pvCompositeDataIDSelectionSource.explanation: Creates an ID selection for composite data (multiblock or AMR): each entry names a block by flat index, a process (piece) and an element id within that block, interpreted as cell or point ids according to FieldType. Use it to pick specific cells or points in specific blocks, for example probe cells reported by an earlier run. For non-composite data use pvIDSelectionSource. A selection is not a dataset: connect it to the Selection input of pvExtractSelection, pvPlotSelectionOverTime or pvAnnotateSelection; it cannot be published as geometry.
pitfalls: Element ids are local to the block and zero-based, not global ids; use pvGlobalIDSelectionSource for global ids.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvComputeConnectedSurfaceProperties.explanation: Deprecated alias of pvConnectedSurfaceProperties (ParaView 5.13 marks it for removal in 5.14); behaviour is identical. Computes the volume, surface area and centroid of each closed object in a polygonal input, plus totals; objects are found as connected components, or taken from an object-ID cell array. Per-object results go to field data (ObjectValidity, ObjectVolumes, ObjectAreas, ObjectCentroids) and per-polygon ObjectIds, Areas and Volumes to cell data. Use it to measure particles, droplets or parts in one surface mesh; use integrate for general integrals.
pitfalls: Prefer pvConnectedSurfaceProperties; this name will disappear with the next ParaView release.
Objects must be closed and manifold for valid volumes; check the ObjectValidity array before trusting a value.
Volumes and areas are in dataset units cubed and squared; no unit conversion is applied.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvComputeDerivatives.explanation: Computes derivatives of point data at each cell's parametric centre and stores them as cell arrays: ScalarGradient (gradient of the selected point scalar) or Vorticity as the vector output, and VectorGradient (9-component tensor) or Strain as the tensor output. Input point and cell data pass through. Use it for cell-wise gradients of point fields on any mesh; use gradient or pvGradient for point-centred gradients and Q-criterion.
pitfalls: The selected arrays must be point data; cell-centred solver fields give no derivatives, so convert them with cellToPoint first.
By ParaView default both a scalar gradient and a vector gradient are requested; set OutputVectorType or OutputTensorType to Nothing for what you do not need.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvComputeMoleculeBonds.explanation: Adds single bonds to a molecule (vtkMolecule) from interatomic distances alone: two atoms are bonded when their distance is below the sum of their covalent radii widened by Tolerance. Valence, hybridization, aromaticity and bond order are ignored, so every bond is single. Use it when atoms come without connectivity, e.g. after pvConvertIntoMolecule or a coordinate-only reader, and follow with pvMoleculeToLines to turn the bonds into line cells.
pitfalls: The covalent radii are VTK's periodic-table (Blue Obelisk) values in ångströms, so atom coordinates must be in ångströms; nanometre or bohr coordinates give missing or spurious bonds.
Every bond is single and inferred from distance alone; do not use the result for bond-order or valence analysis.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvComputeQuartiles.explanation: Computes, for every single-component numeric array, the five order statistics minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum, and outputs them as a table (vtkTable) with one column per array and five rows. For a dataset the point-data arrays are used; a table input uses its columns, and composite input adds one column per block (suffix _Block_<id>). Use it for box-plot style summaries of a field's distribution; use pvHistogram for the full distribution.
pitfalls: Multi-component arrays such as velocity are skipped, not reduced to magnitude; compute a magnitude array first if you need its quartiles.
Cell-data arrays of a dataset are not summarised; convert them with cellToPoint or extract them to a table first.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvComputeSides.explanation: Adds arrays to a cell grid (vtkCellGrid) listing the unshared sides of its cells, i.e. external surfaces and non-conforming internal interfaces, as (cell id, side id) pairs grouped by cell type and side shape. ParaView's cell-grid representation uses these arrays to render the grid efficiently; the cells themselves are unchanged. Use it when preparing cell grids from pvConvertToCellGrid for rendering or boundary extraction.
pitfalls: The cell types must implement VTK's sides query; ordinary datasets need pvConvertToCellGrid first.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvConduit.explanation: In-situ source that converts a Conduit node following the Mesh Blueprint into a VTK dataset. The node is handed over in memory by a running simulation through Catalyst, not read from a file, so a Schemaxis document cannot supply its data. Use file readers for stored results.
pitfalls: In a Schemaxis run nothing provides the Conduit node, so expect an empty or failing output.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCone.explanation: Creates a cone as polydata: a polygonal approximation with Resolution side facets, axis along Direction, height Height and base radius Radius, centred at Center (the midpoint of the axis), with the base capped by default. Use it as reference geometry or a glyph shape. The curated cone operation offers the same geometry with Schemaxis defaults and validated ranges.
pitfalls: ParaView's default Resolution is 6, a visibly hexagonal cone; raise it (e.g. 32) for a round appearance.
Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

pvConnectedSurfaceProperties.explanation: Computes the volume, surface area and centroid of each closed object in a polygonal input, plus totals; objects are found as connected components, or taken from an object-ID cell array. Per-object results go to field data (ObjectValidity, ObjectVolumes, ObjectAreas, ObjectCentroids) and per-polygon ObjectIds, Areas and Volumes to cell data. Use it to measure particles, droplets or parts in one surface mesh; use integrate for general integrals.
pitfalls: Objects must be closed and manifold for valid volumes; check the ObjectValidity array before trusting a value.
Volumes and areas are in dataset units cubed and squared; no unit conversion is applied.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvConnectivity.explanation: Finds connected regions (cells linked through shared points) and outputs an unstructured grid of all regions, the largest one (most cells) or the one closest to ClosestPoint, per ExtractionMode. With ColorRegions (ParaView default true) RegionId arrays number the regions, in the order RegionIdAssignmentMode sets. Use it to separate disjoint parts, remove small fragments or isolate one body; connectivity is the curated version with fewer settings.
pitfalls: Connectivity is topological: parts touching only through duplicate points count as separate regions; merge points with clean or cleanGrid first.
Largest region means most cells, not largest volume or area.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvContingencyStatistics.explanation: Builds contingency tables (joint frequency counts) for pairs of the selected arrays, giving a bivariate probability model and the information entropy, and can assess each observation with joint and conditional probabilities and pointwise mutual information. It suits categorical or discrete variables such as material ids or flags. Output port 0 is the statistical model (a multiblock of tables) and port 1 the input with assessment arrays added; select them with {"node": id, "port": n}.
pitfalls: Select at least two arrays; continuous floating-point arrays produce one category per distinct value, so bin them first.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvContour.explanation: Full native Contour: isosurfaces or isolines of a point scalar (cell scalar for hyper tree grids) at each value in Isosurfaces, output as polydata, with options for normals, gradients, contour-value scalars, triangle output, fast mode for image data, the 3-D strategy, point precision and point merging. Use contour for the common case with Schemaxis defaults.
pitfalls: Isosurfaces has no default; with an empty list the output is empty.
For ordinary datasets the array must be point data; run cellToPoint on cell arrays.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvConvertAMRdatasettoMultiblock.explanation: Converts overlapping AMR data (vtkOverlappingAMR) into a multiblock dataset whose leaves are the individual uniform-grid blocks, so filters or writers that do not understand AMR can process them. The result is a flat multiblock with one block per AMR grid, listed level by level; grids are shallow copies, so their arrays (including any blanking array) are kept, but level and refinement metadata are lost and coarse cells covered by finer levels are not removed. Use pvResampleAMR instead when you need a single uniform grid.
pitfalls: Overlapping levels mean the same region appears at several resolutions; integrals or statistics over all blocks count it more than once unless hidden cells are removed.
Non-overlapping AMR is not accepted by this filter.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvConvertIntoMolecule.explanation: Turns a point set (polydata, unstructured grid or another vtkPointSet) into a molecule (vtkMolecule): every point becomes an atom at the same position, its element read from a one-component point array of atomic numbers, and the other point arrays become atom data. With ConvertLinesIntoBonds (ParaView default true) each line cell becomes a bond. Use it to bring particle or simulation output into the chemistry operations pvComputeMoleculeBonds, pvAppendMolecule and pvMoleculeToLines.
pitfalls: The array must hold element numbers (1 hydrogen, 6 carbon, 8 oxygen…), not a simulation code's atom-type indices; remap types upstream, e.g. with calculator.
If no atomic-number array is selected and the input has no active point scalars, the native filter fails with "does not have atomic numbers as input".
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvConvertPolyhedralCells.explanation: Tries to convert polyhedron (and polygon) cells of an unstructured grid into equivalent simple cells (tetrahedron, pyramid, wedge, hexahedron) when their topology allows; cells that cannot be converted stay as they are. Output is an unstructured grid. Use it on meshes from polyhedral-capable readers such as OpenFOAM to speed up later processing and to allow operations that handle simple cells better.
pitfalls: Genuinely polyhedral cells remain polyhedra; the output can still be mixed.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvConvertSelection.explanation: Converts a selection (a vtkSelection on the Input port, e.g. from pvIDSelectionSource or pvLocationSelectionSource) into another content type, evaluated against the dataset on DataInput: for example cell indices become the global IDs, or the values of a named array, at those cells. The output is again a vtkSelection with no geometry; feed it to pvExtractSelection or pvAnnotateSelection. vtkConvertSelection can produce INDICES, GLOBALIDs, PEDIGREEIDS or VALUES from another type; FRUSTUM, LOCATIONS and THRESHOLDS are only accepted when the input selection already has that type.
pitfalls: ParaView 5.13.3 initializes OutputType to LOCATIONS, which cannot be produced from any other selection type; always set OutputType, usually to INDICES, GLOBALIDs or VALUES.
VALUES output needs at least one name in ArrayNames and THRESHOLDS exactly one; otherwise the native filter reports an error.
GLOBALIDs and PEDIGREEIDS output read the designated global-ID or pedigree-ID array of the DataInput dataset; datasets without one cannot be converted.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvConvertToCellGrid.explanation: Converts an unstructured grid, or a composite whose leaves are unstructured grids with linear cells, into a partitioned dataset collection of cell grids (vtkCellGrid). Field-data annotations written by the IOSS reader promote certain cell arrays to spatially varying discontinuous Galerkin (DG) attributes; data without annotations is converted too. Use it before pvComputeSides, pvCellGridElevation or pvCellGridProbe.
pitfalls: VTK assumes all cells of one shape in a grid have the same order; mixed-order meshes may convert incorrectly.
A cell grid is not a vtkDataSet, so dataset operations cannot take this output; keep the original branch for ordinary processing.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvConvertToMultiBlock.explanation: Wraps any input — a single dataset, table, graph or composite — in a vtkMultiBlockDataSet: a non-composite input becomes one block, other composites keep their hierarchy, and a multiblock passes through. Use it when a later step or writer expects multiblock data, e.g. pvWriteXMLMultiBlockDataWriter; pvConvertToPartitionedDataSetCollection produces the newer partitioned format.
pitfalls: Wrapping adds structure, not data; steps that need a single dataset then require merge or extractBlock.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvConvertToPartitionedDataSetCollection.explanation: Converts any input to a vtkPartitionedDataSetCollection. Multiblock and AMR inputs get a data assembly that reproduces their hierarchy, so blocks can still be chosen by path with extractBlock or pvExtractBlock. Use it for steps or writers that require partitioned collections, such as pvWriteXMLPartitionedDataSetCollectionWriter; pvConvertToMultiBlock produces the older multiblock format.
pitfalls: A single dataset becomes a one-partition collection; use merge to get a plain dataset back.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvConvertToPointCloud.explanation: Converts any dataset into polydata that keeps only the input points and their point-data arrays; cells and cell data are dropped. CellGenerationMode decides whether the result has one vertex cell per point (ParaView default), a single polyvertex cell, or no cells at all. Use it to treat mesh nodes or particles as a point cloud, e.g. before pvPCANormalEstimation or point-based interpolation.
pitfalls: Cell-centred fields are lost; run cellToPoint first if they are needed on the points.
With No cells, many filters and renderers see nothing to draw; keep vertex cells unless a later step needs cell-free points.
On large image or structured inputs the explicit point list can need much more memory than the original grid.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCoordinates.explanation: Adds point coordinates and cell centres as data arrays: PointLocations (3-component point array, a copy of each point's coordinates) and CellCenters (3-component cell array). Geometry and existing arrays are unchanged. Use it when a calculator, export or table needs coordinates as ordinary arrays, e.g. to compute a radius or write x, y, z to CSV. pvCellCenters instead produces points at the cell centres.
pitfalls: Cell centres are parametric centres, which can differ from centroids for distorted cells.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCosmoReader.explanation: Reads binary cosmology particle files in LANL cosmo format (.cosmo, .cosmo64) or Gadget-2 format (vtkPCosmoReader) into an unstructured grid of particles with point arrays velocity, mass, tag and ghost. Several file names form a time series, one file per time step. Its output is the expected input of pvLANLFOFSODHaloFinder. Use pvGenericIOReader for HACC GenericIO output.
pitfalls: Set CosmoFormat to match the file; ParaView starts from Cosmo, and Gadget files read as cosmo give garbage.
Particles outside [0, BoxSideLength) are wrapped periodically, so set the box size of the run.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCountCellFaces.explanation: Adds a cell array (default name "Face Count") with the number of faces of each cell, as reported by VTK: 6 for a hexahedron, 4 for a tetrahedron, the face count of a polyhedron, and 0 for 2-D and lower cells, whose edges are not faces. Use it to inspect polyhedral meshes, e.g. from snappyHexMesh, or to threshold cells by face count.
pitfalls: Surface meshes give 0 everywhere; use pvCountCellVertices for polygons.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCountCellVertices.explanation: Adds a cell array (default name "Vertex Count") with the number of points of each cell, e.g. 3 for triangles, 8 for hexahedra and the point count of polygons and polyhedra. Use it to check mixed meshes or threshold cells by type-like size.
pitfalls: Higher-order cells count their mid-edge nodes too (e.g. 10 for a quadratic tetrahedron).
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCriticalTime.explanation: Scans every time step of a temporal input and records, for each point or cell, the first time value at which the selected array meets a threshold criterion (above, below or between thresholds; comparisons include the threshold values). The result is a static (non-temporal) dataset with one array named <array>_critical_time; other point and cell arrays are dropped, and entries whose criterion is never met are NaN. Use it for arrival or exceedance maps, e.g. when temperature first exceeds a limit. The mesh must keep the same points and cells over time.
pitfalls: The filter executes the whole upstream pipeline for every stored time step, which can be slow for long series.
With the ParaView defaults (Above Upper Threshold, UpperThreshold 0) any non-negative value counts as met, so most entries become the first time; always set the threshold.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCrop.explanation: Extracts a sub-block of an image or volume (vtkImageData) given as a point-index extent [imin, imax, jmin, jmax, kmin, kmax]; the output keeps the input origin and spacing, so cropped points stay at their original positions. Use it to cut a region of interest from a large image before costly filtering or export. To cut by world coordinates or with an arbitrary shape use clip; extractSubset selects an index range with sampling rates as well.
pitfalls: Indices are point indices of the input's extent, not coordinates; convert positions with (x − origin) / spacing.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCurvature.explanation: Generated binding of ParaView's Curvature filter: computes per-point Gaussian (ParaView default) or mean curvature of a polygonal surface into the point array Gauss_Curvature or Mean_Curvature. Gaussian curvature is positive on sphere-like and negative on saddle-like regions (units 1/length²); mean curvature (1/length) assumes outward normals. Use the curated curvature (Schemaxis default Mean) for the usual case; this binding defaults to Gaussian.
pitfalls: Volume meshes are rejected; extract the surface first (surface or pvExtractSurface).
Results are noisy on coarse or poorly shaped triangulations; smooth or refine first.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvCylinder.explanation: Creates a cylinder as polydata with normals and texture coordinates: Resolution side facets, axis parallel to y, centred at Center, with both ends capped by default. Use it as reference geometry, e.g. a pipe or probe region. The orientation is fixed to y; rotate it with transform for other axes.
pitfalls: The axis is always y in this source; Center moves it but cannot tilt it.
ParaView's default Resolution is 6; raise it for a round cross-section.
Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

pvD3.explanation: Parallel repartitioning (distributed data decomposition): builds a k-d tree over the distributed dataset and redistributes cells so each MPI process owns a spatially contiguous, load-balanced region, optionally with ghost-cell layers; output is an unstructured grid. In a serial run it acts almost as a pass-through, but non-composite input is still converted to an unstructured grid. pvRedistributeDataSet is the newer alternative with more output control.
pitfalls: Image, rectilinear and structured grids become explicit unstructured grids, which can need much more memory; ParaView warns about this.
Schemaxis serial examples do not establish MPI behaviour. Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvDEMReader.explanation: Reads a USGS Digital Elevation Model (.dem, the ASCII DEM format) into 2-D uniform image data whose point scalars are elevations; origin and spacing come from the DEM header. Use pvWarpByScalar or warpScalar to turn it into a 3-D terrain surface.
pitfalls: DEM headers can use different units for elevation and ground distance (for example metres versus arc-seconds); check them before warping or combining with other data.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvDICOMReaderSingleFile.explanation: Reads one uncompressed DICOM file (.dcm) into uniform image data with the pixel values as point scalars and the pixel spacing from the header. Use it for a single slice; for a series stored as one slice per file use pvDICOMReaderdirectory.
pitfalls: vtkDICOMImageReader handles neither compressed (encapsulated) transfer syntaxes nor multi-frame files; convert such data first.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvDICOMReaderdirectory.explanation: Reads every DICOM file in one directory as the slices of a single 3-D image volume (uniform image data), the usual layout of CT and MR series. In Schemaxis, FileName must be the directory itself: the value goes straight to vtkDICOMImageReader's SetDirectoryName. Use pvDICOMReaderSingleFile for one file.
pitfalls: Slice spacing comes from Slice Thickness (0018,0050), which is right only for contiguous slices; check the z spacing for gapped or overlapping acquisitions.
Keep one series per directory; every valid DICOM file in it becomes part of the volume. Only uncompressed files are read.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvDataObjectGenerator.explanation: Builds small test datasets from a text Program: atomic templates ID1 (image data), UF1 (uniform grid), RG1 (rectilinear), SG1 (structured), PD1/PD2 (polydata) and UG1 (unstructured grid), nested in composites with MB{ … } (multiblock) or HB[ … ] (hierarchical box AMR, levels in parentheses). For example "MB{ ID1 PD1 MB{} }" gives a multiblock of an image, a polydata and an empty block. Use it to exercise how a pipeline handles particular data types and composite structures.
pitfalls: The generated datasets are tiny templates with id arrays, not physically meaningful fields.
Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

pvDateToNumeric.explanation: Finds string arrays holding dates (point, cell, field or table row data) and adds a numeric copy of each as <name>_numeric, in seconds since the Unix epoch, so dates can be plotted, thresholded or used in calculators. VTK tries DateFormat first, then built-in fallback formats; the format is chosen from the first value, and an array whose first value does not parse is skipped. Typical input is a CSV table read with a CSV reader.
pitfalls: Dates are interpreted in the local time zone of the machine running ParaView (std::mktime), so results shift between machines; store UTC times and compare on one machine.
Values that do not match the chosen format become 0.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvDecimate.explanation: Reduces the triangle count of a triangle surface with vtkDecimatePro, removing vertices in order of least error until TargetReduction (ParaView default 0.9, about 90 % of triangles removed) is reached. By ParaView default PreserveTopology is off, so the surface may be split along feature edges (FeatureAngle 15°) and holes may open to reach the target. Input must be triangles; run triangulate first. decimate is the curated version (Schemaxis defaults 0.5, topology preserved); pvQuadricClustering is faster on very large meshes.
pitfalls: The native defaults remove 90 % of triangles and allow holes; set PreserveTopology true and a smaller TargetReduction when the surface must stay closed.
Only triangles are processed; triangulate general polygons first.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvDecimatePolyline.explanation: Reduces the points of polylines by repeatedly deleting the interior vertex with the smallest error until TargetReduction (ParaView default 0.9) of the segments is removed or the next deletion would exceed MaximumError. The error comes from DecimationStrategy: distance of a vertex from the line through its neighbours (Decimation Distance Strategy, default), the angle at the vertex, or a custom point array. End points are kept, but closed loops can collapse to one segment. Use it to simplify streamlines, contours or GIS polylines.
pitfalls: Separate two-point line cells have no interior vertices; join them into polylines first with pvTriangleStrips and JoinContiguousSegments.
Vertices shared by several polylines are treated independently, which can break junctions.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvDeflectNormals.explanation: Tilts surface normals by a vector field: each new normal is normalize(N + ScaleFactor × V), where N is the input point normal (or the constant UserNormal) and V the selected point vector. The result is a point normal array DeflectedNormals set as the active normals; geometry is unchanged. It is a shading effect for visualizing a vector field on a surface (e.g. bump-like lighting from velocity), not a physical quantity.
pitfalls: Without input point normals ParaView warns and falls back to UserNormal; compute normals first (normals or pvGenerateSurfaceNormals) for curved surfaces.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvDelaunay2D.explanation: Full native Delaunay 2D: triangulates input points (vtkPointSet) into polydata triangles. Beyond delaunay2D it exposes ProjectionPlaneMode — XY Plane (default) ignores z, Best-Fitting Plane projects the points onto their least-squares plane first so tilted, nearly planar sets triangulate correctly — and Offset and BoundingTriangulation, which control the initial bounding triangulation. Alpha and Tolerance act as in delaunay2D (ParaView defaults 0 and 0.00001).
pitfalls: Best-Fitting Plane suits roughly planar data only; strongly curved point sets still fold.
BoundingTriangulation true adds the artificial bounding points and triangles to the output; it is a debugging aid.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvDelaunay3D.explanation: Full native Delaunay 3D: tetrahedralizes input points (vtkPointSet) into an unstructured grid. Beyond delaunay3D it exposes which alpha-shape cell types are output when Alpha > 0 (AlphaTets and AlphaTris on, AlphaLines and AlphaVerts off by ParaView default), the Offset of the initial bounding tetrahedralization (default 2.5) and BoundingTriangulation. Alpha and Tolerance act as in delaunay3D (ParaView defaults 0 and 0.001).
pitfalls: A larger Offset makes a true convex hull more likely but increases the risk of numerical problems.
Delaunay 3D can exhaust memory on large point sets; thin or clean the points first.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvDescriptiveStatistics.explanation: Computes univariate statistics of each selected array: minimum, maximum, mean, raw moments, standard deviation, skewness and kurtosis. Assessment expresses each value as its number of standard deviations from the mean (signed or unsigned). Use it for summary statistics of fields over a mesh or table; counts are per point or cell, not weighted by cell size. Output port 0 is the statistical model (a multiblock of tables) and port 1 the input with assessment arrays added; select them with {"node": id, "port": n}.
pitfalls: On a non-uniform mesh the mean is not a volume average; use integrate and divide by volume for that.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvDisk.explanation: Creates a flat annulus (a disk with a central hole) in the x-y plane centred at the origin, as polydata made of quadrilaterals: InnerRadius to OuterRadius, divided into RadialResolution rings and CircumferentialResolution sectors. Use it as an inlet or outlet patch, seed surface or reference geometry. The curated disk operation exposes the same source with Schemaxis defaults.
pitfalls: ParaView's default InnerRadius is 0.5, so the disk has a hole; set it to 0 for a solid disk.
Position and orientation are fixed (x-y plane at the origin); move it with a transform.
Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

pvDistributePoints.explanation: Redistributes the points of a point set across MPI processes into spatially contiguous regions with roughly equal point counts, by recursively splitting the points in two (a k-d tree). Output is polydata containing the points and their point data but no cells; input cells are ignored. Use it in MPI runs to balance particle or point-cloud data before point-based processing.
pitfalls: The output has no cells, so it is not drawn and cell-based filters see nothing.
Schemaxis serial examples do not establish MPI behaviour. Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvDistributedTrivialProducer.explanation: Trivial producer (vtkDistributedTrivialProducer) that takes its data from a dataset previously registered under a key by native code in the same process (SetGlobalOutput); UpdateDataset names that key. Schemaxis provides no way to register such a dataset, so in a workflow the key finds nothing and the node has no data. It exists for in-situ and embedding applications.
pitfalls: Schemaxis has no authored way to hand a dataset to a trivial producer, so the node is expected to produce an empty output; this has not been run.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvENZOAMRParticlesReader.explanation: Reads particles from an Enzo AMR output (the .hierarchy or .boundary file of a data dump) into a multiblock dataset with one polydata block of particle points per grid. It can keep only every Frequency-th particle, particles inside a box, or one particle type (dark matter, star or tracer). Use pvEnzoReader for the gas fields of the same output.
pitfalls: ParticleType filtering works only when the file has a particle_type array; otherwise all particles are returned.
MaxLocation is the upper corner of the filter box, although ParaView's own documentation calls it the minimum.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvERFHDF5datareader.explanation: Reads ESI Result Format files stored in HDF5 (.erfh5), as written by ESI structural and crash solvers, into a partitioned dataset collection. A file holds stages (top-level groups; the "post" link names the default stage), each with constant data (mesh connectivity, nodes) and singlestate time states; Stages, Blocks and Variables choose what is read. Multistate data are not supported.
pitfalls: Variable names are offered in lower case because the reader treats them case-insensitively; use the lower-case form.

Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so inspect the output blocks, arrays and time steps on your own files before relying on it.

pvElevation.explanation: Adds a floating-point point array named Elevation by projecting each point onto the segment from LowPoint to HighPoint and mapping its position linearly into ScalarRange: the LowPoint end gets the first value, the HighPoint end the second, and points beyond either end are clamped. Use it for height colouring, a linear test ramp or a coordinate along any direction; elevation is the curated version and pvCellGridElevation works on cell grids.
pitfalls: Points beyond the segment all receive the end values; extend LowPoint and HighPoint over the data if the full variation is wanted.
LowPoint and HighPoint may receive input-dependent ParaView defaults; set them explicitly.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvEllipse.explanation: Creates an elliptical arc or full ellipse as a polyline: centred at Center, in the plane normal to Normal, with major radius given by the length of MajorRadiusVector and minor radius Ratio × major. StartAngle and SectorAngle (degrees, measured from the major axis) select part of the perimeter, and Close joins the ends. Use it for annotation, seed curves or circular probes (Ratio 1 gives a circle).
pitfalls: MajorRadiusVector must not be parallel to Normal; VTK then reports an error and produces nothing.
Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

pvEnSightMasterServerReader.explanation: Reads EnSight data written in parallel through a Server-of-Servers master file (.sos) that lists one .case file per partition; the partitions are combined into one multiblock dataset of EnSight parts with the selected node and element variables. Choose it for EnSight output split across processes; for an ordinary .case file use pvEnSightReader. It reads the time given by SetTimeValue and exposes a ByteOrder setting for binary files.
pitfalls: ByteOrder starts as BigEndian; if a binary case loads with nonsensical values, try LittleEndian.
CaseFileName must be the .sos master file, not one of the .case files it lists.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvEnSightReader.explanation: Reads an EnSight 6 or EnSight Gold case (.case, ASCII or binary), a post-processing format exported by many CFD and structural solvers (OpenFOAM's foamToEnsight among them). Output is a multiblock dataset with one block per EnSight part, carrying the node (point) and element (cell) variables selected in PointArrays and CellArrays; transient cases expose their time steps. Use pvEnSightMasterServerReader for a parallel .sos master file and pvWriteEnSightWriter to write EnSight.
pitfalls: CaseFileName must be the .case file; the geometry and variable files it names are located relative to it.
ApplyTetrahedralize (default false) splits every cell into tetrahedra, multiplying the cell count; use it only to work around non-manifold EnSight meshes.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvEnsembleDataReader.explanation: Reads a ParaView ensemble table (.pve): a CSV file with a header row in which each further row describes one ensemble member through parameter columns, and the last column gives that member's data file, relative to the .pve file. CurrentEnsembleMember selects which member is read; the output is whatever that file's reader produces. Use it to step through a parameter study by member number; read a member's file directly when only one is needed.
pitfalls: Member files are opened with ParaView's reader for their extension, so all members should share one format.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvEnvironmentAnnotation.explanation: Produces a text annotation stating the user name, system name, date and time and, optionally, the input's file name, for stamping provenance on images. ParaView marks its output port as text: it is an annotation, not a dataset, and the input data are not passed through. The text depends on the machine, user and run time.
pitfalls: Date/time and user name differ between runs; disable them when images are compared across runs or machines.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvEnzoReader.explanation: Reads an Enzo AMR simulation output (the .hierarchy or .boundary file) into a hierarchical-box (overlapping AMR) dataset of the selected cell and point fields, refinement levels 0 to Level. ConvertToCGS optionally converts the fields from Enzo code units to CGS. Use it for Enzo gas and field data; use pvENZOAMRParticlesReader for its particles.
pitfalls: Level defaults to 1, so only the two coarsest levels are loaded; raise it to see the finest data.
Fields stay in Enzo code units unless ConvertToCGS is true; check which before comparing with physical values.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvEqualizerFilter.explanation: Applies a frequency-domain equalizer to signal columns of a table: each column is Fourier transformed, its spectrum multiplied by a piecewise-linear gain curve given in EqualizerPoints, and transformed back. Output ports: 0 the spectrum, 1 the filtered signal (Result), 2 the normalized spectrum; select one with {"node": id, "port": n}. Use it for band-pass or notch filtering of probe or sensor time series.
pitfalls: Rows are assumed to be equally spaced samples at SamplingFrequencyHz; irregular time steps give a wrong frequency axis.
With fewer than two equalizer points the signal is not modified.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvEvenlySpacedStreamlines2D.explanation: Fills a 2-D vector field with streamlines at roughly uniform spacing (Jobard–Lefer algorithm): starting at StartPosition it integrates forward and backward, seeds new lines SeparatingDistance beside existing ones, and stops a line when it comes closer than SeparatingDistance × SeparatingDistanceRatio to another, closes a loop, leaves the domain, slows below TerminalSpeed or reaches MaximumSteps. Input must lie in the x-y plane with in-plane point vectors; output is polylines with IntegrationTime, interpolated fields and a ReasonForTermination cell array. Use it for even flow pictures of 2-D slices; streamTracer seeds from a chosen source.
pitfalls: A slice not lying in the x-y plane gives wrong or no streamlines; transform it into x-y first.
With the default Cell Length unit, distances are multiples of the diagonal of the cell containing StartPosition, so moving the seed rescales all spacings; choose Length for dataset units.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExodusIIReader.explanation: Reads Exodus II finite-element results (.e, .exo, .g, .ex2 …, written by SEACAS-based codes such as Sierra, MOOSE or Cubit) into a multiblock dataset of unstructured grids: element blocks, optional face and edge blocks, node, side and element sets, and global variables, with nodal and element result variables per time step. By default node positions include the displacement vector (ApplyDisplacements, scaled by DisplacementMagnitude). Use pvRestartedSimExodusReader for a restarted run described by a metadata file, or pvIOSSReader, the IOSS-based alternative.
pitfalls: FilePattern, FilePrefix and XMLFileName are optional, as their ParaView file lists are marked optional. Leave them out to read FileName as given: FilePattern and FilePrefix rebuild the file name from a printf-style pattern, so supplying them changes which file is read, and XMLFileName names an optional part and material description.
VTK's Exodus reader starts with every result variable disabled; list the PointVariables and ElementVariables you need, or the blocks arrive without fields.
Coordinates are deformed by default; set ApplyDisplacements to false to see the undeformed mesh.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractAMRBlocks.explanation: Extracts chosen datasets (boxes) from an AMR input (vtkUniformGridAMR), each identified by its refinement level and its index within that level. The output is a multiblock with one block per level, each holding the extracted uniform grids as pieces. Use it to inspect or process individual AMR patches; pvConvertAMRdatasettoMultiblock or pvResampleAMR convert the whole hierarchy instead.
pitfalls: SelectedDataSets is a flat list of (level, index) pairs; Schemaxis rejects an odd number of entries.
Indices restart at 0 on every level; they are not global block numbers.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractAttributes.explanation: Converts one attribute association of the input (points, cells, field data, vertices, edges or rows) into a table (vtkTable): one column per array, one row per point or cell (or other element). Composite input gives a multiblock of tables. Use it to inspect or export raw array values, e.g. as CSV through a table writer. Geometry and connectivity are dropped unless AddMetaData adds coordinates.
pitfalls: ParaView's default association is Points; set FieldAssociation to Cells for cell-centred solver fields.
Point coordinates are not included by default; enable AddMetaData when you need them.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractBlock.explanation: Full native Extract Block: keeps selected blocks of a multiblock, partitioned dataset collection or AMR input, chosen by Selectors (path expressions) evaluated against the data assembly named in Assembly — the block hierarchy, or an assembly supplied by readers such as IOSS or CGNS that groups blocks by meaning. The composite type is kept (overlapping AMR becomes a partitioned dataset collection). Use extractBlock when the hierarchy is enough.
pitfalls: Selectors must match the chosen assembly; a hierarchy path does not select anything in a reader-defined assembly.
Without selectors no block is selected and the output is empty.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractCTHParts.explanation: Specialized for CTH shock-physics results: for each selected cell-centred volume-fraction array (VolumeArrays) it converts the array to point data and contours it at VolumeFractionValue (ParaView default 0.45), giving one material surface per array. Output is a multiblock with one polydata block per selected array, optionally clipped by a plane (ClipType, ParaView default None) and capped to look closed. Input is CTH data: non-overlapping AMR or multiblock rectilinear grids with cell data, e.g. from pvSpyPlotReader.
pitfalls: VolumeArrays has no static default; list the material volume-fraction arrays explicitly.
The surface level is VolumeFractionValue (0.45 by default, not the 0.5 stated in the upstream description); keep the same value when comparing runs.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractCellsAlongLine.explanation: Extracts every cell of the input that the straight segment from Point1 to Point2 intersects and outputs those cells, with their point and cell data, as an unstructured grid. Use it to inspect the actual mesh cells crossed by a probe line, for example before plotting with probeLine; probeLine instead samples interpolated values at evenly spaced points. Use pvExtractCellsAlongLinesCustomSource for polylines or several lines.
pitfalls: Cells that only touch the line at a point or edge may or may not be counted; extend the segment slightly if boundary cells matter.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractCellsAlongLinesCustomSource.explanation: Extracts the input cells intersected by the line and polyline cells of a second dataset (Source, polydata or unstructured grid) and outputs them as an unstructured grid. Use it with a curved or multi-segment path, e.g. a traced streamline or a polyline read from a file; for a single straight segment pvExtractCellsAlongLine is simpler.
pitfalls: Only line and polyline cells of Source are used; polygons, vertices or 3-D cells in Source are ignored, so extract edges or build a polyline first.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractCellsByRegion.explanation: Extracts the cells lying entirely inside (ParaView default) or entirely outside an implicit region — a Plane (ParaView's default choice, whose inside is the side opposite its normal), Box or Sphere — without cutting them, and outputs an unstructured grid. Extractintersected adds cells straddling the region boundary and Extractonlyintersected keeps only those. Use it to cut out a sub-volume of whole original cells; clip cuts cells exactly at the surface and slice returns the surface itself.
pitfalls: The cut is jagged because whole cells are kept; use clip for an exact boundary.
For a Plane, inside is the negative side, opposite to the normal; flip the normal or choose outside to keep the other half.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractCellsByType.explanation: Keeps only the cells whose VTK cell type is listed in CellTypes, e.g. the Tetrahedron cells of a mixed mesh, or the Triangle and Quadrilateral faces of a surface. The output has the same dataset type as the input; structured inputs (image, rectilinear or structured grids) consist of one cell type, so they come through either whole or empty. Use pvExtractSelection to pick cells by ID or value instead.
pitfalls: No type is selected until you list one, and an empty selection gives an empty output.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractComponent.explanation: Copies one component of a multi-component array (e.g. the z velocity Uz from U) into a new single-component array named OutputArrayName on the same points or cells; the dataset is otherwise unchanged. Use it when a later operation (contour, threshold) needs a scalar. calculator can do the same with an expression such as U_Z.
pitfalls: Component is zero-based: 0 is x, 1 is y, 2 is z.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractEdges.explanation: Native Extract Edges, the same filter as edges: every cell edge becomes a line cell in an output polydata wireframe, with shared edges emitted once and cell data copied from the lowest-numbered cell using the edge. Use edges unless you need the generated pv identifier; featureEdges or pvFeatureEdges return only boundary and sharp edges.
pitfalls: Volume meshes produce all interior edges; ParaView warns that structured inputs can use much memory.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractEnclosedPoints.explanation: Keeps the input points that lie inside a closed, manifold polygonal Surface (second input) and outputs them as a point cloud (polydata) on port 0; with GenerateOutliers, port 1 holds the points outside. Only points and their point data are kept, not the input's cells. Use it to select particles or probe points within a body; to keep mesh cells, use a clip instead.
pitfalls: With an open or non-manifold surface the inside/outside test is undefined; enable CheckSurface so the filter first checks that the surface is closed. If that check fails the filter reports "Bad enclosing surface" and stops without producing output (the node fails); it does not mark the points as outside.
Surface must be a single polygonal surface (not composite); extract the surface of a solid mesh first.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractGhostCells.explanation: Extracts only the ghost cells of the input (the overlap layers that parallel or partitioned data carry to neighbouring pieces) so they can be inspected, and records the original ghost flags in an array named ArrayName. Use it to debug decompositions or ghost-cell generation; data without ghost cells gives an empty output.
pitfalls: ArrayName must differ from vtkGhostType, or the extracted cells are treated as ghosts again and hidden.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractLocation.explanation: Looks up one point in space: in Interpolate At Location mode it outputs a single point with all data interpolated there (a probe); in Extract Cell At Location mode, the ParaView default, it outputs the cell or cells containing the location with their data. Use it for a monitoring-point value or to inspect the element at a position; use probeLine or pvPlotOverLine for lines.
pitfalls: A location outside the mesh gives an empty result (or zero-filled values when interpolating); check the bounds.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractParticlesOverTime.explanation: Finds the particles of a temporal point dataset (Particles port) that pass through a volume (Volume port, a dataset with 3-D cells) at any time step, and outputs the Particles data restricted to those particles, still time-dependent. It visits every input time step, so it can be slow. Particles are matched between steps by IdChannelArray. Use it to isolate particles crossing a region such as an inlet or a reaction zone; pvExtractCellsByRegion selects by position at one time only.
pitfalls: If point order changes between steps and no id array identifies particles, different particles are confused; name an id array in IdChannelArray.
The Volume must contain 3-D cells; a closed surface does not count as a volume here.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractRegionSurface.explanation: Extracts polygonal surfaces of an unstructured grid on its outer boundary and also on internal interfaces between regions, where regions are defined by an integer cell array (RegionArrayName, ParaView default "material"). It suits multi-material meshes: each interface face is output once or once per side (SingleSided), and output faces can record their source cell (OrigCellIds) and the face of that cell (CellFaceIds). Use surface or pvExtractSurface when only the outer boundary is needed.
pitfalls: The region array must be an integer (vtkIntArray) cell array; an array of another type, or a name that does not exist, is not used, and only the outer surface results.
Interfaces are found for unstructured-grid input; other dataset types get the ordinary outer surface.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractSelection.explanation: Extracts the points or cells described by a selection (Selection port, from one of the pv*SelectionSource operations or pvConvertSelection) from Input. By default the result is an unstructured grid holding only the selected elements (a table of selected rows for table input); with PreserveTopology it is a copy of the input with a vtkInsidedness array marking selected elements. Use it to isolate cells by ID, value, threshold, location, frustum or query.
pitfalls: The selection's field type (CELL or POINT on the source) decides whether cells or points are extracted; a POINT selection without ContainingCells yields vertices only.
Selections built from IDs refer to the indices of the dataset they were made for; connect the same upstream data that the IDs came from.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractSelectioninternal.explanation: Internal ParaView variant of Extract Selection (vtkPVExtractSelection) with three output ports: 0 the extracted dataset, 1 a selection of the extracted point/cell indices, and 2 the input selection passed through; select a port with {"node": id, "port": n}. ParaView documents it as internal and recommends Extract Selection; use pvExtractSelection unless you need the index selection on port 1.
pitfalls: Unlike pvExtractSelection it has no PreserveTopology option and accepts no table input.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractSubset.explanation: Extracts a sub-block of a structured dataset (image data, rectilinear or curvilinear grid) by point-index ranges in I, J and K, optionally keeping only every n-th index; the output has the same structured type. Use it to crop or coarsen a structured grid cheaply, e.g. one K-plane of a 3-D grid. Use extractSubset for the same operation with Schemaxis defaults (includeBoundary true).
pitfalls: VOI uses point indices in the input's extent, which need not start at 0; check the input extent first.
With sample rates above 1 the last index is dropped unless IncludeBoundary is true.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractSubsetWithSeed.explanation: From a structured grid (vtkStructuredGrid, including multiblock structured data split across blocks or processes), extracts the grid line (I, J or K) or grid surface (IJ, JK or KI) that passes through the cell containing Seed, following it across block boundaries even when block i-j-k origins differ. Typical use: pick a point to extract a wall-normal grid line or a constant-k surface of a curvilinear CFD mesh. Output keeps the structured cells, as a partitioned dataset for a single grid or the input's composite type otherwise.
pitfalls: A seed outside every cell extracts nothing; place it inside the grid.
Only structured grids are accepted; use pvExtractSubset or extractSubset for index ranges of image or rectilinear data.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractSurface.explanation: Extracts the outer surface of any dataset as polygonal data (vtkGeometryFilter): boundary faces of 3-D cells plus all lower-dimensional cells, with point and cell arrays carried over and internal faces removed. It is the same native filter as the curated surface operation, which has no options; choose pvExtractSurface to control nonlinear-face subdivision, fast mode, ghost-interface removal or piece invariance. For interfaces between materials use pvExtractRegionSurface.
pitfalls: FastMode may miss faces, for example on blanked structured data; keep it off when the surface is measured or exported.
The outer surface of a CFD domain includes inlets, outlets and far-field boundaries, not only walls; extract the patches you need (extractBlock) when a specific boundary matters.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvExtractTimeSteps.explanation: Restricts a time-varying input to selected time steps, given as listed zero-based indices (Select Time Steps, ParaView default) or as an inclusive index range with a stride (Select Time Range). Downstream nodes see only those steps: a request for an unselected time is answered by a selected step chosen by ApproximationMode (Nearest Time Step by default), and times outside the selection get the first or last selected step. Use it to thin a long transient before temporalStatistics or pvParticlePath, or to hold a branch at one step.
pitfalls: Indices are positions in the input's time list, not time values; indices beyond the last step are ignored without warning.
Scene times are still chosen by the Schemaxis times setting; this node only maps them onto the selected steps.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvFDSReader.explanation: Reads Fire Dynamics Simulator results through the Smokeview .smv file, which lists the other output files. The output is a partitioned dataset collection with five groups: Grids (meshes), Devices (point measurements over time), HRR (heat-release-rate tables), Slices and Boundaries (field data on planes and walls). AssemblySelectors chooses which of these are read. Use it for fire and smoke CFD from NIST FDS.
pitfalls: Neither ParaView 5.13.3 nor vtkFDSReader defines default selectors, so an empty selection appears to read nothing; set AssemblySelectors explicitly, e.g. ["/"] for everything.
