pvYieldCriteria.explanation: Evaluates yield criteria of selected symmetric stress tensors from their principal values σ1 ≥ σ2 ≥ σ3: Tresca as |σ3 − σ1| and von Mises as √(((σ1 − σ2)² + (σ2 − σ3)² + (σ1 − σ3)²) / 2), stored as <name> - Tresca Criterion and <name> - Von Mises Criterion in the tensor's units. The Principal Stress choice also keeps the principal value and direction arrays. Use it in structural post-processing to compare stress states with a material's yield strength. Tensor requirements match pvTensorPrincipalInvariants (6 components XX, YY, ZZ, XY, YZ, XZ, or 3 named XX, YY, XY).
pitfalls: The Tresca value here is the full principal-stress difference, twice the maximum shear stress; compare it with the yield strength, not the shear yield strength.
If no criterion is selected the input passes through unchanged.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pvYoungsMaterialInterface.explanation: Reconstructs sharp material interfaces in mixed cells of Eulerian or ALE multi-material simulations (e.g. CTH or other volume-of-fluid output) with Youngs' method: in each cell the material is bounded by a plane perpendicular to its interface normal, placed so the cut volume matches the cell's volume fraction. Input is a composite dataset with one cell-centred volume fraction array per material and, ideally, a 3-component cell normal array per material. Output is a multiblock with one block per material (in VolumeFractionArrays order) holding the interface polygons or, with FillMaterial (ParaView default), the material's volume.
pitfalls: Without a normal array for a material, VTK uses the +x direction, so interfaces come out as planes perpendicular to x; supply normals (e.g. from the volume-fraction gradient).
AxisSymetric is true by ParaView default and treats 2-D meshes as axisymmetric (volumes of revolution); set it false for planar 2-D data.
Only 2-D and 3-D cells are processed and input must be composite (e.g. multiblock); wrap a single mesh with pvGroupDatasets first.
Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

pva2DGlyph.explanation: Creates one flat 2-D marker in the x-y plane as polydata: vertex, dash, cross, thick cross, triangle, square, circle, diamond or one of four arrow styles (GlyphType, ParaView default Arrow), about one unit in size around Center. Use it as the glyph shape for 2-D vector or point-marker plots, or as an annotation symbol.
pitfalls: Filled only affects closed shapes (triangle, square, circle, diamond, thick variants); open shapes stay as lines.
DoublePointed, PointInwards and TipLength only apply to the arrow glyph types.
Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

pva3DText.explanation: Creates polygonal (filled outline) geometry spelling Text in a vector font, lying in the x-y plane with the text starting near the origin and characters about one unit tall. It is real geometry, so it can be transformed, clipped or exported, unlike a screen-space text annotation. Use it to label parts of a 3-D scene.
pitfalls: Only printable ASCII characters and "\n" line breaks are supported.
Scale and place the text with a transform; the source has no size or position options.
Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

pvglTFReader.explanation: Reads a glTF 2.0 asset (.gltf with external buffers, or binary .glb) into a multiblock dataset of polydata for one scene, with skinning, morph targets and enabled animations applied to the geometry when ApplyDeformationsToGeometry is true. Animations become time steps sampled at Framerate. Materials and textures are not applied. Use it to bring 3-D models or animated scenes into a pipeline; for static CAD surfaces pvWavefrontOBJReader or readSTL are simpler.
pitfalls: No animation is enabled by default (glTF does not define which should play); list them in AnimationStatus to get time steps.

pvopenPMDReader.explanation: Reads an openPMD particle-mesh data series (plasma and accelerator simulations such as WarpX or PIConGPU) through a .pmd file: a text file whose first line is the openPMD file pattern, e.g. "data_%T.h5", resolved next to the .pmd file. Output port 0 is the mesh records as image data (a vtkPartitionedDataSet), port 1 the particle species as point clouds (a vtkPartitionedDataSetCollection, one per species); select it with {"node": id, "port": 1}. Values, coordinates and times are converted to SI using the openPMD unit factors.
pitfalls: The reader needs the openpmd_api Python module inside ParaView's Python; without it nothing is read.
Point FileName at the .pmd pattern file, not at an individual HDF5 or ADIOS iteration file.

pitfalls: Both .vrt and .cel files must be present with the same base name.

/properties/nodes.explanation: The processing graph: sources, readers, filters and shared resources, each with a unique id. Execution order follows inputs and $observe/$sample dependencies, not list order, and a scene runs only the nodes its outputs need.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/0.explanation: Combines the meshes of several input nodes (any dataset types, non-composite) into one unstructured grid, ParaView 5.13.3's default output type for Append Datasets. Use it to treat parts as one dataset for a filter or export; use appendGeometry for surfaces, group to keep inputs as separate blocks, and merge for the blocks of one composite node.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/9.explanation: Labels the connected regions of the input (cells linked through shared points) and keeps all regions, the largest one (most cells) or the one closest to a point; output is an unstructured grid. With colourRegions (Schemaxis default true) a RegionId array identifies each region. Use it to separate disjoint bodies, drop small fragments or isolate the part near a location.
pitfalls: Connectivity is topological: parts that touch only geometrically, with duplicate points, count as separate regions; run clean or cleanGrid first.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/10.explanation: Extracts isosurfaces (3-D input) or isolines (2-D input) where a point-centred scalar field equals each of the given values, and outputs them as polydata; several values give several surfaces in one output. Use it for level sets such as a temperature front or a Q-criterion vortex surface. By Schemaxis default the output carries normals and the contour value as an array, but no gradients. Use pvContour for the full native settings.
pitfalls: The scalar must be point data; for cell arrays run cellToPoint first.
Values outside the field's range produce an empty output without an error.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/11.explanation: Computes per-point curvature of a polygonal surface (Gaussian or mean, the two curvature types ParaView 5.13.3 offers) as a point array such as Mean_Curvature or Gauss_Curvature. Use it to locate ridges, valleys or highly curved regions on CAD or scanned surfaces. Mean curvature is in inverse length units and Gaussian in inverse length squared; both are noisy on coarse or irregular triangulations. The mean-curvature sign assumes outward normals.
pitfalls: type accepts only Gaussian or Mean, the entries of ParaView 5.13.3's Curvature enumeration (filters_filtersgeneral.xml:445-485); maximum and minimum principal curvature are not available and any other value is rejected at planning.
If convex regions show negative mean curvature, the normals point inward; set invertMean.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/12.explanation: Creates a polygonal cylinder surface of given radius and height, centred on centre with its axis parallel to y, including point normals and texture coordinates. resolution sets the facets around the axis and capping closes both ends. There is no orientation setting: follow it with transform to rotate the cylinder.
pitfalls: The axis is always along y before any transform; a cylinder meant along z needs a 90-degree rotation about x.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/14.explanation: Builds a 2-D Delaunay triangulation of the input points (any point set, e.g. a point cloud or the points of a mesh; input cells are ignored) and outputs polydata triangles. Triangulation is done in the x-y plane: z is ignored for connectivity but kept on the points, so it suits height fields and nearly planar sets aligned with x-y. With alpha 0 (Schemaxis default) every triangle of the convex hull is kept; a positive alpha keeps only triangles whose circumcircle radius is at most alpha, carving concave outlines and gaps. Use pvDelaunay2D for a best-fitting plane, and delaunay3D for tetrahedra.
pitfalls: Points on a plane not parallel to x-y (e.g. a vertical wall) triangulate badly or collapse; transform them first or use pvDelaunay2D with ProjectionPlaneMode Best-Fitting Plane.
Points closer than tolerance (a fraction of the bounding-box diagonal) are discarded as duplicates.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/15.explanation: Builds a 3-D Delaunay tetrahedralization of the input points (any point set) and outputs an unstructured grid of tetrahedra filling their convex hull. A positive alpha (Schemaxis default 0) produces an alpha shape: only tetrahedra whose circumsphere radius is at most alpha, plus qualifying triangles, are kept, which recovers concave shapes from point clouds. Use it to mesh scattered 3-D samples for interpolation or volume estimates; use delaunay2D for surface-like sets and pvDelaunay3D to choose which alpha cell types are output.
pitfalls: Output grows quickly and ParaView warns that Delaunay 3D can exhaust memory; thin large point sets first.
Points on a regular lattice are degenerate: the result depends on point order, and nearly coplanar points produce sliver tetrahedra.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/17.explanation: Extracts every edge of every cell as a line cell, giving a wireframe polydata of the whole mesh, including interior edges of volume cells. Each shared edge appears once and receives the cell data of the lowest-numbered cell using it. Use it to show or export mesh structure or to measure edge lengths; use featureEdges for only boundary or sharp edges of a surface, and run surface first if only the outer skin's edges are wanted.
pitfalls: On volume meshes the output holds all interior edges and can be several times larger than the input; ParaView warns about memory for structured inputs.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/19.explanation: Extracts selected blocks from a composite dataset (multiblock, partitioned dataset collection or AMR), such as the internalMesh or individual patches of an OpenFOAM case read by foam. Blocks are chosen by selectors, path expressions over the input's block hierarchy such as "/Root/internalMesh" or "//inlet". The output keeps the composite type with only the selected blocks (overlapping AMR becomes a partitioned dataset collection). Use merge afterwards when one dataset is needed; pvExtractBlock also exposes the assembly choice.
pitfalls: Selectors that match nothing give an empty composite rather than an error; check names in the input hierarchy (Studio lists them).
Only blocks that the reader loaded can be extracted; enable the patches in the reader options first.

pitfalls: Indices are in the input's extent space, which need not start at 0; inspect the input extent before choosing the range.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/21.explanation: Extracts edges of a polygonal surface as line cells (polydata): boundary edges (used by one polygon), feature edges (between two polygons whose normals differ by more than angle), non-manifold edges (shared by three or more polygons) and optionally manifold edges. With the Schemaxis defaults (boundary, feature and non-manifold on, manifold off, 30°) it outlines a CAD or CFD surface's creases, open boundaries and T-junctions. Input must be polydata; run surface first on volume meshes. Use edges for every cell edge.
pitfalls: Feature detection uses polygon normals, so inconsistently oriented polygons create spurious feature edges; run normals with consistency first.
Unmerged duplicate points make every polygon edge a boundary edge; run clean first.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/22.explanation: Curated OpenFOAM reader: opens a case through its .foam marker file and outputs a multiblock dataset whose blocks are the selected mesh regions (internalMesh volume cells, patch/<name> boundaries) carrying the selected cell fields, with one time step per stored time directory. Schemaxis defaults read a decomposed case (processor* folders), only internalMesh, and keep the 0 directory; other reader settings keep ParaView's defaults, which also create point data interpolated from the cell fields. Use pvOpenFOAMReader for point or Lagrangian fields, zones, label/scalar size or the other native options.
pitfalls: caseType defaults to Decomposed Case in Schemaxis (ParaView's own default is Reconstructed Case); for a serial or reconstructed case set Reconstructed Case, otherwise the reader finds no data.
Boundary patches are loaded only when listed in regions as patch/<name>.
Pick stored times with the document's times selection using this node as the source.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/191.explanation: Caches the geometry and topology of its input the first time it runs and keeps reusing that mesh for later time steps, updating only point, cell and field data while the point and cell counts stay the same. Use it after readers or filters that rebuild an unchanged mesh at every time step, so that downstream work depending only on the mesh need not be repeated. It handles an unstructured grid, polydata, or the first block of a composite input when that block is an unstructured grid.
pitfalls: If the mesh really moves or is remeshed with the same counts, the cached geometry is wrong, and ParaView 5.13.3 offers no way to force the cache to recompute: ForceCacheComputation has no elements, so invoking it sends no message, and assigning it pushes the XML command SetCacheComputation, which vtkForceStaticMesh lacks (it has SetForceCacheComputation) and which aborts the native process. Schemaxis therefore does not expose it. Use a different filter chain for meshes that change.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/193.explanation: Creates a frustum selection: everything inside a convex volume bounded by six planes, given by the eight corner vertices in Frustum. The output is a vtkSelection (no geometry) for the Selection port of pvExtractSelection or pvAnnotateSelection. For an axis-aligned box clip, pvClip with a Box type is often simpler.
pitfalls: Corner order matters: swapping near and far faces turns the planes inside out and selects nothing.
FieldType defaults to CELL; set POINT when the IDs or values refer to points, otherwise the wrong elements are matched.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/197.explanation: Splats the input points into a uniform volume (vtkImageData, point array SplatterValues): each point adds a Gaussian kernel ScaleFactor × value × exp(ExponentFactor × r² / R²) to nearby voxels within radius R, and overlapping contributions are combined by the accumulation mode (ParaView default Max). Without a selected array, or with scale splats off, each point contributes the kernel alone, giving a smooth point-density field. /properties/nodes/items/oneOf/269.explanation: ParaView-internal data-delivery filter that moves polydata, unstructured grids or AMR data between MPI processes and between data server, render server and client: PassThrough leaves data where they are, Collect gathers them to one process and Clone copies them to all. Its output type is PolyData unless OutputDataType says otherwise. It exists for ParaView's rendering pipeline; in Schemaxis prefer pvAppendReduce or pvReductionFilter to gather data.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/271.explanation: Generates image data whose float point scalar "Iterations" counts the iterations of z → z² + C before |z| exceeds 2 (capped at MaximumNumberofIterations). The 4-D parameter space (C real, C imaginary, X real, X imaginary, where X is the starting z) is sampled from OriginCX over SizeCX, with ProjectionAxes choosing which three parameters map to the image x, y and z axes. Use it as a synthetic image or volume with fine detail for testing.
pitfalls: The native description calls the values unsigned char; VTK produces float values.
The output's origin and spacing are in Mandelbrot parameter units, not physical coordinates.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/272.explanation: Reduces a dataset to a subset of its points, output as polydata points (optionally with vertex cells) carrying the point data. By ParaView default it keeps every OnRatio-th point by point id (2), starting at Offset, until MaximumNumberofPoints (5000) is reached; random modes instead draw a random or spatially uniform sample. Use it to thin points before glyphs (arrows) or for lighter scatter exports.
pitfalls: In the default striding mode the 5000-point cap is reached after the first 10000 point ids, so a large mesh is sampled only over part of its id range; raise MaximumNumberofPoints or use random sampling.
Without GenerateVertices (default false) the output has points but no cells, so it is not drawn and cell-based filters see nothing.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/273.explanation: Finds material fragments in AMR (hierarchical box) data such as CTH Spy Plot output: cells whose material fraction exceeds MaterialFractionThreshold are connected into fragments, whose surfaces form output port 0 (geometry) and whose centres of mass, volumes, masses and selected weighted averages form a point set on port 1 (statistics). It can invert the fraction and clip with a plane or sphere to measure craters, and can write both outputs to text files. Use pvRectilinearGridConnectivity for rectilinear multiblock data.
pitfalls: Material fraction arrays are expected as unsigned char (the Spy Plot reader's down-conversion); float fractions are not offered for SelectMaterialFractionArrays.
Mass arrays pair with fraction arrays by list position; keep both lists in the same order.
WriteGeometryOutput and WriteStatisticsOutput write files outside Schemaxis-managed exports.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/274.explanation: Replaces each pixel or voxel of an image by the median of the selected array over a rectangular neighbourhood of KernelSize pixels, giving image data of the same size. Unlike a mean filter it removes isolated outliers (salt-and-pepper or shot noise) while keeping sharp edges. Each component is filtered separately. Near the image border the neighbourhood is clipped to the image.
pitfalls: With the ParaView default kernel [1, 1, 1] nothing changes; set e.g. [3, 3, 1] for a 2-D image or [3, 3, 3] for a volume.
Even kernel sizes are off-centre and average the two middle values; prefer odd sizes.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/275.explanation: Full native Merge Blocks: appends the leaf datasets of a composite input into one dataset. OutputDataSetType decides the result: Unstructured Grid (ParaView default) merges blocks of any type, Polygonal Mesh merges only polydata blocks and leaves others out. MergePartitionsOnly keeps the block hierarchy and merges only the partitions within each block. Use merge for the common case (merge everything with point merging); use this when you need polydata output, a merge tolerance or partition-only merging.
pitfalls: With Polygonal Mesh output, volume meshes and image blocks are silently omitted; extract their surfaces first if they must be included.
Tolerance is a fraction of the bounding-box diagonal unless ToleranceIsAbsolute is true.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/276.explanation: Combines several time-dependent inputs into one multiblock dataset (one block per input) whose time steps are the union of the inputs' times, or their intersection with Intersection on, with near-duplicates removed using Tolerance. pitfalls: Inputs are not interpolated in time; a block may show an earlier step than the requested time.
Tolerance is absolute (in time units) unless RelativeTolerance is true.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/278.explanation: Adds a cell array Quality rating the shape of each cell with a Verdict metric chosen per cell type (triangle, quad, tetrahedron, pyramid, wedge, hexahedron); other cell types get 0. Use it to locate distorted or degenerate cells before a simulation or to explain solver problems. Each metric has its own scale and ideal value (for example Scaled Jacobian is 1 for an ideal element and negative for inverted ones), so read thresholds from the Verdict documentation. ParaView's defaults are Radius Ratio (triangles, tetrahedra), Edge Ratio (quads, wedges), Shape (pyramids) and Maximum Aspect Frobenius (hexahedra). Use pvCellSize or cellSize for cell size.
pitfalls: On a mixed mesh the single Quality array holds different metrics for different cell types; compare values only within one cell type or choose comparable metrics.
Higher-order cells are measured by their own definition unless LinearApproximation is enabled, which adds Quality (Linear Approx).

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/281.explanation: Computes Minkowski functionals and shapefinders for each polyhedral cell of a Voronoi tessellation (vtkMinkowskiFilter). It adds cell arrays S (surface area), V (volume, copied from the input's Volumes array), C (integrated mean curvature), X (Euler characteristic), G (genus), T = 3V/S (thickness), B = S/C (breadth), L = C/(4 pi (G + 1)) (length), and planarity P and filamentarity F, which characterize whether a structure is sheet-like or filament-like. Use it on merged Voronoi regions from pvVoronoiMergeConnected.
pitfalls: Every cell must be a polyhedron and the input must have a Volumes cell array; other unstructured grids are not handled by the native code.
Lengths and areas are in the dataset's coordinate units; no conversion is applied.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/383.explanation: Sweeps polygonal data around an axis through the coordinate origin (RotationAxis, ParaView default z) to build a swept surface: free edges and lines become surfaces and vertices become lines, so a profile curve becomes an axisymmetric shell (cylinder, bottle), and Translation or DeltaRadius turn it into a spring or spiral. Capping closes the ends with copies of a filled 2-D input. Output is polydata, a surface rather than a volume; use pvVolumeOfRevolution to sweep 2-D cells into volume cells.
pitfalls: The axis passes through (0, 0, 0); translate the profile first (transform) if the physical axis is elsewhere.
Closed surfaces such as a sphere have no free edges, so they give no swept surface, only caps.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/387.explanation: Reads the NetCDF-based mesh and mode files of SLAC's accelerator electromagnetics codes (Omega3P, Tau3P and related tools). MeshFileName is the element mesh; ModeFileName is one mode file (usually an eigenmode with electric and magnetic fields) or several files forming a time series. Output port 0 (External Surface) is the boundary surface and port 1 (Entire Volume) the volume mesh, filled only when ReadInternalVolume is enabled. When a mode file stores a frequency (100 or more, treated as hertz) the complex fields are animated over one period of the lowest frequency: each mode contributes magnitude × FrequencyScale × cos(initial phase + 2πft + PhaseShift) and the modes are summed.
pitfalls: Port 0 is only the external surface; enable ReadInternalVolume and connect {"node": id, "port": 1} for fields inside the cavity.

ModeFileName is optional: omit it to read the mesh alone. A bounded native probe on 2026-10-12 (ParaView 5.13.3, serial, synthetic one-tetrahedron mesh) read the mesh with ModeFileName omitted, with no error (4 points, 4 cells); it has not been run on real SLAC files.
Mode files must use the same points as the mesh file.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/568.explanation: Reconstructs sharp material interfaces in mixed cells of Eulerian or ALE multi-material simulations (e.g. CTH or other volume-of-fluid output) with Youngs' method: in each cell the material is bounded by a plane perpendicular to its interface normal, placed so the cut volume matches the cell's volume fraction. Input is a composite dataset with one cell-centred volume fraction array per material and, ideally, a 3-component cell normal array per material. /properties/nodes/items/oneOf/588.explanation: Cuts the input with one infinite plane through origin, perpendicular to normal, and returns polygonal data: a surface from a volume mesh, lines from a surface. Point arrays are interpolated onto the cut and cell arrays are copied from the cell each polygon came from, so cell-centred CFD fields appear piecewise constant. Use it for cross-sections of 3-D fields; use clip to keep one side of a volume, contour for an isosurface, probeLine for a 1-D profile, and pvSlice for several parallel offsets or other cut shapes.
pitfalls: origin defaults to [0, 0, 0], not to the centre of your data as in the ParaView GUI. A plane that misses the data gives empty geometry, which Schemaxis reports as EMPTY_GEOMETRY; set origin inside the dataset bounds.

Hyper tree grid input is refused with INPUT_TRAIT_MISMATCH (recovery: use pvSlice): this operation sets only ParaView's SliceType, whereas a hyper tree grid is cut by the separate HyperTreeGridImplicitFunction, so origin and normal would have no effect on it.

Native acceptance (examples/schemaxis/acceptance.py) checks that slices lie on the requested plane and that integrals over a wavelet slice match analytic values; crinkle output and real CFD meshes are not separately checked.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/588/proper.explanation: Defines the cutting plane and how the cut is built: origin (Schemaxis default [0, 0, 0]) and normal (default [1, 0, 0], i.e. x+) place the plane, crinkle (default false) keeps whole intersected cells instead of a flat cut, and triangulate (default true) splits cut polygons into triangles. All four are assigned and the slice type is fixed to Plane; slice offset values and the point-merge method are not set by Schemaxis.
Invoke in order before updating this node on every selected visit.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/589.explanation: Applies Laplacian smoothing to a polygonal surface: each iteration moves every point a small step towards the average of its connected neighbours. The output is polygonal data with the same points and connectivity at smoother positions, and arrays are passed unchanged. Use it to reduce faceting or noise on scanned, marching-cubes or STL surfaces before rendering or curvature. Input must be vtkPolyData; run surface first on volume meshes.
pitfalls: Laplacian smoothing shrinks surfaces and rounds sharp features; compare volumes or key dimensions with the input before measuring the result.
VTK's relaxation factor (0.01) is not exposed, so 20 iterations move points only slightly; raise iterations for stronger smoothing.
Feature edges are not protected and open boundaries are smoothed too (VTK defaults: feature-edge smoothing off, boundary smoothing on); neither smooth nor pvSmooth exposes these switches.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/590.explanation: Creates a triangulated polygonal sphere (vtkPolyData with point normals) of given radius about centre, with its poles on the z axis. resolution sets the number of longitude divisions around z (Schemaxis default 24, ParaView's own default 8); latitude divisions are fixed at 24 by Schemaxis. Use it as a marker, a target mesh for resample, a seed surface for streamTracer or simple test geometry; its coordinates are in the units of the data it is combined with.
pitfalls: Latitude resolution (PhiResolution) is fixed at 24, so a very high resolution gives long thin facets; use pvSphere to set ThetaResolution and PhiResolution together or to make a partial sphere.
The facets lie inside the true sphere, so the surface area and enclosed volume are slightly smaller than the analytic values, noticeably so at low resolution.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/591.explanation: Integrates streamlines of a steady vector field from the points of a separate seed dataset and returns polygonal data made of polylines. Connect the flow dataset to input and any point-producing node (line, sphere, a slice) to seed; every seed point starts a trace. Input point arrays are interpolated onto the lines and ParaView adds IntegrationTime, Vorticity, Rotation and AngularVelocity point arrays and a ReasonForTermination cell array. Point vectors are interpolated along the trace. A cell vector array (association CELLS) is traced as constant within each cell, but ParaView's input domain also requires some three-component point array on the input, so a cell-only input fails INPUT_DOMAIN_MISMATCH at update. Convert cell-centred CFD velocity with cellToPoint for the usual smooth traces. The integrator stays at ParaView's Runge-Kutta 4-5 with step lengths in cell lengths. Use pvStreamTracerWithCustomSource to change the integrator, step unit or terminal speed, and pvStreamTracer for ParaView's built-in seed shapes.
pitfalls: These are instantaneous streamlines at the selected time, not pathlines or particle tracks through changing timesteps.
maximumLength (Schemaxis default 20) is an absolute arc length in dataset units, not a fraction of the domain; scale it to your geometry, or lines in a large domain stop early.

Empty or truncated lines usually mean seeds outside the flow cells, the wrong vector array, or speed below ParaView's terminal speed (1e-12). ReasonForTermination tells why each line stopped: 1 left the domain, 4 maximum length, 5 maximum steps, 6 terminal speed.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/592.explanation: Extracts the outer boundary surface of any dataset as polygonal data: the exterior faces of volume cells plus any 2-D, line and vertex cells already present. Use it to turn a volume mesh into a surface for rendering, normals, featureEdges, decimate or surface export, or to see the whole boundary of a CFD domain (walls, inlets and outlets together). Cell arrays are copied from the adjacent cell to each face and point arrays are passed; nothing is interpolated.
pitfalls: Interior faces are removed, so use slice or clip to see inside. Composite data is surfaced block by block, so faces between blocks remain.
Cell values on the surface are those of the adjacent volume cell, not boundary-condition values; for OpenFOAM patch values select the patch regions in foam instead.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/593.explanation: Computes, for every point and cell array of a time-dependent input, its average, minimum, maximum and population standard deviation over all input time steps, which the filter requests itself. The output has the input's type and geometry, no time, and arrays named <name>_average, <name>_minimum, <name>_maximum and <name>_stddev (other arrays are not kept). Every step is weighted equally regardless of time spacing, so this is not a time integral. Schemaxis enables all four statistics by default; use pvTemporalStatistics only if you want the generated binding with native option names.
pitfalls: Unequal time steps bias the average; resample time first if the spacing varies.
Every time step is read and processed, which can take long on large series; restrict the input time range first.
The mesh must keep the same points and cells over time; on changing meshes the statistics are meaningless.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/594.explanation: Keeps the cells of a mesh whose selected point or cell scalar lies inside the inclusive range [lower, upper], producing an unstructured grid. Schemaxis fixes ParaView's ThresholdMethod to Between, requires all three options, checks that lower does not exceed upper and that the named array exists with the stated association. Use it to isolate a region such as hot gas or a recirculation zone; use pvThreshold for inverted, one-sided or component-wise tests.
pitfalls: For point arrays ParaView's AllScalars default (true) applies: a cell is kept only if all of its points are in range, which shrinks the region compared with a cell-array threshold.
Cells are kept whole, so the boundary is stepped; use contour or clip for a smooth iso-boundary.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/595.explanation: Applies a linear transform to the point coordinates: scale, then rotation, then translation, all about the coordinate origin [0, 0, 0]. Vectors and normals are transformed with the geometry (every three-component array while allVectors is true). Polygonal, unstructured and structured grids keep their type; image data and rectilinear grids become an explicit-point dataset. Use it to position, orient or rescale geometry, e.g. scale [0.001, 0.001, 0.001] to convert millimetre coordinates to metres.
pitfalls: Rotation and scaling act about the origin, not the dataset centre, so an object away from the origin also moves. Translate it to the origin first, or use pvTransform with RotateAroundOriginTransform.
Transformed vector arrays are rotated and scaled too: a millimetre-to-metre scale also multiplies velocity-like vectors by 0.001. Field values are never unit-converted.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/596.explanation: Converts polygonal data so that every polygon and triangle strip becomes triangles and polylines become single line segments; vertices are kept. /properties/nodes/items/oneOf/597.explanation: Builds a polygonal tube of constant radius around each line or polyline of polygonal input, typically streamlines from streamTracer, so that thin lines become visible shaded geometry in images and exports. The output is vtkPolyData, and input point arrays are carried onto the tube surface so it can be coloured by the same fields. Schemaxis assigns radius 0.1, 12 sides and capped ends; ParaView's radius variation stays off, so use pvTube for tubes whose radius follows a scalar or vector.
pitfalls: radius is an absolute length in dataset units: 0.1 vanishes on a 100 m domain and swamps a 1 mm one. ParaView's GUI starts from 1% of the input extent, a reasonable first choice.
Lines with repeated consecutive points are not tubed; run clean first if segments are missing.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/598.explanation: Displaces each point along a direction by scale times a point scalar (new position = point + scale x value x direction), turning a field on a flat surface into a relief or carpet plot, or moving a surface by a normal displacement. With useNormal true (Schemaxis default) every point moves along the same normal (default z+); with useNormal false the input's point normals are used when present. The output keeps the input type, except that image data and rectilinear grids become a structured grid; all arrays are carried along.
pitfalls: The warp distance is in dataset units: choose scale so that the field range times scale is a modest fraction of the geometry size, otherwise the relief dwarfs or hides the shape.
Schemaxis normalizes normal, so its length does not change the displacement; express any magnification through scale.

Connect a specific output port of the upstream node. Use this for producers with several outputs, for example a filter that also writes a table or a second dataset. Schemaxis checks the port number against the producer’s actual output ports when the pipeline is built.
Name (id) of the upstream node whose output you are selecting. It must be another node in this document.
Zero-based output port number of that node: 0 is the first output. A port beyond the producer’s number of outputs is rejected when the pipeline is built.
pitfalls: Planning only checks that the port is a nonnegative integer; whether the producer really has that many outputs is checked when the pipeline is built (INVALID_OUTPUT_PORT).

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/598/proper.explanation: Selects the warping scalar (field, required) and the displacement: scale (Schemaxis default 1), the warp direction normal (default [0, 0, 1], z+) and useNormal (default true, which ignores the input's own point normals; ParaView's default is false). All defaults are assigned; XYPlane and GenerateEnclosure keep ParaView's defaults (off).
Invoke in order before updating this node on every selected visit.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/599.explanation: Moves every point by scale times a three-component point vector (new position = point + scale x vector), typically to show a structural displacement field or exaggerate a deformation mode. The output keeps the input type (image data and rectilinear grids become structured grids) and carries all arrays. With scale 1 and a displacement in the same length units as the coordinates the result is the true deformed shape; warping by a velocity is only a visual distortion.
pitfalls: The displacement must be in the coordinate units: a displacement in millimetres on a mesh in metres needs scale 0.001 for the true shape.
Large scales can fold or invert cells; do not compute volumes or mesh quality on an exaggerated warp.

/properties/nodes/items/oneOf/600.explanation: Creates a synthetic uniform image (vtkImageData) whose point array RTData combines a Gaussian peak of height maximum with sinusoidal terms along x, y and z. With the Schemaxis defaults it is a 21 x 21 x 21-point grid with unit spacing spanning -10 to 10 on each axis. Use it as a self-contained input to try slice, contour, clip, streamTracer or scene settings without a real case; its values have no physical meaning or units.

/properties/scenes.explanation: Each scene selects what to publish from the node graph: dataset files (geometry), CSV field tables (measurements), native-format exports, PNG images and glTF. Only the nodes its outputs depend on run, and every requested output is produced once per visit of the scene.
/properties/scenes.label: Scenes
pitfalls: Each scene needs at least one output; visible alone is not an output (EMPTY_PUBLICATION).
Scene ids must be unique (DUPLICATE_SCENE).

/properties/scenes/items.explanation: One scene: an id plus any combination of geometry, measurements, exports, images and gltf. Images and glTF render the nodes in visible; the others publish data directly. Its visits are the selected times × the values of axes its nodes use.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/id.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.explanation: Maps data node ids to display styles for the rendered outputs (images and glTF). Visible nodes are scene roots, so they run even without images, and their combined bounds frame the default cameras.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.label: Visible objects
pitfalls: images and gltf need at least one visible node (EMPTY_SCENE); resources such as lookup tables cannot be visible.
Visible nodes with no points are left out of the framing bounds; if all are empty, rendering fails.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.explanation: Display style for one visible node (the key is the node id): solid colour or colouring by a field, opacity and representation. Keys left out use the Schemaxis defaults: light grey solid colour, opacity 1, Surface, no legend.

Solid colour, used when field is not set: a Matplotlib colour name ("steelblue", "tab:blue", "xkcd:sky blue"), a hex code ("#336699", "#336699cc"), a grey level written as a string ("0.5"), or an RGB/RGBA list. An alpha component multiplies opacity.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.label: Colour
pitfalls: colour has no effect while field is set; the field's lookup table colours the object.
The name "none" means fully transparent (alpha 0) and hides the object.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.label: Runtime value

/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.explanation: Colour as numbers: [red, green, blue] or [red, green, blue, alpha], each 0 to 1. Whole numbers 0 to 255 are read as bytes when every component is an integer and at least one exceeds 1.
pitfalls: Integer lists are read as bytes only when a component exceeds 1: [0, 0, 1] is pure blue, but [0, 0, 2] is read as bytes and is almost black.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.label: Runtime value

/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.explanation: Name of a ParaView colour-map preset applied to the field's lookup table, for example "Cool to Warm" or "Viridis (matplotlib)". Choose perceptually uniform maps for quantitative images. Only used when field is set.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.label: Colour preset
/properties/scenes/items/properties/visi.defaultMeaning: omitted: ParaView's own initial colour map for the lookup table
pitfalls: Names must match a preset installed in ParaView exactly; unknown names fail with UNKNOWN_COLOUR_PRESET.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: PNG renderings of this scene's visible nodes. Each entry is an image writer with a pixel size and a camera list; one PNG is written per camera, per appearance and per visit, then decoded and checked for size and non-uniform pixels.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.label: Images
pitfalls: The PNG check rejects blank images, but it cannot confirm that the chosen colouring is scientifically meaningful.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: One image writer: a unique id within the scene, a size in pixels and a nonempty list of cameras.
Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.
Image [width, height] in pixels, each from 32 to 8192. Automatic framing fits the bounds diagonal into the shorter side, so a portrait image is zoomed out to keep the whole object visible.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.label: Image size

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: One pixel dimension, integer 32 to 8192: the first element is the width, the second the height.
Viewpoints to render, one PNG each. An empty object {} uses every default: camera on the +x side looking at the centre of the visible bounds, z up, parallel projection framed with 10 % padding.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.label: Cameras
pitfalls: To compute cameras from bounds, use the authoring-time {"$value": "fitCamera", ...} for one entry or {"$value": "orbitCameras", ...} for the whole list.
Camera-only variation belongs in this list; an $axis in a camera must name an axis the scene's nodes already vary.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: One camera. Every key is optional and may be a runtime value; framing is computed from the visible nodes' bounds unless bounds, focalPoint, scale or distance are given.
An axis token, a vector, or an azimuth and elevation about an up axis
An axis token, a vector, or an azimuth and elevation about an up axis

Camera side as an axis token: "x+" (also "x", "xp", "+x") places the camera on the +X side of the focal point looking toward −X; "z-" (also "zm", "-z") looks up from below. Case-insensitive; y and z work the same way.
pitfalls: Unknown tokens fail with UNKNOWN_AXIS_TOKEN; only x, y and z with an optional sign or p/m suffix are accepted.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: Direction object: give exactly one of axis, vector, or azimuth and elevation in degrees. /properties/scenes/items/properties/imag.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.label: Exports
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.explanation: Files written by an explicitly chosen ParaView writer, once per visit, each re-read and compared with the live data under the declared comparison and accepted losses before it counts as a verified artifact. Use exports for formats other than the automatic VTK XML files of geometry, or when writer options matter.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: [] (no explicit exports).
pitfalls: Do not set FileName, time-series or file-series writer properties; Schemaxis names the file data.<extension> in a managed directory and writes one selected time per visit.
A writer listed in the catalogue can still reject a data type or fail natively; the readback comparison, not the file's existence, decides success.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.explanation: One export: the data node to write, the writer, and how its file is verified. Choosing writer selects the variant, which fixes the allowed extensions, writer options and resource ports. Its id must be unique within the scene.

Writes the node with ParaView's writers/CGNSWriter (write a dataset in CGNS format), as .cgns. If comparison is omitted, verification uses semantic comparison, which needs acceptLosses to include "structure", "point-identity", "connectivity-order" and "storage-type".
pitfalls: The writer accepts only vtkCompositeDataSet and vtkDataSet input; another data type fails before writing (INPUT_DOMAIN_MISMATCH).
A small serial native fixture for this writer passed in the 2026-09-16 catalogue verification; it covers one small representative dataset with near-default options, not every data type or setting.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.explanation: Give this object a unique name. References use this name to identify the result or object.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.label: Data node
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.explanation: Id of the data node whose output the CGNSWriter writer receives as its Input, evaluated at the visit's time. The writer declares vtkCompositeDataSet and vtkDataSet input. The node becomes a scene root, so it runs even if nothing else in the scene uses it.
pitfalls: Resource nodes (lookup tables, textures) are not datasets and are rejected here (TYPE_MISMATCH); connect them through resources instead.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.label: Writer
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.explanation: pvWriteCGNSWriter selects ParaView's writers/CGNSWriter proxy for this export. The choice fixes the allowed extensions (.cgns), the writer-specific options and the default comparison (semantic); the native identity is checked when the writer is created.

Optional array selection (ChooseArraysToWrite plus one list per association), GhostLevel and UseHDF5, which picks HDF5 (ParaView default) or ADF storage. Omitted settings keep ParaView's values: every array written, no ghost levels, HDF5; the file name and time stepping are managed by Schemaxis.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.label: Writer resources
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.explanation: Resource-port map for this writer. The CGNSWriter writer declares no resource ports, so the only valid value is an empty object; resources are not data inputs.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: {} (no resources connected).

/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.label: File extension
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.explanation: Extension of the written file, chosen from those the CGNSWriter writer declares (.cgns). The file is always named data.<extension> inside a directory Schemaxis creates for this export and visit.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.defaultMeaning: Omitted: the first declared extension, cgns.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.label: Comparison
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.explanation: How the re-read file is compared with the live data. exact: structure, connectivity, arrays and storage types identical. geometry: exterior surface triangles only, for surface formats. pixels: image samples, for image data. table: CSV rows and columns, only for CSV writers. semantic: geometry plus every point and cell field, allowing reordering and regrouping. For the CGNSWriter writer the default is semantic.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.defaultMeaning: Omitted: the writer contract's comparison, semantic.
pitfalls: Every comparison except exact requires its losses in acceptLosses (for semantic: structure, point-identity, connectivity-order and storage-type).
table always parses the file as CSV and pixels requires image data on both sides; pick them only for matching formats.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.label: Tolerance
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.explanation: Largest accepted absolute difference between each live and re-read number. geometry compares only the coordinates of the triangulated exterior surface; semantic compares point and cell coordinates and every input point/cell field value; pixels compares sample values; table compares numeric CSV cells (text cells must match exactly). One tolerance covers all compared quantities, so choose it from the smallest magnitude that matters. exact comparison requires 0.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.units: Units of the compared values (dataset coordinates, field or pixel values); no conversion
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: 0 (values must be equal).
pitfalls: A nonzero tolerance with comparison exact is rejected (INVALID_TOLERANCE).

/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.label: Accepted losses
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.explanation: Your explicit acknowledgement of what the chosen comparison does not verify. It must contain every loss category the comparison requires; the list is recorded in the export receipt. With this writer's default comparison (semantic) the required entries are structure, point-identity, connectivity-order and storage-type.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: [] (no losses accepted, so any comparison other than exact is rejected).
pitfalls: Missing a required category fails before writing (LOSS_NOT_ACCEPTED, listing the required names).
Extra names are accepted without checking spelling; they document intent but change no verification.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.explanation: One accepted loss category. Recognised names: fields (field arrays are not compared); point-identity (point ids and point order may change); interior-cells (only the exterior surface is compared); structure (dataset type or block structure may change); coordinates (spatial coordinates are not compared); topology (cell connectivity is not compared); connectivity-order (cell ordering may change); storage-type (numeric storage types may change).

How an exported file is re-read for verification: null for ParaView's automatic reader, or {"operation": reader, "options": {...}} to use a declared source reader. The file name is always supplied by Schemaxis; only the reader options you author are assigned.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.defaultMeaning: Omitted or null: ParaView's OpenDataFile picks the reader from the extension (PLYReader for pvWritePPLYWriter).
pitfalls: CSV table exports, pvWriteJSONImageWriter and pvWriteHoudiniWriter use built-in verifiers and reject a readback reader (INVALID_READER).
/properties/scenes/items/properties/expo.label: Readback reader

One setting, MeshStaticOverTime (ParaView default false), which writes the mesh only once for a time series. Schemaxis manages the file name and writes one time state per export, so there is no later step to share the mesh with and the cross-step sharing never happens. The setting still changes how a single step is stored: with true, ParaView forces its light-data limit to 1, so heavy data (every array larger than one value) goes into the HDF5 file, and the topology and geometry are stored there as /Topology_<grid> and /Geometry_<grid> datasets. Semantic verification does not depend on it.

/properties/scenes/items/properties/appe.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/properties/scenes/items/properties/appe.label: Runtime value

/properties/scenes/items/properties/appe.explanation: Colour as numbers: [red, green, blue] or [red, green, blue, alpha], each 0 to 1. Whole numbers 0 to 255 are read as bytes when every component is an integer and at least one exceeds 1.
pitfalls: Integer lists are read as bytes only when a component exceeds 1: [0, 0, 1] is pure blue, but [0, 0, 2] is read as bytes and is almost black.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
