/properties/scenes/items/properties/meas.explanation: One measurement table: the node to tabulate and which association's arrays to include.
Id of the data node whose arrays are written. String arrays are skipped; nonfinite values fail (NONFINITE_DATA).
/properties/scenes/items/properties/meas.label: Node
pitfalls: An association with no tuples or no numeric arrays fails (EMPTY_MEASUREMENT).

/properties/scenes/items/properties/meas.explanation: Which arrays become columns: POINTS gives one row per point with point arrays, CELLS one row per cell with cell arrays, ROWS one row per table row (table data only).
/properties/scenes/items/properties/meas.label: Association
pitfalls: ROWS on non-table data fails (INVALID_ASSOCIATION).

/properties/axes.explanation: Named sweeps. A setting reads the current value with {"$axis": name}; a scene's visits are the product of the axes its nodes use, multiplied by the number of times, with the first listed axis varying fastest. Axes no node in the scene uses do not multiply its outputs.
/properties/axes.label: Axes
pitfalls: The total visit count must stay within maxStates (EXPANSION_TOO_LARGE).

/properties/axes/items.explanation: One axis: a unique name plus exactly one of values (explicit samples) or series (generated positions).

/properties/axes/items/properties/name.explanation: Identifier read by {"$axis": name}; unique among axes, starting with a letter.
/properties/axes/items/properties/name.label: Axis name
pitfalls: Duplicate names fail (DUPLICATE_AXIS).

/properties/axes/items/properties/values.explanation: Samples in visit order, one visit per element in scenes that use the axis. Each element may be any JSON value, e.g. a number, an [x, y, z] position or an object whose members are picked with the marker's path.
/properties/axes/items/properties/values.label: Axis values

/properties/axes/items/properties/values.explanation: Free JSON data that the schema does not interpret: a scalar, list or object. Its meaning comes from where it is used, for example reusable blocks read with {"$document": "/definitions/..."} or one sample of an axis read with {"$axis": name}.

/properties/axes/items/properties/series.explanation: Positions along an axis, given as any three of start, end, spacing and count
First position; defaults to the padded lower bound
Last position; defaults to the padded upper bound
Absolute inset applied to bounds-derived ends only
Inset as a fraction of the bounds extent, applied to bounds-derived ends only

/properties/axes/items/oneOf/0.explanation: Explicit-values form: choose it to list the samples yourself, which may be numbers, vectors or objects. series must then be absent.

/properties/axes/items/oneOf/0/not.explanation: Excludes series from an axis that uses values; declaring both fails.

/properties/axes/items/oneOf/1.explanation: Generated-series form: choose it for evenly spaced numeric positions from any consistent three of start, end, spacing and count. values must then be absent.

/properties/axes/items/oneOf/1/not.explanation: Excludes values from an axis that uses series; declaring both fails.

/properties/times.explanation: Simulation times at which every scene is evaluated: an explicit list, or a selection from the times a source node stores. Each time is a separate visit, used for the pipeline update and the render view time.
/properties/times.label: Simulation times

/properties/times/anyOf/0.explanation: Explicit list: choose it for data without stored time steps, or when the exact times are known. Values are used as given, without matching to stored times; what a reader returns between its stored steps is ParaView's behaviour.

/properties/times/anyOf/0/items.explanation: One simulation time, in the data's own time units; visits follow list order.

/properties/times/anyOf/1.explanation: Source selection: choose it for time-dependent readers, such as an OpenFOAM case, to pick from the times the reader actually stores. Schemaxis configures the source in ParaView, reads its TimestepValues, resolves select, then plans with the chosen times and keeps inspection.json and time-selection.json as evidence.

/properties/times/anyOf/1/properties/sou.explanation: Id of the node whose stored times are inspected. It must have no connected inputs (a reader or source), only constant options, and must advertise TimestepValues.
/properties/times/anyOf/1/properties/sou.label: Time source
pitfalls: A filter or a source with runtime options fails (INVALID_TIME_SOURCE); a source without time metadata fails (UNAVAILABLE_TIMES).

/properties/times/anyOf/1/properties/sel.explanation: Shorthand: "latest" selects only the last stored time and "first" only the earliest, by time value.

Selection object: exactly one of latest, first, values, valueRange, indices or indexRange, plus tolerance for values or valueRange. Selected times are deduplicated and processed in increasing time order.
pitfalls: No selector or two selectors fail (UNDER_SPECIFIED_TIMES, OVER_SPECIFIED_TIMES); a selection matching nothing fails (EMPTY_TIME_SELECTION).

/properties/times/anyOf/1/properties/sel.explanation: Nearest stored time to each value
One requested time value; the nearest stored time is selected (ties choose the lower) and any difference is reported. With tolerance, a larger difference fails (TIME_OUT_OF_TOLERANCE).
Every stored time within an inclusive range of values
One end of the inclusive range [low, high] of stored time values to select; the ends may be given in either order, and tolerance widens both.
Zero-based position in the source's stored time list, in the order the reader reports it; a position past the end fails (INVALID_TIME_INDEX).
Every stored time within an inclusive range of positions
One end of the inclusive position range [first, last], zero-based; the ends are sorted, and a last position beyond the final stored time is shortened with a note.
Largest accepted difference between a requested and a stored value

/properties/definitions.explanation: Free JSON data that the schema does not interpret: a scalar, list or object. Its meaning comes from where it is used, for example reusable blocks read with {"$document": "/definitions/..."} or one sample of an axis read with {"$axis": name}.

/properties/dimensions.explanation: Free JSON data that the schema does not interpret: a scalar, list or object. Its meaning comes from where it is used, for example reusable blocks read with {"$document": "/definitions/..."} or one sample of an axis read with {"$axis": name}.

/properties/views.explanation: Free JSON data that the schema does not interpret: a scalar, list or object. Its meaning comes from where it is used, for example reusable blocks read with {"$document": "/definitions/..."} or one sample of an axis read with {"$axis": name}.

/properties/settings.explanation: Free JSON data that the schema does not interpret: a scalar, list or object. Its meaning comes from where it is used, for example reusable blocks read with {"$document": "/definitions/..."} or one sample of an axis read with {"$axis": name}.

/properties/maxStates.explanation: Upper limit on visits: a scene's product of active axis lengths × number of times, series positions, and the per-option sweep check all must stay within it, or planning fails (EXPANSION_TOO_LARGE) before any native work. It guards against accidental combinatorial sweeps.
/properties/maxStates.label: Maximum states

/properties/maxPublications.explanation: Upper limit on planned output files, summed over scenes and visits: per visit, geometry + measurements + exports + appearances × (glTF + all cameras). Exceeding it fails at planning (EXPANSION_TOO_LARGE).
/properties/maxPublications.label: Maximum publications

/$defs/runtime.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
/$defs/runtime.label: Runtime value
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/0.explanation: Reads the current visit's value of a declared axis. Choose it to sweep a setting over the values (or series positions) listed in the top-level axes; every value of an active axis produces its own visit and outputs.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/0/properties/$axis.explanation: Name of an entry in the top-level axes list; the marker evaluates to that axis's value for the current visit. Using it activates the axis for every scene that executes this setting.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/0/properties/$axis.label: Axis name
pitfalls: Names are case-sensitive; an undeclared name fails at planning (UNKNOWN_AXIS).

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/0/properties/path.explanation: Selects part of the axis value when values are lists or objects: object keys and zero-based list indices, applied in order. For example ["position", 2] takes member position, then its third element.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/0/properties/path.label: Value path
pitfalls: A missing key or an index past the end fails with INVALID_SELECTION; strings address objects and integers address lists only.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/0/properties/path/i.explanation: One step into the axis value: a string selects an object member, an integer selects a list element. Steps apply left to right.
Member-name step: use it where the current part of the axis value is an object; the name must match exactly, including case.
Element-index step: use it where the current part of the axis value is a list; zero-based, so 0 is the first element. Negative indices are not supported.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/1.explanation: Reads metadata of another node after it has been updated on this visit: point and cell counts, bounds, data type, and each array's component count and range. Choose it when a setting should follow the data, for example a slice origin at the centre of the current bounds.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/1/properties/$obser.explanation: Id of the node whose observation is read. That node becomes a dependency and is updated first on every visit; resource nodes expose only their kind, native identity and input contracts.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/1/properties/$obser.label: Observed node
pitfalls: Observing a node that is downstream of the setting creates a dependency cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/1/properties/path.explanation: Selects part of the observation instead of the whole object: object keys and zero-based list indices, applied in order. Useful paths are ["bounds"] (six values xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax), ["points"], ["cells"], ["dataType"] and ["fields", "POINTS", name, "range"].
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/1/properties/path.label: Observation path
pitfalls: Tables have bounds null and use the ROWS association; a path that does not exist fails with INVALID_SELECTION.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/1/properties/path/i.explanation: One step into the observation: a string selects an object member, an integer selects a list element. Steps apply left to right.
Member-name step: use it where the current part of the observation is an object; the name must match exactly, including case.
Element-index step: use it where the current part of the observation is a list; zero-based, so 0 is the first element. Negative indices are not supported.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/2.explanation: Evaluates to the current visit's simulation time, taken from the top-level times (explicit list or source selection). Choose it when a setting should change with time, such as a moving probe position; it does not inspect a source's stored times.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/2/properties/$time.explanation: Must be exactly true; the marker then returns the visit's time as a number in the data's own time units. Any other value fails with INVALID_EXPRESSION ("$time must be true"); extra keys beside $time are rejected as unsupported keys (UNKNOWN_ARGUMENT).
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/2/properties/$time.label: Current time

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/3.explanation: Builds an [x, y, z] list from three scalar arguments, each of which may itself be a runtime value. Choose it to assemble a point or direction in which only some components vary, e.g. [0, 0, {"$axis": "height"}].

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/3/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the vector operation of $calc. It needs exactly three scalar arguments and returns a three-component list.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/3/properties/$calc.label: Operation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/3/properties/args.explanation: Exactly three arguments in x, y, z order; each must evaluate to a finite number (not a list), otherwise INVALID_EXPRESSION.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/3/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/3/properties/args/i.explanation: One argument of a $calc operation: a literal JSON scalar, a list of further arguments, or a nested runtime value. Nested parts are evaluated first, then the operation is applied.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/4.explanation: Centre [x, y, z] of six-value bounds [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax], typically {"$observe": node, "path": ["bounds"]}. Unlike boundsCentre3D it accepts zero thickness, so it suits planar data.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/4/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the midpoint operation of $calc. It needs one six-value bounds argument and returns its centre.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/4/properties/$calc.label: Operation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/4/properties/args.explanation: One argument: six finite bounds values with each minimum not greater than its maximum; empty bounds fail (INVALID_BOUNDS).
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/4/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/4/properties/args/i.explanation: One argument of a $calc operation: a literal JSON scalar, a list of further arguments, or a nested runtime value. Nested parts are evaluated first, then the operation is applied.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/5.explanation: Lower corner [xmin, ymin, zmin] of six-value bounds. Choose it to place something at the data's minimum corner or to build the min of a {"min", "max"} box for the bounds functions.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/5/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the boundsMin operation of $calc. It needs one six-value bounds argument and returns the three minima.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/5/properties/$calc.label: Operation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/5/properties/args.explanation: One argument: six finite bounds values [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax] with each minimum not greater than its maximum.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/5/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/5/properties/args/i.explanation: One argument of a $calc operation: a literal JSON scalar, a list of further arguments, or a nested runtime value. Nested parts are evaluated first, then the operation is applied.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/6.explanation: Upper corner [xmax, ymax, zmax] of six-value bounds. Choose it to reach the data's maximum corner or to build the max of a {"min", "max"} box for the bounds functions.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/6/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the boundsMax operation of $calc. It needs one six-value bounds argument and returns the three maxima.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/6/properties/$calc.label: Operation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/6/properties/args.explanation: One argument: six finite bounds values [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax] with each minimum not greater than its maximum.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/6/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/6/properties/args/i.explanation: One argument of a $calc operation: a literal JSON scalar, a list of further arguments, or a nested runtime value. Nested parts are evaluated first, then the operation is applied.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/7.explanation: Sum of two values: numbers, equal-length lists added element by element, or a number added to every element of a list. Choose it to offset a position, e.g. an observed centre plus [0, 0, 1].

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/7/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the add operation of $calc. It takes exactly two arguments, which may be numbers, lists or other runtime values.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/7/properties/$calc.label: Operation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/7/properties/args.explanation: Two arguments, summed. Lists must have equal length; a number is broadcast across a list. Results must stay finite.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/7/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/7/properties/args/i.explanation: One argument of a $calc operation: a literal JSON scalar, a list of further arguments, or a nested runtime value. Nested parts are evaluated first, then the operation is applied.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/8.explanation: First value minus second: numbers, equal-length lists element by element, or with a number broadcast across a list. Choose it for differences such as an extent (max corner minus min corner).

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/8/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the subtract operation of $calc. It takes exactly two arguments, which may be numbers, lists or other runtime values.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/8/properties/$calc.label: Operation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/8/properties/args.explanation: Two arguments in order: the first minus the second. Lists must have equal length; a number is broadcast across a list.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/8/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/8/properties/args/i.explanation: One argument of a $calc operation: a literal JSON scalar, a list of further arguments, or a nested runtime value. Nested parts are evaluated first, then the operation is applied.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/9.explanation: Product of two values: numbers, equal-length lists element by element, or a list scaled by a number. Choose it to scale a sweep value or a vector, e.g. [[1, 2, 3], 2] gives [2, 4, 6].

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/9/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the multiply operation of $calc. It takes exactly two arguments, which may be numbers, lists or other runtime values.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/9/properties/$calc.label: Operation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/9/properties/args.explanation: Two arguments, multiplied. A number times a list scales every element; two lists multiply element by element (not a dot product).
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/9/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/9/properties/args/i.explanation: One argument of a $calc operation: a literal JSON scalar, a list of further arguments, or a nested runtime value. Nested parts are evaluated first, then the operation is applied.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/10.explanation: First value divided by second: numbers, equal-length lists element by element, or with a number broadcast. Choose it for ratios or fractions of an extent; division by zero fails.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/10/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the divide operation of $calc. It takes exactly two arguments, which may be numbers, lists or other runtime values.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/10/properties/$calc.label: Operation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/10/properties/args.explanation: Two arguments in order: the first divided by the second. Division by zero fails (INVALID_EXPRESSION).
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/10/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/10/properties/args/.explanation: One argument of a $calc operation: a literal JSON scalar, a list of further arguments, or a nested runtime value. Nested parts are evaluated first, then the operation is applied.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/11.explanation: Smaller of two values, element by element for lists, or each element against a number. Choose it to clamp a value from above, e.g. limit a computed radius to a maximum.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/11/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the min operation of $calc. It takes exactly two arguments, which may be numbers, lists or other runtime values.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/11/properties/$calc.label: Operation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/11/properties/args.explanation: Two arguments compared: numbers, equal-length lists element by element, or a number broadcast across a list.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/11/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/11/properties/args/.explanation: One argument of a $calc operation: a literal JSON scalar, a list of further arguments, or a nested runtime value. Nested parts are evaluated first, then the operation is applied.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/12.explanation: Larger of two values, element by element for lists, or each element against a number. Choose it to clamp a value from below, e.g. keep a computed size above a minimum.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/12/properties/$calc.explanation: Selects the max operation of $calc. It takes exactly two arguments, which may be numbers, lists or other runtime values.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/12/properties/$calc.label: Operation

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/12/properties/args.explanation: Two arguments compared: numbers, equal-length lists element by element, or a number broadcast across a list.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/12/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/12/properties/args/.explanation: One argument of a $calc operation: a literal JSON scalar, a list of further arguments, or a nested runtime value. Nested parts are evaluated first, then the operation is applied.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13.explanation: Centre [x, y, z] of six-value VTK bounds [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax]; it accepts observed bounds directly and allows zero thickness. Choose it for slice or probe origins at the middle of the data.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/$call.explanation: Selects the registered function boundsCentre; its arguments go in args. Registered functions are pure calculations; no Python or native method can be named here.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/$call.label: Function

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of boundsCentre, by name. Each argument may be a literal or a runtime value; optional arguments left out take their declared defaults, and the result is type-checked before use.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args/.explanation: Six-value VTK bounds [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax], the form returned by {"$observe": node, "path": ["bounds"]}. Equal minimum and maximum are allowed; a minimum above its maximum fails.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args/.label: Bounds

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/13/properties/args/.explanation: Six-value VTK bounds [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax], the form returned by {"$observe": node, "path": ["bounds"]}. Equal minimum and maximum are allowed; a minimum above its maximum fails.
One bound value, in the order xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/14/properties/args/.explanation: Axis-aligned box that is centred, written as {"min": [x, y, z], "max": [x, y, z]} in dataset coordinates.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/15.explanation: Enlarges a {"min", "max"} box by fractions of its own size: min − before × size and max + after × size on each axis. Choose it to add room around a model, e.g. a wake region behind a vehicle.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/17.explanation: Extents [dx, dy, dz] (max − min per axis) of a {"min", "max"} box. Choose it to derive spacings, lengths or scale factors from the size of the data.
pitfalls: Boxes must have positive extent on all three axes; bounds of a flat slice fail. Use boundsCentre or $calc midpoint for planar data.

pitfalls: Each maximum must exceed its minimum on all three axes; a flat box (for example the bounds of a planar slice) fails with FUNCTION_FAILED.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/20.explanation: Computes a whole camera object (direction, up, focalPoint at the box centre, bounds, parallel, scale, distance) that frames a {"min", "max"} box from a chosen side for a given image aspect ratio.
pitfalls: A scene camera entry accepts runtime values only per camera key, so this object result cannot replace a camera there; use the authoring-time {"$value": "fitCamera", "args": {...}} form in images.cameras instead.
Boxes must have positive extent on all three axes; bounds of a flat slice fail. Use boundsCentre or $calc midpoint for planar data.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/20/properties/$call.explanation: Selects the registered function fitCamera; its arguments go in args. Registered functions are pure calculations; no Python or native method can be named here.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/20/properties/$call.label: Function

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/20/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/20/properties/args/.explanation: Axis-aligned box that the camera frames, written as {"min": [x, y, z], "max": [x, y, z]} in dataset coordinates.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/20/properties/args/.label: Bounds box
pitfalls: Each maximum must exceed its minimum on all three axes; a flat box (for example the bounds of a planar slice) fails with FUNCTION_FAILED.
To use observed six-value bounds, build min and max with {"$calc": "boundsMin", "args": [...]} and {"$calc": "boundsMax", "args": [...]}.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/21.explanation: Builds an OpenFOAM region list from two groups of "//patchName" selectors: the result is "internalMesh" followed by "patch/<name>" for every selector, without duplicates. It is a pure authoring helper used for the curated foam reader's regions option.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/21/properties/$call.explanation: Selects the registered function foamRegions; its arguments go in args. Registered functions are pure calculations; no Python or native method can be named here.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/21/properties/args/.explanation: Patch selectors for the tyres group, each "//" followed by one OpenFOAM patch name; each becomes "patch/<name>" in the result, in order, without duplicates.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/21/properties/args/.label: Runtime value

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22.explanation: Computes a list of count cameras evenly spaced in azimuth around the z axis (starting at +x, anticlockwise seen from +z) at a fixed elevation, each framed like fitCamera with z up. Its result is a camera list, not a single camera.
pitfalls: A scene camera entry accepts runtime values only per camera key, so this object result cannot replace a camera there; use the authoring-time {"$value": "orbitCameras", "args": {...}} form in images.cameras instead.
Boxes must have positive extent on all three axes; bounds of a flat slice fail. Use boundsCentre or $calc midpoint for planar data.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22/properties/$call.explanation: Selects the registered function orbitCameras; its arguments go in args. Registered functions are pure calculations; no Python or native method can be named here.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22/properties/$call.label: Function

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of orbitCameras, by name. Each argument may be a literal or a runtime value; optional arguments left out take their declared defaults, and the result is type-checked before use.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22/properties/args/.explanation: Axis-aligned box that the orbit cameras frame, written as {"min": [x, y, z], "max": [x, y, z]} in dataset coordinates.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22/properties/args/.label: Bounds box
pitfalls: Each maximum must exceed its minimum on all three axes; a flat box (for example the bounds of a planar slice) fails with FUNCTION_FAILED.
To use observed six-value bounds, build min and max with {"$calc": "boundsMin", "args": [...]} and {"$calc": "boundsMax", "args": [...]}.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/22/properties/args/.label: Runtime value

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/23.explanation: Midpoint (low + high) / 2 of a two-value range, such as an observed field range. Choose it for a contour value or threshold in the middle of the data range.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/23/properties/$call.explanation: Selects the registered function rangeCentre; its arguments go in args. Registered functions are pure calculations; no Python or native method can be named here.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/23/properties/$call.label: Function

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/23/properties/args.explanation: Arguments of rangeCentre, by name. Each argument may be a literal or a runtime value; optional arguments left out take their declared defaults, and the result is type-checked before use.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/23/properties/args.label: Arguments

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/23/properties/args/.explanation: Two values [low, high], for example an observed field range; the result is their average. The order is not checked.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/23/properties/args/.label: Range

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/23/properties/args/.explanation: Two values [low, high], for example an observed field range; the result is their average. The order is not checked.
One end of the range: first the low value, then the high value.
One end of the range: first the low value, then the high value.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/25.explanation: List of count points spread evenly from min to max along one axis (both ends included), with the other two coordinates at the box centre; count 1 gives the centre. Its result is a list of [x, y, z] points.
pitfalls: $call has no path, so a runtime list of positions cannot be indexed per visit; to step through positions, generate an axis's values with the authoring-time {"$value": "slicePositions", ...} form and read them with $axis.
Boxes must have positive extent on all three axes; bounds of a flat slice fail. Use boundsCentre or $calc midpoint for planar data.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/25/properties/args/.explanation: Axis-aligned box that the positions span, written as {"min": [x, y, z], "max": [x, y, z]} in dataset coordinates.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/25/properties/args/.label: Bounds box
pitfalls: Each maximum must exceed its minimum on all three axes; a flat box (for example the bounds of a planar slice) fails with FUNCTION_FAILED.
To use observed six-value bounds, build min and max with {"$calc": "boundsMin", "args": [...]} and {"$calc": "boundsMax", "args": [...]}.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27.explanation: Reads one numeric data value from an array of an updated upstream node: the tuple at a given index, or one component of it. Choose it to drive a setting from a specific data value, e.g. a probe result or a table cell; it reads stored values by index and does not interpolate in space.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/$samp.explanation: Id of the node whose output array is read; the node becomes a dependency and is updated first.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/$samp.label: Sampled node

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/assoc.explanation: Where the array lives: POINTS for point data, CELLS for cell data, ROWS for the rows of a table (tables only). The index then counts points, cells or rows.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/assoc.label: Association
pitfalls: ROWS on a non-table fails (INVALID_ASSOCIATION); POINTS or CELLS on a multiblock needs block to reach a leaf dataset.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/field.explanation: Name of a numeric array, exactly as in the data (case-sensitive).
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/field.label: Array name
pitfalls: A missing array fails with MISSING_FIELD; string arrays cannot be sampled.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/index.explanation: Zero-based tuple index: the point, cell or row number. It may itself be a runtime value, e.g. {"$axis": "row"} to step through rows.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/index.label: Tuple index
pitfalls: An index at or beyond the tuple count fails (INVALID_SELECTION); counts can change between visits.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/index.explanation: Zero-based tuple index: the point, cell or row number. It may itself be a runtime value, e.g. {"$axis": "row"} to step through rows.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/compo.explanation: Zero-based component of the tuple (0 is x of a vector). Set it to get a single number from a multi-component array.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/compo.label: Component
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/compo.defaultMeaning: Omitted: a number for a one-component array, the whole tuple as a list otherwise.

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/block.explanation: Path of zero-based child indices into nested multiblock data, applied in order, to reach the leaf dataset that holds the array.
/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/block.label: Block path
pitfalls: Only multiblock datasets can be descended; other composite types or a missing block fail (INVALID_SELECTION).

/$defs/runtime/anyOf/27/properties/block.explanation: One child index at the current multiblock level, zero-based.

/$defs/options-append.explanation: Append has no settings in Schemaxis: inputs are combined in the order connected, and ParaView's own options keep their native values, including Unstructured Grid output.

/$defs/options-appendGeometry.explanation: Append Geometry has no settings in Schemaxis; its result depends only on the connected polygonal inputs and their order.

/$defs/options-calculator.explanation: expression and result are required; association chooses whether point or cell arrays are used and where the result is stored (Schemaxis default Point Data). Other Calculator settings keep ParaView's values: double-precision result, invalid values replaced by 0, result stored as an array rather than as point coordinates.

/$defs/options-calculator/properties/exp.explanation: The equation evaluated on the selected point or cell arrays. Use native array names and vector components. For a vector U, sqrt(U_X*U_X+U_Y*U_Y+U_Z*U_Z) computes its magnitude.
/$defs/options-calculator/properties/exp.label: Function (equation)

/$defs/options-calculator/properties/exp.explanation: The equation evaluated on the selected point or cell arrays. Use native array names and vector components. For a vector U, sqrt(U_X*U_X+U_Y*U_Y+U_Z*U_Z) computes its magnitude.

/$defs/options-cylinder/properties/resol.explanation: This property indicates the number of divisions around the cylinder. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-elevation/properties/rang.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-extractBlock.explanation: One required setting, selectors: the hierarchy paths of the blocks to keep. ParaView's Assembly keeps its initial value, the block hierarchy (VTK's default assembly name Hierarchy).

/$defs/options-extractBlock/properties/s.explanation: Choose named parts of the input dataset, such as internalMesh or individual wall patches. Studio reads the input hierarchy and writes the native selector paths for you. Only blocks loaded by the reader can be selected.
/$defs/options-extractBlock/properties/s.label: Blocks to extract

/$defs/options-extractBlock/properties/s.explanation: Choose named parts of the input dataset, such as internalMesh or individual wall patches. Studio reads the input hierarchy and writes the native selector paths for you. Only blocks loaded by the reader can be selected.

One selector: a path expression naming a node of the input's block hierarchy, which selects that block and everything below it. "/Root/internalMesh" gives a full path; "//inlet" matches a node of that name at any depth. Order does not matter and overlapping selectors select a block once.
pitfalls: Hierarchy node names can differ from displayed block names when a name contains characters not allowed in node names; pick names from Studio's hierarchy list.

/$defs/options-extractSubset.explanation: extent (required) gives the inclusive IJK index range; rateI, rateJ and rateK subsample (Schemaxis default 1, no subsampling) and includeBoundary keeps the last index when subsampling (Schemaxis default true, overriding ParaView's false).

/$defs/options-extractSubset/properties/.explanation: This property specifies the minimum and maximum point indices along each of the I, J, and K axes; these values indicate the volume of interest (VOI). The output will have the (I,J,K) extent specified here.
/$defs/options-extractSubset/properties/.label: VOI

/$defs/options-extractSubset/properties/.explanation: This property specifies the minimum and maximum point indices along each of the I, J, and K axes; these values indicate the volume of interest (VOI). The output will have the (I,J,K) extent specified here.

One index bound of the volume of interest, in the order [imin, imax, jmin, jmax, kmin, kmax]. Bounds are inclusive point indices in the input's extent space (for example the wavelet source uses -10 to 10); use equal min and max to extract a single slice along that axis.

/$defs/options-foam.explanation: Settings choose the case marker (required, constant), the case layout (Schemaxis default Decomposed Case, unlike ParaView's Reconstructed Case), mesh regions (Schemaxis default internalMesh only), cell fields (ParaView's own selection when omitted) and whether the 0 directory is skipped (Schemaxis default false, unlike ParaView's true). Other OpenFOAM reader settings keep ParaView's values, e.g. cell-to-point data created.

/$defs/options-foam/properties/file.explanation: Choose the path and filename of a .foam marker in your OpenFOAM case folder, for example /data/coupe/coupe.foam. The marker can be empty: its parent folder contains the actual mesh and time directories. Absolute paths are accepted. Relative paths are resolved from the directory where Studio was launched, not from the JSON file folder. Browse inserts an absolute path; the dataset stays in place and is not uploaded or copied.

/$defs/options-foam/properties/caseType.explanation: Choose Decomposed Case when the results remain in processor0, processor1 and other processor folders. Choose Reconstructed Case for a serial case or results reconstructed into the main case folder. Match the layout of the data you want to read.

/$defs/options-foam/properties/regions.explanation: Mesh regions to load. internalMesh is the volume mesh; add boundary patches with the reader's prefixed names, e.g. "patch/inlet" or "patch/walls", when you also want those surfaces. Names must match regions available in your case. Omitting this setting loads internalMesh.
sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/vtk/vtk/-/raw/master/IO/Geometry/vtkOpenFOAMReader.cxx (region naming: internalMesh, patch/, group/, lagrangian/, /region/ prefix)

Names must match regions available in your case. Omitting this setting loads internalMesh.
sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/vtk/vtk/-/raw/master/IO/Geometry/vtkOpenFOAMReader.cxx (region naming: internalMesh, patch/, group/, lagrangian/, /region/ prefix)

/$defs/options-foam/properties/regions/a.explanation: One mesh region: internalMesh for the volume mesh, patch/<name> for a boundary patch named in constant/polyMesh/boundary (e.g. "patch/inlet") or group/<name> for a patch group. Multi-region cases prefix names with the region, e.g. "/fluid/internalMesh". Each selected region becomes its own block; order has no effect.

/$defs/options-foam/properties/regions/a.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default for the whole list: ["internalMesh"].
pitfalls: A bare patch name such as "inlet" does not match a region; use "patch/inlet".

/$defs/options-line/properties/start/any.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-line/properties/start/any.label: Runtime value

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvAMRFragmentsFilter/prop.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvAMReXBoxLibGridReader/p.explanation: Keep AMR blocks that have already been read in memory, so later updates that change the level or array selection, or revisit a time, do not reread them from disk. It does not change the data produced.
/$defs/options-pvAMReXBoxLibGridReader/p.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts with caching off (false).
pitfalls: Caching trades memory for speed; leave it off for large AMR hierarchies or single-pass publications.

/$defs/options-pvAMReXBoxLibGridReader/p.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvAMReXBoxLibGridReader/p.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvAVSUCDReader/properties.explanation: Path of one AVS UCD file. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; the value is passed when the node is created and must be a constant. Several entries form a time series in list order: if the first file reports no time, entry k is given time k (zero-based); otherwise each file's own times are used.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvAngularPeriodicFilter/p.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvAnimateModes.explanation: Choose the displacement array, the mode (ModeShape, from 1 to the number of input steps), the scale (default 1.0), whether the input is already displaced (default true) and whether a 0-1 time range is advertised for animation (default true).

/$defs/options-pvAnimateModes/properties.explanation: Whether ParaView advertises the [0, 1] phase range as the filter's time range. With false it no longer advertises that range, but the displacement is still scaled by cos(2π t) at whatever time is requested, and Schemaxis always requests the scene time. At time 0 the amplitude is the full DisplacementMagnitude; at any other requested time the shape is scaled by cos(2π t) regardless of this setting. ParaView's own text says that the requested time is used only when the option is set; the source does not do that.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 VTK/Filters/General/vtkAnimateModes.cxx:145-151 (the mode shape time is UPDATE_TIME_STEP when present; scale = DisplacementMagnitude * cos(2 pi t))
src/schemaxis/adaptors/paraview/native.py (UpdatePipeline always requests the scene time)

/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice.explanation: CutFunction sets the axis-aligned plane; OffsetValues adds one hyper-tree-grid slice per offset from that plane, and Level sets the AMR resolution (ParaView may initialize it to the finest level). OffsetValues has no XML default; omitted, it read back empty on a batch run and [0] when the upstream already had data, and a bounded native probe produced the same hyper tree grid slice either way. Give an explicit list, for example [0], when the number of slices matters.

/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.explanation: This property sets the parameters of the cut function.
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.label: Cut Function

/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.explanation: This property sets the parameters of the cut function.

Position of the axis-aligned plane: Origin (a point on it), Normal (which axis it is perpendicular to, after snapping), Offset (a shift along the normal) and AlwaysSnapToNearestAxis. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values (a plane perpendicular to x through Origin, which may be the centre of the input bounds).

/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.explanation: When true, ParaView replaces Normal by the coordinate axis of its largest absolute component, so the plane is always perpendicular to x, y or z. The snapped normal is always positive ([-1, 0, 0] becomes [1, 0, 0]), and tied components are all set to 1 ([1, 1, 0] stays [1, 1, 0]) rather than resolved to one axis. When false, Normal is used as given.
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.label: Always snap to nearest axis
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from true.
pitfalls: The snap is applied when Normal is set and is not undone when snapping is later turned off (SetAxisAligned re-applies the stored, already snapped normal). For an oblique plane, use the Plane choice where the operation offers it.
ParaView keeps the requested Normal in the property while the plane uses the snapped vector, so Schemaxis readback does not reveal the snap; write a pure axis normal such as [0, 0, 1].

/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.explanation: Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value.
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.label: Normal
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 0, 0], a plane perpendicular to the x axis.
pitfalls: A zero vector defines no plane; give at least one non-zero component.

Use a unit-length normal. A longer vector scales the implicit-function values (and the shift produced by Offset), which changes the meaning of value-based settings on the operation, such as slice offsets or a clip value, where the operation has them.

/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.explanation: Moves the plane along its normal without changing Origin: the plane actually used passes through Origin + Offset × Normal. Positive values move it toward the side the normal points to.
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.label: Offset
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.units: Dataset coordinate units when Normal has unit length (the shift is Offset × |Normal|)
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 0 (no shift).
pitfalls: With a non-unit Normal the plane moves by Offset times the normal’s length, not by Offset.

/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.explanation: A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing.
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.label: Origin
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial value (its static default is [0, 0, 0]; ParaView may instead derive it from the centre of the input’s bounding box). Set it explicitly when the result depends on it.
pitfalls: Coordinates are absolute, not fractions of the model: on a part spanning 0–2000 mm, [0.5, 0.5, 0.5] lies at a corner. Use the model’s own units.
Offset is added on top of Origin along Normal; keep Offset at 0 if Origin should be the exact plane position.

/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.explanation: The values in this property specify a list of current slice offset values. This can be used to create multiple slices with different centers. Each entry represents a new slice with its center shifted by the offset value. The 'Values Range' information is the range based on the global bounding box, not necessarily on the current slice geometry configuration. **These offset values are added to the global offset value set through the "Offset" property.**
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.label: Offset Values

/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.explanation: The values in this property specify a list of current slice offset values. This can be used to create multiple slices with different centers. Each entry represents a new slice with its center shifted by the offset value. The 'Values Range' information is the range based on the global bounding box, not necessarily on the current slice geometry configuration. **These offset values are added to the global offset value set through the "Offset" property.**

One slice offset along the plane normal, added to the plane's own Offset; each entry makes one slice, e.g. [-0.5, 0, 0.5] gives three parallel slices. Used for hyper tree grids only; AMR input ignores it.
/$defs/options-pvAxisAlignedSlice/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 declares no default values. In a bounded native probe an omitted list read back [] on a batch run and [0.0] when the upstream already had data, and both produced the same output (one hyper tree grid slice, 518 cells); the probe did not isolate why, so give an explicit list such as [0] when the number of slices matters.

/$defs/options-pvCGNSSeriesReader.explanation: Settings choose which bases, families and point/cell/face arrays are read, whether zone meshes and boundary patches are loaded, coordinate precision and caching, and how unsteady FlowSolution_t nodes are matched to time steps; FileNames is required. /$defs/options-pvCGNSSeriesReader/proper.explanation: Names of the CGNS bases (CGNSBase_t nodes, the top-level groups that hold zones) to read; each selected base becomes one block of the output. /$defs/options-pvCGNSSeriesReader/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkCGNSReader enables only the first base in the file). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Names must match the base names stored in the file exactly; an unknown name selects nothing.

Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; the value is passed when the node is created and must be a constant. Several entries form a time series in list order: if the first file reports no time, entry k is given time k (zero-based); otherwise each file's own times are used. Set IgnoreReaderTime to force the index times when the files' own times are wrong.

/$defs/options-pvCSVReader/properties/Fi.explanation: Path of one delimited-text file. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; the value is passed when the node is created and must be a constant. Several entries form a time series in list order: if the first file reports no time, entry k is given time k (zero-based); otherwise each file's own times are used.

/$defs/options-pvCalculator.explanation: Function and ResultArrayName (ParaView default "Result") define the computation; AttributeType picks the data association by name (ParaView picks it from the input, usually "Point Data") and ResultArrayType the storage type (default Double). Other settings redirect the result to coordinates, normals or texture coordinates, or control replacement of invalid results (default on, value 0).

/$defs/options-pvCalculator/properties/A.explanation: Data association the expression is evaluated on and the result is stored in; the same "Point Data" and "Cell Data" texts select the association in the calculator operation. Chosen by the ParaView entry text: "Point Data", "Cell Data", "Vertex Data", "Edge Data" or "Row Data". ParaView offers only the associations the connected input has (for example "Row Data" for a table), so a text it does not offer fails with NATIVE_DOMAIN_MISMATCH when the node is configured.

/$defs/options-pvCalculator/properties/F.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvCalculator/properties/F.label: Runtime value

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvClip.explanation: ClipType (ParaView default Plane) and Invert (default true) decide what is kept; Scalars and Value are used for scalar clipping, Crinkleclip keeps whole cells, Exact gives an exact box clip, and HyperTreeGridClipper applies to hyper tree grids. Omitted nested settings keep the native function's values.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.explanation: This property specifies the parameters of the clip function (an implicit description) used to clip the dataset.
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.label: Clip Type

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.explanation: This property specifies the parameters of the clip function (an implicit description) used to clip the dataset.

A rectangular box region (ParaView’s vtkPVBox): a unit cube scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation about its minimum corner and moved to Position, or, with UseReferenceBounds, the Bounds box transformed in the same way. The implicit function is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a box-shaped region; slicing or cutting with a box produces the box faces where they cross the data.
pitfalls: ParaView’s initial box may be a unit cube at the origin if the input bounds were not applied; set Position and Length explicitly.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.explanation: A rectangular box region (ParaView’s vtkPVBox): a unit cube scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation about its minimum corner and moved to Position, or, with UseReferenceBounds, the Bounds box transformed in the same way. The implicit function is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a box-shaped region; slicing or cutting with a box produces the box faces where they cross the data.
pitfalls: ParaView’s initial box may be a unit cube at the origin if the input bounds were not applied; set Position and Length explicitly.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.explanation: Placement and size of the box. In the normal mode Position (minimum corner), Length (edge lengths) and Rotation define it; with UseReferenceBounds true, Bounds defines the box and the other three act relative to it. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values, which may cover the whole input.
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.explanation: Placement and size of the box. /$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.explanation: Reference box [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax] used only when UseReferenceBounds is true; the box is then these bounds scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation and translated by Position, all about the coordinate origin, so Length [1, 1, 1], Rotation [0, 0, 0] and Position [0, 0, 0] reproduce Bounds exactly. Ignored otherwise.
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.label: Bounds
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1]; the XML marks it NoDefault, so it is not filled from the input bounds.
pitfalls: Setting Bounds alone has no effect; also set UseReferenceBounds to true.
Give each minimum before its maximum.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.explanation: An infinite flat plane through Origin, oriented by Normal (ParaView’s vtkPVPlane). It is the usual choice, and ParaView’s initial one for most operations that offer it: use it for planar cuts, clips or selections at any orientation. /$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.explanation: Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value.

A node created after its upstream has data therefore gets the data centre, whereas on a Schemaxis batch run (every node is created before any data exist) the bounds are unset and, by the source, the origin stays [0, 0, 0]. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.explanation: No geometric function: the clip is driven by the operation’s own scalar array instead (Scalars, with its Value and Invert settings). Point arrays are clipped through the data so cells are cut at the iso-value; cell arrays are thresholded, keeping or removing whole cells; hyper tree grids are thresholded. Choose it to clip by a field such as pressure or temperature rather than by a shape.
pitfalls: The geometric settings of other choices have no meaning here; set the operation’s Scalars array and Value instead.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.explanation: A sphere (vtkSphere) given by Center and Radius; its implicit function |x − Center|² − Radius² is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a spherical region, or to cut a spherical shell through the data, for example around a probe point or a body.

A sphere (vtkSphere) given by Center and Radius; its implicit function |x − Center|² − Radius² is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a spherical region, or to cut a spherical shell through the data, for example around a probe point or a body.

Centre and radius of the sphere. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values, which may be derived from the input bounds (centre of the bounds, about half the largest extent), so set both for reproducible results.
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/ClipTyp.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.label: Hyper Tree Grid Clipper

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.explanation: This property specifies the parameters of the clip function (an implicit description) used to clip the hyper tree grid.

An axis-aligned box used to clip a hyper tree grid. ParaView’s hyper-tree-grid clip reads only Position and Length from this box: it keeps or removes the region from Position to Position + Length along x, y and z. Choose it to cut a rectangular block out of a hyper tree grid; choose Plane, Sphere or Cylinder for other shapes.
pitfalls: Rotation, Bounds and UseReferenceBounds are accepted but ignored by the hyper-tree-grid clip.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 shared proxy implicit_functions/Axis Aligned Box

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.explanation: Extent of the clipping box. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.explanation: Any point [x, y, z] on the cylinder’s axis line. Moving it along Axis changes nothing; moving it sideways moves the cylinder.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.explanation: An infinite flat plane through Origin, oriented by Normal (ParaView’s vtkPVPlane). It is the usual choice, and ParaView’s initial one for most operations that offer it: use it for planar cuts, clips or selections at any orientation. Where offered, prefer Axis Aligned Plane when the plane must stay exactly perpendicular to x, y or z, and Box, Sphere or Cylinder when the region of interest is closed or curved.
pitfalls: The plane is unbounded: it cuts through every part of the dataset it crosses, including distant parts.

pitfalls: The plane is unbounded: it cuts through every part of the dataset it crosses, including distant parts.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.explanation: Position and orientation of the plane: Origin (a point on it), Normal (its orientation and positive side) and Offset (an extra shift along the normal). Origin and Normal decide the result; omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values, and Origin may be derived from the input bounds, so set both explicitly for reproducible results.
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.explanation: Position and orientation of the plane: Origin (a point on it), Normal (its orientation and positive side) and Offset (an extra shift along the normal). Origin and Normal decide the result; omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values, and Origin may be derived from the input bounds, so set both explicitly for reproducible results.
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.explanation: Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value.
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.label: Normal
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 0, 0], a plane perpendicular to the x axis.
pitfalls: A zero vector defines no plane; give at least one non-zero component.

Use a unit-length normal. A longer vector scales the implicit-function values (and the shift produced by Offset), which changes the meaning of value-based settings on the operation, such as slice offsets or a clip value, where the operation has them.
