/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.explanation: Moves the plane along its normal without changing Origin: the plane actually used passes through Origin + Offset × Normal. Positive values move it toward the side the normal points to.
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.label: Offset
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.units: Dataset coordinate units when Normal has unit length (the shift is Offset × |Normal|)
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 0 (no shift).
pitfalls: With a non-unit Normal the plane moves by Offset times the normal’s length, not by Offset.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.explanation: A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing.
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.label: Origin
/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial value (its static default is [0, 0, 0]; ParaView may instead derive it from the centre of the input’s bounding box). Set it explicitly when the result depends on it.
pitfalls: Coordinates are absolute, not fractions of the model: on a part spanning 0–2000 mm, [0.5, 0.5, 0.5] lies at a corner. Use the model’s own units.
Offset is added on top of Origin along Normal; keep Offset at 0 if Origin should be the exact plane position.

/$defs/options-pvClip/properties/HyperTr.explanation: No geometric function: the clip is driven by the operation’s own scalar array instead (Scalars, with its Value and Invert settings). Point arrays are clipped through the data so cells are cut at the iso-value; cell arrays are thresholded, keeping or removing whole cells; hyper tree grids are thresholded. Choose it to clip by a field such as pressure or temperature rather than by a shape.
pitfalls: The geometric settings of other choices have no meaning here; set the operation’s Scalars array and Value instead.

/$defs/options-pvClipClosedSurface/prope.label: Clipping Plane

/$defs/options-pvClipClosedSurface/prope.explanation: This property specifies the parameters of the clipping plane used to clip the polygonal data.

Position and orientation of the plane: Origin (a point on it), Normal (its orientation and positive side) and Offset (an extra shift along the normal). Origin and Normal decide the result; omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values, and Origin may be derived from the input bounds, so set both explicitly for reproducible results.
/$defs/options-pvClipClosedSurface/prope.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvClipClosedSurface/prope.explanation: Position and orientation of the plane: Origin (a point on it), Normal (its orientation and positive side) and Offset (an extra shift along the normal). Origin and Normal decide the result; omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values, and Origin may be derived from the input bounds, so set both explicitly for reproducible results.
/$defs/options-pvClipClosedSurface/prope.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvClipClosedSurface/prope.explanation: Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value.
/$defs/options-pvClipClosedSurface/prope.label: Normal
/$defs/options-pvClipClosedSurface/prope.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 0, 0], a plane perpendicular to the x axis.
pitfalls: A zero vector defines no plane; give at least one non-zero component.

Use a unit-length normal. A longer vector scales the implicit-function values (and the shift produced by Offset), which changes the meaning of value-based settings on the operation, such as slice offsets or a clip value, where the operation has them.

/$defs/options-pvClipClosedSurface/prope.explanation: A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing.
/$defs/options-pvClipClosedSurface/prope.label: Origin
/$defs/options-pvClipClosedSurface/prope.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial value (its static default is [0, 0, 0]; ParaView may instead derive it from the centre of the input’s bounding box). Set it explicitly when the result depends on it.
pitfalls: Coordinates are absolute, not fractions of the model: on a part spanning 0–2000 mm, [0.5, 0.5, 0.5] lies at a corner. Use the model’s own units.
Offset is added on top of Origin along Normal; keep Offset at 0 if Origin should be the exact plane position.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvCompositeDataIDSelectio.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvComputeSides.explanation: Choose which side dimensions are generated (SidestoInclude, ParaView default Next Lowest Dimension), whether input cells of dimension 2 or lower are kept in the output (PreserveRenderableInputs, default true) and whether sides are skipped for cells that are already renderable surfaces or edges (OmitSidesForRenderableInputs, default true).

/$defs/options-pvComputeSides/properties.explanation: Set this property to true to avoid generating sides for input cells or sides that can be rendered as they are. If false, then sides will be output even for cells/sides that are surfaces or edges. As an example, if an input has hexahedra and triangle cells, this filter will generate quadrilateral sides (for the hexahedra) and edge sides (for the triangles) if OmitSidesForRenderableInputs is true, but only quadrilateral sides (for the hexahedra) if OmitSidesForRenderableInputs is false. Note that this is independent of whether some input cells are preserved or not.
/$defs/options-pvComputeSides/properties.label: Omit Sides For Renderable Inputs

/$defs/options-pvComputeSides/properties.explanation: Set this property to true to avoid generating sides for input cells or sides that can be rendered as they are. Note that this is independent of whether some input cells are preserved or not.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvCone/properties/Capping.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvContingencyStatistics/p.explanation: Attribute association whose arrays are analysed; VariablesofInterest names are looked up in it. Chosen by the ParaView entry text: "Point Data", "Cell Data", "Vertex Data", "Edge Data", "Row Data" or "Field Data". /$defs/options-pvContingencyStatistics/p.explanation:
Specify the task to be performed: modeling and/or assessment.
  1. "Detailed model of input data," creates a set of output tables containing a calculated statistical model of the entire input dataset;
  2. "Model a subset of the data," creates an output table (or tables) summarizing a randomly-chosen subset of the input dataset;
  3. "Assess the data with a model," adds attributes to the first input dataset using a model provided on the second input port; and
  4. "Model and assess the same data," is really just operations 2 and 3 above applied to the same input dataset. The model is first trained using a fraction of the input data and then the entire dataset is assessed using that model.

You should avoid using a large fraction of the input data for training as you will then not be able to detect overfitting. The Training fraction setting will be ignored for tasks 1 and 3.

Not that if ComputeNormals is set to 1, then gradients will have to be calculated, but they will only be stored in the output dataset if ComputeGradients is also set to 1.

Uniform Binning (vtkMergePoints): merges output points whose coordinates are exactly identical, using a uniform grid of buckets, so vertices shared by neighbouring output cells appear once and the generated surface or line set is connected. It is ParaView’s initial choice and suits most data. Choose Octree Binning for very unevenly distributed points (strongly refined or adaptive meshes) and Not Merging Points only when speed matters more than connectivity.

/$defs/options-pvContour/properties/Poin.explanation: Number of buckets along x, y and z of the uniform search grid used to find coincident points. A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvContour/properties/Poin.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvContour/properties/Poin.explanation: Discriminator for this choice: the value "Not Merging Points" selects ParaView’s native incremental_point_locators/NonMergingPointLocator proxy (VTK class vtkNonMergingPointLocator), check-free point insertion that keeps duplicates. Schemaxis assigns this label to the native property, checks that ParaView resolved exactly that proxy, and only then applies the options you wrote.

/$defs/options-pvContour/properties/Redu.explanation: If checked, the filter will optimize the space allocated to store the contour values. /$defs/options-pvConvertIntoMolecule.explanation: AtomicNumbers names the point array giving each atom's element, and ConvertLinesIntoBonds (ParaView default true) decides whether line cells become bonds. AtomicNumbers has no static default (VTK falls back to the active point scalars), so name the array explicitly.

/$defs/options-pvConvertIntoMolecule/pro.explanation: This property indicates the name of the scalar array corresponding to atomic numbers.
/$defs/options-pvConvertIntoMolecule/pro.label: Atomic Numbers

/$defs/options-pvConvertIntoMolecule/pro.explanation: This property indicates the name of the scalar array corresponding to atomic numbers.

One entry of the [association, array name] pair for the atomic numbers: first the association token POINTS (atoms come from points, and the native domain accepts only one-component point arrays), then the array name, e.g. ["POINTS", "atomic_number"]. Order matters and both entries are required.
/$defs/options-pvConvertIntoMolecule/pro.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial array (VTK's own default is the active point scalars).
pitfalls: Writing only the array name fails validation; give the association first.

/$defs/options-pvConvertSelection.explanation: Choose the target selection type (OutputType) and, for VALUES or THRESHOLDS output, the DataInput arrays that describe it (ArrayNames); MatchAnyValues and AllowMissingArray decide how several arrays combine and whether a missing array is an error. Omitted settings keep ParaView's values: OutputType LOCATIONS (set it explicitly), no array names, both flags false.

/$defs/options-pvConvertSelection/proper.explanation: When true, an array the conversion needs but cannot find on DataInput (the array of a value or threshold input selection, or the pedigree-ID array for PEDIGREEIDS output) no longer makes the filter fail; it returns without error, possibly with an empty or partial selection. When false the native filter reports an error instead.
/$defs/options-pvConvertSelection/proper.label: Allow missing array
/$defs/options-pvConvertSelection/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from false.
pitfalls: True can hide a misspelled array name; check that the converted selection is not empty before relying on it.

/$defs/options-pvConvertSelection/proper.explanation: Names of DataInput arrays whose values at the selected elements form the new selection: one or more names for VALUES output, exactly one for THRESHOLDS. The arrays are looked up in the cell data, or in the point data when the input selection is point-based. Ignored for INDICES, GLOBALIDs and PEDIGREEIDS output.
/$defs/options-pvConvertSelection/proper.label: Array names
/$defs/options-pvConvertSelection/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts with an empty list.
pitfalls: With several names and MatchAnyValues false, all arrays go into one selection node and VTK's value selector matches only that node's first array; enable MatchAnyValues so each array is matched.

/$defs/options-pvD3.explanation: Settings: BoundaryMode, how cells crossing region boundaries are handled (ParaView default Assign cells uniquely; or Duplicate cells, Divide cells), MinimalMemory (default false) and MinimumNumberOfGhostLevels (default 0).

/$defs/options-pvD3/properties/BoundaryM.explanation: This property determines how cells that lie on processor boundaries are handled. The "Assign cells uniquely" option assigns each boundary cell to exactly one process, which is useful for isosurfacing. Selecting "Duplicate cells" causes the cells on the boundaries to be copied to each process that shares that boundary. The "Divide cells" option breaks cells across process boundary lines so that pieces of the cell lie in different processes. This option is useful for volume rendering.
/$defs/options-pvD3/properties/BoundaryM.label: Boundary Mode

/$defs/options-pvDecimatePolyline.explanation: TargetReduction (fraction of segments to remove, default 0.9), MaximumError (largest vertex error still allowed to be removed; default 1.79769e+308, effectively unlimited) and DecimationStrategy (default Decimation Distance Strategy), which defines the error. MaximumError is compared with the strategy's raw error without any scaling by the bounding box: a squared distance (dataset length units squared) for the distance strategy, a cosine between -1 and 1 for the angle strategy and an array difference for the custom-field strategy.

Error of each vertex = the cosine of the angle formed at it by its two neighbours: −1 where the line continues straight (removed first), rising toward +1 at sharp turns. Choose it to keep corners regardless of segment length; the operation’s maximum error is then a cosine between −1 and 1.

/$defs/options-pvDecimatePolyline/proper.explanation: Error of each vertex = the squared distance from the vertex to the infinite straight line through its two neighbours (vtkLine::DistanceToLine returns the distance squared), so nearly collinear vertices have the smallest error and are removed first. Choose it to simplify a curve within a geometric tolerance; the operation's MaximumError is then compared with this squared distance, in dataset length units squared, with no normalization by the bounding box.
pitfalls: To stop removing vertices farther than d from the chord, set MaximumError to d squared, not d: 0.01 for d = 0.1.

/$defs/options-pvDescriptiveStatistics/p.explanation:
Specify the task to be performed: modeling and/or assessment.
  1. "Detailed model of input data," creates a set of output tables containing a calculated statistical model of the entire input dataset;
  2. "Model a subset of the data," creates an output table (or tables) summarizing a randomly-chosen subset of the input dataset;
  3. "Assess the data with a model," adds attributes to the first input dataset using a model provided on the second input port; and
  4. "Model and assess the same data," is really just operations 2 and 3 above applied to the same input dataset. The model is first trained using a fraction of the input data and then the entire dataset is assessed using that model.
When the task includes creating a model (i.e., tasks 2, and 4), you may adjust the fraction of the input dataset used for training. You should avoid using a large fraction of the input data for training as you will then not be able to detect overfitting. The Training fraction setting will be ignored for tasks 1 and 3.
/$defs/options-pvDescriptiveStatistics/p.label: Task

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvEnzoReader/properties/C.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the fields in the file (there is no static default). Name the fields explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Field names are case-sensitive and must match the Enzo output exactly.

The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvExodusIIReader/properti.explanation: Use this property to select which blocks of elements (cells) should be loaded. All elements (cells) in the same block will have the same interpolant (tetrahedral, triangular, trilinear hexahedral, etc.) and have the same variables defined over them.

One element block to load: a group of cells of one element type, usually one material or part. Use the name stored in the file, or 'Unnamed block ID: n' when it has none (with UseLegacyBlockNamesWithElementTypes the element type is appended). Listing names loads exactly those blocks; by default every element block loads.

/$defs/options-pvExodusIIReader/properti.explanation: Specify which maps defined over elements (cells) in the mesh should be loaded. An element map is a renumbering of all the elements (across all the element blocks of a file) from their offset in the file to some arbitrary integers, usually specifying a unique global ID across a set of files. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per face. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. The corresponding set must also be loaded using the FaceSetArrayStatus property in order for the variable to appear.
One variable defined on face sets (one value per face of the set) to load. It appears only if the set itself is enabled in FaceSetArrayStatus.
One variable defined on face sets (one value per face of the set) to load. It appears only if the set itself is enabled in FaceSetArrayStatus.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvExodusIIReader/properti.explanation: This property specifies the file name for the Exodus reader.
/$defs/options-pvExodusIIReader/properti.label: File Name

/$defs/options-pvExodusIIReader/properti.explanation: Path of one Exodus II file (.e, .exo, .g, .ex2 …). Several names are read as a file series in time; a single name that is one piece of a spatially partitioned set (such as mesh.e.4.0) may be expanded by the reader to its sibling pieces. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; absolute paths avoid ambiguity. The value is a constructor option, so it must be a constant.

This property contains a text string specifying the pattern used to load files. There are two parts to it: the prefix (%s) and the file number (%i). The format used is the same as that used for printf.
/$defs/options-pvExodusIIReader/properti.label: File Pattern

/$defs/options-pvExodusIIReader/properti.explanation: This property specifies the file root used with the file pattern to format a file name. (See the File Pattern property).

/$defs/options-pvExodusIIReader/properti.explanation: This property controls the indices of the first and last files to be read.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvExodusIIReader/properti.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvExodusIIReader/properti.explanation: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the nodes (points) in a file as sets in their own right. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per node. This property specifies which of those sets should be loaded. The accompanying NodeSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.

/$defs/options-pvExodusIIReader/properti.explanation: An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the of all the elements in a file as sets in their own right. This property specifies which of those sets should be loaded. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per side. For example, a hexahedron has 18 sides: 6 faces and 12 edges. Any of these sides may be individually called out in a set and assigned a result value. The accompanying SideSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.

/$defs/options-pvExtractAMRBlocks/proper.explanation: Specify a pair, level and dataset index, for every dataset from the input AMR dataset to extract.

pitfalls: Pairs must be complete; a trailing level without an index is rejected.

/$defs/options-pvExtractCTHParts/propert.explanation: An infinite flat plane through Origin, oriented by Normal (ParaView’s vtkPVPlane). It is the usual choice, and ParaView’s initial one for most operations that offer it: use it for planar cuts, clips or selections at any orientation. Where offered, prefer Axis Aligned Plane when the plane must stay exactly perpendicular to x, y or z, and Box, Sphere or Cylinder when the region of interest is closed or curved.
pitfalls: The plane is unbounded: it cuts through every part of the dataset it crosses, including distant parts.

/$defs/options-pvExtractCTHParts/propert.explanation: Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value.
/$defs/options-pvExtractCTHParts/propert.label: Normal
/$defs/options-pvExtractCTHParts/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 0, 0], a plane perpendicular to the x axis.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

A rectangular box region (ParaView’s vtkPVBox): a unit cube scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation about its minimum corner and moved to Position, or, with UseReferenceBounds, the Bounds box transformed in the same way. The implicit function is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a box-shaped region; slicing or cutting with a box produces the box faces where they cross the data.
pitfalls: ParaView’s initial box may be a unit cube at the origin if the input bounds were not applied; set Position and Length explicitly.

/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.explanation: Placement and size of the box. In the normal mode Position (minimum corner), Length (edge lengths) and Rotation define it; with UseReferenceBounds true, Bounds defines the box and the other three act relative to it. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values, which may cover the whole input.
/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.explanation: An infinite flat plane through Origin, oriented by Normal (ParaView’s vtkPVPlane). It is the usual choice, and ParaView’s initial one for most operations that offer it: use it for planar cuts, clips or selections at any orientation. Where offered, prefer Axis Aligned Plane when the plane must stay exactly perpendicular to x, y or z, and Box, Sphere or Cylinder when the region of interest is closed or curved.
pitfalls: The plane is unbounded: it cuts through every part of the dataset it crosses, including distant parts.

/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.explanation: Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.explanation: Moves the plane along its normal without changing Origin: the plane actually used passes through Origin + Offset × Normal. Positive values move it toward the side the normal points to.
/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.label: Offset
/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.units: Dataset coordinate units when Normal has unit length (the shift is Offset × |Normal|)
/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 0 (no shift).
pitfalls: With a non-unit Normal the plane moves by Offset times the normal’s length, not by Offset.

/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.explanation: A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing.
/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.label: Origin
/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial value (its static default is [0, 0, 0]; ParaView may instead derive it from the centre of the input’s bounding box). Set it explicitly when the result depends on it.
pitfalls: Coordinates are absolute, not fractions of the model: on a part spanning 0–2000 mm, [0.5, 0.5, 0.5] lies at a corner. Use the model’s own units.
Offset is added on top of Origin along Normal; keep Offset at 0 if Origin should be the exact plane position.

/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.explanation: A sphere (vtkSphere) given by Center and Radius; its implicit function |x − Center|² − Radius² is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a spherical region, or to cut a spherical shell through the data, for example around a probe point or a body.

A sphere (vtkSphere) given by Center and Radius; its implicit function |x − Center|² − Radius² is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a spherical region, or to cut a spherical shell through the data, for example around a probe point or a body.

Centre and radius of the sphere. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values, which may be derived from the input bounds (centre of the bounds, about half the largest extent), so set both for reproducible results.
/$defs/options-pvExtractCellsByRegion/pr.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvExtractComponent/proper.label: Runtime value

Otherwise, the point indices are used.

/$defs/options-pvExtractRegionSurface/pr.explanation: If the input is an unstructured grid with nonlinear faces, this parameter determines how many times the face is subdivided into linear faces. If 0, the output is the equivalent of its linear counterpart (and the midpoints determining the nonlinear interpolation are discarded). If 1, the nonlinear face is triangulated based on the midpoints. If greater than 1, the triangulated pieces are recursively subdivided to reach the desired subdivision. Setting the value to greater than 1 may cause some point data to not be passed even if no quadratic faces exist. This option has no effect if the input is not an unstructured grid.
/$defs/options-pvExtractRegionSurface/pr.label: Nonlinear Subdivision Level

/$defs/options-pvExtractRegionSurface/pr.explanation: If the input is an unstructured grid with nonlinear faces, this parameter determines how many times the face is subdivided into linear faces. If 0, the output is the equivalent of its linear counterpart (and the midpoints determining the nonlinear interpolation are discarded). If 1, the nonlinear face is triangulated based on the midpoints. If greater than 1, the triangulated pieces are recursively subdivided to reach the desired subdivision. Setting the value to greater than 1 may cause some point data to not be passed even if no quadratic faces exist. This option has no effect if the input is not an unstructured grid.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvExtractSurface/properti.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvExtractSurface/properti.explanation: If the input is an unstructured grid with nonlinear faces, this parameter determines how many times the face is subdivided into linear faces. If 0, the output is the equivalent of its linear counterpart (and the midpoints determining the nonlinear interpolation are discarded). If 1, the nonlinear face is triangulated based on the midpoints. If greater than 1, the triangulated pieces are recursively subdivided to reach the desired subdivision. Setting the value to greater than 1 may cause some point data to not be passed even if no quadratic faces exist. This option has no effect if the input is not an unstructured grid.
/$defs/options-pvExtractSurface/properti.label: Nonlinear Subdivision Level

/$defs/options-pvFDSReader/properties/As.label: Assembly Selectors

/$defs/options-pvFDSReader/properties/As.explanation: Specify the selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to extract from the input dataset.

One path expression into the reader's data assembly. The root node is named after the .smv file (without extension) and has the children Grids, Devices, HRR, Slices and Boundaries, each holding named datasets; "/" selects everything and "//Slices" all slices. Several selectors are combined and their order does not matter.
pitfalls: Node names are made valid by vtkDataAssembly (e.g. spaces replaced), so they may differ slightly from the names in the .smv file.

/$defs/options-pvFLASHAMRParticlesReader.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

/$defs/options-pvFastUniformGrid/propert.explanation: The six values in the property indicate the X, Y, and Z extent of the output data. The numbers are inclusive, so values of -10, 10, -10, 10, =10, 10 indicate that the dimensions of the output will be 21 x 21 x 21.
One inclusive index bound of the extent; the six entries are [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax]. Each axis has max - min + 1 points, so [-10, 10] gives 21.
/$defs/options-pvFastUniformGrid/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [-10, 10, -10, 10, -10, 10].
pitfalls: Each max must be at least its min; the point count grows with the product of the three ranges, so large extents use memory quickly.

/$defs/options-pvFidesJSONReader.explanation: FileName (required) is the JSON data model. DataSourcePath maps each data-source name to its BP file or stream, DataSourceEngines optionally sets the ADIOS2 engine per source, and the array lists choose the fields. /$defs/options-pvFlashReader.explanation: Settings choose the FLASH file(s) (required), the cell arrays to load, the finest refinement Level (ParaView default 1) and EnableCaching (default false), which keeps loaded blocks in memory for faster re-reading. VTK's AMR readers start with every array disabled, so the cell-array list matters most: omit it and the output carries the block structure without fields.

/$defs/options-pvFlashReader/properties/.explanation: Names of the cell-centred variables to load from the FLASH file, such as density or pressure fields. Listing names loads exactly those arrays and disables every other array the file offers; an empty list loads none. Fewer arrays mean less memory and faster reads.
/$defs/options-pvFlashReader/properties/.label: Cell arrays
/$defs/options-pvFlashReader/properties/.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView takes the initial selection from the reader, and VTK's AMR readers start with every array disabled, so omitting this usually loads no fields. Name the arrays explicitly.
pitfalls: Names must match the variable names stored in the file exactly; a misspelt name yields no array.

/$defs/options-pvForceStaticMesh.explanation: No options. ParaView's ForceCacheComputation property is not exposed: it has no elements, so invoking it sends no message, and assigning it pushes the XML command SetCacheComputation, which vtkForceStaticMesh lacks (it has SetForceCacheComputation) and which aborts the native process. Neither a setting nor an onVisit command can force the cache to recompute (it is listed in coverage.gaps).

If any of the (min,max) bounds values are min >= max, then the bounds will be computed automatically from the input data. Otherwise, the user-specified bounds will be used.
/$defs/options-pvGaussianResampling/prop.label: Extent to Resample

/$defs/options-pvGaussianResampling/prop.explanation: Set / get the (xmin,xmax, ymin,ymax, zmin,zmax) bounding box in which the sampling is performed. If any of the (min,max) bounds values are min >= max, then the bounds will be computed automatically from the input data. Otherwise, the user-specified bounds will be used.

One bound of the box in which the volume is built, in the order xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax. If any min is not smaller than its max, the box is instead computed from the input bounds, enlarged so that splats near the edge fit.
/$defs/options-pvGaussianResampling/prop.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from all zeros, which means automatic bounds.
pitfalls: The splat radius is a fraction of this box's longest side, so enlarging the box also enlarges every splat.

/$defs/options-pvGaussianResampling/prop.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvGaussianResampling/prop.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvGaussianResampling/prop.explanation: Choose a scalar array to splat into the output cells. If ignore arrays is chosen, point density will be counted instead.

pitfalls: If the named array is absent VTK falls back to the active point scalars; check the array name when the result looks like a plain density.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvGenerateIds/properties/.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvGenerateSpatioTemporalH.explanation: Same setting as pvSpatioTemporalHarmonics: Harmonics, groups of six numbers per summed wave; omitted, ParaView's four example harmonics are used.

This property defines the harmonics that will be computed and summed on each point. Default values are only example values, that would make sense for a dataset of geometrical bounds [-10,10,-10,10,-10,10] and time values greater than or equal to 0 and less than 2*Pi.
/$defs/options-pvGenerateSpatioTemporalH.label: Harmonics

/$defs/options-pvGenerateSpatioTemporalH.explanation: This property defines the harmonics that will be computed and summed on each point. Default values are only example values, that would make sense for a dataset of geometrical bounds [-10,10,-10,10,-10,10] and time values greater than or equal to 0 and less than 2*Pi.

One number of the flat Harmonics list, read in groups of six per harmonic: amplitude A, temporal frequency ω, wave-vector components kx, ky, kz, and phase φ (radians), so the list length must be a multiple of 6. For example [1, 1, 0.6283, 0, 0, 0] is one wave of unit amplitude travelling along x.
pitfalls: A list whose length is not a multiple of 6 shifts every later parameter; write harmonics as complete groups of six.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvGlyph/properties/GlyphT.explanation: The values in this property allow you to specify the transform (translation, rotation, and scaling) to apply to the glyph source.

Transform applied to the glyph shape in its own local coordinates before the operation scales it, turns its x axis onto the orientation vector and places it at each point; within it, points are scaled, then rotated, then translated. Use it to reorient or offset glyphs, for example to make a y-axis shape follow the vectors. Omitted settings keep the identity (no change).
sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/paraview/paraview/-/blob/v5.13.3/VTKExtensions/FiltersGeneral/vtkPVGlyphFilter.cxx (source transform, then scale, x axis rotated onto the orientation vector, then translate)
/$defs/options-pvGlyph/properties/GlyphT.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvGlyph/properties/GlyphT.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvGlyph/properties/GlyphT.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvGlyph/properties/GlyphT.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvGlyph/properties/GlyphT.explanation: A polygonal cylinder of Radius and Height centred at Center, with its axis along its own local y axis. Glyph and Tensor Glyph orient glyphs by their local x axis (Tensor Glyph also maps y to the medium eigenvector), so the cylinder axis does not follow the vector or major eigenvector unless the shape is rotated.
pitfalls: In Glyph, rotate the shape with GlyphTransform (for example Rotate [0, 0, 90]) if the cylinders should lie along the vectors.
sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/paraview/paraview/-/blob/v5.13.3/VTKExtensions/FiltersGeneral/vtkPVGlyphFilter.cxx (source transform, then scale, x axis rotated onto the orientation vector, then translate)

/$defs/options-pvGlyph/properties/ScaleA.explanation: Select the input array to be used for scaling the glyphs. If the scale array is a vector array, you can control how the glyphs are scaled with the **Vector Scale Mode** property.

One entry of the [association, array name] pair for the scale array: POINTS or CELLS, then a 1- or 3-component array, e.g. ["POINTS", "p"]; glyph size is the array value (or vector magnitude or components, per VectorScaleMode) times ScaleFactor. Use ["POINTS", "No scale array"] for uniform size.
/$defs/options-pvGlyph/properties/ScaleA.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial array from the input (the XML value 0 is an internal index, not an array name). Name it explicitly.
pitfalls: Scaling multiplies by raw data values; with large values reduce ScaleFactor, e.g. to the cell size divided by the largest value.

Transform applied to the glyph shape in its own local coordinates before the operation scales it, turns its x axis onto the orientation vector and places it at each point; within it, points are scaled, then rotated, then translated. Use it to reorient or offset glyphs, for example to make a y-axis shape follow the vectors. Omitted settings keep the identity (no change).

/$defs/options-pvGlyphWithCustomSource/p.explanation: Select the input array to be used for scaling the glyphs. If the scale array is a vector array, you can control how the glyphs are scaled with the **Vector Scale Mode** property.

One entry of the [association, array name] pair for the scale array: POINTS or CELLS, then a 1- or 3-component array, e.g. ["POINTS", "p"]; glyph size is the array value (or vector magnitude or components, per VectorScaleMode) times ScaleFactor. Use ["POINTS", "No scale array"] for uniform size.
/$defs/options-pvGlyphWithCustomSource/p.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial array from the input (the XML value 0 is an internal index, not an array name). Name it explicitly.
pitfalls: Scaling multiplies by raw data values; with large values reduce ScaleFactor, e.g. to the cell size divided by the largest value.

/$defs/options-pvGradient/properties/Bou.explanation: Specify how to compute the gradient on the boundaries. 'Smoothed' uses central differencing by duplicating the boundary values to compute the gradient on the boundary elements (corresponds to the old 'Gradient' filter). 'Non-Smoothed' uses forward/backward differencing with the values of a boundary element and its neighbor to compute the gradient (corresponds to the old 'Gradient Of Unstructured DataSet' filter).

/$defs/options-pvH5PartReader/properties.explanation: Path of the H5Part file; all time steps are stored inside it, so one file gives the whole time series. A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvH5PartReader/properties.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvHierarchicalDataIDSelec.explanation: The list of IDs that will be added to the selection produced by the selection source. This takes 3-tuple of values as (level, index, id).

One number of a flat list read in triples (level, index, id): the zero-based AMR level, the zero-based dataset index within that level, then the zero-based point or cell index in that dataset. For example [0, 2, 15] selects element 15 of box 2 on level 0.
pitfalls: Triple order is fixed; putting the element index first selects a different box or nothing.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvHierarchicalFractal/pro.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvHistogram2D/properties/.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvHistogram2D/properties/.label: Runtime value

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvHyperTreeGrid/propertie.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvHyperTreeGridAxisReflec.explanation: PlaneNormal chooses the mirror axis (X Axis, Y Axis or Z Axis) and PlanePosition the plane's coordinate on that axis (ParaView default 0.0, dataset units). If PlaneNormal is omitted ParaView reads back "X Axis" (a bounded native probe), so by the source the grid is mirrored about x = PlanePosition (0 unless set).
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 VTK/Filters/HyperTree/vtkHyperTreeGridAxisReflection.cxx:116-119,181 (offset = 2 * Center for the plane choices; reflected coordinates decrease)

/$defs/options-pvHyperTreeGridAxisReflec.explanation: Axis perpendicular to the mirror plane: X Axis mirrors x coordinates about x = PlanePosition, and Y Axis and Z Axis do the same for y and z.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 VTK/Filters/HyperTree/vtkHyperTreeGridAxisReflection.cxx:116-119,181 (offset = 2 * Center for the plane choices; reflected coordinates decrease)
/$defs/options-pvHyperTreeGridAxisReflec.label: Plane normal
/$defs/options-pvHyperTreeGridAxisReflec.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; a bounded native probe read PlaneNormal back as "X Axis" (6) and PlanePosition as 0 when the node was created, before and after the upstream had data. VTK then mirrors about x = PlanePosition (by the source, not observed: the probe did not obtain valid output bounds), not about the grid's minimum-x face.
pitfalls: Omitted, PlaneNormal reads back "X Axis", so the mirror plane is perpendicular to x; set PlaneNormal to "Y Axis" or "Z Axis" to mirror about y or z.

/$defs/options-pvHyperTreeGridRandom.explanation: Root grid size (Dimensions, ParaView default [6, 6, 3]) and extent (OutputBounds, -10 to 10 on each axis), random seed (0), maximum depth (5), split probability (0.5) and masked fraction (0).

/$defs/options-pvHyperTreeGridRandom/pro.explanation: Grid size as [nx, ny, nz]. VTK's vtkRandomHyperTreeGridSource interprets these as numbers of points per axis, so there are (n - 1) root trees along each axis: the default [6, 6, 3] gives 5 × 5 × 2 roots. The native documentation's "number of root cells" wording is off by one.

pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvIOSSCellGridReader/prop.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvIOSSCellGridReader/prop.explanation: Path of one IOSS database file (ParaView registers .exdg, Exodus discontinuous-Galerkin output, for this reader). With ScanForRelatedFiles on (default) partitions and restart files are found by naming convention. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; the value is passed when the node is created and must be a constant.
To limit reading a subset of files in spatial file-series, specify a valid range. You may also use **FileStride** to step over files in this range.
/$defs/options-pvIOSSCellGridReader/prop.label: File Range

/$defs/options-pvIOSSCellGridReader/prop.explanation: To limit reading a subset of files in spatial file-series, specify a valid range. You may also use **FileStride** to step over files in this range.

One bound of the range of spatial partitions read, as zero-based partition ranks (the r in name.e.N.r): the first value is the first rank read and the second is one past the last (exclusive), stepped by FileStride. When the first is not less than the second, range and stride are ignored and every partition is read.
/$defs/options-pvIOSSCellGridReader/prop.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, -1], an empty range that reads all partitions.
pitfalls: To read partitions 0 to 3 give [0, 4], not [0, 3].

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvIOSSCellGridReader/prop.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvIOSSReader.explanation: Settings choose which blocks, sets and fields are read (by name or assembly selector), how partitioned and restart files are discovered and limited, displacement handling, merging of Exodus blocks, ids, global fields and QA records, caching and field-name grouping. Omitted settings keep ParaView's values: all blocks with all fields, no sets, displacements applied at scale 1, related files scanned and all partitions read.

/$defs/options-pvIOSSReader/properties/A.explanation: Geometric locations can include displacements. When this option is on, the nodal positions are 'displaced' by the standard EXODUS displacement vector. If displacements are turned 'off', the user can explicitly add them by applying a warp filter.
/$defs/options-pvIOSSReader/properties/A.label: Apply Displacements

/$defs/options-pvIOSSReader/properties/F.explanation: Path of one Exodus II or CGNS file (IOSS database). For a spatially partitioned database name one piece (e.g. can.e.4.0): with ScanForRelatedFiles on (default) the other partitions and restart files (-s.001, …) are found by naming convention. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; the value is passed when the node is created and must be a constant.
To limit reading a subset of files in spatial file-series, specify a valid range. You may also use **FileStride** to step over files in this range.
/$defs/options-pvIOSSReader/properties/F.label: File Range

/$defs/options-pvIOSSReader/properties/F.explanation: To limit reading a subset of files in spatial file-series, specify a valid range. You may also use **FileStride** to step over files in this range.

One bound of the range of spatial partitions read, as zero-based partition ranks (the r in name.e.N.r): the first value is the first rank read and the second is one past the last (exclusive), stepped by FileStride. When the first is not less than the second, range and stride are ignored and every partition is read.
/$defs/options-pvIOSSReader/properties/F.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, -1], an empty range that reads all partitions.
pitfalls: To read partitions 0 to 3 give [0, 4], not [0, 3].

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvIOSSReader/properties/N.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvIOSSReader/properties/R.explanation: When set to true (default), the reader will read all files to determine structure of the dataset because some files might have certain blocks that other files don't have. A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvImageDataToAMR/properti.label: Runtime value

The value is a constructor option, so it must be a constant.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
