Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvInSituParticlePath/prop.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvInSituParticlePath/prop.explanation: Setting TerminationTime to a positive value will cause particles to terminate when the time is reached. The units of time should be consistent with the primary time variable.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments.explanation: One setting, SliceType, chooses the intersecting surface (Plane, Box or Sphere) and its parameters; omitted, ParaView starts from a Plane whose placement may depend on the input bounds, so set it explicitly.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: This property sets the type of intersecting geometry, and associated parameters.
/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.label: Slice Type

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: This property sets the type of intersecting geometry, and associated parameters.

A rectangular box region (ParaView’s vtkPVBox): a unit cube scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation about its minimum corner and moved to Position, or, with UseReferenceBounds, the Bounds box transformed in the same way. The implicit function is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a box-shaped region; slicing or cutting with a box produces the box faces where they cross the data.
pitfalls: ParaView’s initial box may be a unit cube at the origin if the input bounds were not applied; set Position and Length explicitly.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: A rectangular box region (ParaView’s vtkPVBox): a unit cube scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation about its minimum corner and moved to Position, or, with UseReferenceBounds, the Bounds box transformed in the same way. The implicit function is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a box-shaped region; slicing or cutting with a box produces the box faces where they cross the data.
pitfalls: ParaView’s initial box may be a unit cube at the origin if the input bounds were not applied; set Position and Length explicitly.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: Placement and size of the box. In the normal mode Position (minimum corner), Length (edge lengths) and Rotation define it; with UseReferenceBounds true, Bounds defines the box and the other three act relative to it. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values, which may cover the whole input.
/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: Reference box [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax] used only when UseReferenceBounds is true; the box is then these bounds scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation and translated by Position, all about the coordinate origin, so Length [1, 1, 1], Rotation [0, 0, 0] and Position [0, 0, 0] reproduce Bounds exactly. Ignored otherwise.
/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.label: Bounds
/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1]; the XML marks it NoDefault, so it is not filled from the input bounds.
pitfalls: Setting Bounds alone has no effect; also set UseReferenceBounds to true.
Give each minimum before its maximum.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: An infinite flat plane through Origin, oriented by Normal (ParaView’s vtkPVPlane). It is the usual choice, and ParaView’s initial one for most operations that offer it: use it for planar cuts, clips or selections at any orientation. Where offered, prefer Axis Aligned Plane when the plane must stay exactly perpendicular to x, y or z, and Box, Sphere or Cylinder when the region of interest is closed or curved.
pitfalls: The plane is unbounded: it cuts through every part of the dataset it crosses, including distant parts.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: Position and orientation of the plane: Origin (a point on it), Normal (its orientation and positive side) and Offset (an extra shift along the normal). Origin and Normal decide the result; omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values, and Origin may be derived from the input bounds, so set both explicitly for reproducible results.
/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value.
/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.label: Normal
/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 0, 0], a plane perpendicular to the x axis.
pitfalls: A zero vector defines no plane; give at least one non-zero component.

Use a unit-length normal. A longer vector scales the implicit-function values (and the shift produced by Offset), which changes the meaning of value-based settings on the operation, such as slice offsets or a clip value, where the operation has them.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: Moves the plane along its normal without changing Origin: the plane actually used passes through Origin + Offset × Normal. Positive values move it toward the side the normal points to.
/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.label: Offset
/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.units: Dataset coordinate units when Normal has unit length (the shift is Offset × |Normal|)

pitfalls: With a non-unit Normal the plane moves by Offset times the normal’s length, not by Offset.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: A point the plane passes through, as [x, y, z] in the input’s own coordinates. With Normal it defines the infinite plane Normal·(x − Origin) = 0 used to clip, slice, cut or select. Moving Origin along the normal shifts the plane; moving it within the plane changes nothing.
/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.label: Origin
/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial value (its static default is [0, 0, 0]; ParaView may instead derive it from the centre of the input’s bounding box). Set it explicitly when the result depends on it.
pitfalls: Coordinates are absolute, not fractions of the model: on a part spanning 0–2000 mm, [0.5, 0.5, 0.5] lies at a corner. Use the model’s own units.
Offset is added on top of Origin along Normal; keep Offset at 0 if Origin should be the exact plane position.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: A sphere (vtkSphere) given by Center and Radius; its implicit function |x − Center|² − Radius² is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a spherical region, or to cut a spherical shell through the data, for example around a probe point or a body.

A sphere (vtkSphere) given by Center and Radius; its implicit function |x − Center|² − Radius² is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a spherical region, or to cut a spherical shell through the data, for example around a probe point or a body.

/$defs/options-pvIntersectFragments/prop.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvJPEGSeriesReader/proper.explanation: Path of one JPEG file. With ReadAsImageStack true (ParaView's default for this reader) the files become z slices in list order and must share width, height and pixel type; with it false each file is one time step. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; absolute paths avoid ambiguity. The value is a constructor option, so it must be a constant.
When set, the reader will read the set of files as an image stack, rather than a temporal file series.

/$defs/options-pvKMeans/properties/Task.explanation:
Specify the task to be performed: modeling and/or assessment.
  1. "Detailed model of input data," creates a set of output tables containing a calculated statistical model of the entire input dataset;
  2. "Model a subset of the data," creates an output table (or tables) summarizing a randomly-chosen subset of the input dataset;
  3. "Assess the data with a model," adds attributes to the first input dataset using a model provided on the second input port; and
  4. "Model and assess the same data," is really just operations 2 and 3 above applied to the same input dataset. The model is first trained using a fraction of the input data and then the entire dataset is assessed using that model.
When the task includes creating a model (i.e., tasks 2, and 4), you may adjust the fraction of the input dataset used for training. You should avoid using a large fraction of the input data for training as you will then not be able to detect overfitting. The Training fraction setting will be ignored for tasks 1 and 3.
/$defs/options-pvKMeans/properties/Task.label: Task

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvKMeans/properties/Toler.label: Runtime value

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvLSDynaReader.explanation: FileName (required) names the d3plot file; the array-status lists choose which parts and which nodal, solid, shell, thick-shell, beam, particle (SPH), rigid-body and road-surface arrays are read; DeformedMesh and RemoveDeletedCells control displacement and erosion. /$defs/options-pvLSDynaReader/properties.explanation: When true, the output point coordinates are replaced by the deflected (current) coordinates at each time step, so the mesh moves with the solution; when false the mesh stays in its original position. pitfalls: If PointArrays omits "Deflected Coordinates", the mesh never moves even with this set to true.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvLinearCellExtrusion/pro.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvLinearCellExtrusion/pro.explanation: Set the custom extrusion direction.
/$defs/options-pvLinearCellExtrusion/pro.label: User Vector

/$defs/options-pvLinearCellExtrusion/pro.explanation: Set the custom extrusion direction.

One component of the extrusion direction, in order x, y, z, used when UseUserVector is true. The vector is not normalized: displacement = cell value × ScaleFactor × UserVector, so its length scales the extrusion.
sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/vtk/vtk/-/raw/master/Filters/Modeling/vtkLinearCellExtrusionFilter.cxx (RequestData: scale * normal, UserVector used as is)
/$defs/options-pvLinearCellExtrusion/pro.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 1].

/$defs/options-pvLinearExtrusion.explanation: Vector (ParaView default [0, 0, 1]) gives the sweep direction and ScaleFactor (default 1) the distance as a multiple of its length; Capping (default true) adds end faces and PieceInvariant (default false) removes internal faces at MPI piece boundaries.

/$defs/options-pvLinearExtrusion/propert.explanation: The value of this property indicates whether to cap the ends of the swept surface. Capping works by placing a copy of the input dataset on either end of the swept surface, so it behaves properly if the input is a 2D surface composed of filled polygons. If the input dataset is a closed solid (e.g., a sphere), then if capping is on (i.e., this property is set to 1), two copies of the data set will be displayed on output (the second translated from the first one along the specified vector). If instead capping is off (i.e., this property is set to 0), then an input closed solid will produce no output.

/$defs/options-pvLinearExtrusion/propert.explanation: The value of this property determines whether the output will be the same regardless of the number of processors used to compute the result. /$defs/options-pvLocationSelectionSource.explanation: Locations holds x, y, z triples; the shared selection settings choose cells or points (FieldType, ParaView default CELL), inversion, connected layers and containing cells. Omitted, the list is empty and nothing is selected.

When field type is POINT, this controls whether single vertex cells will be produced for each selected point, or whether the cells that contain each selected point will be produced. When field type is CELL this has no effect.

By default, the real component of C (represented by 0) is mapped to the X axis; the imaginary component of C (represented by 1) is mapped to the Y axis; and the real component of X, the initial value (represented by 2) is mapped to the Z axis. The imaginary component of X is represented by 3. All values entered must be between 0 and 3, inclusive.

The imaginary component of X is represented by 3. All values entered must be between 0 and 3, inclusive.
Which parameter is mapped to one image axis (x, then y, then z): 0 = C real, 1 = C imaginary, 2 = X real, 3 = X imaginary. Valid values are 0 to 3 and the three entries should differ.

pitfalls: Schemaxis rejects values outside 0 to 3 before execution (the native source fails its update for them); it does not check that the three entries differ.

/$defs/options-pvMaskPoints/properties/R.explanation: Randomized Id Strides picks points with random id increments starting at Offset (the output probably isn't a statistically random sample). Random Sampling generates a statistically random sample of the input, ignoring Offset (fast - O(sample size)). Spatially Stratified Random Sampling is a variant of random sampling that splits the points into equal sized spatial strata before randomly sampling (slow - O(N log N)). The Uniform Spatial Distribution (Bound based) samples points using random poisitions inside the bounds of the data set and a point locator. The Uniform Spatial Distribution (Surface Sampling) samples points randomly via an inverse transform on surface area of each cell (3D cells are ignored). The Uniform Spatial Distribution (Volume Sampling) samples points randomly sampled via an inverse transform on volume area of each cell (2D cells are ignored).

/$defs/options-pvMaterialInterfaceFilter.explanation: An infinite flat plane through Origin, oriented by Normal (ParaView’s vtkPVPlane). It is the usual choice, and ParaView’s initial one for most operations that offer it: use it for planar cuts, clips or selections at any orientation. Where offered, prefer Axis Aligned Plane when the plane must stay exactly perpendicular to x, y or z, and Box, Sphere or Cylinder when the region of interest is closed or curved.
pitfalls: The plane is unbounded: it cuts through every part of the dataset it crosses, including distant parts.

/$defs/options-pvMaterialInterfaceFilter.explanation: Position and orientation of the plane: Origin (a point on it), Normal (its orientation and positive side) and Offset (an extra shift along the normal). Origin and Normal decide the result; omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values, and Origin may be derived from the input bounds, so set both explicitly for reproducible results.
/$defs/options-pvMaterialInterfaceFilter.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvMaterialInterfaceFilter.explanation: Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. It orients the plane and defines its positive side: points toward which the normal points have positive implicit-function values Normal·(x − Origin), points on the other side negative; clip and extract operations use this sign to decide which side to keep. VTK does not normalize the vector, so its length scales the function value.
/$defs/options-pvMaterialInterfaceFilter.label: Normal
/$defs/options-pvMaterialInterfaceFilter.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 0, 0], a plane perpendicular to the x axis.
pitfalls: A zero vector defines no plane; give at least one non-zero component.

Use a unit-length normal. A longer vector scales the implicit-function values (and the shift produced by Offset), which changes the meaning of value-based settings on the operation, such as slice offsets or a clip value, where the operation has them.

A sphere (vtkSphere) given by Center and Radius; its implicit function |x − Center|² − Radius² is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a spherical region, or to cut a spherical shell through the data, for example around a probe point or a body.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvMaterialInterfaceFilter.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvMaterialInterfaceFilter.explanation: Mass arrays are paired with material fraction arrays. This means that the first selected material fraction array is paired with the first selected mass array, and so on sequentially. As the filter identifies voxels meeting the minimum material fraction threshold, these voxel's mass will be used in fragment center of mass and mass calculation. A warning is generated if no mass array is selected for an individual material fraction array. However, in that case the filter will run without issue because the statistics output can be generated using fragments' centers computed from axis aligned bounding boxes.
/$defs/options-pvMaterialInterfaceFilter.label: Select Mass Arrays

Name of one float or double cell mass array. The n-th mass array is paired with the n-th material fraction array and used for that material's fragment mass and centre of mass.
pitfalls: Order matters: list masses in the same order as SelectMaterialFractionArrays. Without a mass array, centres come from axis-aligned bounding boxes.

/$defs/options-pvMedian.explanation: Choose the array to filter (SelectInputScalars) and the neighbourhood size per axis (KernelSize, ParaView default [1, 1, 1], i.e. no filtering). Name the array explicitly; ParaView otherwise chooses it.

/$defs/options-pvMedian/properties/Kerne.explanation: The value of this property specifies the number of pixels/voxels in each dimension to use in computing the median to assign to each pixel/voxel. If the kernel size in a particular dimension is 1, then the median will not be computed in that direction.
/$defs/options-pvMedian/properties/Kerne.label: Kernel Size

/$defs/options-pvMedian/properties/Kerne.explanation: The value of this property specifies the number of pixels/voxels in each dimension to use in computing the median to assign to each pixel/voxel. If the kernel size in a particular dimension is 1, then the median will not be computed in that direction.
Neighbourhood width along one image axis (x, y, then z), in pixels; 1 means no filtering along that axis. Larger kernels remove larger blemishes but erode thin features.
/$defs/options-pvMedian/properties/Kerne.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 1, 1].

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvMergeVectorComponents.explanation: AttributeType (association by name, ParaView picks it from the input, usually "Point Data", or "Cell Data" and so on) selects the association, XArray, YArray and ZArray name the components, and OutputVectorName names the result (default "Vector"). ParaView picks the initial component arrays from the data, so name all three.

/$defs/options-pvMergeVectorComponents/p.explanation: Association of the three component arrays and of the merged vector array. Chosen by the ParaView entry text: "Point Data", "Cell Data", "Vertex Data", "Edge Data" or "Row Data". ParaView offers only the associations the connected input has (for example "Row Data" for a table), so a text it does not offer fails with NATIVE_DOMAIN_MISMATCH when the node is configured.

/$defs/options-pvMetaFileSeriesReader.explanation: Only FileNames (required) is exposed; everything else comes from the MetaImage headers.

/$defs/options-pvMetaFileSeriesReader/pr.explanation: The list of files to be read by the reader. Each file is expected to be in the meta format. The standard extension is .mhd. If more than one file is specified, the reader will switch to file series mode in which it will pretend that it can support time and provide one file per time step.
/$defs/options-pvMetaFileSeriesReader/pr.label: File Names

/$defs/options-pvMetaFileSeriesReader/pr.explanation: Path of one .mhd or .mha file. Several files form a file series read as successive time steps. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; absolute paths avoid ambiguity. The value is a constructor option, so it must be a constant.

/$defs/options-pvMulticorrelativeStatist.explanation:
Specify the task to be performed: modeling and/or assessment.
  1. "Detailed model of input data," creates a set of output tables containing a calculated statistical model of the entire input dataset;
  2. "Model a subset of the data," creates an output table (or tables) summarizing a randomly-chosen subset of the input dataset;
  3. "Assess the data with a model," adds attributes to the first input dataset using a model provided on the second input port; and
  4. "Model and assess the same data," is really just operations 2 and 3 above applied to the same input dataset. The model is first trained using a fraction of the input data and then the entire dataset is assessed using that model.
When the task includes creating a model (i.e., tasks 2, and 4), you may adjust the fraction of the input dataset used for training. You should avoid using a large fraction of the input data for training as you will then not be able to detect overfitting. The Training fraction setting will be ignored for tasks 1 and 3.
/$defs/options-pvMulticorrelativeStatist.label: Task

pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

/$defs/options-pvNetCDFMPASreader/proper.explanation: Fixes the index of each additional NetCDF dimension of the selected variables (any dimension other than Time, nCells and nVertices, e.g. nVertLevels or a tracer dimension), so one slice is loaded. In multilayer view the dimension named by VerticalDimension is read in full and its index is ignored.

/$defs/options-pvNetCDFMPASreader/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView has no static value and vtkMPASReader uses index 0 for every additional dimension.
pitfalls: Schemaxis rejects an odd-length list (INVALID_LENGTH) and an index that is not written as digits (INVALID_ARGUMENT); ParaView would otherwise drop the last name or read a non-numeric index as 0. In this case, it might be necessary to scale and/or bias the vertical height. The height will become height*scale + bias. Keep in mind that if the positive attribute of the vertical dimension is down, then the height is negated. The scaling will be adjusted if it results in invalid (negative) vertical values.
/$defs/options-pvNetCDFReader/properties.label: Vertical Bias

/$defs/options-pvNetCDFUGRIDreader/prope.explanation: If on, any float or double variable read that has a _FillValue attribute will have that fill value replaced with a not-a-number (NaN) value. The advantage of setting these to NaN values is that, if implemented properly by the system and careful math operations are used, they can implicitly be ignored by calculations like finding the range of the values. That said, this option should be used with caution as VTK does not fully support NaN values and therefore odd calculations may occur.

/$defs/options-pvNormalGlyphs/properties.explanation: The value of this property controls whether consistent polygon ordering is enforced. Generally the normals for a data set should either all point inward or all point outward. If the value of this property is 1, then this filter will reorder the points of cells that whose normal vectors are oriented the opposite direction from the rest of those in the data set.

/$defs/options-pvNrrdReader.explanation: Settings choose the .nrrd or .nhdr file (required) and an optional voxel sub-box (DataVOI, default all zeros for the whole volume).

/$defs/options-pvNrrdReader/properties/D.explanation: The data volume of interest (VOI). The VOI is a sub-extent of the data that you want loaded. Setting a VOI is useful when reading from a large data set and you are only interested in a small portion of the data. If left containing all 0's, then the reader will load in the entire data set.
/$defs/options-pvNrrdReader/properties/D.label: Data VOI

/$defs/options-pvNrrdReader/properties/D.explanation: The data volume of interest (VOI). The VOI is a sub-extent of the data that you want loaded. Setting a VOI is useful when reading from a large data set and you are only interested in a small portion of the data. If left containing all 0's, then the reader will load in the entire data set.

One voxel-index bound of the box to load, in the order [imin, imax, jmin, jmax, kmin, kmax]: zero-based and inclusive. All zeros loads the whole volume; any nonzero entry makes the six values the loaded extent.
/$defs/options-pvNrrdReader/properties/D.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] (whole volume).
pitfalls: Give all six bounds: [0, 99, 0, 0, 0, 0] is a single row of 100 voxels, not the first 100 voxels in every direction.

/$defs/options-pvNrrdReader/properties/D.explanation: One voxel-index bound of the box to load, in the order [imin, imax, jmin, jmax, kmin, kmax]: zero-based and inclusive. All zeros loads the whole volume; any nonzero entry makes the six values the loaded extent.
/$defs/options-pvNrrdReader/properties/D.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] (whole volume).
pitfalls: Give all six bounds: [0, 99, 0, 0, 0, 0] is a single row of 100 voxels, not the first 100 voxels in every direction.

/$defs/options-pvNrrdReader/properties/D.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvNrrdReader/properties/D.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvOMETIFFChannelCalculato.explanation: Choose which channel arrays take part in the composite (ChannelVisibilities) and how strongly each contributes (Channel1Weight to Channel10Weight, ParaView default 1.0). The colour map of each channel comes from the ChannelNLUT inputs, not from these settings.

Multiplier applied to the opacity that Channel10LUT gives each pixel of the array Channel_10, before that channel is added into the Colors composite. Larger values make channel 10 more prominent; 0 removes its contribution while keeping it enabled. Colour components are clamped to [0, 1] after blending.
/$defs/options-pvOMETIFFChannelCalculato.label: Channel 10 weight
/$defs/options-pvOMETIFFChannelCalculato.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 1.0.
pitfalls: The weight has no effect unless Channel_10 is listed in ChannelVisibilities and Channel10LUT is connected with opacity mapping enabled.

/$defs/options-pvOMETIFFChannelCalculato.explanation: Select the point data arrays to pass through

Name of one point array (normally Channel_1 to Channel_10) to include in the colour composite. Listed channels are blended; unlisted ones are ignored but still passed through in the output. Order does not matter.
pitfalls: Each listed channel needs its ChannelNLUT input connected, otherwise the filter fails.

/$defs/options-pvOMETIFFChannelCalculato.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvOMETIFFChannelCalculato.label: Runtime value

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvOpenFOAMReader/properti.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvPCANormalEstimation/pro.explanation: Configure how the filter selects the neighbor points used to calculate the PCA. With KNN mode K (SampleSize) points are selected regardless of their location relative to the sampled point. The radius can also be set to ensure that a sufficiently large neighborhood is taken into account, if not (i.e. all points fall inside the radius), the second approach is performed. With Radius mode, neighboring points are selected inside a radius (RADIUS), only the neighborhood of the sampled point is considered. If K (SampleSize) is also set, the number of points found inside the radius must be larger than K, if not the first approach is performed. Both approaches give the same results. The first approach is faster for uniform point clouds, in other cases, the second approach is faster.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvParallelNetCDFPOPreader.explanation: Settings choose the POP NetCDF file(s) (required; several form a time series), which variables are loaded (chosen by ParaView from the file when omitted) and the sampling stride along each grid index direction (ParaView default [1, 1, 1], every point).
The list of files to be read by the reader.
/$defs/options-pvParallelNetCDFPOPreader.label: File Name

/$defs/options-pvParallelNetCDFPOPreader.explanation: Path of one POP NetCDF file (.pop.ncdf or .pop.nc). Further entries form a file series, one time step per file in the order listed. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder. The value must be a constant because file names are passed when the reader is created.
sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/paraview/paraview/-/raw/v5.13.3/VTKExtensions/IOCore/vtkFileSeriesReader.h (files are read in the order they are added)

/$defs/options-pvParallelNetCDFPOPreader.explanation: This property indicates the number of indices per dimension (i,j,k) to skip between each point included in this output.
/$defs/options-pvParallelNetCDFPOPreader.label: Stride

/$defs/options-pvParallelNetCDFPOPreader.explanation: This property indicates the number of indices per dimension (i,j,k) to skip between each point included in this output.
Sampling step along one grid index direction: first i, then j, then k. 1 keeps every point, 2 every second point, and so on; larger strides cut memory and resolution along that direction.
/$defs/options-pvParallelNetCDFPOPreader.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 1, 1].
pitfalls: ParaView's range domain starts at 1; zero or negative strides are not meaningful.

/$defs/options-pvParticlePath/properties.explanation: When animating particles, it is nice to inject new ones every Nth step to produce a continuous flow. Setting ForceReinjectionEveryNSteps to a non zero value will cause the particle source to reinject particles every Nth step even if it is otherwise unchanged. Note that if the particle source is also animated, this flag will be redundant as the particles will be reinjected whenever the source changes anyway.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvPartitionedDataSetColle.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvPlane/properties/Origin.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvPlane/properties/Origin.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.explanation: One setting, SliceType: the implicit function that cuts the surface. Omitted, the compound definition starts from a Plane through [0, 0, 0] with normal [1, 0, 0]; set the type and its options explicitly so the cut lies where the data are.
This property sets the parameters of the slice function.
/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.label: Slice Type

/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.explanation: This property sets the parameters of the slice function.

A rectangular box region (ParaView’s vtkPVBox): a unit cube scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation about its minimum corner and moved to Position, or, with UseReferenceBounds, the Bounds box transformed in the same way. The implicit function is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a box-shaped region; slicing or cutting with a box produces the box faces where they cross the data.
pitfalls: ParaView’s initial box may be a unit cube at the origin if the input bounds were not applied; set Position and Length explicitly.

/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.explanation: A rectangular box region (ParaView’s vtkPVBox): a unit cube scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation about its minimum corner and moved to Position, or, with UseReferenceBounds, the Bounds box transformed in the same way. The implicit function is negative inside and positive outside. Choose it to keep, remove or extract a box-shaped region; slicing or cutting with a box produces the box faces where they cross the data.
pitfalls: ParaView’s initial box may be a unit cube at the origin if the input bounds were not applied; set Position and Length explicitly.

/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.explanation: Placement and size of the box. In the normal mode Position (minimum corner), Length (edge lengths) and Rotation define it; with UseReferenceBounds true, Bounds defines the box and the other three act relative to it. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values, which may cover the whole input.
/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.explanation: Reference box [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax] used only when UseReferenceBounds is true; the box is then these bounds scaled by Length, rotated by Rotation and translated by Position, all about the coordinate origin, so Length [1, 1, 1], Rotation [0, 0, 0] and Position [0, 0, 0] reproduce Bounds exactly. Ignored otherwise.
/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.label: Bounds
/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1]; the XML marks it NoDefault, so it is not filled from the input bounds.
pitfalls: Setting Bounds alone has no effect; also set UseReferenceBounds to true.
Give each minimum before its maximum.

With UseReferenceBounds true: dimensionless scale factors applied to the Bounds box about the coordinate origin.
/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.label: Length
/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.units: Dataset coordinate units (scale factors when UseReferenceBounds is true)
/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial value (its static default is [1, 1, 1]; ParaView may instead derive it from the side lengths of the input’s bounding box, so that the box covers the whole input). Set it explicitly when the result depends on it.
pitfalls: Length is a size, not the far corner: to cover x from 2 to 5, use Position x = 2 and Length x = 3.
Zero or negative lengths give a degenerate or inverted box.

/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.explanation: An infinite flat plane through Origin, oriented by Normal (ParaView’s vtkPVPlane). It is the usual choice, and ParaView’s initial one for most operations that offer it: use it for planar cuts, clips or selections at any orientation. Where offered, prefer Axis Aligned Plane when the plane must stay exactly perpendicular to x, y or z, and Box, Sphere or Cylinder when the region of interest is closed or curved.
pitfalls: The plane is unbounded: it cuts through every part of the dataset it crosses, including distant parts.

/$defs/options-pvPlotOnIntersectionCurve.explanation: Direction perpendicular to the plane, [nx, ny, nz]. A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).

/$defs/options-pvPlotOverLine/properties.explanation: When dealing with composite datasets, partial arrays are common i.e. data-arrays that are not available in all of the blocks. By default, this filter only passes those point and cell data-arrays that are available in all the blocks i.e. partial arrays are removed. When PassPartialArrays is turned on, this behavior is changed to take a union of all arrays present thus partial arrays are passed as well. However, for composite dataset input, this filter still produces a non-composite output. For all those locations in a block of where a particular data array is missing, this filter uses vtkMath::Nan() for double and float arrays, and 0 for all other types of arrays i.e int, char etc.

/$defs/options-pvPlotOverLine/properties.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; never the static [0, 0, 0]. In a bounded native probe with a polydata upstream, an omitted Point1 read back as (1, 1, 1) when the node was created before its upstream had data, which is what a Schemaxis batch run does, a point unrelated to the data (composite inputs give other uninitialised-bounds corners, by the source); with data already present it was the minimum corner of the input's bounding box. Set both endpoints.

AggregateAsPolyData should stay 0 (false) for this operation.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvPlotOverLinesFromCustom.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvPlotOverLinesFromCustom.explanation: When dealing with composite datasets, partial arrays are common i.e. data-arrays that are not available in all of the blocks. By default, this filter only passes those point and cell data-arrays that are available in all the blocks i.e. partial arrays are removed. When PassPartialArrays is turned on, this behavior is changed to take a union of all arrays present thus partial arrays are passed as well. However, for composite dataset input, this filter still produces a non-composite output. For all those locations in a block of where a particular data array is missing, this filter uses vtkMath::Nan() for double and float arrays, and 0 for all other types of arrays i.e int, char etc.
/$defs/options-pvPlotOverLinesFromCustom.label: Pass Partial Arrays

/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.explanation: Settings choose the interpolation kernel and its radius or neighbour count, how points without neighbours are treated (NullPointsStrategy, NullValue, mask array name), the point locator, and whether Source's own arrays are passed through. Omitted settings keep ParaView's values: Voronoi (closest-point) kernel, Null Value strategy with value 0, static point locator, and no pass-through of the probe structure's own arrays.
Specify an interpolation kernel. By default a vtkVoronoiKernel is used (i.e., closest point). The interpolation kernel changes the basis of the interpolation.
/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.label: Kernel

/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.explanation: Specify an interpolation kernel. By default a vtkVoronoiKernel is used (i.e., closest point). The interpolation kernel changes the basis of the interpolation.

Gaussian weighting whose shape is stretched or flattened along each source point’s normal, optionally scaled by a scalar (vtkEllipsoidalGaussianKernel). Choose it for oriented samples such as surface scans, where “pancake” splats aligned with the surface interpolate better than spheres. Without normals it reduces to a spherical Gaussian whose width is scaled by Eccentricity; plain Gaussian Kernel is cheaper in that case.

Gaussian weighting whose shape is stretched or flattened along each source point’s normal, optionally scaled by a scalar (vtkEllipsoidalGaussianKernel). Choose it for oriented samples such as surface scans, where “pancake” splats aligned with the surface interpolate better than spheres. Without normals it reduces to a spherical Gaussian whose width is scaled by Eccentricity; plain Gaussian Kernel is cheaper in that case.

Shape and reach of the ellipsoidal Gaussian: Radius, Sharpness, Eccentricity, and whether normals (UseNormals) and scalars (UseScalars) of the source points are used. The neighbourhood is always the radius footprint. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values (Radius 1, Sharpness 2, Eccentricity 2, normals on, scalars off).
/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

The neighbourhood is always the radius footprint. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values (Radius 1, Sharpness 2, Eccentricity 2, normals on, scalars off).
/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.explanation: Shape of the ellipsoid relative to each point’s normal: 1 is spherical, values below 1 give a needle along the normal, values above 1 a pancake perpendicular to it. In the weight exp(−Sharpness² · (r⊥²/E² + z²)/R²) it divides the distance measured perpendicular to the normal.
/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.label: Eccentricity
/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 2.0.
pitfalls: Without normals (UseNormals false or no normals array) the perpendicular term applies in every direction, so Eccentricity simply widens (E > 1) or narrows (E < 1) a spherical Gaussian.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.explanation: Gaussian-weighted average of the neighbouring source points: weights exp(−(Sharpness · r / Radius)²), normalized to sum to 1; a source point exactly at the sample is copied. Gives smooth fields that favour nearby points; a good general choice. Shepard Kernel honours nearby values more sharply, Linear Kernel weights all neighbours equally, Voronoi Kernel copies the closest point, and Ellipsoidal Gaussian Kernel adds orientation from normals.

Neighbourhood (KernelFootprint with Radius or NumberOfPoints) and fall-off (Sharpness) of the Gaussian weights. Radius is the most influential setting. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values: radius footprint, Radius 1.0, Sharpness 2.
/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.explanation: How the neighbourhood (basis) of source points for each sample point is chosen. “Radius” uses every source point within Radius of the sample (VTK notes it has the better mathematical properties); “N Closest” uses the NumberOfPoints nearest source points regardless of distance, which always finds neighbours in sparse regions but may reach far away.
/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.label: Kernel footprint
/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from "Radius".
pitfalls: With “Radius”, a sample with no source point inside Radius is a null point, handled by the operation’s NullPointsStrategy (null value, mask or closest point). Increase Radius or use “N Closest” if many results are null.
A very large Radius makes every sample use huge neighbourhoods; VTK warns the cost can approach n³.

/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.explanation: Copies the values of a single source point from the neighbourhood: the most probable one when probability weights are supplied, otherwise the closest. ParaView’s point interpolators supply no probabilities, so here it behaves like Voronoi Kernel restricted to the footprint: the closest point within Radius (or among the N closest), and a null point when the radius is empty. Choose Voronoi Kernel for plain nearest-neighbour sampling.

Copies the values of a single source point from the neighbourhood: the most probable one when probability weights are supplied, otherwise the closest. ParaView’s point interpolators supply no probabilities, so here it behaves like Voronoi Kernel restricted to the footprint: the closest point within Radius (or among the N closest), and a null point when the radius is empty. Choose Voronoi Kernel for plain nearest-neighbour sampling.
Footprint within which the closest source point is chosen: KernelFootprint with Radius or NumberOfPoints. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values: radius footprint with Radius 1.0.
/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.explanation: How the neighbourhood (basis) of source points for each sample point is chosen. “Radius” uses every source point within Radius of the sample (VTK notes it has the better mathematical properties); “N Closest” uses the NumberOfPoints nearest source points regardless of distance, which always finds neighbours in sparse regions but may reach far away.
/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.label: Kernel footprint
/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from "Radius".
pitfalls: With “Radius”, a sample with no source point inside Radius is a null point, handled by the operation’s NullPointsStrategy (null value, mask or closest point). Increase Radius or use “N Closest” if many results are null.
A very large Radius makes every sample use huge neighbourhoods; VTK warns the cost can approach n³.

/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.explanation: Nearest neighbour: each sample takes the values of the single closest source point (weight 1), with no radius limit, so an empty neighbourhood never produces a null point. It is fast and preserves original values without blending, but gives piecewise-constant, blocky fields. It is ParaView’s initial kernel for these interpolators; switch to Gaussian or Shepard for smooth fields.
pitfalls: When a sample is equally distant from several source points, one of them is chosen arbitrarily.

/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.explanation: How output points that have no source point in their neighbourhood (null points) get a value. Mask Points adds an output array that marks each point valid (1) or null (0) and also sets the NullValue; Null Value (ParaView's default, entry 1) writes the NullValue to null points; Closest Point uses the closest source point. ParaView's own text calls Closest Point the default, but its XML default is 1 (Null Value), as in vtkPointInterpolator.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 VTKExtensions/Points/Resources/points.xml:1003-1023 (NullPointsStrategy default_values "1" = Null Value; text names ClosestPoint)

/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvPointDatasetInterpolato.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator.explanation: Source settings define the probe line; the remaining settings choose the kernel, null-point handling, locator and pass-through. Omitted settings keep ParaView's values: Voronoi (closest-point) kernel, Null Value strategy with value 0, static point locator, and no pass-through of the probe structure's own arrays.

/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.explanation: Specify an interpolation kernel. By default a vtkVoronoiKernel is used (i.e., closest point). The interpolation kernel changes the basis of the interpolation.
/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.label: Kernel

/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.explanation: Specify an interpolation kernel. By default a vtkVoronoiKernel is used (i.e., closest point). The interpolation kernel changes the basis of the interpolation.

Gaussian weighting whose shape is stretched or flattened along each source point’s normal, optionally scaled by a scalar (vtkEllipsoidalGaussianKernel). Choose it for oriented samples such as surface scans, where “pancake” splats aligned with the surface interpolate better than spheres. Without normals it reduces to a spherical Gaussian whose width is scaled by Eccentricity; plain Gaussian Kernel is cheaper in that case.

Gaussian weighting whose shape is stretched or flattened along each source point’s normal, optionally scaled by a scalar (vtkEllipsoidalGaussianKernel). Choose it for oriented samples such as surface scans, where “pancake” splats aligned with the surface interpolate better than spheres. Without normals it reduces to a spherical Gaussian whose width is scaled by Eccentricity; plain Gaussian Kernel is cheaper in that case.

Shape and reach of the ellipsoidal Gaussian: Radius, Sharpness, Eccentricity, and whether normals (UseNormals) and scalars (UseScalars) of the source points are used. The neighbourhood is always the radius footprint. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values (Radius 1, Sharpness 2, Eccentricity 2, normals on, scalars off).
/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.explanation: Shape of the ellipsoid relative to each point’s normal: 1 is spherical, values below 1 give a needle along the normal, values above 1 a pancake perpendicular to it. In the weight exp(−Sharpness² · (r⊥²/E² + z²)/R²) it divides the distance measured perpendicular to the normal.
/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.label: Eccentricity
/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 2.0.
pitfalls: Without normals (UseNormals false or no normals array) the perpendicular term applies in every direction, so Eccentricity simply widens (E > 1) or narrows (E < 1) a spherical Gaussian.

/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.explanation: Gaussian-weighted average of the neighbouring source points: weights exp(−(Sharpness · r / Radius)²), normalized to sum to 1; a source point exactly at the sample is copied. Gives smooth fields that favour nearby points; a good general choice. Shepard Kernel honours nearby values more sharply, Linear Kernel weights all neighbours equally, Voronoi Kernel copies the closest point, and Ellipsoidal Gaussian Kernel adds orientation from normals.

/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.explanation: How the neighbourhood (basis) of source points for each sample point is chosen. “Radius” uses every source point within Radius of the sample (VTK notes it has the better mathematical properties); “N Closest” uses the NumberOfPoints nearest source points regardless of distance, which always finds neighbours in sparse regions but may reach far away.
/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.label: Kernel footprint
/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from "Radius".
pitfalls: With “Radius”, a sample with no source point inside Radius is a null point, handled by the operation’s NullPointsStrategy (null value, mask or closest point). Increase Radius or use “N Closest” if many results are null.
A very large Radius makes every sample use huge neighbourhoods; VTK warns the cost can approach n³.

/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.explanation: Copies the values of a single source point from the neighbourhood: the most probable one when probability weights are supplied, otherwise the closest. /$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.explanation: How the neighbourhood (basis) of source points for each sample point is chosen. “Radius” uses every source point within Radius of the sample (VTK notes it has the better mathematical properties); “N Closest” uses the NumberOfPoints nearest source points regardless of distance, which always finds neighbours in sparse regions but may reach far away.

/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).

/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.explanation: Nearest neighbour: each sample takes the values of the single closest source point (weight 1), with no radius limit, so an empty neighbourhood never produces a null point. It is fast and preserves original values without blending, but gives piecewise-constant, blocky fields. It is ParaView’s initial kernel for these interpolators; switch to Gaussian or Shepard for smooth fields.
pitfalls: When a sample is equally distant from several source points, one of them is chosen arbitrarily.

/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.explanation: How output points that have no source point in their neighbourhood (null points) get a value. Mask Points adds an output array that marks each point valid (1) or null (0) and also sets the NullValue; Null Value (ParaView's default, entry 1) writes the NullValue to null points; Closest Point uses the closest source point. ParaView's own text calls Closest Point the default, but its XML default is 1 (Null Value), as in vtkPointInterpolator.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 VTKExtensions/Points/Resources/points.xml:1003-1023 (NullPointsStrategy default_values "1" = Null Value; text names ClosestPoint)

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvPointLineInterpolator/p.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial value (its static default is [0, 0, 0]; ParaView may instead derive it from the minimum corner of the input’s bounding box). Set it explicitly when the result depends on it.

/$defs/options-pvPointPlaneInterpolator.explanation: Source settings define the bounded probe plane; the remaining settings choose the kernel, null-point handling, locator and pass-through. Omitted settings keep ParaView's values: Voronoi (closest-point) kernel, Null Value strategy with value 0, static point locator, and no pass-through of the probe structure's own arrays.

/$defs/options-pvPointPlaneInterpolator/.explanation: Specify an interpolation kernel. By default a vtkVoronoiKernel is used (i.e., closest point). The interpolation kernel changes the basis of the interpolation.
/$defs/options-pvPointPlaneInterpolator/.label: Kernel

/$defs/options-pvPointPlaneInterpolator/.explanation: Specify an interpolation kernel. By default a vtkVoronoiKernel is used (i.e., closest point). The interpolation kernel changes the basis of the interpolation.

Gaussian weighting whose shape is stretched or flattened along each source point’s normal, optionally scaled by a scalar (vtkEllipsoidalGaussianKernel). Choose it for oriented samples such as surface scans, where “pancake” splats aligned with the surface interpolate better than spheres. Without normals it reduces to a spherical Gaussian whose width is scaled by Eccentricity; plain Gaussian Kernel is cheaper in that case.

Gaussian weighting whose shape is stretched or flattened along each source point’s normal, optionally scaled by a scalar (vtkEllipsoidalGaussianKernel). Choose it for oriented samples such as surface scans, where “pancake” splats aligned with the surface interpolate better than spheres. Without normals it reduces to a spherical Gaussian whose width is scaled by Eccentricity; plain Gaussian Kernel is cheaper in that case.

Shape and reach of the ellipsoidal Gaussian: Radius, Sharpness, Eccentricity, and whether normals (UseNormals) and scalars (UseScalars) of the source points are used. The neighbourhood is always the radius footprint. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values (Radius 1, Sharpness 2, Eccentricity 2, normals on, scalars off).
/$defs/options-pvPointPlaneInterpolator/.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvPointPlaneInterpolator/.explanation: Shape of the ellipsoid relative to each point’s normal: 1 is spherical, values below 1 give a needle along the normal, values above 1 a pancake perpendicular to it. In the weight exp(−Sharpness² · (r⊥²/E² + z²)/R²) it divides the distance measured perpendicular to the normal.
/$defs/options-pvPointPlaneInterpolator/.label: Eccentricity
/$defs/options-pvPointPlaneInterpolator/.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 2.0.
pitfalls: Without normals (UseNormals false or no normals array) the perpendicular term applies in every direction, so Eccentricity simply widens (E > 1) or narrows (E < 1) a spherical Gaussian.

/$defs/options-pvPointPlaneInterpolator/.explanation: Search radius R in dataset units: source points within it form the neighbourhood, and R also normalizes the distances in the Gaussian weight. If no source point lies within R, the operation’s NullPointsStrategy decides the result.
/$defs/options-pvPointPlaneInterpolator/.label: Radius
/$defs/options-pvPointPlaneInterpolator/.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 1.0.

/$defs/options-pvPointPlaneInterpolator/.explanation: Gaussian-weighted average of the neighbouring source points: weights exp(−(Sharpness · r / Radius)²), normalized to sum to 1; a source point exactly at the sample is copied.
