Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvSliceWithPlane/properti.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvSpatioTemporalHarmonics.explanation: One setting, Harmonics, lists the summed waves as groups of six numbers; omitted, ParaView's four example harmonics are used.

This property defines the harmonics that will be computed and summed on each point. Default values are only example values, that would make sense for a dataset of geometrical bounds [-10,10,-10,10,-10,10] and time values greater than or equal to 0 and less than 2*Pi.
/$defs/options-pvSpatioTemporalHarmonics.label: Harmonics

/$defs/options-pvSpatioTemporalHarmonics.explanation: This property defines the harmonics that will be computed and summed on each point. Default values are only example values, that would make sense for a dataset of geometrical bounds [-10,10,-10,10,-10,10] and time values greater than or equal to 0 and less than 2*Pi.

One number of the flat Harmonics list, read in groups of six per harmonic: amplitude A, temporal frequency ω, wave-vector components kx, ky, kz, and phase φ (radians), so the list length must be a multiple of 6. For example [1, 1, 0.6283, 0, 0, 0] is one wave of unit amplitude travelling along x.
pitfalls: A list whose length is not a multiple of 6 shifts every later parameter; write harmonics as complete groups of six.

/$defs/options-pvSpatioTemporalHarmonics.explanation: The grid extent (ParaView default -10 to 10 on each axis, 21 × 21 × 21 points), the harmonics (groups of six numbers; default four) and the time values to generate (default 20 values from 0 to just below 2π).
This property defines the harmonics that will be computed and summed on each point. By default, it generates harmonics in each direction, with parameters adapted to the default extent.
/$defs/options-pvSpatioTemporalHarmonics.label: Harmonics

/$defs/options-pvSpatioTemporalHarmonics.explanation: This property defines the harmonics that will be computed and summed on each point. By default, it generates harmonics in each direction, with parameters adapted to the default extent.

One number of a harmonic. Harmonics are given as consecutive groups of six: amplitude A, temporal frequency ω (radians per time unit), wave-vector components kx, ky, kz (radians per coordinate unit) and phase φ (radians); each group adds A·sin(ω·t + k·x + φ).
pitfalls: The list length must be a multiple of 6; each harmonic needs all six numbers in order.

/$defs/options-pvSpatioTemporalHarmonics.explanation: This property specifies the timestep values to generate. When generating a range, make sure to remove the max value for the loop to avoid time value duplication (0 == 2*Pi). By default, it generates 20 timesteps from [0;2*Pi[ for data loop.
One time value at which the source reports a step, used directly as t in the harmonic formula. Values are sorted by VTK; Schemaxis accepts 0 to 6.2832 (2π) from the native range domain.
/$defs/options-pvSpatioTemporalHarmonics.units: Time units of the formula (radians when ω = 1)
/$defs/options-pvSpatioTemporalHarmonics.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 20 values 0, 0.3141, …, 5.969 (steps of 2π/20).
pitfalls: Do not include both 0 and 2π: with integer frequencies they produce identical frames, so a looping animation stutters.

/$defs/options-pvSpatioTemporalHarmonics.explanation: The six values in the property indicate the X, Y, and Z extent of the output data. The first two numbers are the minimum and maximum X extent; the next two are the minimum and maximum Y extent; and the final two are the minimum and maximum Z extent. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvSphere/properties/EndPh.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvSplineSource/properties.explanation: Property used to reference the parametric function as data generator.

Control points and closure of the interpolating spline (a cardinal spline in each coordinate that passes through every control point in order). Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values: a straight segment from [0, 0, 0] to [1, 0, 0], open.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvStreamTracer/properties.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvStreamTracer/properties.explanation: Number of equal segments the seed line is divided into; the line has Resolution + 1 points and each one seeds a streamline, so this sets how many streamlines are traced.
/$defs/options-pvStreamTracer/properties.label: Resolution
/$defs/options-pvStreamTracer/properties.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 1000 (1001 seeds).
pitfalls: Very high values produce many overlapping streamlines and long run times; lower Resolution for a first look.

/$defs/options-pvStreamTracer/properties.explanation: Seeds placed at random positions inside a sphere of Radius around Center (NumberOfPoints seeds, uniformly distributed through the sphere’s volume). It is listed first among ParaView’s seed types. Choose it to seed a region around a point of interest, for example a vortex core or an injector; choose Line for an ordered rake.
pitfalls: Seed positions are random; do not rely on exact seed coordinates. Use Line when seed placement must be reproducible.

/$defs/options-pvStreamTracer/properties.explanation: Centre, radius and number of the random seeds. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values: 100 seeds, and a centre and radius that ParaView may derive from the input bounds (static [0, 0, 0] and 1).
/$defs/options-pvStreamTracer/properties.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvStreamTracer/properties.label: Vectors

/$defs/options-pvStreamTracer/properties.explanation: This property contains the name of the vector array from which to generate streamlines.

One entry of the [association, array name] pair naming the velocity field to integrate: first the association token (POINTS, or CELLS for cell-centred vectors), then the array name, e.g. ["POINTS", "U"]. The array must have 3 components.
/$defs/options-pvStreamTracer/properties.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; there is no static default. ParaView picks the input's active vectors array of the right association, else the first listed array, if the input is visible when the node is created (not verified for Schemaxis). Name the array explicitly.
pitfalls: Giving only the array name fails validation; the association comes first.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvTableToPoints/propertie.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvTableToStructuredGrid.explanation: Choose the X, Y and Z coordinate columns and the WholeExtent index ranges of the grid; the extent must account for every row of the table.

/$defs/options-pvTableToStructuredGrid/p.explanation: Index ranges of the structured grid as [imin, imax, jmin, jmax, kmin, kmax] (inclusive point indices). The number of points, (imax-imin+1)(jmax-jmin+1)(kmax-kmin+1), must equal the number of table rows, or ParaView reports an error and produces nothing. For a 2-D grid keep one range collapsed, e.g. kmin = kmax = 0.
/$defs/options-pvTableToStructuredGrid/p.label: Whole extent
/$defs/options-pvTableToStructuredGrid/p.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], a single point.
pitfalls: Using cell counts instead of point counts (e.g. [0, 50, …] for 50 points) mismatches the row count by one per axis; imax = number of points − 1.
Static extents must change whenever the table's resolution changes; derive them from the same source as the table.

/$defs/options-pvTecplotReader/propertie.explanation: Path of one ASCII Tecplot file. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; the value is passed when the node is created and must be a constant. Several entries form a time series in list order: if the first file reports no time, entry k is given time k (zero-based); otherwise each file's own times are used.

/$defs/options-pvTemporalArrayOperator/p.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial array (there is no static default). Name it explicitly.

/$defs/options-pvTemporalArrayOperator/p.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvTemporalArrayOperator/p.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvTemporalInterpolator.explanation: Two settings: DiscreteTimeStepInterval (ParaView default 0, no fixed spacing; a positive value reports steps of that spacing across the input time range) and ResampleFactor (default 1, the stored steps only; n divides each stored interval into n parts). DiscreteTimeStepInterval takes precedence.

/$defs/options-pvTemporalInterpolator/pr.explanation: If Discrete Time Step Interval is set to 0, then the Temporal Interpolator will provide a continuous region of time on its output. If set to anything else, then the output will define a finite set of time points on its output, each spaced by the Discrete Time Step Interval. The output will have (time range)/(discrete time step interval) time steps. (Note that the time range is defined by the time range of the data of the input filter, which may be different from other pipeline objects or the range defined in the animation inspector.) This is a useful option to use if you have a dataset with one missing time step and wish to 'fill in' the missing data with an interpolated value from the steps on either side.
/$defs/options-pvTemporalInterpolator/pr.label: Discrete Time Step Interval

/$defs/options-pvTemporalParticlesToPath.explanation: If a particle disappears from one end of a simulation and reappears on the other side, the track left will be unrepresentative. Set a MaxStepDistance{x,y,z} which acts as a threshold above which if a step occurs larger than the value (for the dimension), the track will be dropped and restarted after the step. That is, the part before the wrap around will be dropped and the newer part kept.
/$defs/options-pvTemporalParticlesToPath.label: Max Step Distance

/$defs/options-pvTemporalParticlesToPath.explanation: If a particle disappears from one end of a simulation and reappears on the other side, the track left will be unrepresentative. Set a MaxStepDistance{x,y,z} which acts as a threshold above which if a step occurs larger than the value (for the dimension), the track will be dropped and restarted after the step. That is, the part before the wrap around will be dropped and the newer part kept.

One component of the per-axis jump threshold [dx, dy, dz], in dataset coordinate units: if a particle moves farther than this along that axis in one time step, its trail is cut and restarted, so particles that wrap through periodic boundaries do not draw lines across the domain.
/$defs/options-pvTemporalParticlesToPath.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1.0, 1.0, 1.0].
pitfalls: The default of 1 per axis breaks every trail in a domain measured in metres with fast particles, or never breaks it in millimetres; scale it to a plausible per-step displacement.

/$defs/options-pvTemporalShiftScale/prop.explanation: If Periodic is true, requests for time will be wrapped around so that the source appears to be a periodic time source. If data exists for times {0,N-1}, setting periodic to true will cause time 0 to be produced when time N, 2N, 2N etc is requested. This effectively gives the source the ability to generate time data indefinitely in a loop. When combined with Shift/Scale, the time becomes periodic in the shifted and scaled time frame of reference. Note: Since the input time may not start at zero, the wrapping of time from the end of one period to the start of the next, will subtract the initial time - a source with T{5..6} repeated periodically will have output time {5..6..7..8} etc.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvTensorGlyph/properties/.explanation: A polygonal cylinder of Radius and Height centred at Center, with its axis along its own local y axis. Glyph and Tensor Glyph orient glyphs by their local x axis (Tensor Glyph also maps y to the medium eigenvector), so the cylinder axis does not follow the vector or major eigenvector unless the shape is rotated.
pitfalls: In Glyph, rotate the shape with GlyphTransform (for example Rotate [0, 0, 90]) if the cylinders should lie along the vectors.
sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/paraview/paraview/-/blob/v5.13.3/VTKExtensions/FiltersGeneral/vtkPVGlyphFilter.cxx (source transform, then scale, x axis rotated onto the orientation vector, then translate)

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvTensorGlyph/properties/.label: Runtime value

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvTensorGlyph/properties/.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvTessellate.explanation: Settings set the error limits (ChordError, ParaView default 0.001; optional per-field FieldError), the maximum subdivisions per edge (default 3), the output dimension (default 3) and point merging (default true).

/$defs/options-pvTessellate/properties/C.explanation: This property controls the maximum chord error allowed at any edge midpoint in the output tessellation. The chord error is measured as the distance between the midpoint of any output edge and the original nonlinear geometry.

The field error is measured as the difference between a field value at the midpoint of an output edge and the value of the corresponding field in the original nonlinear geometry.
/$defs/options-pvTessellate/properties/F.label: Field Error

/$defs/options-pvTessellate/properties/F.explanation: This property controls the maximum field error allowed at any edge midpoint in the output tessellation. The field error is measured as the difference between a field value at the midpoint of an output edge and the value of the corresponding field in the original nonlinear geometry.

Maximum allowed error for one point field at edge midpoints, in that field's units: element i applies to the i-th point array passed to the tessellator (point arrays in order, normals excluded). A value of 0 or less disables the criterion for that field, so only geometry drives refinement.
/$defs/options-pvTessellate/properties/F.units: Units of the corresponding point array
/$defs/options-pvTessellate/properties/F.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView sets no field criteria, so only ChordError controls subdivision.
pitfalls: The index follows the input's point-array order, which is not shown in the form; check the array order before relying on a field criterion.

/$defs/options-pvTessellate/properties/M.explanation: If the value of this property is set to 1, coincident vertices will be merged after tessellation has occurred. Only geometry is considered during the merge and the first vertex encountered is the one whose point attributes will be used. Any discontinuities in point fields will be lost. On the other hand, many operations, such as streamline generation, require coincident vertices to be merged. Toggle whether to merge coincident vertices.
/$defs/options-pvTessellate/properties/M.label: Merge Points

/$defs/options-pvTessellate/properties/O.explanation: The value of this property sets the maximum dimensionality of the output tessellation. When the value of this property is 3, 3D cells produce tetrahedra, 2D cells produce triangles, and 1D cells produce line segments. When the value is 2, 3D cells will have their boundaries tessellated with triangles. When the value is 1, all cells except points produce line segments.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvThresholdSelectionSourc.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvTransform.explanation: Choose the transform (translate, rotate, scale through the Transform choice; identity by default) and whether all 3-component arrays are transformed as vectors (ParaView default true) or only the active vectors and normals.

/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.explanation: The values in this property allow you to specify the transform (translation, rotation, and scaling) to apply to the input dataset.
/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.label: Transform

/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.explanation: The values in this property allow you to specify the transform (translation, rotation, and scaling) to apply to the input dataset.

General affine transform built from Translate, Rotate and Scale (ParaView’s vtkPVTransform): each point is scaled about the coordinate origin, rotated about the origin, then translated. Choose it to move, rotate, resize or mirror a dataset; choose RotateAroundOriginTransform to rotate about another pivot, or GeoTransform to convert between map projections.
pitfalls: Rotation and scaling act about the coordinate origin, so a model far from the origin also moves; use RotateAroundOriginTransform or compensate with Translate.

/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.explanation: General affine transform built from Translate, Rotate and Scale (ParaView’s vtkPVTransform): each point is scaled about the coordinate origin, rotated about the origin, then translated. Choose it to move, rotate, resize or mirror a dataset; choose RotateAroundOriginTransform to rotate about another pivot, or GeoTransform to convert between map projections.
pitfalls: Rotation and scaling act about the coordinate origin, so a model far from the origin also moves; use RotateAroundOriginTransform or compensate with Translate.

/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.explanation: Translate, Rotate and Scale of the transform, applied to points in the order scale, rotate, translate. Omitted settings keep the identity values (no translation, no rotation, scale 1).
/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.explanation: Pure rotation about a pivot point you choose (vtkPVRotateAroundOriginTransform): points are rotated by Rotate about OriginOfRotation, with no scaling or translation. Choose it to turn a part about its own centre or a hinge axis; choose Transform when you also need to move or scale.

Pure rotation about a pivot point you choose (vtkPVRotateAroundOriginTransform): points are rotated by Rotate about OriginOfRotation, with no scaling or translation. Choose it to turn a part about its own centre or a hinge axis; choose Transform when you also need to move or scale.
Pivot (Originofrotation) and angles (Rotate) of the rotation. Omitted settings keep ParaView’s initial values: pivot at [0, 0, 0] and no rotation.
/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.explanation: Converts point coordinates between two cartographic coordinate reference systems described by PROJ strings (vtkGeoTransform), for example longitude/latitude to UTM metres. Choose it for georeferenced data; choose Transform for ordinary Cartesian moves and rotations.
pitfalls: VTK notes that point normals must be removed before this transform, otherwise it does nothing; drop or regenerate normals around it.

/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.explanation: Converts point coordinates between two cartographic coordinate reference systems described by PROJ strings (vtkGeoTransform), for example longitude/latitude to UTM metres. Choose it for georeferenced data; choose Transform for ordinary Cartesian moves and rotations.
pitfalls: VTK notes that point normals must be removed before this transform, otherwise it does nothing; drop or regenerate normals around it.

/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.explanation: Source and destination PROJ definitions and whether z is converted too. Both projections should be written: ParaView declares no default for them.
/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.defaultMeaning: Omitted or {}: Schemaxis assigns none of these settings, so each keeps the native proxy’s initial value described on the individual setting.

/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.explanation: Source and destination PROJ definitions and whether z is converted too. Both projections should be written: ParaView declares no default for them.

/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.explanation: PROJ definition of the output coordinates, e.g. “+proj=utm +zone=33 +datum=WGS84” for UTM eastings and northings in metres, or “+proj=cart +datum=WGS84” for geocentric x, y, z.
/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.label: Destination projection
/$defs/options-pvTransform/properties/Tr.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 declares no default value.
pitfalls: Choose the UTM zone that contains the data; points far outside it are strongly distorted.

/$defs/options-pvTube/properties/VaryRad.explanation: The property determines whether/how to vary the radius of the tube. These additional points increase the number of polynomial terms in each element so that the shape functions can span a larger space of polynomial functions.

/$defs/options-pvUnstructuredNetCDFPOPre.explanation: Path of one POP NetCDF file. Several files form a file series read as successive time steps. The value is a constructor option, so it must be a constant.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvUnstructuredNetCDFPOPre.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvUnstructuredNetCDFPOPre.explanation: Index box [imin, imax, jmin, jmax, kmin, kmax] of the structured POP grid to read, counted after Stride is applied (zero-based, inclusive). It is applied only when at least one maximum is not -1; a bound outside the data is ignored. Use it to read a region of a large ocean grid.
/$defs/options-pvUnstructuredNetCDFPOPre.label: VOI
/$defs/options-pvUnstructuredNetCDFPOPre.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, -1, 0, -1, 0, -1], which reads the whole grid.
pitfalls: The native help says all zeros loads everything; in the reader's code all zeros selects only index 0 in each direction. Use -1 maxima for the full grid.

/$defs/options-pvVPICReader/properties/X.explanation: VPIC data is written one file per simulation processor. This coarse map of files is used in partitioning files between visualizing processors so that each ParaView processor has its own set of files to display. Ghost cell overlap is handled within the reader. To limit the View of VPIC information the extent in the X dimension of "files" can be specified. Only the files selected will be displayed and they will be partitioned between the visualizing processors, allowing a higher resolution over a smaller area.
/$defs/options-pvVPICReader/properties/X.label: X Extent

/$defs/options-pvVPICReader/properties/X.explanation: VPIC data is written one file per simulation processor. This coarse map of files is used in partitioning files between visualizing processors so that each ParaView processor has its own set of files to display. Ghost cell overlap is handled within the reader. To limit the View of VPIC information the extent in the X dimension of "files" can be specified. Only the files selected will be displayed and they will be partitioned between the visualizing processors, allowing a higher resolution over a smaller area.

One end of the inclusive range of simulation files read along x: first the lowest, then the highest file index. Indices are zero-based, from 0 to the number of files along x minus 1 in the .vpc layout; only files in the range are read and shared among the ParaView processes.
/$defs/options-pvVPICReader/properties/X.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [-1, -1], documented as all files, and may replace it with the full file range from the .vpc layout. Set both ends to view a subregion.
pitfalls: These are file (processor tile) indices, not cell indices; one file covers a block of grid cells.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvVTKHDFReader/properties.explanation: The list of files to be read by the reader. Each file is expected to be in the VTKHDF data format storing the same data type. The standard extension is .vtkhdf. If more than one file is specified, the reader will switch to file series mode and provide one file per time step.
/$defs/options-pvVTKHDFReader/properties.label: File Name

/$defs/options-pvVTKHDFReader/properties.explanation: Path of one VTKHDF file. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; the value is passed when the node is created and must be a constant. Several entries form a time series in list order: if the first file reports no time, entry k is given time k (zero-based); otherwise each file's own times are used.
The number of levels that the reader can read when the data type is AMR. Set this to 0 to imply no limit. Default is 0.

/$defs/options-pvVTKHDFReader/properties.explanation: The number of levels that the reader can read when the data type is AMR. Set this to 0 to imply no limit. Default is 0.

One number of a flat list read in pairs (process, value): the MPI process number, then an integer array value to select. The process number -1 applies an entry to every MPI process; in a serial run use -1 or 0. For example [-1, 3, -1, 7] selects values 3 and 7.
pitfalls: Writing only values, e.g. [3, 7], is read as process 3 / value 7; give the process first.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.

These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

/$defs/options-pvVisItBOVReader/properti.explanation: Path of one BOV file (.bov). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. /$defs/options-pvVisItBOVReader/properti.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvVisItCEAucdReader/prope.explanation: Path of one CEA UCD file (.ucd, .inp). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Use absolute paths; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). The plugin locates the companion domain files and the CEA root file from the opened file's name and directory, so keep the case files together.

/$defs/options-pvVisItCTRLReader/propert.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItCTRLReader/propert.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItCTRLReader/propert.explanation: Path of one TB-LMTO ctrl file (.ctrl). /$defs/options-pvVisItChomboReader/prope.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItChomboReader/prope.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItClawReader/propert.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItClawReader/propert.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItClawReader/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. The VisIt bridge registers every point variable as unselected, so normally no point arrays are read (if ParaView's Load All Variables setting is enabled, all are selected). Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) read back the fixture's only variable, a cell variable, as unselected and produced no arrays, with LoadAllVariables false, identically with and without --dr; the bridge treats point variables the same way (vtkAvtFileFormatAlgorithm.cxx:758-790).
pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).

/$defs/options-pvVisItCurve2DReader.explanation: FileName (required) lists the Curve2D files to read, one per time step; MeshStatus, MaterialStatus, PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus choose what the VisIt plugin converts. Omitted selections keep the reader's initial state, which in the VisIt bridge source is the first mesh only and no materials or arrays, so name what you need. These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

/$defs/options-pvVisItCurve2DReader/prop.explanation: The list of files to be read by the reader.

/$defs/options-pvVisItCurve2DReader/prop.explanation: Path of one Curve2D file (.curve, .ultra, .ult, .u). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Use absolute paths; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Each curve in the file starts with a "#" line naming it, followed by one x y pair per line.

Files without their own time values are ordered by their position in the list, so list them in time order.

The Curve2D plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select.

/$defs/options-pvVisItCurve2DReader/prop.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvVisItDDCMDReader/proper.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItDDCMDReader/proper.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItDDCMDReader/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 has no static default for this selection. A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply reads nothing, so copy names exactly.

Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. /$defs/options-pvVisItDyna3DReader.explanation: FileName (required) lists the DYNA3D files to read, one per time step; MeshStatus, MaterialStatus, PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus choose what the VisIt plugin converts. Omitted selections keep the reader's initial state, which in the VisIt bridge source is the first mesh only and no materials or arrays, so name what you need. These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. /$defs/options-pvVisItDyna3DReader/prope.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItDyna3DReader/prope.label: Runtime value

pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvVisItFLASHReader/proper.explanation: Path of one FLASH file (.flash, .f5). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. /$defs/options-pvVisItFluentReader/prope.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvVisItFluentReader/prope.explanation: Path of one Fluent file (.cas). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Use absolute paths; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). The plugin opens the data file by replacing the extension with .dat, so case.cas needs case.dat beside it.

/$defs/options-pvVisItFluentReader/prope.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItFluentReader/prope.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItGGCMReader/propert.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItGGCMReader/propert.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItGTCReader.explanation: FileName (required) lists the GTC files to read, one per time step; MeshStatus, MaterialStatus, PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus choose what the VisIt plugin converts. Omitted selections keep the reader's initial state, which in the VisIt bridge source is the first mesh only and no materials or arrays, so name what you need. These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

/$defs/options-pvVisItGTCReader/properti.explanation: Path of one GTC file (.h5). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Many codes write .h5 files; make sure the file is GTC particle output.

/$defs/options-pvVisItGTCReader/properti.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItGTCReader/properti.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItGTCReader/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).

/$defs/options-pvVisItGULPReader/propert.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItGULPReader/propert.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItGadgetReader/prope.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvVisItImageReader/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. /$defs/options-pvVisItImageReader/proper.explanation: Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from image data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. /$defs/options-pvVisItImageReader/proper.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItImageReader/proper.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItImageReader/proper.explanation: The list of files to be read by the reader.
/$defs/options-pvVisItImageReader/proper.label: File Name

/$defs/options-pvVisItImageReader/proper.explanation: Path of one image file (.pnm, .ppm, .sdt, .spr, .imgvol). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Use absolute paths; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). An .imgvol file is a text list of 2-D image files that the plugin stacks into a volume; the listed images must be readable from it.

Files without their own time values are ordered by their position in the list, so list them in time order.

The image plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select.

/$defs/options-pvVisItLAMMPSDumpReader/p.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItLAMMPSDumpReader/p.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItLAMMPSStructureRea.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItLAMMPSStructureRea.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItLAMMPSStructureRea.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. The VisIt bridge registers every point variable as unselected, so normally no point arrays are read (if ParaView's Load All Variables setting is enabled, all are selected). Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) read back the fixture's only variable, a cell variable, as unselected and produced no arrays, with LoadAllVariables false, identically with and without --dr; the bridge treats point variables the same way (vtkAvtFileFormatAlgorithm.cxx:758-790).
pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).

/$defs/options-pvVisItLinesReader.explanation: FileName (required) lists the Lines files to read, one per time step; MeshStatus, MaterialStatus, PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus choose what the VisIt plugin converts. Omitted selections keep the reader's initial state, which in the VisIt bridge source is the first mesh only and no materials or arrays, so name what you need. These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

/$defs/options-pvVisItLinesReader/proper.explanation: Path of one Lines file (.lines). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Each line is introduced by a header line naming it, followed by one coordinate per line.

/$defs/options-pvVisItM3DC1Reader/proper.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItM3DC1Reader/proper.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItM3DReader/properti.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItM3DReader/properti.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItMFIXCDFReader/prop.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItMFIXCDFReader/prop.label: Runtime value

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItMFIXReader/propert.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItMM5Reader/properti.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItMM5Reader/properti.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItMiliReader/propert.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItMiliReader/propert.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItMirandaReader/prop.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItMirandaReader/prop.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItMirandaReader/prop.explanation: Path of the single Miranda file to read (.mir, .raw); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Name the text .mir metadata file; it lists the grid and data files.
