/$defs/options-pvVisItNASTRANReader/prop.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvVisItNASTRANReader/prop.explanation: Path of one NASTRAN bulk data file (.nas, .f06). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Use absolute paths; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). The plugin reads GRID (including GRID* large-field) points and element cards such as CTRIA, CQUAD, CBAR, CTETRA, CPENTA and CHEXA.

/$defs/options-pvVisItNASTRANReader/prop.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItNASTRANReader/prop.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItNek5000Reader/prop.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItNek5000Reader/prop.label: Runtime value

pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFCCSM_STSDRea.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFFVCOMParticl.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFFVCOMParticl.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFFVCOM_MTMDRe.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFFVCOM_MTMDRe.label: Runtime value

pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).

/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFFVCOM_MTMDRe.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFFVCOM_MTMDRe.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFFVCOM_MTSDRe.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFFVCOM_MTSDRe.label: Runtime value

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

The LODI particle plugin offers particle source identifiers (material set "sourceid") when the file defines them.

/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFLODIParticle.label: Materials
/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFLODIParticle.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. The VisIt bridge registers every material as unselected, so normally no material arrays are produced (if ParaView's Load All Variables setting is enabled, all are selected). Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) found no materials in the fixture (MaterialStatus empty), so the disabled initial state comes from the bridge source (vtkAvtFileFormatAlgorithm.cxx:825-871).
pitfalls: Threshold a material array above 0, not at or above 0: -1 marks cells without that material.
Material names come from the file and are case-sensitive; a misspelt name is not rejected and produces no array.

/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFLODIParticle.explanation: Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The LODI particle plugin offers particle source identifiers (material set "sourceid") when the file defines them.

/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFLODIParticle.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFLODIParticle.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFLODIParticle.label: Meshes
/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFLODIParticle.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 has no static default for this selection. The VisIt bridge enables only the first mesh the plugin reports and ParaView copies that state, so normally only that mesh is read. Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) read back the fixture's one mesh as enabled, with LoadAllVariables false, identically with and without --dr.
pitfalls: An empty list deselects every mesh and gives an empty output.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply reads nothing, so copy names exactly.

/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFLODIReader/p.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFLODIReader/p.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItNetCDFLODIReader/p.explanation: Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The LODI plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select.

/$defs/options-pvVisItOVERFLOWReader/pro.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItOVERFLOWReader/pro.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItOpenFOAMReader.explanation: FileName (required) names the single OpenFOAM file that holds every time step; Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays choose what the VisIt plugin converts. Omitted selections keep the reader's initial state, which in the VisIt bridge source is the first mesh only and no materials or arrays, so name what you need. Each list replaces the whole selection when given.

/$defs/options-pvVisItOpenFOAMReader/pro.explanation: Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from OpenFOAM data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The OpenFOAM plugin offers the volume (cell) and point fields of the case; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file.

/$defs/options-pvVisItOpenFOAMReader/pro.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. The VisIt bridge registers every cell variable as unselected, so normally no cell arrays are read (if ParaView's Load All Variables setting is enabled, all are selected). Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) read back the fixture's only cell variable as unselected and produced no arrays, with LoadAllVariables false, identically with and without --dr.
pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).

The OpenFOAM plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select.

/$defs/options-pvVisItPATRANReader/prope.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItPATRANReader/prope.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItPFLOTRANReader/pro.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItPFLOTRANReader/pro.label: Runtime value

The VisIt bridge enables only the first mesh the plugin reports and ParaView copies that state, so normally only that mesh is read. Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) read back the fixture's one mesh as enabled, with LoadAllVariables false, identically with and without --dr.
pitfalls: An empty list deselects every mesh and gives an empty output.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply reads nothing, so copy names exactly.

/$defs/options-pvVisItPFLOTRANReader/pro.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).

/$defs/options-pvVisItPLOT2DReader.explanation: FileName (required) lists the PLOT2D files to read, one per time step; MeshStatus, MaterialStatus, PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus choose what the VisIt plugin converts. Omitted selections keep the reader's initial state, which in the VisIt bridge source is the first mesh only and no materials or arrays, so name what you need. These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

/$defs/options-pvVisItPLOT2DReader/prope.explanation: Path of one PLOT2D file (.p2d). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Use absolute paths; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). The plugin's VisIt read options stay at their defaults (C binary, 3-D, single grid, big-endian, single precision, no IBLANK) and cannot be changed here.

/$defs/options-pvVisItParaDiSTecplotRead.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).

/$defs/options-pvVisItParaDiSTecplotRead.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItParaDiSTecplotRead.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItParaDiSTecplotRead.label: File Name

/$defs/options-pvVisItParaDiSTecplotRead.explanation: Path of one ParaDiS Tecplot-style file (.fld, .field, .cyl, .cylinder, .dat). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Use absolute paths; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from).

Files without their own time values are ordered by their position in the list, so list them in time order.

/$defs/options-pvVisItParaDiSTecplotRead.explanation: Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The ParaDiS Tecplot-style plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select.

/$defs/options-pvVisItParaDiSTecplotRead.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItParaDiSTecplotRead.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItParaDisReader.explanation: FileName (required) lists the ParaDiS files to read, one per time step; MeshStatus, MaterialStatus, PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus choose what the VisIt plugin converts. Omitted selections keep the reader's initial state, which in the VisIt bridge source is the first mesh only and no materials or arrays, so name what you need. These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

/$defs/options-pvVisItParaDisReader/prop.explanation: Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from ParaDiS data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. /$defs/options-pvVisItParaDisReader/prop.explanation: Path of one ParaDiS file (.prds, .data, .dat). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. /$defs/options-pvVisItParaDisReader/prop.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItParaDisReader/prop.label: Runtime value

The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

/$defs/options-pvVisItProteinDataBankRea.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItProteinDataBankRea.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItRAWReader.explanation: FileName (required) lists the RAW triangle files to read, one per time step; MeshStatus, MaterialStatus, PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus choose what the VisIt plugin converts. Omitted selections keep the reader's initial state, which in the VisIt bridge source is the first mesh only and no materials or arrays, so name what you need. These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

/$defs/options-pvVisItRAWReader/properti.explanation: Path of one RAW triangle file (.raw). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Use absolute paths; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Each line holds one triangle as nine numbers (three vertices); a line with a name starts a new object.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvVisItSAMRAIReader/prope.explanation: Path of one SAMRAI file (.samrai). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Use absolute paths; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Name the .samrai summary file of a time step; it locates the per-processor HDF5 files.

/$defs/options-pvVisItSASReader/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).

/$defs/options-pvVisItSASReader/properti.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItSASReader/properti.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItSASReader/properti.explanation: Path of the single SAS file to read (.sasgeom, .sas, .sasdata); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Keep the .sasgeom geometry and the data files together.

/$defs/options-pvVisItSASReader/properti.explanation: Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The SAS plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select.

/$defs/options-pvVisItSASReader/properti.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItSASReader/properti.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItSiloReader.explanation: FileName (required) lists the Silo files to read, one per time step; MeshStatus, MaterialStatus, PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus choose what the VisIt plugin converts. Omitted selections keep the reader's initial state, which in the VisIt bridge source is the first mesh only and no materials or arrays, so name what you need. These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

/$defs/options-pvVisItSiloReader/propert.explanation: Path of one Silo file (.silo, .pdb). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Use absolute paths; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). For a multi-file Silo dataset name the root file holding the multimesh; it refers to the domain files.

/$defs/options-pvVisItSiloReader/propert.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItSiloReader/propert.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItSpheralReader.explanation: FileName (required) lists the Spheral++ files to read, one per time step; MeshStatus, MaterialStatus, PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus choose what the VisIt plugin converts. Omitted selections keep the reader's initial state, which in the VisIt bridge source is the first mesh only and no materials or arrays, so name what you need. These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

/$defs/options-pvVisItSpheralReader/prop.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItSpheralReader/prop.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItTFTReader.explanation: FileName (required) lists the TFT files to read, one per time step; MeshStatus, MaterialStatus, PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus choose what the VisIt plugin converts. Omitted selections keep the reader's initial state, which in the VisIt bridge source is the first mesh only and no materials or arrays, so name what you need. These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

/$defs/options-pvVisItTFTReader/properti.explanation: Path of one TFT file (.dat, .tft). /$defs/options-pvVisItTFTReader/properti.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

/$defs/options-pvVisItTSurfReader/proper.explanation: Path of one GOCAD TSurf file (.ts_deg83). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Use absolute paths; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). The file must start with a "GOCAD TSurf" header; ParaView registers only the .ts_deg83 extension, but Schemaxis calls the reader directly.

The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvVisItTetradReader/prope.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvVisItUNICReader/propert.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItUNICReader/propert.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItUNICReader/propert.explanation: Path of one UNIC file (.h5). Each entry is one step of a file series: when the files report their own times ParaView uses them, otherwise the steps are numbered 0, 1, 2… in list order. Use absolute paths; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from).

Files without their own time values are ordered by their position in the list, so list them in time order.

/$defs/options-pvVisItUNICReader/propert.explanation: Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The UNIC plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItUNICReader/propert.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItVASPCHGCARReader.explanation: FileName (required) names the single VASP CHGCAR file that holds every time step; Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays choose what the VisIt plugin converts. /$defs/options-pvVisItVASPCHGCARReader/p.explanation: Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The VASP CHGCAR plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select.

/$defs/options-pvVisItVASPCHGCARReader/p.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItVASPCHGCARReader/p.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItVASPOUTCARReader/p.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItVASPOUTCARReader/p.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItVelodyneReader.explanation: FileName (required) lists the Velodyne files to read, one per time step; MeshStatus, MaterialStatus, PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus choose what the VisIt plugin converts. Omitted selections keep the reader's initial state, which in the VisIt bridge source is the first mesh only and no materials or arrays, so name what you need. These keys are ParaView's names for the file-series wrapper; single-file VisIt readers call the same selections Meshes, Materials, PointArrays and CellArrays.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItVsReader/propertie.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItXYZReader/properti.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItXYZReader/properti.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvVisItXmdvReader/propert.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvVisItXmdvReader/propert.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWavelet.explanation: Grid extent (ParaView default -10 to 10 on each axis), function centre ([0, 0, 0]), Gaussian peak Maximum (255) and StandardDeviation (0.5), three wave amplitudes and frequencies, and a SubsampleRate (1) that coarsens the grid.

/$defs/options-pvWavelet/properties/Cent.explanation: Centre of the Gaussian and origin of the wave coordinates, in grid-index units: for each point, x, y and z are the offsets of its grid index from Center, divided by the extent width on that axis, and the Gaussian depends on their length r. /$defs/options-pvWavelet/properties/XFre.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

/$defs/options-pvWriteCGNSWriter.explanation: Optional array selection (ChooseArraysToWrite plus one list per association), GhostLevel and UseHDF5, which picks HDF5 (ParaView default) or ADF storage. Omitted settings keep ParaView's values: every array written, no ghost levels, HDF5; the file name and time stepping are managed by Schemaxis.

/$defs/options-pvWriteCGNSWriter/propert.explanation: Select the cell data arrays to pass through.
/$defs/options-pvWriteCGNSWriter/propert.label: Cell Data Arrays

/$defs/options-pvWriteCGNSWriter/propert.explanation: Select the cell data arrays to pass through.

One cell (element) array name to keep in the CGNS output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then cell arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Kept cell arrays are written as cell-centred CGNS solution fields.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/ServerManager/vtkSIDataArraySelectionProperty.cxx:106-121 (Push: RemoveAllArrays, then enable the listed names)
/$defs/options-pvWriteCGNSWriter/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no cell arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the semantic comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the semantic comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

/$defs/options-pvWriteCGNSWriter/propert.explanation: One field-data array (a whole-dataset value not tied to points or cells) name to keep in the CGNS output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then field arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Field arrays are whole-dataset values; keep only those the receiving CGNS tool needs.

/$defs/options-pvWriteCGNSWriter/propert.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteCGNSWriter/propert.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteCSVWriter.explanation: Settings control what the CSV contains and how numbers are printed: FieldAssociation picks point, cell, vertex, edge, row or field data by entry text such as "Cell Data"; Precision and UseScientificNotation set number formatting; AddMetaData, AddTime and AddTimeStep add extra columns; ChooseArraysToWrite with the array lists restricts columns but is rejected under the table comparison, which needs every input array. Omitted settings keep ParaView's values (Precision 5, general notation, metadata columns added); the file name and time-series writing are managed by Schemaxis.

/$defs/options-pvWriteCSVWriter/properti.label: Add Meta Data

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteCSVWriter/properti.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteCSVWriter/properti.explanation: Attribute data that the writer turns into rows: one row per point, cell, vertex, edge or table row, or the field-data tuples. Chosen by the ParaView entry text: "Point Data", "Cell Data", "Vertex Data", "Edge Data", "Row Data" or "Field Data". ParaView offers only the associations the connected input has (for example "Row Data" for a table), so a text it does not offer fails with NATIVE_DOMAIN_MISMATCH when the node is configured.

/$defs/options-pvWriteCSVWriter/properti.explanation: Number of digits vtkCSVWriter prints for floating-point values. With UseScientificNotation false (ParaView's default) it counts significant digits, so the default 5 writes 101325.7 as 1.0133e+05; with UseScientificNotation true it counts digits after the decimal point of the mantissa. Integer columns are not affected.
/$defs/options-pvWriteCSVWriter/properti.label: Precision
/$defs/options-pvWriteCSVWriter/properti.units: Digits (significant digits, or decimals in scientific notation)
/$defs/options-pvWriteCSVWriter/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 5.
pitfalls: Schemaxis' table verifier compares every written number with the input within the export tolerance (default 0), so 5 significant digits usually fails for floating-point data. Use 17, which reproduces double-precision values exactly, or set a tolerance.

/$defs/options-pvWriteDataSetCSVWriter/p.explanation: Attribute data that the writer turns into rows: one row per point, cell, vertex, edge or table row, or the field-data tuples. Chosen by the ParaView entry text: "Point Data", "Cell Data", "Vertex Data", "Edge Data", "Row Data" or "Field Data". /$defs/options-pvWriteHoudiniWriter/prop.explanation: Select the cell data arrays to pass through.

One cell (element) array name to keep in the Houdini .geo output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then cell arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Kept cell arrays become Houdini primitive attributes written after each polygon record.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/ServerManager/vtkSIDataArraySelectionProperty.cxx:106-121 (Push: RemoveAllArrays, then enable the listed names)
/$defs/options-pvWriteHoudiniWriter/prop.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no cell arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: Fields are not verified for this format (geometry comparison), so trimming arrays here is safe for verification.

/$defs/options-pvWriteHoudiniWriter/prop.explanation: In parallel runs, this writer can consolidate output from multiple ranks to a subset of ranks. This specifies the number of ranks that will do the final writing to disk. If **NumberOfIORanks** is 0, then all ranks will save the local data. If set to 1 (default), the root node alone will write to disk. All data from all ranks will be gathered to the root node before being written out.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

/$defs/options-pvWriteIOSSWriter/propert.explanation: Select the element set arrays to pass through.

One cell-array name to write as a variable of the partitions selected as Exodus element sets (by ElementSetSelectors or the automatic mapping), spelled exactly as in the input. It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then cell arrays not listed are left out for that entity type, and order or repeated names make no difference. Id arrays (global ids, element_side, object_id) are handled by the writer and need not be listed.

/$defs/options-pvWriteIOSSWriter/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no arrays of this association are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the semantic comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

/$defs/options-pvWriteIOSSWriter/propert.explanation: Specify the element sets selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to write from the input dataset.
/$defs/options-pvWriteIOSSWriter/propert.label: Element Set Selectors

/$defs/options-pvWriteIOSSWriter/propert.explanation: Specify the element sets selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to write from the input dataset.

One data-assembly selector naming input partitions to write as Exodus element sets. Element sets are named groups of elements, for example a region used for output or material assignment. The path is read in the assembly named by Assembly: in ParaView's Hierarchy assembly the root is Root and nodes take the block names ("/Root/<name>" or "//<name>" for any depth); for data read by ParaView's IOSS reader, the collection's own assembly groups them under "/IOSS/element_sets/<name>". Order and repeated selectors make no difference.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 VTK/Common/DataModel/vtkDataAssembly.cxx:386-421 (MakeValidNodeName keeps [.-0-9A-Za-z_] and prefixes "_" unless the first character is a letter or "_")
/$defs/options-pvWriteIOSSWriter/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selectors (no static default). When every selector list is empty, the writer maps IOSS-read data to its original blocks and sets and otherwise writes all partitions as element blocks.
pitfalls: Setting any selector list switches off that automatic mapping for all entity types, so list every block and set you want written.

Node names are the block names with every character other than letters, digits, ".", "-" and "_" removed; a name that then starts with anything other than a letter or "_" gets a leading "_" ("3D" becomes "_3D"). Check the input's assembly before writing a path.

/$defs/options-pvWriteIOSSWriter/propert.explanation: Specify the side sets selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to write from the input dataset.

One data-assembly selector naming input partitions to write as Exodus side sets. Side sets are named groups of element sides (faces of 3-D cells, edges of 2-D cells), the usual way to mark boundary patches such as inlets and walls. The path is read in the assembly named by Assembly: in ParaView's Hierarchy assembly the root is Root and nodes take the block names ("/Root/<name>" or "//<name>" for any depth); for data read by ParaView's IOSS reader, the collection's own assembly groups them under "/IOSS/side_sets/<name>". Order and repeated selectors make no difference.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 VTK/Common/DataModel/vtkDataAssembly.cxx:386-421 (MakeValidNodeName keeps [.-0-9A-Za-z_] and prefixes "_" unless the first character is a letter or "_")
/$defs/options-pvWriteIOSSWriter/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selectors (no static default). When every selector list is empty, the writer maps IOSS-read data to its original blocks and sets and otherwise writes all partitions as element blocks.
pitfalls: Setting any selector list switches off that automatic mapping for all entity types, so list every block and set you want written.

Node names are the block names with every character other than letters, digits, ".", "-" and "_" removed; a name that then starts with anything other than a letter or "_" gets a leading "_" ("3D" becomes "_3D"). Check the input's assembly before writing a path.

/$defs/options-pvWriteOpenVDBWriter/prop.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no cell arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteOpenVDBWriter/prop.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteOpenVDBWriter/prop.explanation: Select the field data arrays to pass through.
/$defs/options-pvWriteOpenVDBWriter/prop.label: Field Data Arrays

/$defs/options-pvWriteOpenVDBWriter/prop.explanation: Select the field data arrays to pass through.

One field-data array (a whole-dataset value not tied to points or cells) name to keep in the OpenVDB output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then field arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Field arrays are whole-dataset values and do not form VDB grids.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/ServerManager/vtkSIDataArraySelectionProperty.cxx:106-121 (Push: RemoveAllArrays, then enable the listed names)
/$defs/options-pvWriteOpenVDBWriter/prop.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no field arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterPoly.explanation: One field-data array (a whole-dataset value not tied to points or cells) name to keep in the legacy VTK output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then field arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Kept field arrays are written in the legacy file's FIELD section.
