/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterPoly.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterPoly.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterPoly.explanation: In parallel runs, this writer can consolidate output from multiple ranks to a subset of ranks. This specifies the number of ranks that will do the final writing to disk. If **NumberOfIORanks** is 0, then all ranks will save the local data. If set to 1 (default), the root node alone will write to disk. All data from all ranks will be gathered to the root node before being written out.
/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterPoly.label: Number Of IO Ranks

/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterPoly.explanation: In MPI runs where NumberOfIORanks is greater than 1 and less than the number of ranks, chooses how ranks are grouped to send data to the writing ranks. Contiguous forms consecutive groups (16 ranks, 3 writers: 0-5, 6-10, 11-15, written by ranks 0, 6 and 11); RoundRobin interleaves them (0, 3, ..., 15; 1, 4, ..., 13; 2, 5, ..., 14, written by 0, 1 and 2). Schemaxis runs explicit exports serially, so this has no effect on the file.
/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterPoly.label: Rank assignment mode
/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterPoly.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from Contiguous.
pitfalls: The upstream example names ranks 0, 6 and 15 as writers for Contiguous mode; the first rank of the third group is 11.

/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterUnst.explanation: Select the edge data arrays to pass through.

One graph-edge array name to keep in the legacy VTK output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then edge arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Only graphs carry edge data and this writer accepts unstructured grids, so entries here match nothing.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterUnst.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no field arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterUnst.explanation: In parallel runs, this writer can consolidate output from multiple ranks to a subset of ranks. This specifies the number of ranks that will do the final writing to disk. If **NumberOfIORanks** is 0, then all ranks will save the local data. If set to 1 (default), the root node alone will write to disk. All data from all ranks will be gathered to the root node before being written out.

/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterUnst.explanation: In MPI runs where NumberOfIORanks is greater than 1 and less than the number of ranks, chooses how ranks are grouped to send data to the writing ranks. Contiguous forms consecutive groups (16 ranks, 3 writers: 0-5, 6-10, 11-15, written by ranks 0, 6 and 11); RoundRobin interleaves them (0, 3, ..., 15; 1, 4, ..., 13; 2, 5, ..., 14, written by 0, 1 and 2). Schemaxis runs explicit exports serially, so this has no effect on the file.
/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterUnst.label: Rank assignment mode
/$defs/options-pvWritePDataSetWriterUnst.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from Contiguous.
pitfalls: The upstream example names ranks 0, 6 and 15 as writers for Contiguous mode; the first rank of the third group is 11.

/$defs/options-pvWritePNGWriter.explanation: PNGWriter exposes no settings in Schemaxis. The file name is managed by Schemaxis, and PNG compression is lossless, so nothing here can change the stored pixel values.

/$defs/options-pvWritePOBJWriter.explanation: Optional array selection (it can only keep or drop point normals and texture coordinates, the only arrays OBJ stores), TextureFileName for an optional material file, and the MPI gather settings NumberOfIORanks and RankAssignmentMode, which have no effect in Schemaxis's serial exports. Omitted settings keep ParaView's values: all arrays passed, no material file.

/$defs/options-pvWritePOBJWriter/propert.explanation: In MPI runs where NumberOfIORanks is greater than 1 and less than the number of ranks, chooses how ranks are grouped to send data to the writing ranks. Contiguous forms consecutive groups (16 ranks, 3 writers: 0-5, 6-10, 11-15, written by ranks 0, 6 and 11); RoundRobin interleaves them (0, 3, ..., 15; 1, 4, ..., 13; 2, 5, ..., 14, written by 0, 1 and 2). Schemaxis runs explicit exports serially, so this has no effect on the file.
/$defs/options-pvWritePOBJWriter/propert.label: Rank assignment mode

pitfalls: The upstream example names ranks 0, 6 and 15 as writers for Contiguous mode; the first rank of the third group is 11.

/$defs/options-pvWritePPLYWriter/propert.explanation: When **NumberOfIORanks** is greater than 1 and less than the number of MPI ranks, this controls how the ranks that write to disk are determined. This also affects which ranks send data to which rank for IO. In **Contiguous** mode (default), all MPI ranks are numerically grouped into **NumberOfIORanks** groups with the first rank in each group acting as the `root` node for that group and is the one that does IO. For example, if there are 16 MPI ranks and NumberOfIORanks is set to 3 then the groups are `[0 - 5], [6 - 10], [11 - 15]` with the first rank in each group 0, 6, and 15 doing the IO. In **RoundRobin** mode, the grouping is done in round robin fashion, thus for 16 MPI ranks with NumberOfIORanks set to 3, the groups are `[0, 3, ..., 15], [1, 4, ..., 13], [2, 5, ..., 14]` with 0, 1 and 2 doing the IO.
/$defs/options-pvWritePPLYWriter/propert.label: Rank Assignment Mode

/$defs/options-pvWriteSerialHTGMultiBloc.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no cell arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). /$defs/options-pvWriteSerialHTGMultiBloc.explanation: Select the point data arrays to pass through.

One point (node) array name to keep in the multiblock hyper tree grid (.vtm/.htg) output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then point arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Hyper tree grids keep their fields as cell data, so point-array entries normally match nothing for this writer.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteSerialHTGMultiBloc.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteSerialHTGMultiBloc.explanation: Whether the writer adds the dataset's current time as a TimeValue field-data array in the XML file, so that readers can recover the time from the file alone. /$defs/options-pvWriteSerialHTGMultiBloc.label: Write time value
/$defs/options-pvWriteSerialHTGMultiBloc.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis sets false when omitted, overriding ParaView's initial value (true).
pitfalls: Enabling it adds a TimeValue field array that the input node lacks, so exact verification is likely to fail for time-dependent inputs.

/$defs/options-pvWriteTIFFWriter.explanation: One setting, Scalars, chooses the point array written as the TIFF pixel values. Omitted, ParaView keeps its own initial array selection, which depends on the input's arrays, so name the array whenever the image has more than one.

/$defs/options-pvWriteTIFFWriter/propert.explanation: This property contains the name of the scalar array to be saved.
/$defs/options-pvWriteTIFFWriter/propert.label: Scalars

/$defs/options-pvWriteTIFFWriter/propert.explanation: This property contains the name of the scalar array to be saved.

One entry of the two-entry Scalars pair. The first entry is the association token (POINTS for image point data, the usual case) and the second is the array name, e.g. ["POINTS", "Temperature"]. Order matters and both entries are required.
pitfalls: Writing only the array name fails validation; always give the association first.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLHierarchicalBox.label: Cell Data Arrays

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLHierarchicalBox.explanation: Select the cell data arrays to pass through.

One cell (element) array name to keep in the VTK XML AMR (.vthb) output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then cell arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/ServerManager/vtkSIDataArraySelectionProperty.cxx:106-121 (Push: RemoveAllArrays, then enable the listed names)
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLHierarchicalBox.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no cell arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLHierarchicalBox.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no field arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). /$defs/options-pvWriteXMLHierarchicalBox.explanation: Specify the selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to extract from the input dataset.

One data-assembly selector naming AMR levels to write when ChooseBlocksToWrite is true. In the Hierarchy assembly of AMR data the root is Root and each refinement level is a node named Level0, Level1, ... (coarsest first), so "/Root/Level0" keeps the base level and "/Root" everything. Order and repeated selectors make no difference.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLHierarchicalBox.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selectors (no static default). Selectors are ignored while ChooseBlocksToWrite is false, ParaView's default.
pitfalls: ChooseBlocksToWrite true is rejected at planning (BLOCK_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE) because no declared comparison accepts missing levels; reduce the data upstream instead.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLMultiBlockDataW.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLMultiBlockDataW.explanation: Select the field data arrays to pass through.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLMultiBlockDataW.label: Field Data Arrays

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLMultiBlockDataW.explanation: Select the field data arrays to pass through.

One field-data array (a whole-dataset value not tied to points or cells) name to keep in the VTK XML multiblock (.vtm) output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then field arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Applies to field arrays of the multiblock and of its blocks.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/ServerManager/vtkSIDataArraySelectionProperty.cxx:106-121 (Push: RemoveAllArrays, then enable the listed names)
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLMultiBlockDataW.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no field arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLMultiBlockDataW.explanation: Specify the selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to extract from the input dataset.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLMultiBlockDataW.label: Selectors

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLMultiBlockDataW.explanation: Specify the selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to extract from the input dataset.

One data-assembly selector naming blocks to write when ChooseBlocksToWrite is true, as an XPath-like path in the assembly named by Assembly. In the Hierarchy assembly the root is Root and blocks are named after their block names (invalid characters removed) or Block0, Block1, ... when unnamed: "/Root" selects everything, "/Root/Fluid" one top-level block, "//inlet" any block named inlet at any depth. Order and repeated selectors make no difference.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLMultiBlockDataW.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selectors (no static default). Selectors are ignored while ChooseBlocksToWrite is false, ParaView's default.
pitfalls: ChooseBlocksToWrite true is rejected at planning (BLOCK_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE) because no declared comparison accepts missing blocks; extract blocks upstream with pvExtractBlock and export that node instead.

pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPImageDataWrite.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no cell arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPPartitionedDat.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPPartitionedDat.explanation: Select the field data arrays to pass through.

One field-data array (a whole-dataset value not tied to points or cells) name to keep in the VTK XML partitioned dataset (.vtpd) output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then field arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/ServerManager/vtkSIDataArraySelectionProperty.cxx:106-121 (Push: RemoveAllArrays, then enable the listed names)
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPPartitionedDat.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no field arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPPolyDataWriter.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPPolyDataWriter.explanation: Select the field data arrays to pass through.

One field-data array (a whole-dataset value not tied to points or cells) name to keep in the parallel VTK XML (.pvtp) output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then field arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Kept field arrays are written in the piece's FieldData section.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/ServerManager/vtkSIDataArraySelectionProperty.cxx:106-121 (Push: RemoveAllArrays, then enable the listed names)
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPPolyDataWriter.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no field arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPPolyDataWriter.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPPolyDataWriter.explanation: Where the .vtp piece files go: true stores them in a subfolder named after the summary file without its extension (data/ for Schemaxis's managed name data.pvtp); false puts them directly beside data.pvtp. Only the file layout and the relative paths inside the summary change, not the data, so verification is unaffected; both layouts stay inside the export's managed output folder.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPPolyDataWriter.label: Store data in subdirectory
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPPolyDataWriter.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from true (pieces in a subfolder).
pitfalls: When copying the export elsewhere, move data.pvtp together with its pieces (and the subfolder when true), or the summary's relative references break.

sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/ServerManager/vtkSIDataArraySelectionProperty.cxx:106-121 (Push: RemoveAllArrays, then enable the listed names)
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPRectilinearGri.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no cell arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

One point (node) array name to keep in the parallel VTK XML (.pvtr) output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/ServerManager/vtkSIDataArraySelectionProperty.cxx:106-121 (Push: RemoveAllArrays, then enable the listed names)
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPRectilinearGri.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no point arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.explanation: The mode uses for writing the file's data i.e. ascii, binary, appended binary.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.explanation: Select the edge data arrays to pass through.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.label: Edge Data Arrays

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.explanation: Select the edge data arrays to pass through.

One graph-edge array name to keep in the parallel VTK XML (.pvts) output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then edge arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Only graphs carry edge data and this writer accepts structured grids, so entries here match nothing.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.explanation: Select the field data arrays to pass through.

One field-data array (a whole-dataset value not tied to points or cells) name to keep in the parallel VTK XML (.pvts) output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then field arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Kept field arrays are written in the piece's FieldData section.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/ServerManager/vtkSIDataArraySelectionProperty.cxx:106-121 (Push: RemoveAllArrays, then enable the listed names)
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no field arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.explanation: Integer width of the size headers in front of each binary or appended data block of the VTK XML files. UInt64 is needed when one array's data exceeds 4 GiB; UInt32 gives marginally smaller files for readers limited to 32-bit headers. It does not affect Ascii output or the stored values.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.label: Header type
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from UInt64 (default_values 64), although the upstream description says the default is UInt32.
pitfalls: If an older third-party reader rejects the file, try UInt32, provided no array exceeds 4 GiB.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.explanation: Whether the writer adds the dataset's current time as a TimeValue field-data array in the XML file, so that readers can recover the time from the file alone. Schemaxis records the published time in its receipt instead, and switches this output off whenever the option is omitted.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.label: Write time value
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPStructuredGrid.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis sets false when omitted, overriding ParaView's initial value (true).
pitfalls: Enabling it adds a TimeValue field array that the input node lacks, so exact verification is likely to fail for time-dependent inputs.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPTableWriter/pr.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no field arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPTableWriter/pr.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPTableWriter/pr.explanation: Where the .vtt piece files go: true stores them in a subfolder named after the summary file without its extension (data/ for Schemaxis's managed name data.pvtt); false puts them directly beside data.pvtt. Only the file layout and the relative paths inside the summary change, not the data, so verification is unaffected; both layouts stay inside the export's managed output folder.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPTableWriter/pr.label: Store data in subdirectory
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPTableWriter/pr.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from true (pieces in a subfolder).
pitfalls: When copying the export elsewhere, move data.pvtt together with its pieces (and the subfolder when true), or the summary's relative references break.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.explanation: Optional array selection, GhostLevel (ghost-cell layers per piece, ParaView default 1, which adds nothing in a single-piece serial export), UseSubdirectory for the piece layout, and VTK XML storage settings (DataMode, HeaderType, compression, base64 encoding, WriteTimeValue). Omitted settings keep ParaView's values, except WriteTimeValue, which Schemaxis turns off unless you set it.
Select the cell data arrays to pass through.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.label: Cell Data Arrays

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.explanation: Select the cell data arrays to pass through.

One cell (element) array name to keep in the parallel VTK XML (.pvtu) output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then cell arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Kept cell arrays (for example cell-centred solver fields) are written as CellData of the .vtu piece.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/ServerManager/vtkSIDataArraySelectionProperty.cxx:106-121 (Push: RemoveAllArrays, then enable the listed names)
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no cell arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.explanation: Integer width of the size headers in front of each binary or appended data block of the VTK XML files. UInt64 is needed when one array's data exceeds 4 GiB; UInt32 gives marginally smaller files for readers limited to 32-bit headers. It does not affect Ascii output or the stored values.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.label: Header type
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from UInt64 (default_values 64), although the upstream description says the default is UInt32.
pitfalls: If an older third-party reader rejects the file, try UInt32, provided no array exceeds 4 GiB.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.label: Point Data Arrays

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.explanation: Select the point data arrays to pass through.

One point (node) array name to keep in the parallel VTK XML (.pvtu) output, spelled exactly as in the input (case-sensitive). It is used only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then point arrays not listed are left out, and order or repeated names make no difference. Kept point arrays (for example interpolated U or p) are written as PointData of the .vtu piece.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts this list empty and no domain fills it, so with ChooseArraysToWrite true and the list omitted no point arrays are written (the list only matters when ChooseArraysToWrite is true). Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact, semantic or table comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), so this list only applies with a comparison that accepts missing fields, such as geometry.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.explanation: Where the .vtu piece files go: true stores them in a subfolder named after the summary file without its extension (data/ for Schemaxis's managed name data.pvtu); false puts them directly beside data.pvtu. Only the file layout and the relative paths inside the summary change, not the data, so verification is unaffected; both layouts stay inside the export's managed output folder.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.label: Store data in subdirectory
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from true (pieces in a subfolder).
pitfalls: When copying the export elsewhere, move data.pvtu together with its pieces (and the subfolder when true), or the summary's relative references break.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.explanation: Whether the writer adds the dataset's current time as a TimeValue field-data array in the XML file, so that readers can recover the time from the file alone. Schemaxis records the published time in its receipt instead, and switches this output off whenever the option is omitted.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.label: Write time value
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPUnstructuredGr.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis sets false when omitted, overriding ParaView's initial value (true).
pitfalls: Enabling it adds a TimeValue field array that the input node lacks, so exact verification is likely to fail for time-dependent inputs.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPVDWriter.explanation: Settings control the XML encoding: DataMode (ParaView default Appended), CompressorType (default None) and CompressionLevel (default 6), EncodeAppendedData (default false, raw binary), HeaderType (default UInt64) and GhostLevel (default 0), plus optional array filtering. All encodings are lossless; the file name and time-series writing are managed by Schemaxis.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPVDWriter/prope.explanation: Select the cell data arrays to pass through.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPVDWriter/prope.label: Cell Data Arrays

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPVDWriter/prope.explanation: Select the cell data arrays to pass through.

One cell-data (per-cell) array name to keep in the PVD export when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; arrays of that kind not listed are dropped before writing. Ignored while ChooseArraysToWrite is false (ParaView's default), when every array is written. Schemaxis rejects ChooseArraysToWrite true with the exact comparison at planning (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because that comparison checks every array against the writer's input; drop arrays upstream with pvPassArrays instead.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPVDWriter/prope.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPartitionedData.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPartitionedData.label: Runtime value

The list is applied only when ChooseArraysToWrite is true; then exactly the listed field arrays are written and the others are dropped. Order and duplicates do not matter; names must match exactly.
pitfalls: ChooseArraysToWrite true is rejected at planning with the exact comparison (ARRAY_SELECTION_UNVERIFIABLE), because the file would lack arrays that comparison requires; to export fewer arrays, remove them upstream with pvPassArrays and export that node.

/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPolyDataWriter/.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvWriteXMLPolyDataWriter/.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvWriteXdmfWriter.explanation: One setting, MeshStaticOverTime (ParaView default false), which writes the mesh only once for a time series. Schemaxis manages the file name and writes one time state per export, so there is no later step to share the mesh with and the cross-step sharing never happens. The setting still changes how a single step is stored: with true, ParaView forces its light-data limit to 1, so heavy data (every array larger than one value) goes into the HDF5 file, and the topology and geometry are stored there as /Topology_<grid> and /Geometry_<grid> datasets. Semantic verification does not depend on it.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 VTK/IO/Xdmf2/vtkXdmfWriter.cxx:330-332 (MeshStaticOverTime forces LightDataLimit to 1, so heavy data goes to the HDF5 file)
ParaView 5.13.3 VTK/IO/Xdmf2/vtkXdmfWriter.cxx:505-515,930-945 (topology and geometry HDF5 datasets become /Topology_<grid> and /Geometry_<grid>)

/$defs/options-pvWriteXdmfWriter/propert.explanation: With true, ParaView writes the topology and geometry of the first time step once and lets later steps reference them. Schemaxis writes one time state per export, so that sharing never happens, but the setting still changes a single step: ParaView forces all heavy data into the HDF5 file (light-data limit 1) and stores topology and geometry as /Topology_<grid> and /Geometry_<grid> HDF5 datasets.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvXMLPartitionedRectiline.label: Runtime value

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvXMLUniformGridAMRReader.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvXMLUnstructuredGridRead.explanation: FileName (required) lists the .vtu file or files; CellArrayStatus and PointArrayStatus choose the arrays read and TimeArray the field-data array that supplies each file's time. /$defs/options-pvXMLUnstructuredGridRead.explanation: Path of one VTK XML unstructured grid file (.vtu) or a .vtu.series index. Listing several paths switches the reader to file-series mode, one file per time step in the order listed. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; absolute paths avoid ambiguity. The value must be a constant.

/$defs/options-pvYoungsMaterialInterface.explanation: Settings name the per-material arrays (volume fractions, optional normals and ordering) and control the reconstruction: fraction thresholds, normal sign, material order, onion-peel normals, axisymmetry and whether full material volumes or only interfaces are output. For 2-D cells, treats the mesh as an axisymmetric section (volume of revolution about the axis) when placing interfaces, so cut positions honour revolved volumes rather than planar areas. It has no effect on 3-D cells. Native name keeps ParaView's spelling.

/$defs/options-pvYoungsMaterialInterface.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from true.
pitfalls: Planar 2-D simulations need false; the default true shifts interfaces toward the axis.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-pvYoungsMaterialInterface.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvYoungsMaterialInterface.explanation: Assigns an ordering cell array to materials, as a flat list of pairs [volume-fraction array, ordering array, …]. In each cell, materials are processed in ascending order of their ordering value (descending with ReverseMaterialOrder), which matters with OnionPeel. Materials without one have ordering 0 and keep their VolumeFractionArrays order.
/$defs/options-pvYoungsMaterialInterface.label: Ordering arrays
/$defs/options-pvYoungsMaterialInterface.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView assigns no ordering arrays (NoDefault hint), so the VolumeFractionArrays order is used.
pitfalls: The list must have an even length with the volume-fraction name first in each pair. Schemaxis rejects an odd length (INVALID_LENGTH) but does not check that the named arrays exist.

/$defs/options-readImageData/properties/.label: File Name

/$defs/options-readImageData/properties/.explanation: Path of the VTK XML image data file (.vti). Exactly one file is accepted, so no file series is read. The value must be a constant, passed when the reader is created.

/$defs/options-reflect.explanation: Choose the mirror plane (Schemaxis default X, the plane x = centre), its position centre (default 0, used only by the X, Y and Z planes) and whether the original is kept beside its reflection (default true). All three are assigned; Schemaxis's X replaces ParaView's native first choice, X Min. FlipAllInputArrays keeps ParaView's default (on).
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/Application/Resources/filters_filtersparallel.xml: filters/ReflectionFilter Plane, Center, CopyInput, FlipAllInputArrays

/$defs/options-reflect/properties/plane.explanation: The value of this property determines which plane to reflect across. If the value is X, Y, or Z, the value of the Center property determines where the plane is placed along the specified axis. The other six options (X Min, X Max, etc.) place the reflection plane at the specified face of the bounding box of the input dataset.
/$defs/options-reflect/properties/plane.label: Plane

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-reflect/properties/plane/.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-reflect/properties/centre.explanation: If the value of the Plane property is X, Y, or Z, then the value of this property specifies the center of the reflection plane.
/$defs/options-reflect/properties/centre.label: Center

/$defs/options-reflect/properties/centre.explanation: If the value of the Plane property is X, Y, or Z, then the value of this property specifies the center of the reflection plane.

/$defs/options-resample.explanation: passPointArrays (Schemaxis default true) and passCellArrays (default false) keep the mesh node's own arrays next to the sampled ones; categorical (default false) samples by nearest neighbour instead of linear interpolation, for integer labels. /$defs/options-resample/properties/passP.defaultMeaning: Schemaxis default: true (ParaView's own default is false).
pitfalls: It never passes the input node's arrays; those are always sampled. The imported native wording "the input's point data" refers to the mesh port.

/$defs/options-slice.explanation: Defines the cutting plane and how the cut is built: origin (Schemaxis default [0, 0, 0]) and normal (default [1, 0, 0], i.e. x+) place the plane, crinkle (default false) keeps whole intersected cells instead of a flat cut, and triangulate (default true) splits cut polygons into triangles. All four are assigned and the slice type is fixed to Plane; slice offset values and the point-merge method are not set by Schemaxis.

/$defs/options-slice/properties/origin.explanation: A point lying on the cutting plane, expressed as [X, Y, Z] in dataset coordinates. Moving it along the normal moves the cut.
/$defs/options-slice/properties/origin.label: Plane origin

/$defs/options-slice/properties/origin/a.explanation: A point lying on the cutting plane, expressed as [X, Y, Z] in dataset coordinates. Moving it along the normal moves the cut.

One coordinate (x, y, then z) of a point on the cutting plane, in dataset coordinate units. Any point on the plane gives the same cut, so only the position along the normal matters: with normal z+, origin [0, 0, 0.5] cuts at z = 0.5.

Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-transform/properties/tran.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-transform/properties/rota.explanation: Rotation angles in degrees about the x, y and z axes through the origin [0, 0, 0]. vtkPVTransform composes RotateZ, RotateX, RotateY, so the points are turned about y first, then x, then z (fixed axes), after scaling and before translation. Positive angles follow the right-hand rule about each positive axis.
/$defs/options-transform/properties/rota.label: Rotation angles
pitfalls: With several non-zero angles the order is y, x, z; chain separate transform nodes with one angle each if you need another order.

/$defs/options-transform/properties/scal.explanation: Factors [sx, sy, sz] multiplying the x, y and z coordinates about the origin, applied before rotation and translation. Equal factors change size or units, e.g. [0.001, 0.001, 0.001] for millimetres to metres; unequal factors stretch the geometry.

/$defs/options-warpScalar.explanation: Selects the warping scalar (field, required) and the displacement: scale (Schemaxis default 1), the warp direction normal (default [0, 0, 1], z+) and useNormal (default true, which ignores the input's own point normals; ParaView's default is false). All defaults are assigned; XYPlane and GenerateEnclosure keep ParaView's defaults (off).

/$defs/options-warpScalar/properties/fie.explanation: Two entries naming the scalar that sets the displacement: the association token POINTS and the array name, e.g. ["POINTS", "height"]. Each point moves by scale times its value along the warp direction, so negative values move points the opposite way.
/$defs/options-warpScalar/properties/fie.label: Scalar field (association and array)
pitfalls: CELLS is rejected with INVALID_ASSOCIATION at planning when the association is written literally and the node uses no runtime expressions; otherwise it is rejected before the first update of that visit because the filter reads one value per point; convert cell data with cellToPoint first.

/$defs/options-warpScalar/properties/fie.explanation: One entry of the two-entry field pair: first the association token POINTS, then the name of a point array on the input, e.g. ["POINTS", "pressure"]. Order matters and both entries are required.
pitfalls: For a multi-component array only the first component is used; compute the quantity you want, e.g. a magnitude, with calculator first.

It applies to every point while useNormal is true, and when useNormal is false only if the input has no point normals.

/$defs/options-wavelet/properties/centre.explanation: One coordinate (x, y, then z) of the centre of the Gaussian peak and the reference of the sinusoids, in the wavelet's coordinates (equal to grid indices). Moving it shifts where RTData peaks.

A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/options-wavelet/properties/centre.label: Runtime value

Raising it strengthens the central peak relative to the ripples.

/$defs/readback.explanation: How an exported file is re-read for verification: null for ParaView's automatic reader, or {"operation": reader, "options": {...}} to use a declared source reader. The file name is always supplied by Schemaxis; only the reader options you author are assigned.
/$defs/readback.label: Readback reader
/$defs/readback.defaultMeaning: Omitted or null: ParaView's OpenDataFile picks the reader from the extension (PLYReader for pvWritePPLYWriter).
pitfalls: CSV table exports, pvWriteJSONImageWriter and pvWriteHoudiniWriter use built-in verifiers and reject a readback reader (INVALID_READER).

/$defs/readback/anyOf/0.explanation: Automatic readback: ParaView opens the file with the reader registered for its extension. Choose it when the default reader loads every array the comparison needs.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1.explanation: Explicit reader: choose it when automatic selection picks the wrong reader or needs options, for example to enable arrays or blocks the comparison must see. Only source readers with exactly one managed file-name property qualify, and that property must not be authored.
pitfalls: Setting the reader's file name fails (MANAGED_FILENAME); Schemaxis injects the exported path.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/0.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvADIOS2CoreImageReader (Reads variables from an ADIOS2 BP file or BP4/BP5 directory as arrays on a uniform image (vtkImageData)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Identifies pvADIOS2CoreImageReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property lists all adios2 arrays that can be read. Based on the dimension info, arrays will be parsed as point or cell data.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/0/properti.label: Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Name of one ADIOS2 variable to load as an image array, spelled as in the BP file. Whether it becomes point or cell data follows from its dimensions; order and duplicates do not matter.
Use the dimension info of the array to populate image dimension.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/0/properti.label: Image Dimension

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: Use the array to populate time steps info.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/0/properti.label: Time step array

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/0/properti.explanation: The dimension of image data is 1 larger than its cell data's dimension.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/0/properti.label: Use dimension array as cell data

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/1.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvADIOS2VTXReader (Reads an ADIOS2 BP file or BP4 directory that embeds a VTK XML schema (VTX), either as a BP attribute or as a vtk.xml subfile, describing image data (vti) or unstructured grid (vtu) content; the output is that dataset, with time steps from the BP steps). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/1/properti.explanation: Identifies pvADIOS2VTXReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/2.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvAMReXBoxLibGridReader (Reads AMReX/BoxLib plotfiles (directories named like plt00000) into a hierarchical-box (overlapping AMR) dataset of cell-centred grid variables, levels 0 to Level). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Identifies pvAMReXBoxLibGridReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Select the cell arrays to read load.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/2/properti.label: Cell Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Name of one cell-centred plotfile variable to load, e.g. density or Temp, as listed in the plotfile Header. Unlisted variables are not read; order does not matter.
pitfalls: If CellArrayStatus is omitted ParaView chooses the initial selection; list the variables later nodes depend on.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Keep AMR blocks that have already been read in memory, so later updates that change the level or array selection, or revisit a time, do not reread them from disk. It does not change the data produced.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/2/properti.label: Cache loaded blocks
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/2/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts with caching off (false).
pitfalls: Caching trades memory for speed; leave it off for large AMR hierarchies or single-pass publications.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: This property specifies the desired level of resolution that will be visible.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/2/properti.label: Level

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Select the point arrays to read load.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/2/properti.label: Point Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/2/properti.explanation: Name of one point (node-centred) array to load, if the plotfile provides any; most AMReX grid variables are cell-centred and appear in CellArrayStatus instead.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/3.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvAMReXBoxLibParticlesReader (Reads particles stored in AMReX plotfiles, producing point data (polydata blocks) with the selected particle components as point arrays; ParticleType names the particle container subdirectory inside each plotfile (ParaView default "particles")). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: Identifies pvAMReXBoxLibParticlesReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Set the type of particles to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/3/properti.label: Particle Type

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: Select the point arrays to read load.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/3/properti.label: Point Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/3/properti.explanation: Name of one particle component (real or integer attribute such as mass or velocity components) to load as a point array. Order does not matter.
pitfalls: If omitted ParaView chooses the initial selection; list components explicitly when later nodes use them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/4.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvAVSUCDReader (Reads AVS Unstructured Cell Data files (.inp, ASCII or binary) into an unstructured grid with optional point (node) and cell arrays). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/4/properti.explanation: Identifies pvAVSUCDReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Names of the cell-data components in the UCD file to read as cell arrays. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/4/properti.label: Cell arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/4/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkAVSucdReader enables every cell array). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/4/properti.explanation: One cell-data label as written in the UCD file. Order does not matter.

Names of the node-data components in the UCD file to read as point arrays. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/4/properti.label: Point arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/4/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkAVSucdReader enables every point array). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/4/properti.explanation: One node-data label as written in the UCD file. Order does not matter.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/5.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvAdaptiveCosmoCore (Reads LANL cosmo-format particle data that an adaptive-sampling preprocessor split into resolution levels (vtkACosmoReader, extension .cosmo)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: Identifies pvAdaptiveCosmoCore as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
The box side length is used to wrap particles around if they exceed rL (or less than 0) in any dimension.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/5/properti.label: Box Size

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: If checked, the data will be read and byte-swapped.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/5/properti.label: Byte Swap

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: Specify the desired level of resolution.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/5/properti.label: Level

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/5/properti.explanation: Width of the integer particle id (tag) stored with each particle: 32-bit or 64-bit. It must match how the file was written, otherwise records are misaligned and positions and velocities are garbage.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/5/properti.label: Tag size
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/5/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from "32-bit". The upstream text describing it as endianness is wrong; ByteSwap controls byte order.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/6.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvBDFReader (Reads a Nastran Bulk Data File (.bdf) in free-field format into an unstructured grid). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/6/properti.explanation: Identifies pvBDFReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/7.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvBYUReader (Reads Movie.BYU geometry files (.g) into polydata made of polygons). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/7/properti.explanation: Identifies pvBYUReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvCGNSSeriesReader (Reads CFD General Notation System files (.cgns, ADF or HDF5 based) into a multiblock dataset organized by base and zone: each zone becomes a structured or unstructured grid and, with LoadPatches, its boundary-condition patches are added beside the volume mesh). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: Identifies pvCGNSSeriesReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Names of the CGNS bases (CGNSBase_t nodes, the top-level groups that hold zones) to read; each selected base becomes one block of the output. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Bases
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkCGNSReader enables only the first base in the file).
