Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Names must match the base names stored in the file exactly; an unknown name selects nothing.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: One base name, spelled as the CGNSBase_t node in the file (often "Base"). Order does not matter and a repeated name adds nothing.

When true, the element connectivity of unstructured zones is read once and reused from memory at later time steps instead of being re-read at every step. It shortens transient reads on a fixed mesh at the cost of memory and does not change the values read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Cache unstructured connectivity
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from false (connectivity re-read at each time step).
pitfalls: VTK documents this cache for time-invariant connectivity; leave it false when the mesh topology changes between time steps (adaptive or remeshed cases).

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: When true, zone point coordinates are read once, stored per base and zone, and reused at later time steps instead of being re-read. It saves read time for transient results on a static mesh at the cost of memory.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Cache mesh points
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from false (coordinates re-read at each time step).
pitfalls: Do not enable it for moving or deforming meshes: cached coordinates would be reused for every time step.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: Names of cell-centred FlowSolution_t fields (CellCenter location) to load as cell data on the zone blocks. Used when DataLocation is "Cell Data"; face-centred fields are chosen in FaceArrayStatus instead. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Cell arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkCGNSReader registers every cell array as disabled, so none is loaded unless ParaView's Load All Variables setting is on). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Omitting this list is the usual reason a CGNS case shows geometry but no fields.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: One cell-centred array name as stored in the file's FlowSolution_t nodes (for example "Pressure" or "Density" in CGNS SIDS naming). Order does not matter.

Debug option: when true, every FlowSolution_t node of a zone is output as its own child block under that zone, instead of the solution for the current time step being attached to the zone mesh. VTK warns that the output may not be correct, so it is meant for inspecting file structure, not for analysis.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Each solution as block (debug)
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from false.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: Specifies whether to read cell or face information from the mesh. Face-based reading is only available if the element connectivity is defined with NGON_n element type.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Data Location

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: When true, mesh coordinates are stored as 64-bit doubles; false stores 32-bit floats and halves coordinate memory. When the file's precision differs from the requested one, the coordinates are converted while reading, which costs time. Field arrays are not affected.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Double-precision mesh
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from true.
pitfalls: Float coordinates lose resolution in large domains with very small cells; keep true unless memory is the constraint.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: Names of face-centred FlowSolution_t fields (FaceCenter location) to load. Used only when DataLocation is "Face Data", which builds the mesh from faces and requires NGON_n element connectivity. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Face arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkCGNSReader registers every face array as disabled). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Ignored while DataLocation is "Cell Data" (the native default); set DataLocation first.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: One face-centred array name as stored in the file. Order does not matter.

Names of CGNS families (Family_t nodes, such as a family grouping wall patches or a fluid region) whose zones and boundary patches are read. Zones or patches tagged with a family that is not selected are skipped; zones without a family are always read. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Families
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkCGNSReader enables every family). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Listing only a boundary family also drops volume zones that belong to another family; list those families too.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: One family name, spelled as the Family_t node in the file. Order does not matter.

When checked, the reader will simply ignore **FlowSolutionPointers** in the CGNS file since they are either incomplete or invalid. To locate unsteady solution, the **UseUnsteadyPattern** option should then be activated.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Ignore FlowSolutionPointers

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: When reading a file-series, if each file in the series does not provide correct time information, the reader will not be able to animate through the file series correctly. Check this to ignore the time information provided by each file.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Ignore Reader Time

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: Toggle whether zone mesh must be read for selected bases/families.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Load Mesh

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: Toggle whether boundary condition patches must be read for selected bases/families.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Load Patches

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: Names of vertex-located FlowSolution_t fields (Vertex location) to load as point data on the zone blocks. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Point arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkCGNSReader registers every point array as disabled). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: One vertex-located array name as stored in the file. Order does not matter.

Index assigned to the first time step when UseUnsteadyPattern matches FlowSolution_t nodes by the time-step index at the end of their names. Only used when UseUnsteadyPattern is true; the value must be 0 or more.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: First unsteady time-step index
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 0.
pitfalls: Match the numbering of the solution node names: if they start at 1, set 1, or each time step is paired with the wrong solution or none.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: When true, vector fields of a 2-D solution (physical dimension 2) get a third component so they behave as 3-D vectors in filters such as glyphs or stream tracing; false keeps the solution's physical dimension (two components). It has no effect on 3-D cases.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Use 3-D vectors
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from true.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.explanation: When true, the reader finds the FlowSolution_t node for each time step by name pattern (nodes whose names end in the time-step index) instead of relying on FlowSolutionPointers. Use it, usually together with IgnoreFlowSolutionPointers, for unsteady files whose pointers are missing or invalid; UnsteadySolutionStartTimestep sets the first index.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.label: Use unsteady pattern
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/8/properti.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from false.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/9.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvCMLMoleculeReader (Reads a Chemical Markup Language file (.cml, an XML description of atoms and bonds) into a vtkMolecule: atoms with element numbers and 3-D positions plus the bonds between them). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/9/properti.explanation: Identifies pvCMLMoleculeReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/10.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvCONVERGECFDCGNSReader (Reads CONVERGE CFD post-processing files written in CGNS (.cgns): the volume mesh, surfaces and parcels (Lagrangian spray or particle data stored in PARCEL_DATA UserDefinedData_t nodes) into a partitioned dataset collection with mesh and parcel datasets). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/10/propert.explanation: Identifies pvCONVERGECFDCGNSReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

One mesh cell-data array name to read, as listed by the file (CONVERGE cell variables of the volume mesh). Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.

One parcel array name to read on the parcel point clouds. Parcel variables stored as _X, _Y and _Z component nodes appear under one name without the suffix and are read as a vector; PARCEL_X/Y/Z themselves are the parcel positions and are not listed. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.

One mesh point-data array name to read (variables stored at mesh vertices). Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/11.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvCONVERGECFDReader (Reads CONVERGE CFD HDF5 post files (.h5) into a partitioned dataset collection: each stream in the file is a top-level group holding its mesh (cell data), surfaces and parcels (point clouds of spray or particle data)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/11/propert.explanation: Identifies pvCONVERGECFDReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

One mesh cell variable to read. Variables stored as NAME_X, NAME_Y and NAME_Z components are offered once, as NAME, and read as a 3-component vector. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.

One parcel variable to read on the parcel point clouds; X/Y/Z component triples are offered once without the suffix, and the parcel positions (PARCEL_X/Y/Z) are not listed. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvCSVReader (Reads delimited text (.csv, .tsv, .txt) into a table (vtkTable): one column per field, typed as numbers when DetectNumericColumns is on (ParaView default), with the first line as column names by default). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12/propert.explanation: Identifies pvCSVReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property indicates whether to add the tab character as a field delimiter to the list of other delimiter characters. This is needed since in the GUI the user can't enter a tab character.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12/propert.label: Add Tab Field Delimiter

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12/propert.explanation: When set to true, the reader will detect numeric columns and create vtkDoubleArray or vtkIntArray for those instead of vtkStringArray.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12/propert.label: Detect Numeric Columns

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12/propert.explanation: This property lists the characters that may be used to separate fields. For example, a value of "," indicates a comma-separated value file. A value of ".:;" indicates that columns may be separated by a period, colon or semicolon. The order of the characters in the text string does not matter.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12/propert.label: Field Delimiter Characters

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12/propert.explanation: If the value of this property is 1, treat the first line of the file as headers.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12/propert.label: Have Headers

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12/propert.explanation: Whether to merge successive delimiters. Use this if (for example) your fields are separated by spaces but you don't know exactly how many.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12/propert.label: Merge Consecutive Delimiters

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12/propert.explanation: This property indicates whether to use the string delimiter.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/12/propert.label: Use String Delimiter

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/13.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvCesium3DTilesReader (Reads a Cesium 3D Tiles tileset (the tileset .json file and the glTF, GLB or B3DM tiles it references) into a partitioned dataset collection with one partitioned dataset per tile). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/13/propert.explanation: Identifies pvCesium3DTilesReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Level in the tree we read tiles from.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/13/propert.label: Level

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/14.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvCityGMLReader (Reads a CityGML (.gml) city model into a multiblock dataset: top-level blocks per CityGML element type (buildings, roads, water bodies, vegetation …) labelled by an element field array, with polygonal leaves carrying a gml_id field array and, when textured, tcoords and a texture_uri). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: Identifies pvCityGMLReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Reads buildings between BeginBuildingIndex and EndBuildingIndex - 1 in the file.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/14/propert.label: Begin Building Index

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: Reads buildings between BeginBuildingIndex and EndBuildingIndex - 1 in the file.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/14/propert.label: End Building Index

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: Specify the level of detail (LOD) to read. Valid values are from 0 (least detailed) through 4 (most detailed), default value is 3.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/14/propert.label: LOD

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: Number of buildings to read from the file.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/14/propert.label: Number Of Buildings

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/14/propert.explanation: Certain input files use app:transparency as opacity. Set this field true to show that correctly. The default is false.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/14/propert.label: Use Transparency As Opacity

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/15.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvCompositeCellGridReader (Reads cell-grid data (.dg JSON files, e.g). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/15/propert.explanation: Identifies pvCompositeCellGridReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Select the cell attributes to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/15/propert.label: Cell Attributes

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/15/propert.explanation: Name of one cell attribute (a field defined on the cell grid) to keep, as named in the file. Unlisted attributes are removed after reading; order and duplicates do not matter.
Select the cell types to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/15/propert.label: Cell Types

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/15/propert.explanation: Name of one cell type of the cell grid to keep (for example a DG hexahedron or tetrahedron type, as listed for the file). Cells of unlisted types are removed; order and duplicates do not matter.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/16.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvCosmoReader (Reads binary cosmology particle files in LANL cosmo format (.cosmo, .cosmo64) or Gadget-2 format (vtkPCosmoReader) into an unstructured grid of particles with point arrays velocity, mass, tag and ghost). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/16/propert.explanation: Identifies pvCosmoReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
The box side length is used to wrap particles around if they exceed rL (or less than 0) in any dimension.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/16/propert.label: Box Side Length

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/16/propert.explanation: If checked, the data will be read as the LANL Cosmo format. If unchecked, the data will be read as Gadget-2 format.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/16/propert.label: Cosmo Format

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/16/propert.explanation: The space (in rL units) to extend processor particle ownership for ghost particles/cells. It is needed for correct halo calculation when halos cross processor boundaries in parallel computation.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/16/propert.label: Overlap

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/17.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvDEMReader (Reads a USGS Digital Elevation Model (.dem, the ASCII DEM format) into 2-D uniform image data whose point scalars are elevations; origin and spacing come from the DEM header). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/17/propert.explanation: Identifies pvDEMReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/18.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvDICOMReaderSingleFile (Reads one uncompressed DICOM file (.dcm) into uniform image data with the pixel values as point scalars and the pixel spacing from the header). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/18/propert.explanation: Identifies pvDICOMReaderSingleFile as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/19.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvDICOMReaderdirectory (Reads every DICOM file in one directory as the slices of a single 3-D image volume (uniform image data), the usual layout of CT and MR series). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/19/propert.explanation: Identifies pvDICOMReaderdirectory as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvENZOAMRParticlesReader (Reads particles from an Enzo AMR output (the .hierarchy or .boundary file of a data dump) into a multiblock dataset with one polydata block of particle points per grid). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.explanation: Identifies pvENZOAMRParticlesReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Turns on filtering of particles by location
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.label: Filter Location

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.explanation: This property sets the frequency interval for loading particles.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.label: Frequency

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.explanation: Upper corner [x, y, z] of the axis-aligned box used when FilterLocation is true: particles with any coordinate above it (or below MinLocation) are dropped. Coordinates are in the file's units. ParaView's own documentation calls this the minimum location; the reader uses it as the maximum.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.label: Maximum location
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 0].
pitfalls: Ignored unless FilterLocation is true.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.explanation: One coordinate (x, y, then z) of the maximum corner of the axis-aligned box used to keep particles when FilterLocation is true, in the file's coordinate units. A particle is kept only if every coordinate lies within [MinLocation, MaxLocation], inclusive.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 0] for the whole corner.
pitfalls: With FilterLocation true and both corners left at [0, 0, 0], almost every particle is removed; set both corners.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.explanation: This property sets the minimum 3-D coordinate location by which the particles will be filtered out.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.label: Min Location

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.explanation: One coordinate (x, y, then z) of the minimum corner of the axis-aligned box used to keep particles when FilterLocation is true, in the file's coordinate units. A particle is kept only if every coordinate lies within [MinLocation, MaxLocation], inclusive.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 0] for the whole corner.
pitfalls: With FilterLocation true and both corners left at [0, 0, 0], almost every particle is removed; set both corners.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.explanation: Names of the particle arrays to read (for example particle_mass or velocity components); unlisted arrays are skipped, saving memory and time. Positions are always read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.label: Particle arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the arrays found in the file (there is no static default). Name the arrays explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: ParticleType filtering needs the particle_type array; keep it selected when you filter by type.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.explanation: Name of one particle array to read, spelled as in the file. Order does not matter and a repeated name adds nothing.

Keeps only particles of one Enzo particle type: Dark Matter, Active (Star) or Passive (Tracer), compared with each particle's particle_type value; All Particles disables the test. Choose a type to study one population, e.g. stars formed in a galaxy simulation.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.label: Particle type
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/20/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from All Particles.
pitfalls: If the file has no particle_type array (or it is not selected), every particle is returned regardless of this setting.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/21.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvERFHDF5datareader (Reads ESI Result Format files stored in HDF5 (.erfh5), as written by ESI structural and crash solvers, into a partitioned dataset collection). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/21/propert.explanation: Identifies pvERFHDF5datareader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Names of the blocks stored in the ERF HDF5 file to load; the available names are listed by the file itself. Listing names replaces ParaView’s current selection, and unlisted blocks are not read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/21/propert.label: Blocks to read
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/21/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the file’s block list. Name blocks explicitly when the output must be predictable.
pitfalls: A name that is not in the file reads nothing rather than failing; check the reader’s block list first.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/21/propert.explanation: One data block to read: a child group of the stage such as constant or singlestate (erfheader is always read and multistate is skipped, so neither is offered). Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.

Names of the stages (result sets) stored in the ERF HDF5 file to load; the available names are listed by the file itself. Listing names replaces ParaView’s current selection, and unlisted stages are not read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/21/propert.label: Stages to read
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/21/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the file’s stage list. Name stages explicitly when the output must be predictable.
pitfalls: A name that is not in the file reads nothing rather than failing; check the reader’s stage list first.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/21/propert.explanation: One stage to read: a top-level group of the file (a solver stage, or "post", the link to the default stage). By default only "post" is enabled. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.

One result variable to read, as listed under the file's constant/variable group and converted to lower case by the reader. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/22.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvEnSightMasterServerReader (Reads EnSight data written in parallel through a Server-of-Servers master file (.sos) that lists one .case file per partition; the partitions are combined into one multiblock dataset of EnSight parts with the selected node and element variables). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/22/propert.explanation: Identifies pvEnSightMasterServerReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property indicates the byte order of the binary file(s).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/22/propert.label: Byte Order

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/22/propert.explanation: This property lists which cell-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/22/propert.label: Cell Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/22/propert.explanation: One EnSight per-element variable to load from the case files listed in the .sos master file, named as in their VARIABLE section. Listing names loads exactly those cell variables.
This property lists which point-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/22/propert.label: Point Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/22/propert.explanation: One EnSight per-node variable to load from the case files listed in the .sos master file, named as in their VARIABLE section. Listing names loads exactly those point variables.
This property indicates which time value to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/22/propert.label: Set Time Value

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/23.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvEnSightReader (Reads an EnSight 6 or EnSight Gold case (.case, ASCII or binary), a post-processing format exported by many CFD and structural solvers (OpenFOAM's foamToEnsight among them)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/23/propert.explanation: Identifies pvEnSightReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property set if we want to tetrahedralize the output to prevent non manifold mesh later (generated by the Ensight Solver).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/23/propert.label: Apply Tetrahedralize

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/23/propert.explanation: This property lists which cell-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/23/propert.label: Cell Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/23/propert.explanation: One EnSight per-element variable to load, named as in the VARIABLE section of the .case file. Listing names loads exactly those cell variables and disables the rest.
This property lists which point-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/23/propert.label: Point Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/23/propert.explanation: One EnSight per-node variable to load, named as in the VARIABLE section of the .case file. Listing names loads exactly those point variables and disables the rest.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/24.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvEnsembleDataReader (Reads a ParaView ensemble table (.pve): a CSV file with a header row in which each further row describes one ensemble member through parameter columns, and the last column gives that member's data file, relative to the .pve file). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/24/propert.explanation: Identifies pvEnsembleDataReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
The index of the dataset in the ensemble.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/24/propert.label: Current Ensemble Member

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvEnzoReader (Reads an Enzo AMR simulation output (the .hierarchy or .boundary file) into a hierarchical-box (overlapping AMR) dataset of the selected cell and point fields, refinement levels 0 to Level). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.explanation: Identifies pvEnzoReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Names of the cell-centred Enzo fields to load, such as Density, Temperature or velocity components. Unlisted fields are not read, which saves memory on deep hierarchies.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.label: Cell arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the fields in the file (there is no static default). Name the fields explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Field names are case-sensitive and must match the Enzo output exactly.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.explanation: Name of one cell-centred Enzo field to load. Order does not matter and a repeated name adds nothing.
This property specifies whether or not units will be converted to CGS.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.label: Convert To CGS

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.explanation: Keep AMR blocks that have already been read in memory, so later updates that change the level or array selection, or revisit a time, do not reread them from disk. It does not change the data produced.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.label: Cache loaded blocks
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts with caching off (false).
pitfalls: Caching trades memory for speed; leave it off for large AMR hierarchies or single-pass publications.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.explanation: This property specifies the desired level of resolution that will be visible.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.label: Level

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.explanation: Names of the point-centred arrays to load, when the Enzo output provides any; most Enzo fields are cell-centred and belong in CellArrayStatus.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.label: Point arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the arrays in the file (there is no static default).

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/25/propert.explanation: Name of one point-centred array to load. Order does not matter.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/27.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvFDSReader (Reads Fire Dynamics Simulator results through the Smokeview .smv file, which lists the other output files). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/27/propert.explanation: Identifies pvFDSReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Specify the selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to extract from the input dataset.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/27/propert.label: Assembly Selectors

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/27/propert.explanation: One path expression into the reader's data assembly. The root node is named after the .smv file (without extension) and has the children Grids, Devices, HRR, Slices and Boundaries, each holding named datasets; "/" selects everything and "//Slices" all slices. Several selectors are combined and their order does not matter.
pitfalls: Node names are made valid by vtkDataAssembly (e.g. spaces replaced), so they may differ slightly from the names in the .smv file.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvFLASHAMRParticlesReader (Reads particles from a FLASH HDF5 checkpoint or plot file into a multiblock dataset of polydata particle points with the selected particle arrays). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.explanation: Identifies pvFLASHAMRParticlesReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Turns on filtering of particles by location
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.label: Filter Location

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.explanation: This property sets the frequency interval for loading particles.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.label: Frequency

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.explanation: Upper corner [x, y, z] of the axis-aligned box used when FilterLocation is true: particles with any coordinate above it (or below MinLocation) are dropped. Coordinates are in the file's units. ParaView's own documentation calls this the minimum location; the reader uses it as the maximum.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.label: Maximum location
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 0].
pitfalls: Ignored unless FilterLocation is true.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.explanation: One coordinate (x, y, then z) of the maximum corner of the axis-aligned box used to keep particles when FilterLocation is true, in the file's coordinate units. A particle is kept only if every coordinate lies within [MinLocation, MaxLocation], inclusive.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 0] for the whole corner.
pitfalls: With FilterLocation true and both corners left at [0, 0, 0], almost every particle is removed; set both corners.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.explanation: This property sets the minimum 3-D coordinate location by which the particles will be filtered out.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.label: Min Location

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.explanation: One coordinate (x, y, then z) of the minimum corner of the axis-aligned box used to keep particles when FilterLocation is true, in the file's coordinate units. A particle is kept only if every coordinate lies within [MinLocation, MaxLocation], inclusive.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 0] for the whole corner.
pitfalls: With FilterLocation true and both corners left at [0, 0, 0], almost every particle is removed; set both corners.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.explanation: Names of the particle arrays to read (for example particle_mass or velocity components); unlisted arrays are skipped, saving memory and time. Positions are always read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.label: Particle arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the arrays found in the file (there is no static default). Name the arrays explicitly when later nodes depend on them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/28/propert.explanation: Name of one particle array to read, spelled as in the file. Order does not matter and a repeated name adds nothing.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/29.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvFacetReader (Reads a Facet file (.facet): a simple ASCII format listing point coordinates and the polygons connecting them, producing polygonal data). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/29/propert.explanation: Identifies pvFacetReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvFidesJSONReader (Reads ADIOS2 data through Fides using an explicit Fides data model given as a JSON file, which describes how ADIOS2 variables form coordinates, cells and fields). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.explanation: Identifies pvFidesJSONReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property lists which cell-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.label: Cell Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.explanation: Name of one cell-centred array to read, as defined by the Fides data model. Order and duplicates do not matter; arrays not listed are not loaded.

Whether the data read by Fides are converted to native VTK datasets (true) or left in VTK-m form. Downstream ParaView filters generally need VTK datasets, so keep the default unless you know the following steps accept VTK-m data.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.label: Convert to VTK
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from true.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.explanation: This property allows Fides to close gaps between blocks of structured grids by utilizing shared points.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.label: Create shared points

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.explanation: Flat list of [source name, ADIOS2 engine] pairs choosing the engine used for each Fides data source, e.g. ["source", "BPFile"]. ADIOS2 engines include BP file engines and the SST staging engine; choosing SST switches the reader to streaming mode. Unlisted sources use the BP file engine.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.label: Data source engines
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no engine is assigned, so Fides uses the BP engine.
pitfalls: Give an even number of entries; each source name must match a data source of the data model.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.explanation: One entry of the flat engine list: entries alternate data-source name, then engine name (for example "source" followed by "BPFile").

Flat list of [source name, path] pairs telling the reader where each data source named in the JSON data model is: a BP file or directory for file engines, or a stream name for staging engines, e.g. ["source", "/data/run/output.bp"]. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; absolute paths avoid ambiguity. The value must be a constant.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.label: Data source paths
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no paths are assigned, so the reader has no data to open. Provide one pair per data source.
pitfalls: Give an even number of entries, alternating source name and path.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.explanation: One entry of the flat path list: entries alternate data-source name (as in the JSON data model), then the path or stream name for that source.
This property lists which field arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.label: Field Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.explanation: Name of one field (whole-dataset) array to read, such as a scalar time or step value defined by the Fides data model. Order and duplicates do not matter.
This property lists which point-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.label: Point Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.explanation: Name of one point-centred array to read, as defined by the Fides data model. Order and duplicates do not matter; arrays not listed are not loaded.

Reads the data as a stream, one step at a time as the writer releases it, instead of random access to all stored time steps. It is used for staging engines (SST) and BP5 streaming, and is switched on automatically when an SST engine is set.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.label: Stream steps
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/30/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from false.
pitfalls: Leave it false for files on disk; streaming mode is meant for live staging engines that deliver steps one after another.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvFidesReader (Reads ADIOS2 output through the Fides library, which maps ADIOS2 variables to meshes using a data model; for a BP file or BP4/BP5 directory written with Fides metadata the data model is found automatically). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.explanation: Identifies pvFidesReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property lists which cell-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.label: Cell Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.explanation: Name of one cell-centred array to read, as defined by the Fides data model. Order and duplicates do not matter; arrays not listed are not loaded.
This property determines whether data should be converted to VTK or stay in VTK-m format.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.label: Convert To VTK

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.explanation: This property allows Fides to close gaps between blocks of structured grids by utilizing shared points.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.label: Create shared points

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.explanation: Flat list of [source name, ADIOS2 engine] pairs choosing the engine used for each Fides data source, e.g. ["source", "BPFile"]. ADIOS2 engines include BP file engines and the SST staging engine; choosing SST switches the reader to streaming mode. Unlisted sources use the BP file engine.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.label: Data source engines
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no engine is assigned, so Fides uses the BP engine.
pitfalls: Give an even number of entries; each source name must match a data source of the data model.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.explanation: One entry of the flat engine list: entries alternate data-source name, then engine name (for example "source" followed by "BPFile").
This property lists which field arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.label: Field Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.explanation: Name of one field (whole-dataset) array to read, such as a scalar time or step value defined by the Fides data model. Order and duplicates do not matter.
This property lists which point-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.label: Point Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.explanation: Name of one point-centred array to read, as defined by the Fides data model. Order and duplicates do not matter; arrays not listed are not loaded.

Reads the data as a stream, one step at a time as the writer releases it, instead of random access to all stored time steps. It is used for staging engines (SST) and BP5 streaming, and is switched on automatically when an SST engine is set.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.label: Stream steps
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/31/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from false.
pitfalls: Leave it false for files on disk; streaming mode is meant for live staging engines that deliver steps one after another.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvFlashReader (Reads output of the FLASH astrophysics code (HDF5 plot or checkpoint files) into an overlapping AMR (hierarchical box) dataset: nested refinement levels of uniform blocks with cell-centred variables). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32/propert.explanation: Identifies pvFlashReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Names of the cell-centred variables to load from the FLASH file, such as density or pressure fields. Listing names loads exactly those arrays and disables every other array the file offers; an empty list loads none. Fewer arrays mean less memory and faster reads.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32/propert.label: Cell arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView takes the initial selection from the reader, and VTK's AMR readers start with every array disabled, so omitting this usually loads no fields. Name the arrays explicitly.
pitfalls: Names must match the variable names stored in the file exactly; a misspelt name yields no array.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32/propert.explanation: One cell-centred variable name to load, spelled as stored in the FLASH file. Order does not matter and a repeated name adds nothing.

Keep AMR blocks that have already been read in memory, so later updates that change the level or array selection, or revisit a time, do not reread them from disk. It does not change the data produced.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32/propert.label: Cache loaded blocks
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts with caching off (false).
pitfalls: Caching trades memory for speed; leave it off for large AMR hierarchies or single-pass publications.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32/propert.explanation: This property specifies the desired level of resolution that will be visible.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32/propert.label: Level

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32/propert.explanation: Names of point-centred arrays to load. This reader lists only cell-centred variables from the file (its array setup registers cell arrays only), so there is normally nothing to select here; use CellArrayStatus and convert with cellToPoint if you need point data.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32/propert.label: Point arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView takes the (normally empty) selection from the reader.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/32/propert.explanation: One point-centred array name to load. The reader normally offers none, so entries here usually have no effect.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/33.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvFluentCFFCaseReader (Reads ANSYS Fluent results in the HDF5-based Common Fluids Format: the case file (.cas.h5) and, automatically, the data file of the same name (.dat.h5)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/33/propert.explanation: Identifies pvFluentCFFCaseReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Names of the cell-centred solution fields to read from the .dat.h5 file (for example pressure, velocity or temperature as named by Fluent). Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/33/propert.label: Cell arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/33/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkFLUENTCFFReader enables every cell array). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/33/propert.explanation: One cell array name exactly as the reader lists it for the file. Order does not matter.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/34.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvFluentCaseReader (Reads ANSYS Fluent legacy case files (.cas, or .msh mesh files) and the data file whose name replaces the extension with .dat, producing a multiblock dataset of unstructured grids with cell-centred fields). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/34/propert.explanation: Identifies pvFluentCaseReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Names of the cell-centred solution fields to read from the .dat file, as the reader lists them for the case. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/34/propert.label: Cell arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/34/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkFLUENTReader enables every cell array). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/34/propert.explanation: One Fluent cell array name as listed by the reader. Order does not matter.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/35.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvGDALRasterReader (Reads a GIS raster (GeoTIFF, DEM, ERDAS and the other formats supported by GDAL) into a uniform grid (vtkUniformGrid, supporting blanking of no-data pixels) whose bands are cell-data arrays, one cell per raster pixel). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/35/propert.explanation: Identifies pvGDALRasterReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Sets which GDAL bands to load from the file.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/35/propert.label: Cell Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/35/propert.explanation: Name of one raster band array to load, as listed by the reader for the file. Order and duplicates do not matter; unlisted bands are not loaded.
pitfalls: Band names depend on the file; with CollateBands true, colour bands appear as one combined array rather than separate bands.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/35/propert.explanation: Sets if bands are collated in one scalar array or not. Currently we collate bands into RGB, RGBA, gray alpha and pallete. The default is true.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/35/propert.label: Collate Bands

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/35/propert.explanation: Set the desired width and height of the image.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/35/propert.label: Target Dimensions

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/35/propert.explanation: One output size in pixels: first the width (x), then the height (y). A smaller size makes GDAL resample the raster to fewer pixels, which speeds up large images; -1 keeps the raster's own size along that axis.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/35/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [-1, -1] (native size).

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/36.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvGDALVectorReader (Reads one layer of a GIS vector file (Shapefile, GeoJSON, KML, GML, DXF and other GDAL vector formats) into polydata: points, lines and polygons with the feature attributes as cell-data arrays). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/36/propert.explanation: Identifies pvGDALVectorReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Zero-based index of the layer to read from a multi-layer GDAL vector source (for example one table of a GeoPackage or one layer of a shapefile directory). Only this layer is read unless AppendFeatures combines all layers.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/36/propert.label: Active layer
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/36/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 0, the first layer.
pitfalls: Layer order is defined by the data source, not alphabetically; inspect the source with GDAL (ogrinfo) if the wrong features appear.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/36/propert.explanation: Set whether feature IDs should be generated. Some GDAL primitives (e.g., a polygon with a hole in its interior) are represented by multiple VTK cells. If you wish to identify the primitive responsible for a VTK cell, turn this on. It is off by default for backwards compatibility. The array of feature IDs will be the active cell-data pedigree IDs.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/36/propert.label: Add Feature Ids

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/36/propert.explanation: Set whether features are appended to a single vtkPolyData. Turning the option on is useful when a shapefile has a number of features which could otherwise lead to a huge multiblock structure.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/36/propert.label: Append Features

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/37.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvGaussianCubeReader (Reads a Gaussian Cube file (.cube) produced by the Gaussian quantum-chemistry package). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/37/propert.explanation: Identifies pvGaussianCubeReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvGenericIOMultiBlockReader (Reads HACC GenericIO particle files (.gio) into a multiblock dataset with one unstructured-grid block per block stored in the file (usually one per writing MPI rank), vtkPGenericIOMultiBlockReader). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.explanation: Identifies pvGenericIOMultiBlockReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Method used to assign blocks to processes.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.label: Block Assignment Strategy

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.explanation: Which data array in the file contains the halo ids. This is used with the halo ids to load to determine which points to load.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.label: Halo Id

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.explanation: Only load in points with these halo ids from the file. If no halo ids are specified, load all the points.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.label: Halos To Load

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.explanation: One halo id to load; only particles whose value in the HaloId array equals a listed id are read into the blocks. An empty list loads every particle. Order does not matter.
pitfalls: Set HaloId to the array holding halo ids (for example fof_halo_tag); without it the filter has nothing to compare the ids with.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.explanation: Names of the GenericIO variables to load as point arrays on the particles (for example vx, vy, vz, id, fof_halo_tag). Unlisted variables are not read, which saves memory; the coordinate variables named by xAxis, yAxis and zAxis are always read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.label: Particle arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the variables found in the file (there is no static default). Name the arrays explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Names must match the file's variable names exactly.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.explanation: One GenericIO variable name to load as a point array; order and duplicates do not matter.
Method used for reading, either MPI or POSIX is used.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.label: Read Method

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.explanation: Name of the GenericIO variable used as the first (x) particle coordinate. All three coordinate variables must exist in the file, otherwise the reader reports missing coordinate arrays and produces no points.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.label: X coordinate variable
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; there is no static default and ParaView may pick an initial name from the file's variable list. Set it explicitly (HACC files usually call it "x").

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.explanation: Name of the GenericIO variable used as the second (y) particle coordinate. All three coordinate variables must exist in the file, otherwise the reader reports missing coordinate arrays and produces no points.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.label: Y coordinate variable
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; there is no static default and ParaView may pick an initial name from the file's variable list. Set it explicitly (HACC files usually call it "y").

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.explanation: Name of the GenericIO variable used as the third (z) particle coordinate. All three coordinate variables must exist in the file, otherwise the reader reports missing coordinate arrays and produces no points.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.label: Z coordinate variable
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/38/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; there is no static default and ParaView may pick an initial name from the file's variable list. Set it explicitly (HACC files usually call it "z").

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvGenericIOReader (Reads HACC GenericIO particle files (.gio) into one unstructured grid of particles (vtkPGenericIOReader): xAxis, yAxis and zAxis name the coordinate variables, PointArrayStatus chooses the other variables to load, and HalosToLoad with HaloId can restrict reading to particles of chosen halos). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.explanation: Identifies pvGenericIOReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Method used to assign blocks to processes.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.label: Block Assignment Strategy

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.explanation: Which data array in the file contains the halo ids. This is used with the halo ids to load to determine which points to load.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.label: Halo Id

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.explanation: Only load in points with these halo ids from the file. If no halo ids are specified, load all the points.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.label: Halos To Load

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.explanation: One halo id to load; only particles whose value in the HaloId array equals a listed id are read into the particle grid. An empty list loads every particle. Order does not matter.
pitfalls: Set HaloId to the array holding halo ids (for example fof_halo_tag); without it the filter has nothing to compare the ids with.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.explanation: Names of the GenericIO variables to load as point arrays on the particles (for example vx, vy, vz, id, fof_halo_tag). Unlisted variables are not read, which saves memory; the coordinate variables named by xAxis, yAxis and zAxis are always read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.label: Particle arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the variables found in the file (there is no static default). Name the arrays explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Names must match the file's variable names exactly.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.explanation: One GenericIO variable name to load as a point array; order and duplicates do not matter.
If checked, only the data of the RankInQuery and its neighbors will be rendered.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.label: Query Rank Neighbors

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.explanation: Used in combination with QueryRankNeighbors, this property tells the reader to only render the data of this rank and its neighbors.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.label: Rank In Query

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.explanation: Method used for reading, either MPI or POSIX is used.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.label: Read Method

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.explanation: Name of the GenericIO variable used as the first (x) particle coordinate. All three coordinate variables must exist in the file, otherwise the reader reports missing coordinate arrays and produces no points.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.label: X coordinate variable
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; there is no static default and ParaView may pick an initial name from the file's variable list. Set it explicitly (HACC files usually call it "x").

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.explanation: Name of the GenericIO variable used as the second (y) particle coordinate. All three coordinate variables must exist in the file, otherwise the reader reports missing coordinate arrays and produces no points.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.label: Y coordinate variable
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; there is no static default and ParaView may pick an initial name from the file's variable list. Set it explicitly (HACC files usually call it "y").

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.explanation: Name of the GenericIO variable used as the third (z) particle coordinate. All three coordinate variables must exist in the file, otherwise the reader reports missing coordinate arrays and produces no points.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.label: Z coordinate variable
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/39/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; there is no static default and ParaView may pick an initial name from the file's variable list. Set it explicitly (HACC files usually call it "z").

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvH5PartReader (Reads H5Part particle files (.h5part, an HDF5 layout used by accelerator and plasma codes) into polydata points with the selected particle arrays; every step stored in the file becomes a time step (time values from the file, or the step index when they are missing)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.explanation: Identifies pvH5PartReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

When true, one vertex cell is created per particle; false produces points and point arrays only. Many ParaView filters and representations operate on cells, so keep it on unless only coordinates are needed and memory is tight.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.label: Generate vertex cells
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from true (the VTK class itself defaults to false).

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.explanation: When true, a request for a time before the first or after the last stored step returns an empty dataset; when false the reader clamps to the first or last step. Turn it on when combining with data that span a longer time so particles do not appear frozen.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.label: Mask out-of-range times
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from false.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.explanation: This property lists which point-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.label: Point Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.explanation: One particle array name to read, as stored in the file's step groups (for example px or id). Scalar arrays named like name_0, name_1, name_2 are combined into one vector array by the reader's default. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
This property lists which point array to use for coordinates.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.label: Xarray

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.explanation: This property lists which point array to use for coordinates.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.label: Yarray

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.explanation: This property lists which point array to use for coordinates.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/40/propert.label: Zarray

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/41.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvHDF5RageReader (Reads RAGE simulation output stored in HDF5 through an ASCII descriptor that lists the data files and the type and order of the variables (ParaView registers the .h5rage extension; the native text calls it a .pio file)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/41/propert.explanation: Identifies pvHDF5RageReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Variables written to the data files are described in the .pio file and are presented for selection. Only selected variables are loaded for a time step.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/41/propert.label: Point Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/41/propert.explanation: One RAGE variable listed in the descriptor, loaded as a point array of the image for each time step. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/42.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvHDRReader (Reads a Radiance HDR image (.hdr, run-length-encoded RGBE or XYZE) into 2-D uniform image data with 32-bit floating-point colour channels, keeping the full dynamic range for analysis or image-based lighting). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/42/propert.explanation: Identifies pvHDRReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/43.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvHyperTreeGridReader (Reads a VTK XML hypertree grid file (.htg): an adaptive tree-based mesh (vtkHyperTreeGrid) in which each coarse cell is refined recursively, typical of AMR codes). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/43/propert.explanation: Identifies pvHyperTreeGridReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

This property sets the bounding box to select HyperTrees. HyperTrees completely included or intersecting with the bounding box will be selected and fully loaded (no partial tree). 	 The 6 fields are coordinates of the bounding box, in the following order: Xmin, Xmax, Ymin, Ymax, Zmin, Zmax.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/43/propert.label: Bounding Box By Coordinates

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/43/propert.explanation: One bound of the selection box, in the order Xmin, Xmax, Ymin, Ymax, Zmin, Zmax. Trees completely inside or intersecting the box are loaded whole; trees outside it are skipped.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/43/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from -1.79769e+308 to 1.79769e+308 on each axis, so every tree is loaded.
pitfalls: Trees are not cut at the box; clip afterwards when an exact boundary is needed.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/43/propert.explanation: This property sets the maximum level to load. Setting it to 1 shows the coarse grid of trees, and setting it at or past maximum level of the data will load the data at finest resolution. When set to a value between (excluded) 1 and the maximum level of the trees, data will be loaded at the required lower resolution, considerably faster.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/43/propert.label: Maximum Number Of Levels
