/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/44.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvIGESReader (Reads a IGES CAD file through OpenCASCADE and tessellates its B-rep faces into triangles, giving a multiblock dataset with one polydata block per shape (named from the file, or Unnamed) and a per-cell Colors array from the CAD colours). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/44/propert.explanation: Identifies pvIGESReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Limits the angle between two subsequent segments.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/44/propert.label: Angular Deflection

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/44/propert.explanation: Limits the distance between a curve and the resulting tesselation.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/44/propert.label: Linear Deflection

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/44/propert.explanation: Determines if 1D cells will be read. If enabled, surface boundaries are read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/44/propert.label: Read Wire

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/44/propert.explanation: Determines if the deflection values are relative to object size.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/44/propert.label: Relative Deflection

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvIOSSCellGridReader (Reads IOSS databases (Exodus, including the discontinuous-Galerkin .exdg variant) into a partitioned dataset collection whose partitions are cell grids (vtkCellGrid), ParaView's representation for higher-order and DG cells with attributes defined per cell type). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: Identifies pvIOSSCellGridReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Geometric locations can include displacements. When this option is on, the nodal positions are 'displaced' by the standard EXODUS displacement vector. If displacements are turned 'off', the user can explicitly add them by applying a warp filter.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Apply Displacements

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: Specify the selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to extract from the input dataset.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Assembly Selectors

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One path expression into an assembly defined in the file (an IOSS/Exodus grouping of blocks and sets), for example "//Low". Every block or set under a selected node is read in addition to those enabled by the name lists. Only meaningful when the file defines assemblies.
When displacements are being applied, they are scaled by this amount. Set to 1 for no scaling.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Displacement Magnitude

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: Select the edge sets fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Edge Set Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One field defined on edge sets to read. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the edge sets to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Edge Sets

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One edge set to read: a named group of mesh edges. Sets are off by default (vtkIOSSReader); listing names enables exactly these.
Select the element blocks fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Element Block Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One element (cell) field to read on element blocks, such as stress, plastic strain or a material property, named as listed by the reader. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the element blocks to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Element Blocks

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One element block to read, by its name in the file (e.g. block_1): an element block holds the cells of one element type and usually one material, output as a cell grid partition. All blocks of this type are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the element sets fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Element Set Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One field defined on element sets to read. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the element sets to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Element Sets

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One element set to read: a named subset of elements that may span several blocks. Sets are off by default (vtkIOSSReader); listing names enables exactly these.
Select the face sets fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Face Set Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One field defined on face sets to read. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the face sets to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Face Sets

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One face set to read: a named group of mesh faces. Sets are off by default (vtkIOSSReader); listing names enables exactly these.
Set the character used to separate suffix from the field.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Field Suffix Separator

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: To limit reading a subset of files in spatial file-series, specify a valid range. You may also use **FileStride** to step over files in this range.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: File Range

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One bound of the range of spatial partitions read, as zero-based partition ranks (the r in name.e.N.r): the first value is the first rank read and the second is one past the last (exclusive), stepped by FileStride. When the first is not less than the second, range and stride are ignored and every partition is read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, -1], an empty range that reads all partitions.
pitfalls: To read partitions 0 to 3 give [0, 4], not [0, 3].

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: Specify the stride to use when reading a subset of files as dictated by the **FileRange**.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: File Stride

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: When checked, the reader will add a cell array called 'file_id' indicate which partitioned file the cell came from.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Generate File Id

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: Set whether the reader should treat numeric suffices for a vector field as vector components of a vtkDataArray. By default, fields with numeric suffices are not grouped into a single vtkDataArray.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Group Numeric Vector Field Components

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: Names of the nodal (point) fields to read, i.e. fields of the node block shared by every block and set, such as displacement, velocity or temperature. vtkIOSSReader enables all fields by default; listing names keeps only these. (The ParaView 5.13.3 XML text says "edge blocks" here, which is a copy error.)
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Node block fields
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkIOSSReader enables every field). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/Application/Resources/readers_ioioss.xml: sources/IOSSCellGridReader NodeBlockFields (documentation says edge blocks)

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One nodal field to read: point data shared by all blocks, such as displacement, velocity or temperature. The native label text says "edge blocks", but this selects node-block (point) fields. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the node sets fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Node Set Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One field defined on node sets (values stored only for the set's nodes) to read. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the node sets to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Node Sets

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One node set to read: a named group of nodes, typically where a boundary condition or load is applied, output as a vertex partition. Sets are off by default (vtkIOSSReader); listing names enables exactly these.

When set to true (default), the reader will read all files to determine structure of the dataset because some files might have certain blocks that other files don't have. Set to false if you are sure that all files have the same structure, i.e. same blocks and sets. When set to false, the reader will only read the first file to determine the structure. which is faster than reading all files.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Read All Files To Determine Structure

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: When checked, the reader will read global fields, if available.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Read Global Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: When checked, the reader will read 'ids' and 'element_side' fields, if available.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Read Ids

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: When checked, the reader will read quality assurance and information records, if available.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Read QA And Information Records

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: This reader can lookup additional related files using pattern matching based on the files provided. This is useful to lookup restarted results, for example. To avoid this behavior, uncheck this property.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Scan For Related Files

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: Select the side sets fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Side Set Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One field defined on side sets (for example a pressure or flux on the faces) to read. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the side sets to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Side Sets

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One side set to read: named element faces or edges, such as a loaded or wetted surface, output as a surface partition. Sets are off by default (vtkIOSSReader); listing names enables exactly these.
Select the structured blocks fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Structured Block Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One field to read on structured blocks, named as listed by the reader. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the structured blocks to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.label: Structured Blocks

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/45/propert.explanation: One structured block (an i, j, k zone, as found in CGNS databases read through IOSS) to read. All blocks of this type are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvIOSSReader (Reads Exodus II and CGNS databases through Sandia's IOSS library into a partitioned dataset collection: one partitioned dataset per selected block or set, organized in an assembly by entity type). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: Identifies pvIOSSReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Geometric locations can include displacements. When this option is on, the nodal positions are 'displaced' by the standard EXODUS displacement vector. If displacements are turned 'off', the user can explicitly add them by applying a warp filter.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Apply Displacements

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: Specify the selectors for the data assembly chosen using **Assembly** to choose the blocks to extract from the input dataset.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Assembly Selectors

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One path expression into an assembly defined in the file (an IOSS/Exodus grouping of blocks and sets), for example "//Low". Every block or set under a selected node is read in addition to those enabled by the name lists. Only meaningful when the file defines assemblies.
This reader can cache the data that it read across different time steps. The default is off.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Caching

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: When displacements are being applied, they are scaled by this amount. Set to 1 for no scaling.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Displacement Magnitude

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: Select the edge blocks fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Edge Block Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One field defined on edge blocks to read. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the edge blocks to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Edge Blocks

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One edge block to read: a block of one-dimensional edge entities with their own connectivity (Exodus edge blocks), separate from the element blocks. All blocks of this type are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the edge sets fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Edge Set Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One field defined on edge sets to read. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the edge sets to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Edge Sets

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One edge set to read: a named group of mesh edges. Sets are off by default (vtkIOSSReader); listing names enables exactly these.
Select the element blocks fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Element Block Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One element (cell) field to read on element blocks, such as stress, plastic strain or a material property, named as listed by the reader. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the element blocks to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Element Blocks

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One element block to read, by its name in the file (e.g. block_1): an element block holds the cells of one element type and usually one material, output as a unstructured grid partition. All blocks of this type are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the element sets fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Element Set Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One field defined on element sets to read. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the element sets to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Element Sets

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One element set to read: a named subset of elements that may span several blocks. Sets are off by default (vtkIOSSReader); listing names enables exactly these.
Select the face blocks fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Face Block Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One field defined on face blocks to read. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the face blocks to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Face Blocks

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One face block to read: a block of face entities with their own connectivity (Exodus face blocks), separate from the element blocks. All blocks of this type are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the face sets fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Face Set Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One field defined on face sets to read. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the face sets to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Face Sets

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One face set to read: a named group of mesh faces. Sets are off by default (vtkIOSSReader); listing names enables exactly these.
Set the character used to separate suffix from the field.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Field Suffix Separator

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: To limit reading a subset of files in spatial file-series, specify a valid range. You may also use **FileStride** to step over files in this range.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: File Range

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One bound of the range of spatial partitions read, as zero-based partition ranks (the r in name.e.N.r): the first value is the first rank read and the second is one past the last (exclusive), stepped by FileStride. When the first is not less than the second, range and stride are ignored and every partition is read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, -1], an empty range that reads all partitions.
pitfalls: To read partitions 0 to 3 give [0, 4], not [0, 3].

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: Specify the stride to use when reading a subset of files as dictated by the **FileRange**.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: File Stride

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: When checked, the reader will add a cell array called 'file_id' indicate which partitioned file the cell came from.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Generate File Id

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: Set whether the reader should treat numeric suffices for a vector field as vector components of a vtkDataArray. By default, fields with numeric suffices are not grouped into a single vtkDataArray.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Group Numeric Vector Field Components

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: Set whether to merge entity blocks into a single block. This is useful only when the format is EXODUS.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Merge Exodus Entity Blocks

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: Names of the nodal (point) fields to read, i.e. fields of the node block shared by every block and set, such as displacement, velocity or temperature. vtkIOSSReader enables all fields by default; listing names keeps only these. (The ParaView 5.13.3 XML text says "edge blocks" here, which is a copy error.)
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Node block fields
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkIOSSReader enables every field). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/Application/Resources/readers_ioioss.xml: sources/IOSSReader NodeBlockFields (documentation says edge blocks)

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One nodal field to read: point data shared by all blocks, such as displacement, velocity or temperature. The native label text says "edge blocks", but this selects node-block (point) fields. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the node sets fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Node Set Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One field defined on node sets (values stored only for the set's nodes) to read. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the node sets to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Node Sets

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One node set to read: a named group of nodes, typically where a boundary condition or load is applied, output as a vertex partition. Sets are off by default (vtkIOSSReader); listing names enables exactly these.

When set to true (default), the reader will read all files to determine structure of the dataset because some files might have certain blocks that other files don't have. Set to false if you are sure that all files have the same structure, i.e. same blocks and sets. When set to false, the reader will only read the first file to determine the structure. which is faster than reading all files.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Read All Files To Determine Structure

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: When checked, the reader will read global fields, if available.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Read Global Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: When checked, the reader will read 'ids' and 'element_side' fields, if available.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Read Ids

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: When checked, the reader will read quality assurance and information records, if available.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Read QA And Information Records

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: Node related data, including point coordinates, point field data etc. is typically shared between all blocks and sets. By default, the reader will remove unused points for each block or set. To avoid this, set this flag to false.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Remove Unused Points

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: This reader can lookup additional related files using pattern matching based on the files provided. This is useful to lookup restarted results, for example. To avoid this behavior, uncheck this property.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Scan For Related Files

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: Select the side sets fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Side Set Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One field defined on side sets (for example a pressure or flux on the faces) to read. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the side sets to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Side Sets

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One side set to read: named element faces or edges, such as a loaded or wetted surface, output as a surface partition. Sets are off by default (vtkIOSSReader); listing names enables exactly these.
Select the structured blocks fields / arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Structured Block Fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One field to read on structured blocks, named as listed by the reader. All fields are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.
Select the structured blocks to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.label: Structured Blocks

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/46/propert.explanation: One structured block (an i, j, k zone, as found in CGNS databases read through IOSS) to read. All blocks of this type are enabled by default; listing names keeps only these.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvImageReader (Reads headerless raw binary voxel files (.raw) into uniform image data). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: Identifies pvImageReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property indicates the byte order of the binary file(s).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.label: Data Byte Order

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: This property specifies the minimum and maximum index values of the data in each dimension (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.label: Data Extent

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: One voxel-index bound in the order [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax]; bounds are zero-based and inclusive, so a 256-voxel row is 0 to 255. With ReadAsImageStack and 2-D files, the z range is set from the number of files.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] (one voxel).

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: The coordinate contained in this property specifies the position of the point with index (0,0,0).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.label: Data Origin

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: One coordinate (x, y, then z) of the world position of voxel index (0, 0, 0), in dataset units; it shifts the whole image without resampling.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 0].

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: The value of this property indicates the scalar type of the pixels/voxels in the file(s): short, int, float ...
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.label: Data Scalar Type

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: This property specifies the size of a voxel in each dimension.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.label: Data Spacing

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: Voxel size along one axis (x, y, then z) in dataset units; the image spans spacing times (voxel count minus 1) along that axis.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 1, 1].
pitfalls: Raw files store no units; use the same length unit as the data you will combine with this image.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: This property indicates whether the file(s) in this dataset contain slices (2D) or volumes (3D).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.label: File Dimensionality

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: This property determines whether the data originates in the lower left corner (on) or the upper left corner (off). Most scientific data is written with a right-handed axes that originates in the lower left corner. However, several 2D image file formats write the image from the upper left corner.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.label: File Lower Left

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: This property specifies the number of components the scalar value at each pixel or voxel has (e.g., RGB - 3 scalar components).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.label: Number Of Scalar Components

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: When set, the reader will read the set of files as an image stack, rather than a temporal file series.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.label: Read As Image Stack

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.explanation: This property contains a text string listing a name to assign to the point-centered data array read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/47/propert.label: Scalar Array Name

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/48.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvJPEGSeriesReader (Reads JPEG images (.jpg, .jpeg) into uniform image data with 8-bit greyscale or RGB point scalars). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/48/propert.explanation: Identifies pvJPEGSeriesReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Set the spacing to use for the image output by this reader.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/48/propert.label: Data Spacing

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/48/propert.explanation: Pixel size along one axis (x, y, then z between stacked slices) in your chosen length unit; JPEG files store no physical size, so this sets the image's world dimensions.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/48/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 1, 1].

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/48/propert.explanation: When set, the reader will read the set of files as an image stack, rather than a temporal file series.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/48/propert.label: Read As Image Stack

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvLSDynaReader (Reads an LS-DYNA d3plot database (the d3plot file and its numbered family files d3plot01, d3plot02… holding later states) as a time series). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.explanation: Identifies pvLSDynaReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Select which beam arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.label: Beam Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.explanation: One cell array of the beam elements to read, e.g. "AxialForce", "ShearResultant", "BendingResultant", "AxialStress" or "PlasticStrain".

When true, the output point coordinates are replaced by the deflected (current) coordinates at each time step, so the mesh moves with the solution; when false the mesh stays in its original position. This only works when the nodal array "Deflected Coordinates" is selected in PointArrays; the reader then also adds a "Deflection" displacement array either way.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.label: Deformed mesh
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from true.
pitfalls: If PointArrays omits "Deflected Coordinates", the mesh never moves even with this set to true.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.explanation: Select which part arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.label: Part Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.explanation: One part name to load. Each selected part becomes one block of the output; parts not listed are left empty. Names come from the input deck when available, otherwise they follow the pattern "PartXXX" (or "PartXXX (MatlYYY)").
Select which particle arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.label: Particle Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.explanation: One array of the smoothed-particle hydrodynamics (SPH) particles to read, e.g. "InfluenceRadius", "Density", "Pressure" or "Mass".
Select which point-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.label: Point Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.explanation: One nodal (point) array to read, e.g. "Velocity", "Acceleration", "Temperature" or "Deflected Coordinates". Include "Deflected Coordinates" when the mesh should move with the solution.
Should cells that have been deleted (failed structurally, for example) be removed from the mesh?
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.label: Remove Deleted Cells

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.explanation: Select which rigid body arrays to load.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.label: Rigid Body Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.explanation: One array of the rigid-body elements to read. Rigid bodies carry motion data such as velocity but no deflection; use the names the database lists.
Select which road surface arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.label: Road Surface Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.explanation: One array of the road-surface segments to read, e.g. "SegmentID" (which acts as a material id) or the surface velocity.
Select which shell arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.label: Shell Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.explanation: One cell array of the 2-D shell elements to read, e.g. stress or strain at the shell surfaces or resultants, as listed by the database.
Select which solid arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.label: Solid Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.explanation: One cell array of the 3-D solid elements to read, e.g. "Stress" (six-component tensor) or "EffPlastStrn" (effective plastic strain).
Select which thick shell arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.label: Thick Shell Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/49/propert.explanation: One cell array of the thick-shell elements to read, e.g. "Stress", "StressInnerSurf", "StressOuterSurf" or "EffPlastStrn".

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/50.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvLegacyVTKReader (Reads a legacy-format VTK file (.vtk, ASCII or binary), the older single-file format that can hold structured points (image data), a structured, rectilinear or unstructured grid, or polydata, with point and cell arrays; the output type is whatever the file stores). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/50/propert.explanation: Identifies pvLegacyVTKReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/51.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvMFIXReader (Reads MFIX multiphase-flow results: the restart file (.RES) supplies the cylindrical or rectilinear mesh, converted to an unstructured grid, and the SP* files beside it supply transient cell data, with one time step per stored output). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/51/propert.explanation: Identifies pvMFIXReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Select which cell-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/51/propert.label: Cell Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/51/propert.explanation: One MFIX variable to read as cell data (gas and solids volume fractions, velocities, pressure, temperatures and species as named by the reader). Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/52.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvMRCSeriesReader (Reads MRC volumes (.mrc, also .st, .rec, .ali), the format of cryo-electron microscopy maps and tomograms, into uniform image data). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/52/propert.explanation: Identifies pvMRCSeriesReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/53.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvMetaFileSeriesReader (Reads MetaImage files (.mhd header with a separate data file, or single-file .mha), common in ITK-based medical imaging and segmentation, into uniform image data; dimensions, spacing, origin and element type come from the header). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/53/propert.explanation: Identifies pvMetaFileSeriesReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/54.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvMotionFXCFGReader (Reads a MotionFX .cfg motion definition: rigid-body motions (such as translation, rotation or planetary motion) applied to STL bodies listed in the file). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/54/propert.explanation: Identifies pvMotionFXCFGReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Specify the number of timesteps to generate in the animation.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/54/propert.label: Time Resolution

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvMultiResGenericIO (Reads a multi-resolution set of HACC GenericIO files described by a JSON .gios file (vtkPMultiResolutionGenericIOReader)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55/propert.explanation: Identifies pvMultiResGenericIO as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Names of the GenericIO variables to load as particle point arrays at every level (for example vx, vy, vz, id). Unlisted variables are not read; the coordinate variables are always read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55/propert.label: Particle arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the variables of the first level (there is no static default). Name the arrays explicitly.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55/propert.explanation: One GenericIO variable name to load; it is applied to every level that has that variable. Order and duplicates do not matter.
Name of the GenericIO variable used as the first (x) particle coordinate at every resolution level.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55/propert.label: X coordinate variable
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; the reader class starts from "x", but ParaView may pick an initial name from the file's variable list. Set it explicitly.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55/propert.explanation: Name of the GenericIO variable used as the second (y) particle coordinate at every resolution level.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55/propert.label: Y coordinate variable
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; the reader class starts from "y", but ParaView may pick an initial name from the file's variable list. Set it explicitly.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55/propert.explanation: Name of the GenericIO variable used as the third (z) particle coordinate at every resolution level.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55/propert.label: Z coordinate variable
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/55/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; the reader class starts from "z", but ParaView may pick an initial name from the file's variable list. Set it explicitly.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/56.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvNek5000Reader (Reads Nek5000 spectral-element results through a .nek5000 metadata file that names the field-file template and the time steps). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/56/propert.explanation: Identifies pvNek5000Reader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Add Spectral Element Ids as cell-data (optional)
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/56/propert.label: Add Spectral Element Ids as Cell Data

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/56/propert.explanation: Clean the dataset by merging coincident points. May use a lot of memory.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/56/propert.label: Merge Points to Clean grid

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/56/propert.explanation: This property lists which point-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/56/propert.label: PointArrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/56/propert.explanation: One field name to read as a point array, as listed by the reader for this case. Order has no effect; fields not listed are skipped, which saves memory and read time.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvNetCDFMPASreader (Reads one MPAS (Model for Prediction Across Scales) NetCDF file on a global unstructured Voronoi mesh and builds its dual grid as an unstructured grid: MPAS cell variables become point data and vertex variables become cell data). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.explanation: Identifies pvNetCDFMPASreader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property lists which NetCDF dual-grid cell variables to load.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.label: Cell Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.explanation: One MPAS variable to load as cell data of the dual grid. Because the reader builds the dual grid, these are variables defined on MPAS vertices (nVertices). Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
This property specifies where the center will be viewed for a lat/lon projection.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.label: Center Longitude

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.explanation: Fixes the index of each additional NetCDF dimension of the selected variables (any dimension other than Time, nCells and nVertices, e.g. nVertLevels or a tracer dimension), so one slice is loaded. Give a flat list of [dimension name, index] pairs, with zero-based indices written as strings, e.g. ["nVertLevels", "5"]. In multilayer view the dimension named by VerticalDimension is read in full and its index is ignored.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.label: Extra dimension indices
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView has no static value and vtkMPASReader uses index 0 for every additional dimension.
pitfalls: Entries must come in pairs; an odd-length list leaves the last dimension without an index.
Schemaxis passes the strings unchanged and has not checked this property natively; confirm the loaded level in the output.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 Remoting/Application/Resources/readers_ionetcdf.xml: sources/MPASReader DimensionCurrentIndex (label Extra Dimension Indices)

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.explanation: One entry of the flat pair list: entries at even positions (0, 2, …) are dimension names and the following entry is that dimension's zero-based index, written as a string such as "0".
This property indicates whether data is atmospheric. Checking this ensures the vertical levels will go up away from the sphere instead of down towards the center.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.label: Is Atmosphere

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.explanation: This property specifies how thick the layer should be if viewing the data in multilayer view. Each layer corresponds to a vertical level. A good starting point is 100,000 for the spherical view and 10 for the lat/lon projection. Click on -Z after applying this change, since the scale may change drastically.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.label: Layer Thickness

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.explanation: This property lists which NetCDF dual-grid point variables to load.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.label: Point Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.explanation: One MPAS variable to load as point data of the dual grid; these are variables defined on MPAS cells (nCells), whose centres become the dual-grid points. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
This property indicates whether to view the data in the lat/lon projection.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.label: Project Lat Lon

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.explanation: This property indicates whether to show multiple layers in one view, with each vertical level having the same thickness, specified by the layer thickness slider. For ocean data, the layers correspond to data at vertical level whose number increases towards the center of the sphere. For atmospheric data, the layers correspond to data at vertical levels increasing away from the center.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.label: Show Multilayer View

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.explanation: This property ensures that the dimension info is always shown in the ParaView GUI.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.label: Use Dimensioned Array Names

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.explanation: Name of the NetCDF dimension that represents vertical levels; the multilayer view (ShowMultilayerView) stacks one layer per index of this dimension. Change it for variables on another vertical dimension, such as interface levels (nVertLevelsP1 in MPAS files).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.label: Vertical dimension
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/57/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from "nVertLevels".
pitfalls: Use a dimension name that exists in the file; otherwise no dimension is treated as vertical.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/58.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvNetCDFPOPreader (Reads Parallel Ocean Program (POP) NetCDF output into a rectilinear grid). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/58/propert.explanation: Identifies pvNetCDFPOPreader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property indicate the number of indices per dimension (i,j,k) to skip between each point included in this output.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/58/propert.label: Stride

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/58/propert.explanation: One subsampling step, in grid order (i, j, k), which per vtkNetCDFPOPReader is the reverse of the NetCDF dimension order. A value n keeps every n-th point along that index; 1 keeps all. The minimum is 1.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/58/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 1, 1].

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/58/propert.explanation: Names of the NetCDF variables to load as arrays on the rectilinear grid; only three-dimensional variables are offered by the reader. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/58/propert.label: Variables
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/58/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkNetCDFPOPReader enables every three-dimensional variable). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/58/propert.explanation: One NetCDF variable name, as stored in the file (for example TEMP). Order does not matter.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvNetCDFReader (Reads NetCDF files using the CF (and COARDS) conventions into structured VTK data: image data when nothing else is known, or rectilinear or curvilinear grids when CF coordinate metadata describes them; latitude/longitude grids can be shaped as a sphere (SphericalCoordinates)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59/propert.explanation: Identifies pvNetCDFReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Load the grid with the given dimensions. Any arrays that conform to these dimensions will be loaded.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59/propert.label: Dimensions

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59/propert.explanation: Specifies the type of data that the reader creates. If Automatic, the reader will use the most appropriate grid type for the data read. Note that not all grid types support all data. A warning is issued if a mismatch occurs.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59/propert.label: Output Type

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59/propert.explanation: If on, any float or double variable read that has a _FillValue attribute will have that fill value replaced with a not-a-number (NaN) value. The advantage of setting these to NaN values is that, if implemented properly by the system and careful math operations are used, they can implicitly be ignored by calculations like finding the range of the values. That said, this option should be used with caution as VTK does not fully support NaN values and therefore odd calculations may occur.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59/propert.label: Replace Fill Value With Nan

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59/propert.explanation: If on, then data with latitude/longitude dimensions will be read in as curvilinear data shaped like spherical coordinates. If false, then the data will always be read in Cartesian coordinates.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59/propert.label: Spherical Coordinates

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59/propert.explanation: The bias of the vertical component of spherical coordinates. It is common to write the vertical component with respect to something other than the center of the sphere (for example, the surface). In this case, it might be necessary to scale and/or bias the vertical height. The height will become height*scale + bias. Keep in mind that if the positive attribute of the vertical dimension is down, then the height is negated. The scaling will be adjusted if it results in invalid (negative) vertical values.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59/propert.label: Vertical Bias

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59/propert.explanation: The scale of the vertical component of spherical coordinates. It is common to write the vertical component with respect to something other than the center of the sphere (for example, the surface). In this case, it might be necessary to scale and/or bias the vertical height. The height will become height*scale + bias. Keep in mind that if the positive attribute of the vertical dimension is down, then the height is negated. The scaling will be adjusted if it results in invalid (negative) vertical values.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/59/propert.label: Vertical Scale

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/60.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvNetCDFUGRIDreader (Reads a NetCDF file that follows the UGRID conventions for unstructured meshes (used by some ocean, coastal and climate models) into an unstructured grid). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/60/propert.explanation: Identifies pvNetCDFUGRIDreader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Face-located UGRID variables to load as cell arrays, for example a water level or depth stored on mesh faces. Variables not listed are not read; an empty list loads the mesh without face data.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/60/propert.label: Cell arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/60/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the face variables found in the file (there is no static default). Name them explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Names must match the NetCDF variable names exactly; list them with ncdump -h if unsure.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/60/propert.explanation: One face-located variable name, spelled as in the NetCDF file. Order has no effect on what is read.

Node-located UGRID variables to load as point arrays, for example a velocity component or bathymetry stored at mesh nodes. Variables not listed are not read; an empty list loads the mesh without node data.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/60/propert.label: Point arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/60/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the node variables found in the file (there is no static default). Name them explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: A variable stored on faces is not offered here; select it in CellArrayStatus.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/60/propert.explanation: One node-located variable name, spelled as in the NetCDF file. Order has no effect on what is read.

If on, any float or double variable read that has a _FillValue attribute will have that fill value replaced with a not-a-number (NaN) value. The advantage of setting these to NaN values is that, if implemented properly by the system and careful math operations are used, they can implicitly be ignored by calculations like finding the range of the values. That said, this option should be used with caution as VTK does not fully support NaN values and therefore odd calculations may occur.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/60/propert.label: Replace Fill Value With Nan

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/61.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvNetworkImageSource (ParaView-internal source that reads an image file on one process and makes the image available on the client and render-server processes, used for textures and background images). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/61/propert.explanation: Identifies pvNetworkImageSource as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Set the mode in which image data is read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/61/propert.label: Mode

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/61/propert.explanation: Set the key used to locate the image data object on the server.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/61/propert.label: Trivial Producer Key

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/62.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvNrrdReader (Reads NRRD images (.nrrd, or a detached .nhdr header with its data file) into uniform image data, taking dimensions, type and spacing from the header). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/62/propert.explanation: Identifies pvNrrdReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

The data volume of interest (VOI). The VOI is a sub-extent of the data that you want loaded. Setting a VOI is useful when reading from a large data set and you are only interested in a small portion of the data. If left containing all 0's, then the reader will load in the entire data set.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/62/propert.label: Data VOI

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/62/propert.explanation: One voxel-index bound of the box to load, in the order [imin, imax, jmin, jmax, kmin, kmax]: zero-based and inclusive. All zeros loads the whole volume; any nonzero entry makes the six values the loaded extent.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/62/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0] (whole volume).
pitfalls: Give all six bounds: [0, 99, 0, 0, 0, 0] is a single row of 100 voxels, not the first 100 voxels in every direction.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/63.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvOMETIFFReader (Reads an OME-TIFF microscopy file (.ome.tif, .ome.tiff), using its OME-XML metadata to split the TIFF pages into z-planes, channels and time steps; the output is uniform image data with time steps). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/63/propert.explanation: Identifies pvOMETIFFReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Set the spacing to use for the image output by this reader. This is used only when **UseCustomDataSpacing** is set to 1.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/63/propert.label: Custom Data Spacing

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/63/propert.explanation: Voxel size along one axis (x, y, then z) used instead of the spacing the reader derives from the file when UseCustomDataSpacing is true; ignored otherwise. No unit conversion is applied.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/63/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 1, 1].
pitfalls: Setting CustomDataSpacing alone changes nothing; also set UseCustomDataSpacing to true.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/63/propert.explanation: When checked, data values in the TIFF file will not be mapped to colors using the color map specified in the TIFF, if any. This is useful for files where the color map may be incorrectly specified.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/63/propert.label: Ignore Color Map

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/63/propert.explanation: To manually specify a custom spacing using **CustomDataSpacing**, set this property to 1 (checked).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/63/propert.label: Use Custom Data Spacing

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/64.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvOMFReader (Reads an Open Mining Format (.omf) project into a partitioned dataset collection with one entry per selected element: point sets (e.g). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/64/propert.explanation: Identifies pvOMFReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Are volumes written in column major data order as opposed to standard row major order.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/64/propert.label: Column Major Ordering

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/64/propert.explanation: Select which data elements to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/64/propert.label: Data Elements

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/64/propert.explanation: Name of one OMF element (point set, line set, surface or volume) to load, as named in the project. Order and duplicates do not matter; unlisted elements are not read.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/65.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvObjectFileFormatOFFReader (Reads Object File Format geometry (.off: vertex list followed by polygon faces) into polydata with polygons and lines). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/65/propert.explanation: Identifies pvObjectFileFormatOFFReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvOpenFOAMReader (Full native OpenFOAM reader: opens a case through its .foam marker and outputs a multiblock dataset with the selected mesh regions (internalMesh, patches, patch groups, Lagrangian clouds and optionally zones) carrying cell, point and Lagrangian fields for each stored time). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: Identifies pvOpenFOAMReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Read dimensional units from field data and add them to array names as human-readable string.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Add dimensional units to array names

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: Cache the OpenFOAM mesh between GUI selection changes.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Cache mesh

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: The property indicates whether decomposed mesh or reconstructed mesh should be read
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Case Type

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: Cell-centred fields to read from the time directories (OpenFOAM volume fields such as p, U, T, k or nut). Fields not listed are not loaded; an empty list loads the mesh without cell fields. With Createcelltopointfiltereddata on (ParaView default) each selected field is also interpolated to points.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Cell arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the fields found in the case (there is no static default). Name them explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Names are the field file names and are case-sensitive: "U", not "u".

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: One cell field name, spelled as its file in a time directory, e.g. "p" or "U". Order has no effect on what is read.
Copy data of internal mesh to the cell zones
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Copy data to cell zones

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: Create point data from cell data. Beware: the filter does not do inverse distance weighting.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Create cell-to-point filtered data

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: The expected label-size for the OpenFOAM data.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Label Size

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: Fields of Lagrangian particle clouds (files under <time>/lagrangian/<cloud>/, such as d for diameter or U for particle velocity) to attach to the particle points. They appear only for clouds whose lagrangian/<cloud> region is selected in MeshRegions.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Lagrangian arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the cloud fields found in the case (there is no static default). Name them explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Selecting fields without the cloud's lagrangian/<cloud> region in MeshRegions loads no particles.
Positions written by OpenFOAM 1.4 to 2.4 carry extra data; set Lagrangianpositionswithoutextradata to false for them.
sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/vtk/vtk/-/raw/master/IO/Geometry/vtkOpenFOAMReader.cxx (region naming: internalMesh, patch/, group/, lagrangian/, /region/ prefix)

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: One Lagrangian field name as listed by the reader for the case's clouds, e.g. "d". Order has no effect on what is read.
Lagrangian positions without extra data (before OpenFOAM 1.4, after 2.4)
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Lagrangian positions without extra data

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: List time directories listed according to the settings in controlDict.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: List timesteps according to controlDict

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: Mesh parts to load, each becoming a block: internalMesh (volume cells), patch/<name> boundaries, group/<name> patch groups and lagrangian/<cloud> particle clouds; with Readzones on, zones are offered too. Multi-region cases prefix names with /<region>/. Loading fewer regions reduces memory and read time.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Mesh regions
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the regions in the case (there is no static default). List the regions explicitly, e.g. ["internalMesh"], when the result depends on them.
pitfalls: Use the prefixed names, e.g. "patch/inlet", not the bare patch name.
sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/vtk/vtk/-/raw/master/IO/Geometry/vtkOpenFOAMReader.cxx (region naming: internalMesh, patch/, group/, lagrangian/, /region/ prefix)

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: One region name, e.g. "internalMesh", "patch/outlet" or "lagrangian/kinematicCloud". Order has no effect on what is read.
sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/vtk/vtk/-/raw/master/IO/Geometry/vtkOpenFOAMReader.cxx (region naming: internalMesh, patch/, group/, lagrangian/, /region/ prefix)

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: Point fields stored by the case itself (OpenFOAM point fields, e.g. pointDisplacement in moving-mesh cases). These are not the interpolated point data created from cell fields by Createcelltopointfiltereddata, which needs no selection here.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Point arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the point fields found in the case (there is no static default). Name them explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Most cases store no point fields, so this list is often empty; select solver results in CellArrays.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: One point-field name, spelled as its file in a time directory, e.g. "pointDisplacement". Order has no effect on what is read.
Read point/face/cell-Zones?
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Read zones

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: The expected scalar-size for the OpenFOAM data.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Scalar Size

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: Ignore the 0/ time directory.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Skip Zero Time

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.explanation: Use cell size as weight in cell data-to-point data procedure.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/66/propert.label: Weight Point Data By Cell Size

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/67.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvOpenVDBReader (Reads an OpenVDB (.vdb) file, the sparse volume format used in visual effects and some simulation tools). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/67/propert.explanation: Identifies pvOpenVDBReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

This parameter controls the sampling rate of the image volume. A value of 1 will lead to a volume with the same resolution as the read one. A value of 0.5 will downsample the file by half along each axis.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/67/propert.label: Downsampling Factor

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/67/propert.explanation: This property lists which grid arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/67/propert.label: Grid Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/67/propert.explanation: One grid name to read, as stored in the .vdb file (for example density or temperature in a smoke volume). Grids not listed are skipped; order has no effect on what is read.
When enabled, the different requested image grids will be merged into a single ImageData. When disabled, the different requested image grids will be stored into individual blocks.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/67/propert.label: Merge Image Volumes

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/67/propert.explanation: When enabled, the different requested point clouds will be merged into a single PolyData. When disabled, the different requested point clouds will be stored into individual blocks.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/67/propert.label: Merge Point Sets

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/68.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvPDALReader (Reads LiDAR and other point-cloud files through the PDAL library (LAS/LAZ, PCD, PLY, text and the other formats PDAL supports) into polydata points with per-point attribute arrays such as Intensity, Classification and colour). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/68/propert.explanation: Identifies pvPDALReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/69.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvPDBReader (Reads a Protein Data Bank file (.pdb) of macromolecular structure into polydata: atoms as points with arrays such as atom_type, residue, chain and secondary_structures, and bonds as lines estimated from atomic distances). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/69/propert.explanation: Identifies pvPDBReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/70.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvPIOReader (Reads xRAGE PIO dump files (Los Alamos radiation-hydrodynamics code) through an ASCII .pio file describing the dump directory, cycles and variables). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/70/propert.explanation: Identifies pvPIOReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Variables written to the data files are described in the .pio file and are presented for selection. Only selected variables are loaded for a time step.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/70/propert.label: Cell Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/70/propert.explanation: One xRAGE variable name as listed in the .pio file. Only listed variables are loaded for each time step; order has no effect.
This property determines if tracer data is read into a second unstructured grid.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/70/propert.label: Load Tracers

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/70/propert.explanation: This property determines if the AMR and tracer variable data is read as 64 bit float.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/70/propert.label: Load variables as doubles (Float64)

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/70/propert.explanation: Chooses which value labels each time step: SimulationTime (ParaView's XML default), CycleIndex or PIOFileIndex; any other entry, including "None", numbers the steps with the integers 0, 1, 2, ... ParaView's own description calls the no-selection entry "Default", but the list's entry is "None".
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/70/propert.label: Time Array
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 VTK/IO/PIO/vtkPIOReader.cxx:150-190 (the choices are SimulationTime, CycleIndex and PIOFileIndex; any other name gives step numbers)

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/70/propert.explanation: This property determines if AMR in the PIO file is created as a hypertree grid rather than as an unstructured grid.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/70/propert.label: Use HyperTree Grid (HTG) for AMR Mesh

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/71.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvPLOT3DMetaFileReader (Reads a PLOT3D case through a .p3d meta file: a small JSON file naming the grid (.xyz), solution (.q) and optional function files for each time value, and recording the format settings PLOT3D files do not describe themselves (binary or ASCII, byte order, precision, multi-grid, Fortran byte counts, blanking, 2-D, R, gamma, derived functions)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/71/propert.explanation: Identifies pvPLOT3DMetaFileReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/73.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvPLYReader (Full native PLY reader: reads Stanford PLY polygon files (ASCII or binary) into polydata). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/73/propert.explanation: Identifies pvPLYReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

If true (default) and the "face" element has the property "texcoord" duplicate face points if they have 2 or more different texture coordinates. Otherwise, each texture coordinate for a face point overwrites previously set texture coordinates for that point.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/73/propert.label: Duplicate Points For Face Texture

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/73/propert.explanation: Tolerance used to detect different texture coordinates for shared points for faces
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/73/propert.label: Face Texture Tolerance

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/74.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvPNGSeriesReader (Reads PNG images (.png) into uniform image data with 8- or 16-bit, 1 to 4 component point scalars). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.
