/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/74/propert.explanation: Identifies pvPNGSeriesReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Set the spacing to use for the image output by this reader.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/74/propert.label: Data Spacing

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/74/propert.explanation: Pixel size along one axis (x, y, then z between stacked slices) in your chosen length unit; PNG files carry no reliable physical size here, so this sets the image's world dimensions.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/74/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 1, 1].

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/74/propert.explanation: When set, the reader will read the set of files as an image stack, rather than a temporal file series.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/74/propert.label: Read As Image Stack

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/75.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvPTSReader (Reads an ASCII PTS point cloud (.pts: point count, then x y z [intensity [r g b]] per line), as produced by laser scanners, into polydata with one vertex cell holding all points and Intensities and Color arrays when present). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/75/propert.explanation: Identifies pvPTSReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Limits the number of points read in from file
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/75/propert.label: Limit Number Of Points Read

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/75/propert.explanation: Restrict the point to cloud to a specified volume.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/75/propert.label: Limit Point Cloud To Bounds

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/75/propert.explanation: Specify the max number of point to be read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/75/propert.label: Max Number Of Points

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/75/propert.explanation: Define the spatial volume that will restrict the extent of the point cloud [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax]
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/75/propert.label: Read Bounds

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/75/propert.explanation: One bound of the box that keeps points: the six values are ordered [xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax] in the file's coordinate units, and points on the box faces are kept. Used only when LimitPointCloudToBounds is true.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/75/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, 100, 0, 100, 0, 100].
pitfalls: The order is min/max per axis, not [xmin, ymin, zmin, …].
When LimitNumberOfPointsRead is also on, subsampling is applied first, so fewer points than MaxNumberOfPoints may remain inside the box.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/76.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvPVDReader (Reads a ParaView .pvd collection: an XML index listing VTK XML data files (.vtu, .vtp, .vti, .vtm, .vtt …) with timestep, part and group attributes). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/76/propert.explanation: Identifies pvPVDReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property lists which cell-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/76/propert.label: Cell Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/76/propert.explanation: One cell-data array name to load from the files listed in the .pvd. Listing names loads exactly those cell arrays and drops the others; spelling must match the files.
This property lists which columns to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/76/propert.label: Column Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/76/propert.explanation: One column name to load when the collection references tables (VTK XML table files, .vtt). Listing names loads exactly those columns; the list has no effect on mesh datasets.
This property lists which point-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/76/propert.label: PointArrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/76/propert.explanation: One point-data array name to load from the files listed in the .pvd. Listing names loads exactly those point arrays and drops the others; spelling must match the files.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/77.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvParallelNetCDFPOPreader (Reads Parallel Ocean Program (POP) output stored in NetCDF (.pop.ncdf, .pop.nc) into a rectilinear grid, with only some MPI processes reading the file and sending the data to the others). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/77/propert.explanation: Identifies pvParallelNetCDFPOPreader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property indicates the number of indices per dimension (i,j,k) to skip between each point included in this output.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/77/propert.label: Stride

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/77/propert.explanation: Sampling step along one grid index direction: first i, then j, then k. 1 keeps every point, 2 every second point, and so on; larger strides cut memory and resolution along that direction.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/77/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 1, 1].
pitfalls: ParaView's range domain starts at 1; zero or negative strides are not meaningful.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/77/propert.explanation: NetCDF variables to load onto the grid, e.g. potential temperature or salinity (POP names such as TEMP or SALT). Variables not listed are not read, which saves memory and transfer between processes.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/77/propert.label: Variables
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/77/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the variables found in the file (there is no static default). Name them explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Names must match the NetCDF variable names exactly, including capitalization.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/77/propert.explanation: One POP NetCDF variable name, spelled as in the file. Order has no effect on what is read.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/78.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvParticlesReader (Reads simple particle files (text or binary records of x, y, z and an optional scalar, as float or double) into polydata points with vertex cells and, when HasScalar is true, one scalar point array). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/78/propert.explanation: Identifies pvParticlesReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Set/Get the byte ordering of the file you are trying to read in.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/78/propert.label: Byte Order

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/78/propert.explanation: Get/Set the data type. The options are: - Float (10) (default) single precision floating point. - Double (11) double precision floating point.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/78/propert.label: Data Type

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/78/propert.explanation: Set the file type. The options are: - Unknown (0) (default) the reader will attempt to determine the file type. If this fails then you should set the file type yourself. - Text (1) the file type is text. - Binary (2) the file type is binary.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/78/propert.label: File Type

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/78/propert.explanation: Default: 1. If 1 then each particle has a value associated with it.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/78/propert.label: Has Scalar

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/79.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvPartitionedLegacyVTKReader (Reads a partitioned legacy VTK data set: a .pvtk summary file listing several legacy .vtk piece files (structured points, structured, rectilinear or unstructured grid, or polydata), which are read as one data set). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/79/propert.explanation: Identifies pvPartitionedLegacyVTKReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/80.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvPhastaReader (Reads results of the PHASTA parallel CFD solver through its .pht meta-file, an XML description of the geometry and field files per time step and partition). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/80/propert.explanation: Identifies pvPhastaReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/82.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvResourceImageTexture (Typed texture resource (vtkTexture) that loads its image from a file such as a PNG or JPEG). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/82/propert.explanation: Identifies pvResourceImageTexture as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

When color mode is Default, 8-bits textures is equivalent to Direct Scalars, while equivalent to Map Scalars for 16-bits textures. In the case of Map Scalars, all the values are mapped to a generic color map.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/82/propert.label: Color Mode

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/82/propert.explanation: Set the mode in which image data is read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/82/propert.label: Mode

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/82/propert.explanation: Rendering-only choice used when an image exceeds the graphics card's maximum texture size and must be resampled to power-of-two dimensions: true rounds each dimension down (smaller, blurrier texture), false rounds up. It never changes the image data that consumers such as pvLogo receive.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/82/propert.label: Restrict power-of-two image smaller
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/82/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from false.
pitfalls: Has no visible effect for normal-sized images; do not use it to downsample a texture.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/82/propert.explanation: Set the key used to locate the image data object on the server.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/82/propert.label: Trivial Producer Key

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvRestartedSimSpyPlotReader (Reads a CTH (Spy Plot) simulation that was restarted, through a metadata file (.spcth-timeseries) listing the output file sets of each restart, so the sets behave as one continuous time series). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.explanation: Identifies pvRestartedSimSpyPlotReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Names of the cell-centred arrays to load from the Spy Plot files (for example material volume fractions, masses, pressure or velocity components). Arrays not listed are absent from the output; listing fewer reduces memory and read time. The available names come from the files themselves.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.label: Cell arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView chooses the initial selection from the arrays found in the files (there is no static default). Name the arrays explicitly when later nodes depend on them.
pitfalls: Names must match the file's array names exactly, including spaces and capitalization.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.explanation: One cell-array name to read, spelled as in the Spy Plot files. Order does not matter and a repeated name adds nothing.
In parallel mode, if this property is set to 1, the reader will distribute files or blocks.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.label: Distribute Files

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 0, the type of the volume fraction is float; is set to 1, the type is unsigned char.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.label: Down Convert Volume Fraction

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores the active status of a block.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.label: Generate Active Block Array

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores a unique blockId for each block.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.label: Generate Block Id Array

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores the level of each block.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.label: Generate Level Array

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 1, a second output will be created using the markers data stored in the file.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.label: Generate Markers

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores the coordinates of any tracers.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.label: Generate Tracers

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.explanation: This hidden property must always be set to 1 for this proxy to work.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/84/propert.label: Use Meta File

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/85.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvSAVGReader (Reads a NIST SAVG file (.savg), a plain-text format of coloured points, lines and polygons used for immersive-visualization scenes). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/85/propert.explanation: Identifies pvSAVGReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvSEPReader (Reads Stanford Exploration Project seismic data: a text .H header describing up to 32 named axes (labels such as CDP, LINE, OFFSET, DEPTH) with their sizes, origins and sampling, which points to the raw .H@ data file). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.explanation: Identifies pvSEPReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property specifies the extent mode.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.label: Extent Split Mode

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.explanation: Name of an extra SEP axis that is not mapped to x, y or z; the output is the single slice at FixedDimension1Value along it (for example one offset of a prestack volume).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from "OFFSET" (ParaView may replace it with a name from the file's axis list).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.label: Fixed dimension 1

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.explanation: Zero-based index along FixedDimension1 of the slice to read, e.g. which offset gather.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3's static default is 1, but ParaView may reset it to the low end of the file's range (0).
pitfalls: Keep the value below that axis's size; VTK only warns about larger values.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.label: Fixed dimension 1 value

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.explanation: Name of a second fixed SEP axis, used only with 2-D output (OutputGridDimension 2D): the axis that would otherwise be z is held at FixedDimension2Value.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from "DEPTH" (ParaView may replace it with a name from the file's axis list).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.label: Fixed dimension 2

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.explanation: Zero-based index along FixedDimension2 of the slice to read in 2-D output; ignored for 3-D output.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3's static default is 1, but ParaView may reset it to the low end of the file's range (0).
pitfalls: Keep the value below that axis's size; VTK only warns about larger values.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.label: Fixed dimension 2 value

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.explanation: This property specifies the dimension of the output data set.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.label: Output Grid Dimension

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.explanation: Name of the SEP axis mapped to the output x direction; that axis's origin and sampling in the header become the image's x origin and spacing. It must be one of the axis labels in the .H header.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from "CDP" (ParaView may replace it with a name from the file's axis list).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.label: X dimension

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.explanation: Name of the SEP axis mapped to the output y direction, supplying the image's y origin and spacing. It must be one of the axis labels in the .H header.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from "LINE" (ParaView may replace it with a name from the file's axis list).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.label: Y dimension

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.explanation: Name of the SEP axis mapped to the output z direction. Only used when OutputGridDimension is 3D; in 2-D output this axis is not used and FixedDimension2 is held fixed instead.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from "DEPTH" (ParaView may replace it with a name from the file's axis list).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/86/propert.label: Z dimension

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/88.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvSLACParticleDataReader (Reads particle data written by SLAC's accelerator codes (NetCDF files with the SLAC particle conventions) into polydata: a set of particle points in 3-D space). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/88/propert.explanation: Identifies pvSLACParticleDataReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/89.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvSTEPReader (Reads a STEP CAD file through OpenCASCADE and tessellates its B-rep faces into triangles, giving a multiblock dataset with one polydata block per shape (named from the file, or Unnamed) and a per-cell Colors array from the CAD colours). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/89/propert.explanation: Identifies pvSTEPReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Limits the angle between two subsequent segments.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/89/propert.label: Angular Deflection

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/89/propert.explanation: Limits the distance between a curve and the resulting tesselation.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/89/propert.label: Linear Deflection

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/89/propert.explanation: Determines if 1D cells will be read. If enabled, surface boundaries are read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/89/propert.label: Read Wire

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/89/propert.explanation: Determines if the deflection values are relative to object size.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/89/propert.label: Relative Deflection

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/90.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvSTLReader (Full native STL reader: reads ASCII or binary stereolithography files (.stl) into triangle polydata, and a list of several files into a time series). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/90/propert.explanation: Identifies pvSTLReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvSegYReader (Reads a SEG-Y seismic file). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.explanation: Identifies pvSegYReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Treats the file as a 2-D line even if it is a 3-D survey: the crossline and inline numbers are ignored and the traces are connected in file order into one structured-grid sheet through 3-D space. Use it for 2-D lines whose headers would otherwise be misread as 3-D.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.label: Force 2D
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from false.
pitfalls: The upstream help text for this property repeats the StructuredGrid description; Force2D itself only changes how traces are connected.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.explanation: Specify if we create a Structured Grid even when the data is SEG-Y 3D. Note this consumes more memory but it shows the precise location for each point and the correct shape of the data. The default value is true. If we set this option to false we create an Image Data for a SEG-Y 3D dataset.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.label: Structured Grid

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.explanation: Specify whether the vertical coordinates in the SEG-Y file are heights (positive up) or depths (positive down). By default, the vertical coordinates are treated as heights (i.e. positive up). This means that the Z-axis of the dataset goes from 0 (surface) to -ve depth (last sample). Note. As per the SEG-Y rev 2.0 specification, this information is defined in the Location Data Stanza of the Extended Textual Header. However, as of this revision, SegYReader does not support reading the extended textual header.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.label: Vertical CRS

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.explanation: One-based byte position in each trace header from which the trace x coordinate is read when XYCoordMode is Custom (Source uses bytes 73/77, CDP 181/185). Use it for files that store coordinates at non-standard positions.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.label: X coordinate byte
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.units: Byte position in the trace header (one-based)
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 73.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.explanation: Specify whether to use source x/y coordinates or CDP coordinates or custom byte positions for data position in the SEG-Y trace header. Defaults to source x/y coordinates. As per SEG-Y rev 2.0 specification: - Source XY coordinate bytes = (73, 77) - CDP XY coordinate bytes = (181, 185)
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.label: XY Coord Mode

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.explanation: One-based byte position in each trace header from which the trace y coordinate is read when XYCoordMode is Custom (Source uses bytes 73/77, CDP 181/185).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.label: Y coordinate byte
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.units: Byte position in the trace header (one-based)
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/91/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from 76 (its XML default), although the help text and VTK's own default give 77.
pitfalls: In Custom mode always set YCoordByte explicitly; the initial 76 is one byte off the standard source-Y position.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvSpyPlotReader (Reads a CTH Spy Plot case: an ASCII .spcth case file listing the binary files that hold the data). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.explanation: Identifies pvSpyPlotReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property lists which cell-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.label: Cell Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.explanation: One cell-array name to read, spelled as in the Spy Plot files. Order does not matter and a repeated name adds nothing.

If this property is set to 1, the reader will convert derived variables like material density for the materials that the user has selected. For Density the user needs to have selected Material Mass and Material Volume Fraction.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.label: Compute Derived Variables

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.explanation: In parallel mode, if this property is set to 1, the reader will distribute files or blocks.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.label: Distribute Files

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 0, the type of the volume fraction is float; is set to 1, the type is unsigned char.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.label: Down Convert Volume Fraction

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores the active status of a block.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.label: Generate Active Block Array

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores a unique blockId for each block.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.label: Generate Block Id Array

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores the level of each block.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.label: Generate Level Array

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 1, a second output will be created using the markers data stored in the file.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.label: Generate Markers

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 1, a cell array will be generated that stores the coordinates of any tracers.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.label: Generate Tracers

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.explanation: If this property is set to 1, cell arrays named (for example) X velocity, Y velocity and Z velocity will be combined into a single vector array named velocity.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/92/propert.label: Merge XYZ Components

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/93.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvTIFFReader (Reads one TIFF file (.tif, .tiff) into uniform image data; it is kept for backward compatibility, and pvTIFFSeriesReader reads the same files with stacking, time series and custom spacing added). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/93/propert.explanation: Identifies pvTIFFReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/94.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvTIFFSeriesReader (Reads TIFF images (.tif, .tiff; 8- or 16-bit integer or 32-bit float) into uniform image data). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/94/propert.explanation: Identifies pvTIFFSeriesReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Set the spacing to use for the image output by this reader. This is used only when **UseCustomDataSpacing** is set to true.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/94/propert.label: Custom Data Spacing

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/94/propert.explanation: Voxel size along one axis (x, y, then z between stacked slices) used when UseCustomDataSpacing is true, replacing the spacing derived from the TIFF resolution tags; ignored otherwise. No unit conversion is applied.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/94/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 1, 1].
pitfalls: Setting CustomDataSpacing alone changes nothing; also set UseCustomDataSpacing to true.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/94/propert.explanation: When set, the reader will read the set of files as an image stack, rather than a temporal file series.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/94/propert.label: Read As Image Stack

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/94/propert.explanation: To manually specify a custom spacing using **CustomDataSpacing**, set this property to 1 (checked).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/94/propert.label: Use Custom Data Spacing

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/95.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvTRUCHASReader (Reads output of TRUCHAS (Los Alamos casting, solidification and heat-transfer code) stored in HDF5 into a multiblock dataset, with selectable mesh blocks and point and cell arrays at each stored time step). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/95/propert.explanation: Identifies pvTRUCHASReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Select the grids to be loaded from the dataset, if any.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/95/propert.label: Blocks

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/95/propert.explanation: One mesh block (grid) name to load, as listed by the reader for this file. Blocks not listed are left out of the output; order has no effect.
This property lists which cell-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/95/propert.label: Cell Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/95/propert.explanation: One cell-centred TRUCHAS variable to read, spelled as listed by the reader. Order has no effect on what is read.
This property lists which point-centered arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/95/propert.label: Point Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/95/propert.explanation: One point-centred TRUCHAS variable to read, spelled as listed by the reader. Order has no effect on what is read.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/96.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvTecplotReader (Reads ASCII Tecplot files (.dat, .tec, .tp) into a multiblock dataset with one block per zone; each block is a structured grid (ordered zones) or unstructured grid (finite-element zones)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/96/propert.explanation: Identifies pvTecplotReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Names of the Tecplot variables to read as arrays on every zone; each variable becomes point or cell data according to the file's packing and VARLOCATION. Coordinate variables are not listed. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/96/propert.label: Data arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/96/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView copies the reader's own initial selection from the file (vtkTecplotReader enables every variable). Whether the file information is available before Schemaxis applies options has not been verified, so list names explicitly when later nodes depend on them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/96/propert.explanation: One variable name as written in the file's VARIABLES line. Order does not matter.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/97.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvTecplotTableReader (Reads a Tecplot ASCII data file (.dat) as a table (vtkTable): one column per variable and one row per data record, with column names taken from a header line). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/97/propert.explanation: Identifies pvTecplotTableReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
The line that contains the column names.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/97/propert.label: Line with column names

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/97/propert.explanation: The maximum number of records to read. Use this to preview a file.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/97/propert.label: Max. Number of Records

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/97/propert.explanation: The number of lines that form the header.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/97/propert.label: Number of header lines

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/97/propert.explanation: Number of fields to skip while reading column names.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/97/propert.label: Skip #column name fields

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/98.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvUnstructuredNetCDFPOPreader (Reads Parallel Ocean Program (POP) NetCDF output (.pop.nc, .pop.ncdf) and converts its logically structured grid into an unstructured grid on a sphere: horizontal positions come from a companion GRID.nc file in the same folder, depth comes from depth_t and is negated so deeper layers have lower z, and the Earth radius is 6371000 (metres)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/98/propert.explanation: Identifies pvUnstructuredNetCDFPOPreader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
This property indicate the number of indices per dimension (i,j,k) to skip between each point included in this output.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/98/propert.label: Stride

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/98/propert.explanation: Subsampling step along one logical index direction, in the order i (east-west), j (north-south), k (depth): 1 keeps every point, 2 every second point. Striding is applied before VOI; the minimum is 1.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/98/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 1, 1].
pitfalls: Striding in depth (k other than 1) disables the VerticalVelocity computation.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/98/propert.explanation: Index box [imin, imax, jmin, jmax, kmin, kmax] of the structured POP grid to read, counted after Stride is applied (zero-based, inclusive). It is applied only when at least one maximum is not -1; a bound outside the data is ignored. Use it to read a region of a large ocean grid.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/98/propert.label: VOI
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/98/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, -1, 0, -1, 0, -1], which reads the whole grid.
pitfalls: The native help says all zeros loads everything; in the reader's code all zeros selects only index 0 in each direction. Use -1 maxima for the full grid.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/98/propert.explanation: One bound of the index box [imin, imax, jmin, jmax, kmin, kmax] to keep, as zero-based inclusive indices in the strided index space. The box applies only when at least one maximum differs from -1, and each bound only if it lies inside the data.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/98/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [0, -1, 0, -1, 0, -1], which reads the whole grid.
pitfalls: All zeros does not mean 'everything' here (despite older documentation): it keeps only index 0 in each direction.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/98/propert.explanation: If there is a velocity vector with only 2 components, specify that the reader should compute the third component.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/98/propert.label: VerticalVelocity

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/99.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvVASPAnimationReader (Reads a VASP molecular-dynamics animation file (NPT_Z_ANIMATE.out) into a time-varying vtkMolecule, one frame of atom positions per time step). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/99/propert.explanation: Identifies pvVASPAnimationReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/100.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvVASPTessellationReader (Reads a VASP NPT_Z_TESSELLATE.out file). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/100/proper.explanation: Identifies pvVASPTessellationReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/101.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvVPICReader (Reads VPIC kinetic plasma particle-in-cell output through its ASCII .vpc file, which describes the per-processor data files, grid size and time steps). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/101/proper.explanation: Identifies pvVPICReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.
Variables written to the data files are described in the .vpc file and are presented for selection. Only selected variables are loaded for a time step.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/101/proper.label: Point Arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/101/proper.explanation: One VPIC variable name as listed from the .vpc file (a field or hydro quantity). Only listed variables are loaded for a time step; order has no effect.
VPIC data may be very large and not all is needed for effective visualization. Setting the stride selects every nth data item within the files for display.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/101/proper.label: Stride

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/101/proper.explanation: Sampling step along one axis: first x, then y, then z. 1 reads every grid point and n every n-th point, reducing memory and resolution by about n along that axis.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/101/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [1, 1, 1].

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/101/proper.explanation: VPIC data is written one file per simulation processor. This coarse map of files is used in partitioning files between visualizing processors so that each ParaView processor has its own set of files to display. Ghost cell overlap is handled within the reader. To limit the View of VPIC information the extent in the X dimension of "files" can be specified. Only the files selected will be displayed and they will be partitioned between the visualizing processors, allowing a higher resolution over a smaller area.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/101/proper.label: X Extent

Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/103/proper.explanation: One cell-data array name stored in the VTKHDF file's CellData group. Listing names is exclusive: ParaView switches every other available name off, so include all you need; an empty list reads none.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/103/proper.label: Maximum Levels To Read By Default For AMR

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/103/proper.explanation: Make the reader merge parts in the input data set. If false, the reader will output a partitioned data set.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/103/proper.label: Merge Parts

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/103/proper.explanation: Select the point arrays to read.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/103/proper.label: Point Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/103/proper.label: Use Cache

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvVelodyneAMRReader (Reads Velodyne AMR files (.xamr) into an overlapping AMR dataset: nested refinement levels of uniform blocks with cell-centred variables). /$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104/proper.explanation: Identifies pvVelodyneAMRReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Names of the cell-centred variables to load from the Velodyne XAMR file, such as density or pressure fields. Listing names loads exactly those arrays and disables every other array the file offers; an empty list loads none. Fewer arrays mean less memory and faster reads.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104/proper.label: Cell arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView takes the initial selection from the reader, and VTK's AMR readers start with every array disabled, so omitting this usually loads no fields. Name the arrays explicitly.
pitfalls: Names must match the variable names stored in the file exactly; a misspelt name yields no array.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104/proper.explanation: One cell-centred variable name to load, spelled as stored in the Velodyne XAMR file. Order does not matter and a repeated name adds nothing.

Keep AMR blocks that have already been read in memory, so later updates that change the level or array selection, or revisit a time, do not reread them from disk. It does not change the data produced.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104/proper.label: Cache loaded blocks
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts with caching off (false).
pitfalls: Caching trades memory for speed; leave it off for large AMR hierarchies or single-pass publications.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104/proper.explanation: This property specifies the desired level of resolution that will be visible.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104/proper.label: Level

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104/proper.explanation: Names of point-centred arrays to load. This reader lists only cell-centred variables from the file (its array setup registers cell arrays only), so there is normally nothing to select here; use CellArrayStatus and convert with cellToPoint if you need point data.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104/proper.label: Point arrays
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView takes the (normally empty) selection from the reader.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/104/proper.explanation: One point-centred array name to load. The reader normally offers none, so entries here usually have no effect.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/105.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvVisItANSYSReader (Reads an ASCII ANSYS input deck (.inp) through VisIt's ANSYS plugin: the nodes and elements in its NBLOCK and EBLOCK blocks become one unstructured-grid block named "mesh"). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/105/proper.explanation: Identifies pvVisItANSYSReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from ANSYS input data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The ANSYS input plugin defines no variables, so this list has nothing to select.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/105/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. The VisIt bridge registers every cell variable as unselected, so normally no cell arrays are read (if ParaView's Load All Variables setting is enabled, all are selected). Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) read back the fixture's only cell variable as unselected and produced no arrays, with LoadAllVariables false, identically with and without --dr.
pitfalls: Any name given here produces nothing because the format has no variables.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/105/proper.label: Cell arrays

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/107.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvVisItBOVReader (Reads VisIt's BOV (brick of values) format: a short text header (.bov) giving DATA_FILE, DATA_SIZE, DATA_FORMAT, BRICK_ORIGIN, BRICK_SIZE, VARIABLE and CENTERING for one raw binary array on a regular grid). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/107/proper.explanation: Identifies pvVisItBOVReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from BOV data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The BOV plugin offers the one variable named by VARIABLE in the header; CENTERING NODAL makes it a point array and ZONAL a cell array; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/107/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. The VisIt bridge registers every cell variable as unselected, so normally no cell arrays are read (if ParaView's Load All Variables setting is enabled, all are selected). Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) read back the fixture's only cell variable as unselected and produced no arrays, with LoadAllVariables false, identically with and without --dr.
pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/117/proper.explanation: Names of the FLASH meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The FLASH plugin reports the block-structured AMR mesh "amr_mesh", a "particles" point mesh when particles are stored, and diagnostic meshes (for example Morton-curve and block/processor meshes). Selecting only the AMR mesh gives vtkOverlappingAMR output.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/117/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 has no static default for this selection. The VisIt bridge enables only the first mesh the plugin reports and ParaView copies that state, so normally only that mesh is read. Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) read back the fixture's one mesh as enabled, with LoadAllVariables false, identically with and without --dr.
pitfalls: An empty list deselects every mesh and gives an empty output.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply reads nothing, so copy names exactly.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/117/proper.explanation: Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from FLASH data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The FLASH plugin offers the FLASH unknowns (cell-centred on the AMR mesh) and particle properties (on the particle mesh); which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/117/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. The VisIt bridge registers every point variable as unselected, so normally no point arrays are read (if ParaView's Load All Variables setting is enabled, all are selected). Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) read back the fixture's only variable, a cell variable, as unselected and produced no arrays, with LoadAllVariables false, identically with and without --dr; the bridge treats point variables the same way (vtkAvtFileFormatAlgorithm.cxx:758-790).
pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/117/proper.label: Point arrays

Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The image plugin offers per-pixel channels; each is offered twice, as a cell array on "ImageMesh" and with the suffix _nodal as a point array on "ImageMesh_nodal"; colour formats add 4-component "color"/"color_nodal" arrays; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/124/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. The VisIt bridge registers every point variable as unselected, so normally no point arrays are read (if ParaView's Load All Variables setting is enabled, all are selected). Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) read back the fixture's only variable, a cell variable, as unselected and produced no arrays, with LoadAllVariables false, identically with and without --dr; the bridge treats point variables the same way (vtkAvtFileFormatAlgorithm.cxx:758-790).
pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/124/proper.label: Point arrays

pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.

pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/153/proper.explanation: Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from ParaDiS data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The ParaDiS plugin offers node and segment quantities such as "Node-Type", "Segment-Burgers-Type" and "Segment-Index"; which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/153/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. The VisIt bridge registers every point variable as unselected, so normally no point arrays are read (if ParaView's Load All Variables setting is enabled, all are selected). Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) read back the fixture's only variable, a cell variable, as unselected and produced no arrays, with LoadAllVariables false, identically with and without --dr; the bridge treats point variables the same way (vtkAvtFileFormatAlgorithm.cxx:758-790).
pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/156/proper.explanation: Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from Protein Data Bank data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. For Protein Data Bank data these are per-atom values such as "element", "restype", "resseq", "backbone", "occupancy" and "tempFactor" (numeric only).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/156/proper.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; no static default. The VisIt bridge registers every point variable as unselected, so normally no point arrays are read (if ParaView's Load All Variables setting is enabled, all are selected). Observed: a bounded native probe on a BOV fixture (ParaView 5.13.3 pvbatch, serial, 2026-10-12) read back the fixture's only variable, a cell variable, as unselected and produced no arrays, with LoadAllVariables false, identically with and without --dr; the bridge treats point variables the same way (vtkAvtFileFormatAlgorithm.cxx:758-790).
pitfalls: Omitting the list normally gives geometry without fields; name every array later nodes use.
A list replaces the whole selection, and a misspelt name is not rejected; it simply yields no array, so copy names exactly (case and spaces matter).

/$defs/json.explanation: Free JSON data that the schema does not interpret: a scalar, list or object. Its meaning comes from where it is used, for example reusable blocks read with {"$document": "/definitions/..."} or one sample of an axis read with {"$axis": name}.

/$defs/json/anyOf/0.explanation: A single value: null, true/false, a number or a string.

/$defs/json/anyOf/1.explanation: A list of JSON values, kept in order; for example an [x, y, z] vector.

/$defs/json/anyOf/1/items.explanation: Free JSON data that the schema does not interpret: a scalar, list or object. Its meaning comes from where it is used, for example reusable blocks read with {"$document": "/definitions/..."} or one sample of an axis read with {"$axis": name}.

/$defs/json/anyOf/2.explanation: An object of named JSON values; members can be selected later with a $document pointer or an $axis path.

/$defs/json/anyOf/2/additionalProperties.explanation: Free JSON data that the schema does not interpret: a scalar, list or object. Its meaning comes from where it is used, for example reusable blocks read with {"$document": "/definitions/..."} or one sample of an axis read with {"$axis": name}.

/$defs/runtimeValue.explanation: One argument of a $calc operation: a literal JSON scalar, a list of further arguments, or a nested runtime value. Nested parts are evaluated first, then the operation is applied.

/$defs/runtimeValue/anyOf/0.explanation: Literal scalar argument. Arithmetic, vector and bounds operations accept only finite numbers; null, booleans and strings fail when used as operands.

/$defs/runtimeValue/anyOf/1.explanation: List argument, e.g. a vector [x, y, z] or six-value bounds, whose elements may themselves be runtime values; lists are combined element by element.

/$defs/runtimeValue/anyOf/1/items.explanation: One argument of a $calc operation: a literal JSON scalar, a list of further arguments, or a nested runtime value. Nested parts are evaluated first, then the operation is applied.

/$defs/runtimeValue/anyOf/2.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
/$defs/runtimeValue/anyOf/2.label: Runtime value

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Alternatives (any)
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: Groups of clauses. An element is selected when at least one group matches; use a single group for an ordinary AND query. 1 to 16 groups, joined with | in the generated text.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Group
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: One alternative: an object whose "all" list holds the clauses that must all be true for this group to match.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Clauses (all)
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: Clauses that must all be true for this group to match. 1 to 16 clauses, each wrapped in parentheses and joined with & in the generated text.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Clause
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: One condition: a test plus the members that test needs. Comparison, between, oneOf, statistic and mean tests apply to a term (array, optionally with component or magnitude, or ids); pointNear and cellContaining test element locations instead. negate inverts the clause.
pitfalls: A member the chosen test does not use is rejected rather than ignored (INVALID_SELECTION_QUERY).

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Array
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: Name of the point or cell array to test, as it appears in the data; ElementType chooses the association. Schemaxis converts it to ParaView's variable name by keeping ASCII letters, digits and underscores and adding a leading "a" when the result would not start with a letter.
pitfalls: Two names that sanitise to the same variable cannot be told apart, as in ParaView.
Names equal to a Python keyword or built-in, a query function, inputs, points or id, or containing a double underscore, are rejected; rename the array upstream, for example with pvPassArrays.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Component
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: Zero-based component of a multi-component array to test, written array[:, n] in the generated text. Omit it for one-component arrays.
pitfalls: Cannot be combined with magnitude or ids.
Selecting a component of a one-component array fails in ParaView when the selection is extracted.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Element index
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: Set to true to test the zero-based element index (ParaView's id) instead of an array.
pitfalls: Cannot be combined with array, component or magnitude.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Magnitude
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: Set to true to test the Euclidean magnitude of a multi-component array, written mag(array) in the generated text.
pitfalls: Cannot be combined with component or ids.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Lower bound
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: Exclusive lower bound for the between test, in the units of the tested array.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Upper bound
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: Exclusive upper bound for the between test, in the units of the tested array; it must exceed minimum.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Negate
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: Set to true to select the elements for which this clause is false; the generated text wraps the clause in logical_not.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Location
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: World coordinates [x, y, z] for pointNear (points within tolerance of the location) or cellContaining (cells that contain the location).
pitfalls: pointNear selects points, so set ElementType to 0; cellContaining selects cells (ElementType 1, the ParaView default). Schemaxis does not check this pairing.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Coordinate
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: One world coordinate of the location, in the dataset's coordinate units.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Test
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: The condition to apply. Comparisons ==, !=, <, <=, >, >= use value; between is strictly between minimum and maximum; oneOf matches any of values; isMinimum and isMaximum match the global extreme and their PerBlock forms the extreme of each block; isNaN matches NaN; atMostMean and atLeastMean compare with the array mean; nearMean is within tolerance of the mean; pointNear and cellContaining test locations.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Tolerance
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: Non-negative distance: for pointNear, the search radius in world units; for nearMean, the allowed deviation from the array mean in the array's units.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Value
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: Number compared with the term by a comparison test, in the units of the tested array.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Values
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: Numbers for the oneOf test; an element matches when its term equals any of them (ParaView in1d). 1 to 256 values.

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.label: Value
/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: One number in the oneOf list.
Groups of clauses. An element is selected when at least one group matches; use a single group for an ordinary AND query. 1 to 16 groups, joined with | in the generated text.
One alternative: an object whose "all" list holds the clauses that must all be true for this group to match.
Clauses that must all be true for this group to match. 1 to 16 clauses, each wrapped in parentheses and joined with & in the generated text.

pitfalls: A member the chosen test does not use is rejected rather than ignored (INVALID_SELECTION_QUERY).

/$defs/options-pvSelectionQuerySource/pr.explanation: A runtime value replaces a literal setting with an expression that Schemaxis evaluates on each selected visit (one combination of simulation time and active axis values) before this setting is applied; $observe and $sample read upstream nodes after they have been updated on that visit. Main forms: {"$axis": name} reads the current sweep value, {"$time": true} the current simulation time, {"$observe": node, "path": [...]} metadata such as bounds or field ranges of an updated upstream node, {"$sample": node, ...} one numeric data value, {"$calc": ...} arithmetic, vector and bounds operations, and {"$call": name, "args": {...}} a registered function such as boundsCentre. The result must still be valid for this setting; see docs/dollar-reference.md.
pitfalls: Constructor settings, such as reader file names, must be constant; a runtime value there fails (DYNAMIC_CONSTRUCTOR).
$observe and $sample make the named node a dependency, so it must be upstream; pointing back at this node or a consumer creates a cycle (PIPELINE_CYCLE).
A marker replaces the whole value; it is not interpolated inside a string.
In scene styles and cameras, $axis may only name an axis the scene's nodes already vary; use an explicit camera list for camera-only variation.
