/$defs/options-pvPLOT3DReader/properties.explanation: Path of one optional PLOT3D solution file (.q) holding density, momentum and energy for every grid block; its blocks and dimensions must match the grid file. Further entries form a file series, one time step per file in the order listed. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder.
sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/paraview/paraview/-/raw/v5.13.3/VTKExtensions/IOCore/vtkFileSeriesReader.h (files are read in the order they are added)
ParaView 5.13.3 VTK/IO/Parallel/vtkMultiBlockPLOT3DReader.cxx:1558-1579 (no q file: nothing is read)

/$defs/options-pvSLACDataReader/properti.explanation: Path of one optional SLAC mode file whose points are the same as the mesh file's. A single file is usually one eigenmode; several files are usually successive time steps, and the order of the list also fixes which FrequencyScale and PhaseShift entry applies to each mode. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 VTK/IO/NetCDF/vtkSLACReader.cxx:665-686 (mode files are read only when the list is non-empty)

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvExodusIIReader (Reads Exodus II finite-element results (.e, .exo, .g, .ex2 …, written by SEACAS-based codes such as Sierra, MOOSE or Cubit) into a multiblock dataset of unstructured grids: element blocks, optional face and edge blocks, node, side and element sets, and global variables, with nodal and element result variables per time step). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: Identifies pvExodusIIReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvPLOT3DReader (Reads NASA PLOT3D structured-grid data: a grid file (.xyz) with block coordinates, solution files (.q) holding density, momentum and stagnation energy, and a function file (.f) of extra variables). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.explanation: Identifies pvPLOT3DReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/81.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvRTXMLPolyDataReader (real-time VTK XML polydata reader (vtkRTXMLPolyDataReader): it can watch a data directory (Location, optional) for .vtp files arriving from a running simulation; each run of its UpdateToNextFile command reads the next unprocessed file, and ResetReader rescans the directory). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/81/propert.explanation: Identifies pvRTXMLPolyDataReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvRestartedSimExodusReader (Reads an Exodus simulation that was restarted, through a metadata file listing the output file sets of each restart, so they behave as one continuous time series). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.explanation: Identifies pvRestartedSimExodusReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87.explanation: Verify the exported file by reading it back with pvSLACDataReader (Reads the NetCDF-based mesh and mode files of SLAC's accelerator electromagnetics codes (Omega3P, Tau3P and related tools)). Choose this when ParaView’s automatic reader choice is wrong for the file, or when you need this reader’s settings (for example which arrays to load) for the comparison.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.explanation: Identifies pvSLACDataReader as the readback reader for this choice. Schemaxis supplies the exported file name itself; do not author it.
Configure the operation here. Required fields must be supplied; enable optional fields when you want to specify them.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: If this flag is on and HasModeShapes is also on, then this reader will report a continuous time range [0,1] and animate the displacements in a periodic sinusoid. If this flag is off and HasModeShapes is on, this reader ignores time. This flag has no effect if HasModeShapes is off.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Animate Vibrations

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: Geometric locations can include displacements. When this option is on, the nodal positions are 'displaced' by the standard exodus displacement vector. If displacements are turned 'off', the user can explicitly add them by applying a warp filter.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Apply Displacements

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: When displacements are being applied, they are scaled by this amount. Set to 1 for no scaling.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Displacement Magnitude

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: Use this property to select which blocks of edges should be loaded. All edges in the same block will have the same interpolant (linear, quadratic, etc.) and have the same variables defined over them.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Edge Blocks

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One edge block to load: explicitly stored edge elements of one type. Edge blocks are disabled by default. Listing names loads exactly those edge blocks.

Specify which maps defined over edges in the mesh should be loaded. An edge map is a renumbering of all the edges (across all the edge blocks of a file) from their offset in the file to some arbitrary integers, usually specifying a unique global ID across a set of files.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Edge Map Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One edge map to load: a renumbering of all edges in the edge blocks to arbitrary integers, usually global ids. Only the first map of each kind is loaded by default.

An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the edges (across all edge blocks) in a file as sets in their own right. This property specifies which of those sets should be loaded. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per edge. The accompanying EdgeSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Edge Set Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One edge set to load: a subset of the edges in the edge blocks, appearing as its own block of the output. Sets are disabled by default.

An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the edges (across all edge blocks) in a file as sets in their own right. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per edge. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. The corresponding set must also be loaded using the EdgeSetArrayStatus property in order for the variable to appear.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Edge Set Result Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One variable defined on edge sets (one value per edge of the set) to load. It appears only if the set itself is enabled in EdgeSetArrayStatus.

Use this property to select which variables defined over edges should be loaded. Edges are oriented boundaries of one or more higher-dimensional cells also present in the mesh. Edge variables specify a single value per entry in some edge block.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Edge Variables

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One variable defined on edge blocks (one value per edge) to load for each time step. It appears only on edge blocks that are themselves loaded.

Use this property to select which blocks of elements (cells) should be loaded. All elements (cells) in the same block will have the same interpolant (tetrahedral, triangular, trilinear hexahedral, etc.) and have the same variables defined over them.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Element Blocks

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One element block to load: a group of cells of one element type, usually one material or part. Use the name stored in the file, or 'Unnamed block ID: n' when it has none (with UseLegacyBlockNamesWithElementTypes the element type is appended). Listing names loads exactly those blocks; by default every element block loads.

Specify which maps defined over elements (cells) in the mesh should be loaded. An element map is a renumbering of all the elements (across all the element blocks of a file) from their offset in the file to some arbitrary integers, usually specifying a unique global ID across a set of files. These are sometimes called new-style maps because they are specified differently than in older Exodus files, which only allowed a single element map.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Element Map Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One element map to load: a renumbering of all elements to arbitrary integers, usually global element ids across a partitioned mesh. Only the first map of each kind is loaded by default.

An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the elements (across all element blocks) in a file as sets in their own right. This property specifies which of those sets should be loaded. Variables, such as feature classifiers, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per element. The accompanying ElementSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Element Set Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One element set to load: a subset of elements taken across element blocks (for example a region tagged by a classifier), appearing as its own block of the output. Sets are disabled by default.

An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the elements (across all element blocks) in a file as sets in their own right. Variables, such as feature classifiers, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per element. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. The corresponding set must also be loaded using the ElementSetArrayStatus property in order for the variable to appear.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Element Set Result Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One variable defined on element sets (one value per element of the set) to load. It appears only if the set itself is enabled in ElementSetArrayStatus.
Use this property to select which variables defined over elements (cells) should be loaded. Element variables specify a single value per entry in some element block.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Element Variables

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One element (per-cell) result variable to load for each time step, such as a stress or plastic-strain field; component variables are combined into vectors or tensors as for PointVariables. Result variables are disabled by default.

Use this property to select which blocks of faces should be loaded. All faces in the same block will have the same interpolant (triangular, bilinear quadrilateral, etc.) and have the same variables defined over them.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Face Blocks

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One face map to load: a renumbering of all faces in the face blocks to arbitrary integers, usually global ids. Only the first map of each kind is loaded by default.

The accompanying FaceSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Face Set Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One face set to load: a subset of the faces in the face blocks, appearing as its own block of the output. Sets are disabled by default.

Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per face. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. /$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Face Set Result Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from [-1, -1].

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Generate File Id Array

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: Should the reader retrieve the first new-style element map, or if that is not present, the solitary old-style element map (which always exists but may be procedurally generated if it is not stored with the file)?
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Generate Global Element Id Array

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: Should the reader retrieve the first new-style node map, or if that is not present, the solitary old-style node map (which always exists but may be procedurally generated if it is not stored with the file)?
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Generate Global Node Id Array

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Generate Object Id Cell Array

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Global Variables

Rather, each represents the vibration at a different "mode." Setting the value of this property to 1 changes the semantics of the reader to not report the time steps to downstream filters.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Has Mode Shapes

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: If on, the reader will ignore the time value reported at each time step, using the index of the time step as the time value. This is useful for Exodus files where different time steps are overloaded to represent different aspects of a data set rather than the data set at different time values.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Ignore File Time

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: Specify which mode shape to animate when HasModeShapes is on.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Mode Shape

These are sometimes called new-style maps because they are specified differently than in older Exodus files, which only allowed a single node map.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Node Map Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One node map to load: a renumbering of all nodes to arbitrary integers, usually global ids that tie together the pieces of a partitioned mesh. Only the first map of each kind is loaded by default.

Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per node. This property specifies which of those sets should be loaded. /$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Node Set Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One node set to load: a named subset of nodes, typically where a boundary condition applies. A loaded set appears as its own block of the output. Sets are disabled by default.

Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per node. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. /$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Node Set Result Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Point Variables

Components stored as separate variables ending in X, Y, Z (for example DISPLX, DISPLY, DISPLZ) are combined into one vector named without the suffix (DISPL); use the name the reader lists. Result variables are disabled by default.

Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per side. For example, a hexahedron has 18 sides: 6 faces and 12 edges. Any of these sides may be individually called out in a set and assigned a result value. The accompanying SideSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Side Set Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One side set to load: a set of element sides (faces or edges of elements), typically a boundary surface for loads or contact. A loaded set appears as its own block of the output. Sets are disabled by default.

An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the of all the elements in a file as sets in their own right. /$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Side Set Result Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.explanation: One variable defined on side sets (one value per side) to load, such as a pressure or flux on a boundary. It appears only if the set itself is enabled in SideSetArrayStatus.

This has issues with consistency when naming blocks across ranks for partitioned files. Hence we no longer do that. For legacy pipelines, one can enable the old behavior by setting this flag to true.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Use Legacy Block Names With Element Types

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.label: Use Meta File
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/26/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; ParaView 5.13.3 starts from false.
pitfalls: The native help text ('must always be set to 1') was written for the restart reader; setting it true here makes the reader expect a metadata file.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.label: Auto Detect Format

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.explanation: This property indicates whether the data files are binary.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.label: Binary File

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.explanation: This property specifies the byte order of any binary file(s).
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.label: Byte Order

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.label: Double Precision

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.label: Force Read

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.explanation: This property lists which functions (point-centered arrays) to compute.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.label: Functions

pitfalls: VTK notes that Pressure Coefficient, Mach Number and Sound Speed need an OVERFLOW-style Q file with gamma; check them against your solver's output.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.explanation: This property indicates whether this file uses Fortran leading-trailing byte counts.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.label: Has Byte Count

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.explanation: This property indicates whether this dataset has visibility information.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.label: I Blanking

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.explanation: This property indicates whether these files have multiple-block information.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.label: Multi Grid

This is useful to avoid using up memory for arrays that are not relevant for the analysis.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.label: Preserve Intermediate Functions

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/72/propert.explanation: This property indicates whether the data is two- or three-dimensional.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.explanation: One node set to load: a named subset of nodes, typically where a boundary condition applies. A loaded set appears as its own block of the output. Sets are disabled by default.

An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the nodes (points) in a file as sets in their own right. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per node. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. The corresponding set must also be loaded using the NodeSetArrayStatus property in order for the variable to appear.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.label: Node Set Result Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.explanation: One variable defined on node sets (one value per node of the set) to load. It appears only if the set itself is enabled in NodeSetArrayStatus.
Use this property to select which nodal (i.e., per-point) variables should be loaded.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.label: Point Variables

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.explanation: One nodal (per-point) result variable to load for each time step. Components stored as separate variables ending in X, Y, Z (for example DISPLX, DISPLY, DISPLZ) are combined into one vector named without the suffix (DISPL); use the name the reader lists. Result variables are disabled by default.

An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the of all the elements in a file as sets in their own right. This property specifies which of those sets should be loaded. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per side. For example, a hexahedron has 18 sides: 6 faces and 12 edges. Any of these sides may be individually called out in a set and assigned a result value. The accompanying SideSetResultArrayStatus property specifies which variables defined over those sets should be loaded.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.label: Side Set Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.explanation: One side set to load: a set of element sides (faces or edges of elements), typically a boundary surface for loads or contact. A loaded set appears as its own block of the output. Sets are disabled by default.

An Exodus II file may define subsets of all the of all the elements in a file as sets in their own right. Variables, such as boundary conditions, may then be defined over these sets by specifying a single number per side. For example, a hexahedron has 18 sides: 6 faces and 12 edges. Any of these sides may be individually called out in a set and assigned a result value. This property specifies which of those variables should be loaded. The corresponding set must also be loaded using the SideSetArrayStatus property in order for the variable to appear.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.label: Side Set Result Array Status

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.explanation: One variable defined on side sets (one value per side) to load, such as a pressure or flux on a boundary. It appears only if the set itself is enabled in SideSetArrayStatus.

In previous versions, the reader added the type of elements in the block to the block name when no name was provided for the block. This has issues with consistency when naming blocks across ranks for partitioned files. Hence we no longer do that. For legacy pipelines, one can enable the old behavior by setting this flag to true.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.label: Use Legacy Block Names With Element Types

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.explanation: This hidden property must always be set to 1 for this proxy to work.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/83/propert.label: Use Meta File

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.explanation: Sets the scale factor for each mode. By default, each scale factor is set to 1.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.label: Frequency Scale

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.explanation: Amplitude factor for one mode, by position: the first element applies to the first mode file, the second to the second, and so on. For oscillating (frequency) modes each mode's field magnitude is multiplied by its factor before the modes are summed, so the factors set the relative weight of superposed modes.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; every mode starts with factor 1 (ParaView documentation and vtkSLACReader).
pitfalls: The factor is used only for mode files that store a frequency; time-series mode files are read as stored.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.explanation: Sets the phase offset for each mode. By default, shift is set to 0.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.label: Phase Shift

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.explanation: Phase offset added to one mode, by position (first element for the first mode file, and so on). The reader evaluates each oscillating mode as cos(initial phase + 2πft + shift), so a shift moves that mode within its cycle, e.g. to align superposed modes.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.defaultMeaning: Not set by Schemaxis; every mode starts with shift 0.
pitfalls: Degrees are not converted: a quarter period is 1.5708, not 90.

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.explanation: If on, read the external surfaces of the data set.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.label: Read External Surface

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.explanation: If on, read the internal volume of the data set.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.label: Read Internal Volume

/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.explanation: If on, reads midpoint information for external surfaces and builds quadratic surface triangles.
/$defs/readback/anyOf/1/oneOf/87/propert.label: Read Midpoints

/$defs/options-pvPLOT3DReader/properties.explanation: Path of one optional PLOT3D solution file (.q) holding density, momentum and energy for every grid block; its blocks and dimensions must match the grid file. Further entries form a file series, one time step per file in the order listed. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder.
sources: https://gitlab.kitware.com/paraview/paraview/-/raw/v5.13.3/VTKExtensions/IOCore/vtkFileSeriesReader.h (files are read in the order they are added)
ParaView 5.13.3 VTK/IO/Parallel/vtkMultiBlockPLOT3DReader.cxx:1558-1579 (no q file: nothing is read)

/$defs/options-pvSLACDataReader/properti.explanation: Path of one optional SLAC mode file whose points are the same as the mesh file's. A single file is usually one eigenmode; several files are usually successive time steps, and the order of the list also fixes which FrequencyScale and PhaseShift entry applies to each mode. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder.
sources: ParaView 5.13.3 VTK/IO/NetCDF/vtkSLACReader.cxx:665-686 (mode files are read only when the list is non-empty)
